# Changelog

All notable changes to `bsv-rs` are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed: the node oracle's judge after its first live day: the sync's stage R run is judged, one verdict per head, the sweep's words (#97, fix-97c)

- What was wrong. A run of `sibling-run.yml` the `GITHUB_TOKEN` dispatches raises no `workflow_run` (GitHub: events the token triggers create no workflow run, `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` excepted), so the trampoline never judged it, and the judgement of the same head's pull request run, finding the newer run, posted nothing and trusted that run's own judgement to come (witness 11, #947: run 43476255821 judged by no event, run 43476238287 answered `superseded by run 43476255821`). The sync's step starts stage R exactly so: a sync pull request would never have earned `sibling-judge`. The sweep named GitHub's failed `push` run of an unparsed `sibling-run.yml` with a re-judge act that is silent, and read `check absent` for a head whose judgement was running. The trampoline's comment said no judgement is cancelled or dropped; GitHub keeps one pending run per concurrency group and a newer pending run replaces it.
- The sync (`.github/workflows/sync-main-into-beta.yml`): the stage R step takes the run's id from the dispatch's answer (`return_run_details`), waits for that run and dispatches `sibling-judge.yml` on main with the id; a refused dispatch or a run not completed in 40 minutes fails the job. It holds no key. Pinned by `SYNC_STAGE_R`, `SYNC_FILE_DIGEST` and `the_sync_stage_r_step_waits_for_its_own_run_and_dispatches_its_judge_97c` (seven plants).
- The judge (`.github/scripts/sibling_judge.py`): one verdict per head. A judgement resolves its run to the newest stage R run of the same head (path, head repository and event stage R's), at its latest attempt, waiting up to 300 s for one still running, and reads the identity on the run judged; still running after the wait, no check and the sweep names the head. `report` resolves again with no wait, and where its own reading owes a check it does not trust the judge job's `post=no` (`NOT JUDGED` with the re-judge). The sweep counts a stage R run by path, event and head repository, names a push of a parsing file for an unparsed stage R, a re-judge once a running run completes, and `check judge in progress` for a head whose judgement is queued or running. `test_sibling_judge.py`: 104 tests (92), the interleavings table of `docs/lanes/fix-97c.md` one test a row; 15 failures and 1 error on the base's script (a scratch copy without git adds one error of its own).
- The trampoline: its concurrency comment says what GitHub does and what recovers a dropped judgement; the group stays per head.
- The manual and RELEASING step 25 say what a pull request that edits `sibling-run.yml` runs (its own file, GitHub runs the event's workflow file) and that its success's only signal is the title `JUDGE CHANGE`; `tests/sibling/CLAUDE.md`'s "What the judge does not hold" gains the public repository `report`'s reads need, the environment's two settings an admin can change, and the head's own build as review's to catch.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#97, fix-97c)

No SDK has a twin of the judge's workflows. No verdict, word or byte of the crate moves, and no row of the root `CLAUDE.md` divergence list is touched.

### Fixed: to_ef, to_hex_ef and from_json's fields refuse an amount of 2^53 satoshis or more; the plain writer stays the node's serializer, stated (#843d7)

- What was wrong. Since #844 every reader of a transaction refuses an output amount, and `from_ef` a source amount, of 2^53 satoshis or more, in the reference's words. Two doors still built or wrote what those readers refuse. `Transaction::to_ef` and `to_hex_ef` wrote such an amount (an output's, or a linked source output's) as EF bytes `Transaction::from_ef` refuses, where the reference's `toEF` and `toHexEF` throw at the amount (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/transaction/Transaction.ts:1127-1164`, the source amount at `:1150`, an output's at `:1158`; `primitives/WriterUint8Array.ts:184-185`; `primitives/BigNumber.ts:460-463`, `The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)`). And `Transaction::from_json` of a document without `hex` held an output's `satoshis` member as any `u64` (#845's stated cell): the one door where text from outside built a transaction whose bytes the readers of #844 refuse (the one-input door reads them, #874). And for an input that names no txid (`TransactionInput::with_source_transaction`, `add_input_from_tx`: this crate's builder path, `sign` never writing the txid) `to_ef` judged the spent output's amount alone, after the unlocking script, where the reference writes that outpoint from the source's `hash()` (`Transaction.ts:1137-1138`) and so throws for such an amount in any output of the source, ahead of the unlocking script's check (the rule read of PR #913: no recorded cell, test or differential input named no txid until its fold).
- The decision (the dated decision of `docs/design/843-identity-and-framing.md` section 9, item 8 (the freeze plan's row 7); six design reads of 2026-11-12, five of six, the tie-break three of three). The plain writer does not change: `to_binary`, `to_hex`, `hash` and `id` stay infallible and write any 64-bit amount as its eight little-endian bytes, the node's serializer. The fact that decided it: an amount has faithful bytes, and 2^53 is the edge of a JavaScript number, no wire rule. That difference from the reference is stated (the note below), never silent.
- The fix. `to_ef` and `to_hex_ef` refuse an output amount, or a linked source output's amount, of 2^53 or more as `TransactionError("The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)")`, the reference writer's words, at the two places an amount is written, so in the reference's written order (`amount::written_amount`); for an input that names no txid, ahead of its other checks, every output of its source and of each source reached through inputs naming no txid, each source once (`amount::unnamed_source_amounts`), as the reference's `hash()` of the source throws. `from_json` of a document without `hex` (absent or empty) refuses an output `satoshis` of 2^53 or more as `TransactionError("Number can only safely store up to 53 bits")`, the byte readers' words, before the output's script is read, as the byte readers read the amount ahead of the script (`amount::held_amount`, the judgment `read_amount` makes).
- The reference's answers by a run. `tests/support/transaction_amount_doors_843d7.mjs` (the SDK at the pin bundled with bun, Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical) records `toEF` and `toHexEF` to `tests/vectors/transaction_amount_doors_843d7.json`: block 170's transaction with a third output, its input linked to a source, with 2^53 - 1, 2^53, 2^63 and 2^64 (as a JavaScript number; this crate's test takes `u64::MAX`) at output 0, 1, 2 and at the source output (sixteen cells: the four at 2^53 - 1 written, the twelve others refused in the writer's words), two controls, and three two-fault cells for the order (a source amount at input 0 with input 1 unlinked answers the amount; an output amount with an input unlinked answers `All inputs must have source transactions when serializing to EF format`; with a linked input lacking its unlocking script, `unlockingScript is undefined`). The fold adds, by the same recorder (two runs byte-identical, the earlier keys unchanged byte for byte): `no_txid`, input 0 naming no txid over a source of two outputs whose own input names no txid over a grandparent, the four edges at the spent output, the unspent one and the grandparent's (twelve cells: the three at 2^53 - 1 written, the nine others refused in the writer's words), its control, and six two-fault orders (the amount's words ahead of input 0's missing unlocking script, for the spent and the unspent output; ahead of `Source output index out of bounds`; ahead of a later unlinked input; `unlockingScript is undefined` at a named input 0 ahead of an unnamed input 1's amount; an unnamed input 1's amount ahead of an output's); and `strength_cells`, the strength read's three orders (S1 a named input's spent amount behind its missing unlocking script, `unlockingScript is undefined`; S2 an unlinked input 0 ahead of input 1's amount, the unlinked `TypeError`; S3 a named input's source carrying an unspent output at 2^53, written). The second fold (the scoped re-read of the fold) adds `walk` by the same recorder (two runs byte-identical, every earlier key unchanged byte for byte), four cells, each input naming a txid there naming `33`x32: M1, input 0 naming no txid over a source whose own input names a txid and links a grandparent of one output at 2^53, written (the plain writer writes a named outpoint from its text and never hashes what it links, `Transaction.ts:1069-1071`); M2, a clean named input 0 and an unnamed input 1 whose source carries 2^53 in an output it does not spend, refused in the writer's words; and the residual the re-read named, a source of input 0 (naming no txid) whose own input lacks its unlocking script, with 2^53 in the source's unspent output (that input naming a txid: `unlockingScript is undefined` there, `:1072-1074` before `:1083`; the amount's words here, stated) or in a grandparent's output (that input naming no txid: the grandparent's hash written ahead of that check, `:1067`, the amount's words on both). The third fold (the second scoped re-read) adds `walk.space` by the same recorder (two runs byte-identical, every earlier key unchanged byte for byte, `walk.cells` and `walk.named_txid` among them): a fixed sample of 38 cells of the property's space below (for each depth 1 to 4 and each unnamed input 0 to 3, every link naming no txid with 2^53 at the deepest level's output 1, refused, and every link naming none but the last with 2^53 at the deepest level's output 0, written (at depth 1 no 2^53); then six mixed cells), so every depth and every index appears at least twice, and the re-read's two deeper cells among them (`u0_d3_links_un_at_l3o0`, a level whose input names a txid over a level at 2^53, written; `u2_d1_links_none_at_l1o1`, an unnamed input 2 whose source carries 2^53, refused): 19 written, 19 refused in the writer's words.
- What pins it. `tests/transaction_amount_doors_843d7.rs`: `a_json_output_amount_of_two_to_the_53_is_refused_843d7` (the field document, `hex` absent and `""`, the amount at output 0, 1 and 2; 2^53 - 1 held; ahead of a script that is no hex); `to_ef_refuses_an_amount_the_ef_reader_refuses_843d7` (every recorded cell: the reference's hex where it writes, read back by `from_ef`, its words where it throws); `the_writer_is_the_nodes_serializer_stated_843d7` (the stating pin: 4,200 seeded transactions, every amount class at output 0, a middle one and the last; `to_binary` each amount's eight bytes, `id` their double hash, `SpendingTransaction::from_bytes` reading every one, `from_binary` reading back exactly when every amount is below 2^53; tx-00026 rebuilt from its fields the node oracle's bytes; since the fold the field document of each of the 4,200 answering as `from_binary` of its bytes, verdict, id and error, the strength read's F2); `to_ef_on_an_input_that_names_no_txid_refuses_as_the_reference_843d7` (the twelve cells, the control and the six orders) and `the_three_orders_the_strength_read_named_are_the_references_843d7` (S1 to S3); since the second fold `the_walk_stops_at_a_named_input_and_judges_every_input_843d7` (the four `walk` cells: M1 and M2 and the agreeing residual cell on bytes and words, the stated one on both sides' words). Its RED: on a scratch copy of the tip, the walk descending through an input that names a txid (`amount.rs`, `if true` for `if input.source_txid.is_none()`) RED at M1 (`left: "The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)"`, `right: "written"`), and the check applied to input 0 alone (`transaction.rs`, the `to_ef` hook) RED at M2 (`left: "written"`); every other test green under both, as the re-read found. Since the third fold the two rules are a property over their whole small space, `the_walk_is_the_references_over_every_depth_and_input_843d7`: an oracle written in the test from the reference's lines alone (`#writeEF` `:1131-1158`, `#writeTransactionBody` `:1059-1089`: the hash of an unnamed input's source throws exactly when 2^53 sits at a level every link above it reaches naming no txid), held before anything else against the 38 recorded cells (verdict, words, and this crate's bytes where both write), then every one of the 452 cases (four inputs, the unnamed one at index 0 to 3; a chain of 1 to 4 levels of two outputs each, every pattern of the links between them named or not; 2^53 nowhere or at either output of any level), built by this crate's builders, through `to_ef` and `to_hex_ef` against the oracle, every differing case named by its description. The space is the property's bound: depth up to 4 and the unnamed input at index up to 3; a fault that shows only past it (a fifth level, a fifth input, two unnamed inputs in one transaction, a level of two link inputs) is outside what it pins. Its RED, each plant alone on a scratch copy of the tip (its own target, removed): the walk descending through a named input (`if true`, the earlier re-read's M1) 184 cases, the earliest `u0_d2_links_n_at_l2o0`; the walk stopping at a named input only among the source's own inputs (`|| !std::ptr::eq(tx, source)`, the second re-read's P2) 48, the earliest `u0_d3_links_un_at_l3o0`; the check on input 0 alone (M2) 111, the earliest `u1_d1_links_none_at_l1o1`; on the last input alone (P1) 111, the earliest `u0_d1_links_none_at_l1o1`; on inputs 0 and 1 alone (P3) 74, the earliest `u2_d1_links_none_at_l1o1`; and a wrong oracle (descending through named links) fails on the recording, 14 recorded cells by both doors, the earliest `u0_d2_links_n_at_l2o0`. Under P2 and P3 every earlier test is green. `fuzz_transaction_parser` reads its input as JSON too: a transaction `from_json` builds holds no amount of 2^53 or more and reads back from its bytes to its txid (F3, a JSON seed in its corpus). In `tests/transaction_numbers_844.rs` the stated `the_json_fields_carry_an_amount_the_readers_refuse_stated_844` is replaced in place by `the_json_fields_refuse_an_amount_the_readers_refuse_843d7`. The fold's RED, on a scratch copy of the tip before it (`75c41e40`, its own target): `to_ef_on_an_input_that_names_no_txid_refuses_as_the_reference_843d7` RED, 20 differing lines (six cells by two doors written, `from_ef` reading the bytes back; four orders by two doors in other words), the four others green; on the tip six plants each RED and restored: S1, S2 and S3 each in the strength test (the spent amount judged ahead of the unlocking script; every spent amount in a pass ahead of the loop; a named input's source judged whole), F2 in the stating pin (`from_json` holding the amount), the source walk stopped at the source and the walk moved after the unlocking script in the no-txid test; and F3 by the fuzz target on a 2^53 JSON input with `from_json` holding the amount. On the base (`6ca95187`, a scratch copy, its own target) the JSON test, the EF test and the replaced test are RED (`unwrap_err()` on an `Ok`; 26 differing lines, `here Ok(..)` whose bytes `from_ef` refuses); the stating pin is green there and RED under two plants in the serializer on a scratch copy of the tip (a refusal of an amount of 2^53 or more; a clamp of it to 2^53 - 1).
- Migration. No signature moves and no public item (the rustdoc JSON of base and tip differ in the docs of `to_ef`, `to_hex_ef` and `from_json` alone; cargo-semver-checks 0.51.0 as a patch: 229 checks pass, no semver update required). Three doors answer `Err` where they answered `Ok`:
  - `Transaction::to_ef` and `to_hex_ef` on a transaction with an output amount, or a linked source output's amount, of 2^53 or more, or with an input naming no txid whose source (or a source it reaches through inputs naming no txid) carries such an amount in any output: `TransactionError("The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)")`; on such an unnamed input ahead of its missing unlocking script and of `Source output index out of bounds`, which it answered until the fold (an `Err` either way). No node accepts such an output (`MAX_MONEY` is 21e14, below 2^53), and `from_ef` refused the bytes already. `TeranodeBroadcaster::broadcast` maps `to_ef`'s error as before, so it answers `EF_SERIALIZATION_ERROR` for such a transaction before any request. Where the amount sits at an earlier input than an unlinked one, the answer is the amount's words where it was the unlinked input's (an `Err` either way).
  - `Transaction::from_json` of a document without `hex` whose output `satoshis` is 2^53 or more: `TransactionError("Number can only safely store up to 53 bits")`, the error `from_hex` gives the same transaction's bytes.
  - A differential over 20,000 seeded transactions (a tenth with an amount at or past 2^53 at an output, a linked source's spent output or a second, unspent output of a linked source; since the fold a third of the linked inputs, 12,522, naming no txid), beta (`bb248ec7`) against the tip, eight calls each: `to_binary`, `to_hex`, `id`, `to_json` and `from_json(to_json())` 0 differing lines of 20,000 each; `to_ef` and `to_hex_ef` each 1,418 `Ok` now the decided `Err` (606 by an output, 391 by a named input's spent amount, 199 by an unnamed one's, 222 by an unnamed input's unspent source output) and 30 `Err` whose words moved from a later unlinked input's to the amount's (the recorded order); the field `from_json` 692 `Ok` now the decided `Err`. The 464 transactions whose unsafe amount sits at a named input's unspent source output write on both, as the reference writes them. Against the tip before the fold (`75c41e40`) the moved lines are the 222 and the 6 of the unspent unnamed kind alone. No other line differs.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#843d7)

The plain writer is stated, not conformed. The reference's `#writeTransactionBody` writes each output's amount through `writeUInt64LE` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:1083`), which builds a `BigNumber` of the JavaScript number and throws `The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)` past 2^53 - 1 (`WriterUint8Array.ts:184-185`, `BigNumber.ts:460-463`), so its `toBinary`, `toHex`, `hash` and `id` throw for such an amount; this crate's `to_binary`, `to_hex`, `hash` and `id` write it, as the node serializes an amount (bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `src/primitives/transaction.h:190-194`, `READWRITE(nValue)`; `src/amount.h:109-112`, any 64-bit value; `MAX_MONEY`, `amount.h:130`, is validation's) and as go-sdk@2ca481c writes any `uint64` (`transaction/output.go:92`; EF `transaction/transaction.go:465`). This crate's one-input door reads those bytes back since #874; its other readers refuse them (#844). `toEF` and `toHexEF` are followed on every recorded cell, verdict, words and bytes, an input that names no txid included (the fold of the rule read of PR #913): the reference writes that outpoint from `i.sourceTransaction.hash()` (`Transaction.ts:1137-1138`), its plain writer, ahead of the unlocking script's check (`:1143-1145`), so its `toEF` throws the writer's words for an amount of 2^53 or more in any output of that source, or of a source reached through its own inputs naming no txid, and `to_ef` refuses there in those words, ahead of that input's other checks. The reference's plain writer's other refusals of such a source (`:1063-1075`: an input of it naming nothing, a txid `requireTXID` refuses, no unlocking script) are not ported to that path: through `to_ef` such a source is written here and refused there, stated (the lane record's rows left); where that source also carries an amount of 2^53 or more, both refuse, the reference in its plain writer's words for the earliest input it meets and this crate in the amount's (the recorded `walk` cell `source_input_named_lacking_its_unlocking_script_with_source_other_output`: `unlockingScript is undefined` there, `The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)` here), stated in the same row. The plain writer's reach at the two raw-hex broadcasters, read and not recorded: `WhatsOnChainBroadcaster::broadcast` and the deprecated `ArcBroadcaster::broadcast` post `to_hex()` of a transaction holding such an amount, where the reference's throw at `tx.toHex()` or `tx.toHexEF()` before any request (`WhatsOnChainBroadcaster.ts:45`, `ARC.ts:93-103,325`). The JSON form has no reference twin (`Transaction.ts` has no JSON reader or writer); go-sdk's JSON type holds `Satoshis uint64` (`transaction/txjson.go:28-31`). `to_json` is unchanged and stated: it writes the amount and a `hex` its own `from_json` refuses (`tests/transaction_numbers_844.rs`). Ours: the plain writer, the node's serializer. Theirs: none.

### Changed (breaking): `PeerOptions`, `AuthFetchOptions` and `WebSocketTransportOptions` are `#[non_exhaustive]`, built by `new`/`Default` and `with_` setters; every all-public struct under `src/` is attributed or listed with its reason (#843d8a)

**What changed.** The three auth option records carry `#[non_exhaustive]` (the freeze plan's row 8, part a; the captain's rulings of 2026-11-12 on three design reads). Their fields stay `pub` and readable; a struct literal or a functional update outside the crate no longer compiles (E0639), and a pattern over one ends in `..`. `PeerOptions::new(wallet, transport)` sets no certificates to request, no session manager (a new one at `Peer::new`), no originator and `auto_persist_last_session` true, the reference's default; `with_certificates_to_request`, `with_session_manager`, `with_auto_persist_last_session` and `with_originator` set the other four. `AuthFetchOptions` keeps its `Default` and takes `with_method`, `with_headers`, `with_body`, `with_retry_counter`, `with_payment_retry_attempts`, `with_labels`. `WebSocketTransportOptions::new(base_url: impl Into<String>)` sets no read deadline (30 seconds, as before) and takes `with_read_deadline_secs`. Each setter takes its field's own type (`with_x(self, value) -> Self`), the shape of `WorkBudget` (`src/transaction/work_budget.rs`). No behaviour, wire byte, verdict, error text, default, field type or existing signature moves; no other struct is opened.

**Why a literal was wrong.** A record of options grows: the reference's `Peer` constructor took six arguments at `ts-sdk@9e3ede6b` (`src/auth/Peer.ts:85-92`) and takes seven at `ts-stack@edf6e03` (`packages/sdk/src/auth/Peer.ts:139-147`, the seventh `messageValidation: AuthMessageValidationOptions = {}`), and its fetch options are a record of seven optional members (`packages/sdk/src/auth/clients/AuthFetch.ts:33-49`), where this crate's has six. A struct every field of which is `pub` is built by a literal downstream, so its next field breaks every caller; opened now, a later field is no break.

**What pins it.** Each of the three structs is pinned by `tests/arch_non_exhaustive_pins_819.rs` (#896's machine, one for every `#[non_exhaustive]` type under `src/`): its doc carries a `compile_fail,E0639` functional update naming no field (`fn rebuilt(value: T) -> T { T { ..value } }`) and its compiling twin (`fn kept`), `assert_no_drop!` of its name and its pin's path follows it, and the doc suite's log carries both lines by name (`DOC_PINS`); `PeerOptions`, a generic struct, is pinned at `PeerOptions<ProtoWallet, MockTransport>` (the fold below); with the attribute removed in a copy of the tip each one's `compile_fail` test is RED (it compiles) and the machine names all three. `tests/auth_options_843d8a.rs` (5 tests): `new`'s values, every setter set and reset, `Default` unchanged, a `Peer` and a `WebSocketTransport` built from them; compile-RED on `43ee8c85` (5 errors, E0599). `tests/arch_non_exhaustive_843d.rs` (6 tests, lexical, on `tests/arch_support`): every `pub struct` under `src/` whose fields are all `pub` (219 on this change: 218 braced, one tuple, `HeadersFn`; six generic, seven inside `key_args!`, each read by name) carries the attribute (12: the nine before and the three) or is a row `file:Name` with a class and a reason: `Record` (125, each a reference record's `path:line` at `edf6e03`), `ParameterBlock` (3: `SpendParams`, `TxSpendParams`, `SighashParams`, their field names pinned; a further knob is a `Spend` setter), `Deprecated` (2: `ArcConfig`, `BeefLimits`), `Pending` (20: the freeze plan's 8b and 8c; the length pinned, only lowered) and `Unruled` (57, the same); a row naming no such struct, or an attributed one, fails; each `pub` field of an attributed struct has a `with_<field>` or is a parameter of its `new`, else the struct is a row of `ASSIGNED` with its reason (six of the twelve: `Certificate`'s `received_unsigned`, `ChainParams`, `AbortAcceptance`, `LookupLimits`, `LookupRequestOptions`, `InputVerified`); a `pub struct` inside a macro other than `key_args!` is refused, never passed; `#[non_exhaustive]` alone attributes a struct, and another spelling (a `cfg_attr`, a list) is read as none here and refused by #896's machine (the fold below). On `43ee8c85` with the file overlaid it is RED naming exactly the three; a `pub struct Planted { pub a: u8 }` planted in a copy of the tip is RED naming it.

**The break, measured.** `cargo semver-checks check-release --baseline-rev 43ee8c85 --all-features --release-type patch` (0.51.0): 229 checks, 228 pass, 31 skip, one lint fires, `struct_marked_non_exhaustive`, on the three structs alone. The rustdoc JSON of base and change (nightly, `--all-features`) differs in the three structs' attribute and docs, the thirteen new methods (five on `PeerOptions`, six on `AuthFetchOptions`, two on `WebSocketTransportOptions`), and the doc text of the rewritten examples (`auth`'s, `Peer`'s and the two transport modules'). The dependents' literals (read-only, `git grep`): `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs` 1 `PeerOptions` on `main` and 4 on `beta`, `bsv-overlay-cloudflare` 5 `PeerOptions` (one test file), `bsv-wallet-cli` (both lines) and `rust-message-box` none; no `AuthFetchOptions` or `WebSocketTransportOptions` literal anywhere.

**Migration.** `PeerOptions { wallet, transport, certificates_to_request: c, session_manager: s, auto_persist_last_session: p, originator: o }` becomes `PeerOptions::new(wallet, transport).with_certificates_to_request(c).with_session_manager(s).with_auto_persist_last_session(p).with_originator(o)`, a `None` or a `true` left out, a `false` kept. `AuthFetchOptions { a: v, ..Default::default() }` becomes `AuthFetchOptions::default().with_a(v)`. `WebSocketTransportOptions { base_url, read_deadline_secs: d }` becomes `WebSocketTransportOptions::new(base_url).with_read_deadline_secs(d)`. A pattern over one of the three ends in `..`. This crate's own 31 literals in 17 test files moved by that rule alone (26 `PeerOptions`, every one keeping `.with_auto_persist_last_session(false)`; 4 `AuthFetchOptions`; 1 `WebSocketTransportOptions`), no assertion moved.

**The fold (the rebase onto beta `b36bca93`, after #896, #913 and #815).** A pull request that landed ahead built `PeerOptions` by a literal (`tests/socketio_app_event_receiver_843d23.rs`, #843d23), E0639 at Clippy and the integration tests; it takes the constructor form above, so this crate's own literals moved are 32 in 18 test files, no assertion moved (`cargo check --all-targets --all-features` names no other site; the twelve slices of Clippy build no test). One machine for the pins, one for the table: the three structs' blocks take #896's form (the full path, no `use` line) and its lists name them (`DOC_PINS` 21 to 24; the machine reads 30 `#[non_exhaustive]` types, 24 pinned, 6 listed, from 27, 21 and 6); `tests/arch_non_exhaustive_843d.rs` keeps the table and drops its refusal of another spelling of the attribute, which #896's reader holds (`arch_non_exhaustive_pins_819.rs`' plants at `cfg_attr(all(), ..)` and an attribute list), so no type is judged by two readers of the attribute. ### Fixed: the identity client's by-key, attribute and discovery doors refuse what the reference's wallet door refuses, before any host is asked (#818b, #905)

**What changed.** `IdentityClient::resolve_by_identity_key`, `discover_certificates`, `discover_certificates_by_type` and `resolve_by_attributes` judge their arguments before any lookup, as the reference's wallet door judges them: the key through `validateDiscoverByIdentityKeyArgs` and the attribute map through `validateDiscoverByAttributesArgs` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/wallet/validationHelpers.ts:1535-1587`), in their order and words, a refusal `Error::WalletRefusal` of class `InvalidParameter` (code 6), nothing asked and no host charged. With `override_with_contacts`, `resolve_by_identity_key` judges the key ahead of that by the contacts manager's rule (`ContactsManager.ts:83-94`, `Error::IdentityError` in its words), as the reference's `getContacts(identityKey)` does ahead of its wallet (`IdentityClient.ts:575`). The attribute map is judged as the caller gave it, before the contacts load and before a lone attribute is rewritten to `any`. `discover_certificates_by_type` judges its type after the key by `query`'s rule (`certificateTypes[0]`, the overlay's words, #756's fold): no reference door takes a type, so that rule is this crate's own. The by-key doors' subject filter compares a certificate's subject with the key the validated text names (trimmed as JavaScript trims, lower-cased; `Wallet.ts:1012`), where it compared the text lower-cased and untrimmed; the question still carries the text as given (`Wallet.ts:1004`).

**Why it was wrong.** The reference's `IdentityClient` hands its arguments to its wallet (`IdentityClient.ts:569`, `:614`), whose `WalletClient` validates them before it connects (`WalletClient.ts:509-511`, `:524`), and the toolbox wallet runs the same two validators (`wallet-toolbox/src/Wallet.ts:971`, `:1029`). This crate sent them: `resolve_by_identity_key("zz", false)` asked every host, each refused the whole question (`IdentityLookupService.ts:83-123`), the resolver read the refusal as an empty answer, charged the host for the caller's input and the call answered `Ok([])`, where the reference throws `The identityKey parameter must be hexadecimal string.` with nothing asked. #818's second line held the doors as after-cut on the reading that the reference checks nothing; the rule read of PR #897 found the check one layer down.

**Added.** `wallet::validate_discover_by_identity_key_args(&DiscoverByIdentityKeyArgs) -> Result<PublicKey>` and `wallet::validate_discover_by_attributes_args(&DiscoverByAttributesArgs) -> Result<()>`, public and re-exported at `wallet::` beside #609's, in `src/wallet/validation/client.rs`: the key (`validate_public_key`) then `limit` from 1 to 10000; the map (at most 100000 names, none of `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`, then 1 to 32, then each name 1 to 50 UTF-8 bytes and its value 1 to 500, in the order `Object.keys` walks it, array-index names ahead) then `limit`. `js_order` moved there unchanged; `identity::client_attributes` keeps its name by a `pub(super) use`. The identity doors' checks are in `src/identity/client_door_args.rs`.

**What pins it.** `tests/wallet_discovery_args_818b.rs` (6 tests) and `tests/identity_door_args_818b.rs` (7 tests), against `tests/vectors/identity_door_args_818b.json` (new: 46 cases and 2 subject cells, every door cell with and without contacts, recorded by `tests/support/identity_door_args_818b.mjs` under Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical): the two validators called directly, and the reference's `IdentityClient` over `new WalletClient(double)`, the double counting every call. Every refused cell is refused here in the recorded words with no question sent (#752's recording facilitator), every accepted cell sends one question carrying the text as given; the by-type door's type cases are `tests/vectors/identity_query_bounds_756.json`'s; a space-padded and an upper-case key keep their subject's certificate on #553's reference token. RED on a scratch copy of `5a87392e`: the door file 7 of 7 (`Ok([]), 1 sent` on every refused cell; the padded key `left: 0, right: 1`), the validator file at compile (E0432). Three pins moved to the refusal: `tests/identity_query_attributes_751.rs` (the empty map), `tests/identity_discover_type_744.rs` `the_asked_type_is_compared_as_its_canonical_text_744` (the unpadded type) and `tests/identity_lock_position_537.rs`' key-only case, asked under `02aa` until now and under the generator's key since (its skip unchanged).

**Migration.** No signature moves; a call that answered `Ok` for a malformed argument answers `Err`:
- `resolve_by_identity_key(key, false)`, `discover_certificates(key)`, `discover_certificates_by_type(key, _)`: a key the wallet's rule refuses answers `Err(Error::WalletRefusal { class: WalletRefusalClass::InvalidParameter, message })`, `message` starting `The identityKey parameter must be ` (where it answered `Ok([])`).
- `resolve_by_identity_key(key, true)`: a key the contacts manager's rule refuses answers `Err(Error::IdentityError(message))`, `message` starting `Invalid contact: identityKey `; an upper-case or space-padded key, which the wallet's rule admits, is among them.
- `resolve_by_attributes(map, _)`: a map the wallet's rule refuses, the empty map among them, answers `Err(Error::WalletRefusal { class: WalletRefusalClass::InvalidParameter, message })`, `message` starting `The attributes parameter must be `, `The field name ` or `The attributes.` (where it answered `Ok([])`).
- `discover_certificates_by_type(_, cert_type)`: a type `query` refuses answers `Err(Error::IdentityError(message))`, `message` starting `Invalid lookup query: certificateTypes[0] must be ` (where it answered `Ok([])`).
- A space-padded key at `resolve_by_identity_key(key, false)`, `discover_certificates` and `discover_certificates_by_type` answers its subject's identities or certificates, where it answered `Ok([])`.

### Fixed: sign and verify refuse an input whose source_txid differs from its linked source's id, as the reference does (#848)

An input can carry both a `source_txid` and a linked `source_transaction`. The serializer writes the text when it is 64 hex digits, whatever the source (#869's one rule), while `sign` handed each template the LINKED source's amount and locking script and `verify` found each source by the NAMED txid among the reachable transactions, never by the link. Nothing compared the two. So `sign` committed a signature to the named outpoint with another transaction's amount and script, and `verify` judged an input whose named txid was another reachable transaction's id against that transaction's output: on a transaction whose input 0 links A and names B, with B linked at input 1, it answered `Ok(true)`, where the reference and go-sdk refuse.

Now both doors make the reference's comparison, through one helper over the outpoint rule (`source_named_otherwise`, `src/transaction/source_link.rs`, crate-private, reading `fields.rs`' `outpoint_txid`: an input whose text is 64 hex digits, of either case, over a linked source whose id is another; the source's cached hash, so each source is hashed once):

- `sign`, over every input (a template or not) before any template runs and before any field moves, refuses such an input whose source has an input or a merkle path: `Input N sourceTXID does not reference its supplied source transaction.` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:964-984`). A source with neither is an EF descriptor, which carries only claimed outpoint data, and stays exempt, as the reference's comment says (`:970-972`): the three descriptor doors (`from_ef`, `add_input_from`, `add_inputs_from_utxos`) sign as before.
- `verify`, in every variant and for every unproven transaction of the ancestry, refuses such an input whatever its source holds: `Verification failed because input N of transaction <txid> does not reference its supplied source transaction.` (`Transaction.ts:1423-1432`), after the linked source's output is found (a missing one is named ahead of it, as in the reference) and its amount checked and summed. The walk stays by txid.
- `verify` reads a txid text in upper case as the 32 bytes it names (the serializer's reading, the reference's `requireTXID`, `:95-100`): such an input over its own source was refused (`Input N has no source transaction`) and now verifies.

- `verify` refuses an input that links no source, in the reference's words, `Verification failed because the input at index N of transaction <txid> is missing an associated source transaction. This source transaction is required for transaction verification because there is no merkle proof for the transaction spending a UTXO it contains.` (`Transaction.ts:1396-1400`), whether or not the txid it names is another input's source: until #848's fold such an input was judged against that source when one was reachable (`Ok(true)` on the recorded `unlinked_named_reachable`, input 0 naming B and linking nothing beside input 1 linking B) and refused as `Input N has no source transaction` when none was.
- `verify` reads amounts as the reference does (`requireSatoshiAmount`, `addSatoshiAmount`, `:1414-1418`, `:1464-1474`): every output's amount before any input (`#validateUnminedTransactionStructure`, `:1367`), refused when absent or past 21e14 (`Output N amount must be a non-negative safe integer no greater than 21e14.`) and the total past 21e14 (`Transaction output total exceeds the maximum valid monetary range.`); each source amount refused the same way (`Input N source amount must be ...`) ahead of the mismatch, and the input total past 21e14 (`Transaction input total exceeds ...`). Until the fold an absent amount was read as 0 (an absent source amount `Ok(false)` on the recorded cell) and a total was bounded by `u64` (`Input satoshis overflow`).

A text that is not 64 hex digits is outside this change: the serializer writes the linked source's hash there, so nothing disagrees (#869's cells, #845's writer half).

What reaches the fold's two refusals: an input that links nothing is built by hand (`TransactionInput::new`) or read by `from_binary`, `from_hex` or `from_json`, whose inputs link nothing, so such a transaction was refused by `verify` before (`Input N has no source transaction`) unless another input linked the txid; `from_beef` and `from_atomic_beef` link every input whose source the BEEF holds (a second spend of one parent by a stub of its id, whose copy `verify` does not judge), so no BEEF the readers accept reaches it (pinned). An absent amount is a hand-built state (`TransactionOutput::new_change` before `fee`, or `satoshis: None`); no reader builds one. An amount past 21e14 and below 2^53 is read by every transaction reader (the readers refuse 2^53 and above, #844), so a transaction read from bytes reaches that refusal; the node refuses such an output at every door (`MAX_MONEY`, `MoneyRange`, bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `amount.h:130`, `validation.cpp:543-551`), so no node verdict moves.

Pinned by `tests/transaction_source_txid_mismatch_848.rs` (11) on `tests/vectors/source_txid_mismatch_848.json` (`tests/support/source_txid_mismatch_848.mjs`, `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical): twelve cells (matching; a mismatch over a complete, a proven, an anchored input-less and a descriptor source; a `fromEF` transaction; the text in upper case; the named txid another input's source's id; three orders of two refusals), each fixture built by this crate's writers to the recording's bytes, every recorded `sign` and tracker `verify` answer asserted, no template called and no field moved on a refusal. 8 of 11 RED on `3e1ade84` with the file and vector overlaid on a scratch copy (`left: Ok(true)` for the named txid of another reachable transaction; `left: Ok(())` at `sign`); the fixtures, the unparsable text and the surveyed doors green on both. The fold's `tests/transaction_source_txid_fold_848.rs` (11) on the same vector's two added sections (`templates`, 14 cells; `verify_fold`, 10 cells; the recorder extended, two runs byte-identical, the earlier cells unchanged): every recorded `verify_fold` answer asserted, 4 of 11 RED on a scratch copy of the fold's base with the file and vector overlaid (`left: Ok(Bool(true))` on `unlinked_named_reachable`, `left: Ok(Bool(false))` on `absent_source_amount`), the template cells, the input-1 pin and the BEEF survey green on both.

Migration: a caller that links a complete or proven source under another 64-hex txid now gets `Err(Error::TransactionError(..))` from `sign` and from `verify`; link the source the outpoint names, or drop the link. `verify`'s words for an input whose linked source is not the one named change from `Input N has no source transaction` to the sentence above (a transaction read by `from_ef`, or built by `add_input_from` or `add_inputs_from_utxos`, among them: refused before, refused now). No public item changes and no signature.

Migration (the fold): `verify` of a transaction holding an input that links no source, whose txid another input's source carries, now returns `Err(Error::TransactionError(..))` where it returned `Ok(true)`; link the source at every input (`from_beef` does). `verify` of a transaction whose output or reachable source output has no amount (`satoshis: None`, a change output before `fee`) now returns `Err(Error::TransactionError(..))` where it read 0 (`Ok(false)` or `Ok(true)`); compute the amounts (`fee`) before `verify`. `verify` of one holding an output or a source output past 21e14, or a total past it, now returns `Err(..)` where it could return `Ok(true)`. The words for an input that links nothing move from `Input N has no source transaction` to the reference's sentence above; an input whose text does not parse keeps the old words. `Input satoshis overflow` is gone from `verify` (the reference's total words).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#848)

The two refusals and their words are the reference's (`Transaction.ts:964-984`, `:1423-1432`), and go-sdk@2ca481c refuses at verify too, in its own words (`spv/verify.go:252-262`, `ErrSourceTransactionMismatch`). Stated, ours: (1) the reference's `verify('scripts only')` skips the comparison and uses the named txid (`:1425`, `:1433-1436`), a mode this crate does not have, so a descriptor-sourced transaction (a `from_ef` one) is not verifiable here: refused in the mismatch's words, as the reference refuses it under a tracker (recorded), where the reference's scripts-only run answers `has no inputs` for the descriptor (recorded); (2) the reference's `preimage` refuses a mismatch over any linked source (`sourceTXID does not match sourceTransaction`, `:2157-2169`), a door with no twin here (`SigningContext` takes the raw bytes, the amount and the script, and reads no linked source); (3) where one input breaks two rules both sides refuse and the words can differ: an input with a mismatch and a missing source output is named for the output by the reference's `sign` (`Input N references a source output that does not exist.`) and for the mismatch here (this crate's `sign` reads a source output only for an input with a template); one with a mismatch and no unlocking script is `unlockingScript is undefined` at the reference's `verify` and the mismatch here; and this crate's `verify` reads every input's source before it runs a script, so a mismatch at a later input is named ahead of an earlier input's failing script, which the reference names (three recorded cells, asserted as stated); and a linked source output whose amount is absent or past 21e14 beside a mismatch is named for the amount by the reference's `sign` (`Input N source amount must be a non-negative safe integer no greater than 21e14.`, `:969`, ahead of the comparison) and for the mismatch by this crate's (run on both sides by the cold read of PR #901, not recorded; at `verify` both name the amount since the fold, recorded, `absent_source_amount_and_mismatch`); and under a fee model the reference runs its fee check (`verifyTransactionFee`, `:1318-1333`, through `toEF` and `fee`) before its inputs (`:1654-1655`), so an input that links nothing is named there in `All inputs must have source transactions when serializing to EF format` (`:1134`) and an absent source amount in `Transaction inputs are insufficient for the requested outputs and fee.` (`:859`), where this crate's `verify` reads every source before its fee check and names both in the fold's words above (run on both sides by the review of the fold on the recorded `unlinked_named_reachable` and `absent_source_amount` shapes with `SatoshisPerKilobyte(1)`, not recorded; an absent output amount and a source amount past 21e14 are named alike on both sides); (4) `fee`, `get_fee`, `total_input_satoshis` and `to_ef` read the linked output beside the named txid and make no comparison, as the reference's `fee`, `getFee` and `toEF` make none (recorded on the complete-source mismatch: 895, 895 and the EF bytes, this crate's the same); (5) the reference's stock templates make a comparison of their own, with no exemption: `resolveSourceDetails` (`script/templates/SignatureUtils.ts:94-106`, called by `P2PKH.ts:90`, `PushDrop.ts:232`, `RPuzzle.ts:102` and `OverlayAdminTokenTemplate.ts:328`) throws `The input sourceTXID does not match the input sourceTransaction.` for an input whose `sourceTXID` is not its linked source's id, a no-input descriptor included, so the reference's `sign` of a descriptor-sourced input (a `fromEF` one) under one of those templates is refused at the template, where this crate's `sign` hands the template the descriptor's amount and script and signs the named outpoint: `add_input_from` and `add_inputs_from_utxos` build exactly that input, and a template here takes a `SigningContext`, which reads no linked source. Recorded (the vector's `templates`, 14 cells, by the fold): at all four templates the `add_input_from` descriptor and a `fromEF` transaction are refused in those words and signed here; a complete source under another txid is refused by `Transaction.sign`'s own check ahead of any template on both sides; and the reference signs a claimed outpoint by the named txid alone, no source linked, the amount and script handed to `P2PKH.unlock` or `PushDrop.unlock` (`named_alone`), which this crate cannot express (`Input 0 is missing source satoshis for signing`) and whose unlocking script is byte for byte the one this crate's `sign` writes over the descriptor. Not conformed: the refusal would refuse what `add_input_from` and `add_inputs_from_utxos` exist to do; put to the captain.

### Changed (breaking): no public signature names another crate's number or channel type (#843d23)

**What changed.** `BigNumber` hides its representation: `as_bigint()` and `from_bigint()` are crate-private (and compiled only with `script`, their one caller, the interpreter's arithmetic), and `impl From<num_bigint::BigInt> for BigNumber` and `impl From<BigNumber> for num_bigint::BigInt` are removed. `socketio::install_app_event_listener` returns `(AppEventReceiver, u32)` where it returned `(futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<AppEvent>, u32)`: `AppEventReceiver` is this crate's type (re-exported beside `AppEvent` at `bsv_rs::`, `auth::` and `auth::transports::`), `Send`, with `async fn recv(&mut self) -> Option<AppEvent>` (`None` once the listener is gone, its `Peer` dropped or the callback removed, and the queue empty) and `fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Option<AppEvent>`, and a `Debug` that prints no event. No `Stream` impl: nothing in this tree or the relay consumes the receiver as one, and the trait would put a foreign type back in the surface; the named type can gain it later without a break.

**Why it was wrong.** A type of another crate in a public signature makes that crate's major release this crate's break (rule 9 of `CLAUDE.md`): a `num-bigint` 0.5 or a `futures` 0.4 would have changed `bsv-rs`'s API without a line of `bsv-rs` changing. The owner's word on #843 of 2026-11-10 (item 3 of the freeze plan) took both out before the freeze. No caller wanted the doors: zero uses in `tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`, `fuzz/` and in `rust-message-box`, `bsv-overlay-cloudflare`, `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs` and `bsv-wallet-cli` (grepped at their heads).

**The class, by a machine (rule 11).** `tests/arch_no_foreign_type_843d23.rs` reads every `pub fn` signature, `pub` field, `pub type`, variant field of a `pub enum`, method a `pub trait` declares and trait impl header under `src/` (test modules excepted) and refuses any that names `num_bigint`, `futures` (and `futures_channel`, `futures_util`, `futures_core`), `tokio` (and `tokio_tungstenite`), `reqwest`, `k256`, `p256` or `serde_json` (by path or by an identifier the file imports from it; these roots and no other crate's: `indexmap`'s `IndexMap`, in public fields and signatures of `auth`, `wallet` and `identity`, is not read) unless its enumerated list names the site with a reason; the totals are pinned (`num_bigint`, `futures`, `k256`, `p256` 0; `tokio` 3, `reqwest` 4, `serde_json` 28), and a row matching nothing fails. What it cannot see (a glob import, a macro-built signature, a trait method's copy in an impl, a foreign re-export, reachability) is in its header, covered once by a rustdoc JSON survey at the base and the tip (`docs/lanes/fix-843d23.md`: 42 sites on the base, 36 on the tip; the six removed are this entry's).

**Pinned by** `tests/arch_no_foreign_type_843d23.rs` (on the base it fails naming exactly the five sites), `tests/socketio_app_event_receiver_843d23.rs` (two `Peer`s on `start`, an event built by `build_envelope_payload` read back through `recv`, `try_recv` empty before it, `None` after the peer is dropped and after the listener is removed; compile-RED on the base, E0432 and E0308), `tests/primitives_bignumber_migration_843d23.rs` (the migration lines below, run), and two `compile_fail` doc tests on `BigNumber` (both compile on the base).

**What the receiver asks of `futures` (the fold after the three reads).** `Cargo.toml` asks `futures = "0.3"`, and the receiver as it was written called `UnboundedReceiver::try_recv`, which futures-channel has from 0.3.32 alone: with the `futures` family held at 0.3.31, `cargo check --features "auth,socketio"` failed (`error[E0599]: no method named try_recv`, `src/auth/transports/socketio/app_event.rs:36`), so a consumer whose lockfile held 0.3.31 or older stopped compiling. The manifest's floor stays where it is and the receiver asks nothing newer of it: `try_recv` is one poll of the stream's `next` (`FutureExt::now_or_never` over `StreamExt::next`), an item ready `Some`, an empty open queue `None`, a closed queue `None`, the three answers the method gave. The receiver also drops its channel when the channel answers its end and never polls it again, in `recv` and in `try_recv`: futures-channel 0.3.11 to 0.3.13 panic on a poll after the end (`Receiver::next_message called after None`), later ones answer `None`, and the receiver's documented answer (`None`, and `None` again) is now its own on every one of them. Pinned by four unit tests beside the type (`src/auth/transports/socketio/app_event.rs`: the item ready in the order sent, the empty open queue twice and the queue still open, the closed queue after its queued items and asked again by `recv` and `try_recv`, and a `recv` after an empty `try_recv` woken by the next event), green with the family at 0.3.31 and at 0.3.34, the integration file green on both; the same form and the three answers were run in a crate of their own on the whole family at 0.3.11 (the lowest `futures` crates.io has not yanked; every futures-util below 0.3.31 is yanked, so a lockfile resolved today holds futures-util, and through it futures-channel, at 0.3.31 or later, and the family below that is reached only by a lockfile written before the yanks or held by hand), 0.3.12, 0.3.13, 0.3.14, 0.3.30, 0.3.31, 0.3.32 and 0.3.34, the closed answer RED at 0.3.11 to 0.3.13 before the channel was dropped at its end. This tree's graph does not resolve with futures-util below 0.3.31 (`cargo update -p futures-util --precise 0.3.30` is refused), so the in-tree runs are 0.3.31 and 0.3.34, and no in-tree test sees the drop at the end: on 0.3.14 and later a poll after the end answers `None` with or without it. A build of the tip at its manifest's floors (`cargo +nightly update -Z direct-minimal-versions`) finds other floors too low, `tokio = "1"` among them (`watch::Sender::subscribe`, `send_replace` and `Clone`, the last from 1.37.0): listed in `docs/lanes/fix-843d23.md`, none changed here.

**Migration.** Through the public text, each line run by `a_bignumber_crosses_to_a_bigint_by_its_public_text_843d23` on both signs, zero and a 300-bit value:

- `n.as_bigint()` or `BigInt::from(n)`: `BigInt::parse_bytes(n.to_hex().as_bytes(), 16).unwrap()` (or `n.to_dec_string().parse::<BigInt>()`)
- `BigNumber::from(b)` or `BigNumber::from_bigint(b)`: `BigNumber::from_hex(&b.to_str_radix(16))?` (or `BigNumber::from_dec_str(&b.to_string())?`)
- `rx.next().await` on the listener's receiver: `rx.recv().await`; `rx.try_next()`: `rx.try_recv()`

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#843d23)

Neither reference exposes another package's number type through its big number (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/primitives/BigNumber.ts` is its own class; go-sdk@2ca481c's `primitives/ec` takes the standard library's `*big.Int`, `ec.go:80-116`) or has this queue (`@bsv/authsocket-client` dispatches events to callbacks, `packages/messaging/authsocket-client/src/AuthSocketClient.ts:105-120,171-180`). No reference line decides this row: it is this crate's own surface. No wire byte, verdict or error text differs; no divergence row opens or closes (the root `CLAUDE.md` list names neither door).

### Security: the deprecated `KVStoreInterpreter::verify_signature_legacy` answered `true` for every token and every key; it now answers `true` only for a token whose controller field is that key and whose last field is that key's signature over the other fields (GHSA-mj2m-jxgv-r446)

- What was wrong. `verify_signature_legacy(&PushDrop, &PublicKey)` read neither argument and answered `true`: a token no controller signed, a signed token checked against a key other than its controller's, and a PushDrop with no fields all passed. Its documentation said it delegated to the `KVStoreFields`-based `verify_signature`; it did not. Every published version answers this way: `0.2.0`, the crate's first release, through `0.8.8`, and `0.9.0-beta.1` through `0.9.0-beta.7`. The stable line takes the same fix in its next patch release.
- The reach. A caller that checks, with this function, a KVStore token it did not write (an overlay lookup's answer, a transaction output a peer hands it) and acts on `true`. No door of this crate calls it.
- The fix (`src/kvstore/legacy_signature.rs`, the function's one caller). `true` only for a PushDrop of five or six fields whose controller field is the given key's compressed form and whose last field is that key's signature over the other fields, under the derivation the token's protocol field names: the `[level, name]` namespace with the key as the key ID and the locking key derived from the controller, or a plain protocol name with the key ID `kvstore-token`, the two this crate's writers have used. A field read as `OP_0`'s single zero byte is taken as signed either as that byte or as an empty field, the two values `OP_0` pushes. The tags' bounds are not judged here. The signature of the function is unchanged and it stays deprecated.
- The tests. `tests/kvstore_legacy_signature_verdict.rs` (13): a token whose controller field names a stranger and whose signature is junk, in each derivation, tagged and untagged; a PushDrop of no fields; a signed token checked against another key; one-change copies of a signed token; a token of four or seven fields its controller signed; a namespace token whose protocol field, signed as written, is not canonical JSON; a token its controller signed whose controller field names another key; all `false`. Signed tokens with any tags, an empty or zero-byte value, an empty key or tags field, a plain-name token under any locking key, and 100 generated tokens over the four shapes `true` against their controllers and `false` with any one byte changed; `tests/vectors/token_envelope_544.json`'s kvstore tokens answered by their signatures. On a scratch copy of the base (`bb248ec7`) with the test file alone, 11 of 13 RED, the two cells that answer `true` whatever the door (any tags, any locking key) green; green on the fix; each of the five cells added after the fix's reviews RED on a copy of the fix with the one check it pins weakened. Twenty thousand tokens of every shape this crate's writers make (either derivation, tagged or not, empty and zero-byte fields among them) signed by their controllers answer `true` on the base, on the fix and on the published `0.9.0-beta.7`, their scripts and answers equal by one SHA-256; checked against another token's controller, 19,999 answer `true` on the base and none on the fix. `fuzz_script_parser` now passes every script `PushDrop::decode` reads through the function and asserts that `true` comes only for five or six fields whose controller field is the key checked; with the base's body planted it fails on a committed seed.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller that relied on `true` for a token whose controller field is another key, or whose last field is not that key's signature over the others, now gets `false`. A token its controller signed, checked against that controller, answers `true` as before. There is no workaround: the fix is in this release.

### Fixed: the contacts manager signs its update and removal over the output it authenticated, at the input the wallet bound, sends the reference's requests and returns the wallet's failures (#904)

- What was wrong. The contacts manager authenticated a listed contact token by its outpoint's txid, then signed its spend over another reading: the listing's BEEF by position (`beef.txs.first()`), the output at the listed index of that transaction, at input 0, the spend keyed 0 (`src/identity/contacts_actions.rs`). A contact not yet mined is listed with its ancestors ahead of it, the ordinary case (every BEEF writer puts a transaction's sources above it), so the update and the removal signed the parent's output, or answered `Unable to update contact` where the parent had no output at the token's index; and a wallet that bound the token's input anywhere but 0 was handed the spend at the wrong input. Beside it (the bucket #907's line 1): `add_contact` turned a failed tag HMAC, a failed listing and a failed or empty createAction into `Ok(())` with the contact in the cache alone, `remove_contact` emptied its cache before asking the wallet, answered `ContactNotFound` for a key it had not cached and `Ok(())` when the HMAC or the listing failed, a signAction answering a txid and no transaction was taken as a finished spend, nothing aborted the action after a failure, and `list_contacts_with_refresh(true)` refreshed a failed listing to no contacts. The requests were not the reference's either: `Add Contact: <name>`, `Remove Contact: <key>`, `Previous contact output`, `Contact output to remove`, `Contact: <key's ten characters>`, the label `contacts`, `signAndProcess`, and on the update and the removal `noSend: true`, so the wallet never sent either.
- The reference, `ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/identity/ContactsManager.ts`: `#readListedSource` (`:633-659`, `Transaction.fromBEEF(outputs.BEEF, txid)`, the output's script and satoshis) read for the authentication and again for the spend (`:784`, `:948`); `#findBoundInput` (`:666-697`, the one input at the outpoint); `pushdrop.unlock(..., source.satoshis, source.lockingScript).sign(signable, inputIndex)` and the spend keyed by `inputIndex`, no options (`:819-838`, `:987-1005`); the signed transaction held to the signable one (`#assertTransactionTemplate`, `:699-727`; the input unmoved, the signature kept, `#requireContactOutput`, `:729-736`, `:841-851`, `:1008-1015`); `#abortPartialAction` on any failure after createAction (`:738-745`); `saveContact` letting each wallet error through and writing its cache after the action (`:527-570`, `if (tx == null) throw new Error('Failed to create contact output')` at `:882`); `removeContact` asking the wallet whatever its cache holds and committing after (`:891-938`); `#loadContactsFromWallet` throwing on a failed listing (`:353-368`); the requests at `:787-811`, `:865-881`, `:964-979`.
- The fix. `src/identity/contacts_actions.rs`: `listed_source` is `#readListedSource` whole, its answer (`ListedSource`: the outpoint, the script, the satoshis) the one reading the authentication and the spend share; `sign_bound` finds the input bound to the outpoint, signs it there over the source and keys the spend by its index; `spend_listed` refuses no signable transaction in the reference's words, then aborts the action by its reference on any failure and returns the failure as it came; the three createActions are the reference's. `src/identity/contacts_spend.rs` (new) holds the reference's checks around the spend (`parse_atomic`, `input_outpoint`, `find_bound_input`, `assert_template`, `require_contact_output`, `check_signed`, the update's and removal's words). `add_contact`, `remove_contact` and the listing return every wallet failure; `remove_contact` removes the cache entry after the spend, or when nothing listed stores the contact.
- The runs on the base (`43ee8c85`, item 1 of the lane's brief, the two rows found by reading): a contact token's transaction C listed after its parent P (`C.to_beef(true)`, P's output 0 the token's own lock at 1000 satoshis): the unlocking script the update and the removal handed signAction is refused by the node's block word against C's output 0 (`OP_CHECKSIG requires failing signatures to be empty.`) and valid against P's (the output signed); the token at C's output 1 over a one-output P: `Unable to update contact`, no signAction; the contact's input at index 1 of the signable transaction: the spend keyed 0. The reference, on the same listings at the pin, signs C's output at the bound input (its removal's unlocking scripts are this crate's now byte for byte).
- The tests. `tests/contacts_listed_spend.rs` (7): the three shapes for the update and the removal, each unlocking script valid under the node's block word against C's output and keyed by the bound input; the removal's createAction, signable transaction and unlocking script the reference's byte for byte, the update's createAction save the new token's script (its ciphertext drawn here); the create request the reference's. `tests/contacts_wallet_failures.rs` (20): each failure cell beside the reference's recorded outcome, the cache untouched where the chain failed, the abort by reference, a removal of an uncached key asking the wallet; and a signable transaction spending the contact's outpoint twice or not at all, or without the contact output, refused before signAction and aborted (the strength read's survivors, read at the pin, not recorded; each RED in a scratch copy under its mutant); and the same two shapes at the removal, refused before signAction and aborted, the reference's recorded `remove_duplicate_input` and `remove_missing_input` (the fold's re-read found the removal path's refusal pinned by no test: with the refusal skipped on the removal path alone, the input taken as 0, every contacts and identity test passed; RED under that plant at the no-signAction assertion (`:378` then, `:475` since the third fold inserted a test above it), whose message prints the call list, `duplicate_input: [.., "create_signature", "sign_action", "abort_action"]`);   - **The replay.** `tests/contacts_replay.rs` replays `tests/vectors/contacts_replay.json` (written by `tests/support/contacts_replay_reference.mjs`, a mode of the #326 recorder: `signaction_reference_326.mjs --contacts-replay`, `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical). The corpus is 320 sequences of 4 to 16 steps (3,155 steps) generated from the seed `bsv-rs#904 fold7`, over three contacts and a wallet that keeps a basket (`tests/support/contacts_replay_wallet.rs`, the recorder's twin), plus 13 directed sequences, one for each survivor of the six re-reads. Every step is a plain read, a forced read, a read by identity key, a save, an update, a removal or a clear, with zero to two of the faults the pull request's tests inject; a rare wallet step fills the basket to the listing's bound. After every step the replay compares the outcome, the contacts answered, the wallet's calls in order and the pinned arguments with the reference's, naming the sequence and the step that differ. It runs in about 6 s.
  - **What it catches.** On a scratch copy, with the replay alone run, it catches 12 of the 12 code survivors of the six re-reads. Two of those were caught only after the generator was widened, never by a directed sequence: the update's two signable checks swapped (it now applies two modes of one call together) and a removal with nothing spent leaving the cache (it now retries a failed call). The thirteenth, `get_contacts_by_tag`'s match made case-sensitive, has no reference twin and is a row. It also catches 20 of 20 changes of meaning of the fold's own.
  - **The tool's counts.** `cargo mutants` over `contacts_cache.rs` with the replay in the test set: 29 made, 20 caught, 6 unviable, 3 missed (the sixth fold's 18 caught and 5 missed). The two that moved are the 1000-entry listing bound's, the bound's row 13, now held; the three left are equivalent.
  - **What it shows about the tip.** One difference: the order of a plain read over a warm cache, mended by the eighth fold (the next item).
- The eighth fold (the captain's ruling on the seventh fold's one difference: a fault to mend, not a divergence to state). What was wrong: the cache was a `HashMap` keyed by identity key (`ContactsCache::contacts`, older than #904), so a plain read over a warm cache of two or more contacts answered in its iteration order, which changes from run to run, where the reference answers its cache array (`ContactsManager.ts:326-328`, `:381-391` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`). The fix (`src/identity/contacts.rs`, `ContactsCache`): the contacts held in a `Vec` in the reference's order, the listing's on a load (`:376`), a new contact appended and an update written in place at its key's first entry (`saveContact`, `:532-534`), a removal filtering every entry of its key and keeping the others in order (`#commitCachedRemoval`, `:934`), a forced refresh the same as a load; a read by key answers the key's first entry (`:390`); an index from each key to its first position keeps a lookup at one hash at the manager's bound of 1,000, a load and a removal rebuilding it as the reference rewrites its array there. `search_contacts` and `get_contacts_by_tag`, which have no reference twin, now answer in the same order. No public type changed; no dependency added. What pins it: `tests/contacts_replay.rs` compares every answer in order (the seventh fold compared the cached ones as sets): RED alone on the code before the fix, 28 and then 25 of 333 sequences on two runs of the same binary, every difference a plain read's order; green 333 of 333 on three runs after it. Ten changes of order of the fold's own (an append made a prepend or an insert at the second place, an update moved to the end or the front, a removal by `swap_remove` or followed by a rotation, a load sorted by key or reversed, a read sorted by name or reversed), each caught by the replay alone, 10 of 10; `cargo mutants` over `contacts_cache.rs` 29 made, 20 caught, 6 unviable, 3 missed (the seventh fold's figures, the three the same equivalent bound mutants, now at `:87`), and over `ContactsCache` in `contacts.rs` 10 made, 8 caught, 2 unviable. The corpus is unchanged (the reference's answers were always ordered).
- The censuses. The seed sweep (`tests/support/beef_seeds_817.rs`) reads every BEEF any JSON file under `tests/vectors` holds, and the new vector holds nine distinct ones, every one V1 and read by `Beef::from_binary`: the three listings' BEEFs (`shapes.token_at_0`, `token_at_1`, `input_at_1`: the token's transaction after its parent, or the token alone, no BUMP) and six Atomic signable transactions over V1 (`cases.*.signable`, three entries each, no BUMP); none is valid under `verify_valid` (no entry proven), which the sweeps do not ask, as they judge the writers and `merge_beef` on any BEEF the reader reads. Three pinned totals moved, each read off its failing assertion's `left` on `origin/beta` `4dc92be3` with the vector, and held on `ad43c269` (that rebase brought no vector): the pre-pass census (`src/transaction/beef/prepass_621_tests.rs`) from 363 BEEFs to 372 under 17 states, 6,171 to 6,324 (2,467 to 2,566 `Ok`, 3,704 to 3,758 refused, 1,789 by the reader and 252 `RootNotCarried` unmoved), `SWEPT` in `tests/beef_v1_txid_only_writer_817.rs` from `(363, 126)` to `(372, 135)`, and `tests/beef_writer_refusals_817.rs`' `6 * 363` to `6 * 372` (2,232). The lane's three runs had not run the whole suite, so the move was seen by CI's Test Suite on PR #929.

### Added: the node oracle's judge wired: stage R `sibling-run.yml`, the trampoline `sibling-judge.yml`, the sync's dispatch of stage R; nothing made required (#97)

The judge the previous entry built on beta now runs. `.github/workflows/sibling-run.yml` (stage R, job `raw`) runs on every pull request into `beta` and on a dispatch, with no secret, no environment and `contents: read` alone: it checks the head out by its sha (never the merge ref) and beta to `judge/`, reads the head's `tests/sibling/PIN`, checks the sibling out at it, runs beta's `sibling_harness.py raw` under `python3 -I -B` on the head's tree and uploads the allowlist's members as `sibling-raw` (`overwrite: true`, so a re-run replaces its earlier attempt's artifact; 30 days; no file an error), the upload's `always()` its one condition. `.github/workflows/sibling-judge.yml` (stage J, the trampoline, the one of the two `main` takes by `git cherry-pick -x`) starts on a `workflow_run` of `sibling-run` or a dispatch with a run id, runs from `main` alone, checks beta out to `judge/` and runs beta's `sibling_judge.py`: `judge` holds no key and writes four outputs; `report`, in the environment `sibling-judge`, mints the App's token (`actions/create-github-app-token` v3.3.0, `permission-checks: write` alone) and posts the check `sibling-judge` on the run's head, never opening the artifact; one concurrency group per judged head (a re-judge dispatch keyed by its run id), never cancelled. `sync-main-into-beta.yml` dispatches `sibling-run.yml` on its branch in a step of its own after `ci.yml`'s, since a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push starts no run. Why: until now nothing ran the judge, so a pull request that edited `ci.yml`'s `sibling` job edited its own judge beside it. Nothing is required: `sibling-judge` joins beta's protection by the owner's PATCH after the witnesses and the soak (`RELEASING.md` step 25, which also carries the J-diff rule, the lift, `strict`, the silence list, the two re-drives, the sequencer's line and the key's rotation; the direction rule's sentence of 2026-11-12).

The opening items from lane 1's three reads, in `.github/scripts/`: each comparison of the stamp and the run's record with what the judge read is pinned alone, and the dispatch's stamp naming no pull request (`StampAndRecord`, each RED with its comparison removed); every split of corpus, words, log and manifest text is on a line feed alone (`sibling_harness.lines_of`: `str.splitlines` also splits on U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, which a JSON string holds raw; `LineFeeds`; no corpus at the pin holds one, so no column moves); the branch name is `shlex.quote`d in the re-push act and the sweep's act (`Quoting`); `standing()` counts a check only when its app id is the configured one (`Standing`, RED on a check with no app); the judge reads only an artifact created at or after the judged attempt started (`Rerun`: a re-run judged, both artifacts listed or the old one replaced); the script and the manual say one thing, stage R runs beta's harness (`StageRScript`).

The tests: `tests/arch_ci_sibling_judge_97.rs` pins both workflows whole, byte for byte, and by named rules (`the_two_workflows_of_the_judge_are_pinned_whole_97`, `stage_r_holds_its_named_rules_97`, `stage_j_holds_its_named_rules_97`, `the_key_the_environment_and_workflow_run_belong_to_the_trampoline_alone_97`, 49 plants); `tests/arch_ci_lines.rs` holds their shape (`the_judges_two_workflows_have_a_workflows_shape_97`) and the sync's dispatch step pinned whole after ci.yml's (`SYNC_STAGE_R`, its `--ref`, `if:` and place held: `a_sync_stage_r_dispatch_retargeted_unconditioned_or_moved_is_refused_97`; and every variable those steps read defined where the test says, `SYNC_BRANCH` once in the workflow's `env:`, `GH_TOKEN` in a step's own `env:`, no other `GH_*` setting: `every_variable_the_stage_r_dispatch_reads_has_its_one_definition_97`, a scan of the spellings it names; and since the third fold the whole workflow pinned by its digest, `SYNC_FILE_DIGEST`, so a definition in any spelling moves the file and fails: `the_sync_workflow_is_pinned_whole_by_its_digest_97`, the second re-read's flow mapping with no space, multiline `$GITHUB_ENV` write and YAML-escaped key each refused by the digest's message where the scan passed them. The bound: what holds the sync's dispatch is the pinned step's text and the digest of the whole workflow; what neither sees is a change that edits the workflow and its digest in the same pull request (a reviewer's matter, visible in the diff), and a value GitHub keeps outside the file (an organization or repository variable, which reaches a job only through a `${{ vars.NAME }}` the file would carry, and of which the repository and its organization held none on 2026-11-13); `tests/support/nightly_cap_rules.rs`' `STATED` names the sync's dispatch of `sibling-run.yml` (`arch_nightly_cap_rules_709`); `.github/scripts/test_sibling_judge.py` 90 tests (74 before; an artifact created at the instant its attempt started judged, the re-push act printed with its command on a line of its own; the attempt's start judged to the second inside its minute, an earlier attempt's artifact made earlier in the same minute left out, and the line named behind when the trampoline differs read from its two commit times at a second before, the same second and a second after; since the third fold 92: the two times parsed and compared as times, never as text (`sibling_judge.instant`; `git log --format=%ct` read as a decimal integer or not at all), a time that does not parse `NOT JUDGED` naming it, and the start at `10:07:37Z`, on no coarser mark, an artifact made at `10:07:36Z` the earlier attempt's, at the same second and one after this attempt's, an offset and a fraction read as the instants they name).
