### Fixed: on beta the semver check holds a pull request to minor unless it carries api-break; a transient read is tried again before the reconciler goes red; a yanked version is not the newest stable, for the mark or for the reconciler (#886)

Three findings of the reads of 2026-11-11 beside the front pages (#883), none a security matter; no SDK behaviour, wire byte, verdict or error text moves. No cross-SDK parity note: no reference line is involved, the change being to this repository's own machines (a workflow step, the front-page script and their tests), and no row of the divergence list moves (said here and under no `### Notes` heading, which `front_pages.py notes` would count as a parity note on the Release page).

**The `semver` check on `beta` (`ci.yml`).** The required check ran `cargo-semver-checks check-release --baseline-rev <the last tag> --all-features` with the release type inferred. Every version on `beta` is a prerelease, and cargo-semver-checks 0.51.0 reads any prerelease step as a major one: 0 checks, 260 skipped, exit 0, whatever the pull request removed. A required check that judges nothing is a claim CI makes and does not keep. For a pull request whose base is `beta` the step now runs `check-release --baseline-rev "$baseline" --all-features --release-type minor` (an addition passes, a break the tool has a lint for fails: the 202 major lints of 0.51.0 name a removed or renamed item, a changed parameter count or receiver, a type newly `#[non_exhaustive]` and the like; none reads a changed return type beyond a value gained or lost, or a changed parameter type, so such a change is green without the label and stays the reads' to judge; the lint list read in the tool's source, not run), `baseline` the commit the pull request is tested on (`git rev-parse HEAD^1` of the merge ref; against the last tag one labelled break would fail every later pull request until the next tag). The pull request's labels are read live through the API before the check (the Test Suite's line, under `set -euo pipefail`; a failed read fails the job, the event's copy is never read, no `labeled` trigger): with `api-break` the same command runs, a lint failure (the tool's exit 100) is printed with one `::notice::` line naming the label and the step ends green; any other failure stays red. The job gains `permissions: contents: read, pull-requests: read`, what `release.yml` grants its call of `ci.yml` (`RELEASING.md` step 22). A base other than `beta` keeps its lines: the last tag, the release type inferred. The step's own lines, copied from `ci.yml` and run on a scratch clone with cargo-semver-checks 0.51.0 (the labels set by hand through a stand-in `gh`):

| Run | The tree against its base | Labels | The tool's lines | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) | `Script::is_data` made `pub(crate)` | none | `Checked [   0.113s] 202 checks: 201 pass, 1 fail, 0 warn, 58 skip`; `failure inherent_method_missing: pub method removed or renamed`; `Summary semver requires new major version: 1 major and 0 minor checks failed` | 100 |
| (b) | the same | `full-suite,api-break` | the same three lines, then `::notice::The public API breaks above are allowed by the api-break label on this pull request (#886).` | 0 |
| (c) | one public function added | none | `Checked [   0.125s] 202 checks: 202 pass, 58 skip`; `Summary no semver update required` | 0 |
| (d) | (a)'s tree, the base's command (the branch a base other than `beta` takes) | none | `Checking bsv-rs v0.9.0-beta.7 -> v0.9.0-beta.7 (no change; assume major)`; `Checked [   0.000s] 0 checks: 0 pass, 260 skip`; `Summary no semver update required` | 0 |

Two more beside them: the labels `api-breaks,not-api-break` on (a)'s tree exit 100 (the label is matched whole), and a label read that fails exits 1 before the tool runs. `tests/arch_ci_semver_holds_beta_886.rs` pins the step from `ci.yml` alone, whole: the step that runs the tool (its name, condition, `env:` and `run:` text, the beta branch among them) is the constant `SEMVER_STEP` byte for byte, as `SIBLING_JOB` is pinned, and the job's one checkout named no `ref:` and no `repository:` (the fold after the three reads of the pull request: the named rules below read lines and their order, so a line inserted between them passed every one; `a_line_inserted_in_the_semver_step_is_refused_by_the_pin_886` plants the reads' seven, `labels=api-break` after the read, a second `baseline=`, `status="0"` after the check, `BASE_REF=main` before the branch, the label appended after the echo, any failure made a lint failure under a forced label, a `ref:` on the checkout, and six more, each refused by the pin naming `ci.yml`'s line and the line found, or by the checkout's; on a scratch copy of the tree with each of the seven planted in `ci.yml` the test of `1592e699` passed six and failed the seventh only on a plant's own count, and the tip's failed all seven by those messages). The job around the step is pinned as text too (the scoped re-read of that fold: the checkout rule read `ref:` by its line's prefix, so a quoted key `"ref":`, a space before the colon `ref :` and a flow mapping `with: { .., ref: .. }` passed it): its id and its keys beside `steps:` with their values are `JOB_HEAD`, each step's opening line in order (and any key written after the steps) is `STEP_HEADS`, and the checkout from its `- uses:` line to the line before the next step is `CHECKOUT_STEP`, each line for line with comments and blank lines aside, a failure naming `ci.yml`'s line, the line found and the line pinned; `the_checkout_the_steps_and_the_job_keys_are_pinned_whole_886` plants the re-read's three, the fold's two stated residuals (a step inserted ahead of the check that puts a `gh` of its own on `PATH`, a job-level `env:`) and eight more (a `path:` on the checkout, a step ahead of the checkout, a step opened by a lone `-`, a job-level `defaults:` and `container:`, a quoted job key, a third permission, `continue-on-error` after the steps), each refused by its pin's message; with the five planted one at a time in `ci.yml` the test of `27de56b7` passed its guard on each (the flow mapping failing only its plant test, on a plant's own count) and the tip's guard failed on each by its pin's message. Not seen, stated: another workflow file, a reusable workflow's inputs, the workflow's own keys, and the bodies of the six steps pinned by their opening line alone (the docs-only report among them). The named rules stay, each saying why a change matters: `the_semver_step_holds_beta_to_minor_unless_labelled_886` (the live read's line whole, the `api-break` match, `--release-type minor`, the `HEAD^1` baseline, the job's two permissions, the read before the check, the other base's lines) and `a_planted_semver_step_is_refused_886` (twenty plants on the file's own text, each refused by its message: `minor` dropped, the read behind `|| true`, the read from the event payload, the label skipping the tool, the baseline back on `git describe`, `pull-requests: read` removed or widened, the label spelled otherwise or matched as a substring, and the rest); both RED on a scratch copy of `3e1ade84` with the file overlaid. The README's sentence on the check (marker F7) says what the step does on each line, and its producer in `tests/front_page.rs` requires the lines that make the `beta` clause true (RED over the base's `ci.yml`: `ci.yml no longer holds` the beta branch). The live witness of the label read is CI's, on the pull request: #898's own run (43260752079, job 131331050524, `Contents: read`, `PullRequests: read`) printed `labels: ci,after-cut`, took `3e1ade84`, `HEAD^1` of the merge `fbcfa31a`, as its baseline and ended `Checking bsv-rs v0.9.0-beta.7 -> v0.9.0-beta.7 (assume minor change)`, `202 checks: 202 pass, 58 skip`; the red path and the label's path have the scratch runs above alone. The tool's exits, read in its source (`src/main.rs` of 0.51.0): 100 for a completed check with a failed lint and nothing else, 101 for every error the check returns (a build, a baseline it cannot read) and for a witness error, so the label waives a judged break alone.

**A transient read (`front_pages.py check`).** `guarded` recorded `FAIL <rule>: could not read` the moment a source did not answer, so one 5xx reddened a release run. A rule whose source raises `Unavailable` is now run once more after `RETRY_PAUSE` (20 seconds), from the state before the failed attempt (the result's lines and counts, the shared `crate`, `releases` and `advisories`; of these `crate` and `releases` are written today before a read that can still fail, `versions` updating `crate` before it reads the Latest release and the tags and `pages` extending `releases` before it reads the tags; the restore of `releases` is the one a test turns RED, and the restores of `crate`, of `advisories` and of the result's lines have no test, the lines and `advisories` being written after their rule's last read), and is red only when the second attempt fails too. What is read again is `Unavailable`, whatever raised it: a 5xx, a timeout, a failed `gh` call (its 404 of `repo`, `tags` or `releases` and a refused token among them) and crates.io's 404 for the crate itself, none of them an answer about a page. A 404 a source reads as an answer (docs.rs's for a queued release, no rendered README, no Latest release, no `SECURITY.md`) raises nothing and is not read again, nor is `Stop`, a refusal; the script's comment said "a 404 is an answer" of every 404 and says this now, the code unchanged. `notes` and `flags` are outside `guarded` and unchanged, so `flags`' one read of crates.io in the page job still fails that job on a miss (a re-run heals it). Pinned by `test_a_source_that_fails_once_is_read_again_886`, `test_a_source_that_fails_twice_is_red_once_886` and `test_a_retried_rule_keeps_nothing_of_its_failed_attempt_886` (each RED on the base's script; the third RED too with the restore of the shared lists removed), and the two kinds of 404 by `test_a_404_read_as_an_answer_is_not_read_again_886`, `test_crates_io_404_for_the_crate_is_unavailable_and_read_again_886` and `test_the_live_source_says_which_404_is_an_answer_886` (pins of what the code did already, green before and after).

**A yanked version (`front_pages.py flags` and `check`).** `flags` took every version crates.io lists as served, yanked ones too, while the reconciler's `versions` rule reads `max_stable_version`, which leaves them out: after a yank of the highest stable version, a later stable tag below it would be marked `--latest=false` and the reconciler would then fail `versions`. And the `versions` rule itself took the highest stable `v*` tag as the newest whether or not crates.io lists that version as yanked, so after such a yank it stayed red, with the mark on either page, until a higher stable version was tagged. One function now works the newest stable version out, `newest_stable(versions, left_out)` (the highest stable version of those given, the yanked ones passed over, none when none is left), and both ask it: `flags` over the versions crates.io lists and the tag's own (a version the index does not show yet is counted; one crates.io lists as yanked never takes the mark, the tag's own included, where it answered `--latest` when it was the highest), and `versions` over the `v*` tags. They are the script's only two places that work that version out (`test_flags_and_the_versions_rule_ask_the_one_function_886` reads the source for it); the rules after `versions` read crates.io's own `max_stable_version`. After a yank of the highest stable version the reconciler is green once Latest stands on the page of crates.io's highest stable version, and red, not pending, while it is left on the yanked version's page: moving the mark is a hand's (`gh release edit vX.Y.Z --latest`), as no release run follows a yank. The yanked version keeps its tag and its page (`pages` still asks for one). Pinned by `test_a_yanked_version_is_not_the_highest_stable_886` (RED on `3e1ade84`'s script: `'--latest=false' != '--latest'`), and by the fold's `test_versions_leave_a_yanked_versions_tag_out_of_the_newest_stable_886` (RED on `1592e699`'s script: `['FAIL versions: crates.io max_stable_version 0.8.7, GitHub Latest v0.8.7, newest stable tag v0.8.8'] != []`), `test_a_tag_whose_own_version_is_yanked_never_takes_the_mark_886` (RED there: `'--latest' != '--latest=false'`) and `test_the_highest_stable_version_with_the_yanked_left_out_886`. Not probed live: that crates.io's `max_stable_version` leaves a yanked version out is read in its source (`crates_io_database` `models/krate.rs`, `models/version.rs`), no yank was made to watch it.

The issue's fourth line asked for a witness of the run-log reads, with no code: `front_pages.py notes v0.8.7 --run 43128351965` and `notes v0.9.0-beta.7 --run 41883696761`, read-only against the two release runs, each print a whole "Measured at this tag" block with no `not recorded` line (`docs/lanes/fix-886.md`).

### Added: the node oracle's judge, built and tested on beta with nothing fired: the pin in a file, `raw`, `sibling_judge.py` and its gate (#97)

The verdict of a pull request on the node's oracle is to come from files the pull request cannot edit (the two-stage judge decided 2026-11-10; the three design reads of 2026-11-12; the owner's six decisions of 2026-11-12 about 18:07Z). Until now `ci.yml`'s `sibling` judged a pull request with the pull request's own script, column and pin, so a pull request that edited the job edited its judge beside it. This is the half of the answer that fires nothing: no workflow file and no trigger is added, no check is created, nothing is made required (`REQUIRED_ON_BETA` and RELEASING's count of contexts do not move). The wiring lane adds the two workflows from its own brief.

### Fixed: a merkle walk pairs an odd-length hash text as the reference's concatenation does (#817)

`MerklePath`'s walk (`hash_pair`, `src/transaction/merkle_path_walk.rs`, behind `new`, `new_unchecked` and `compute_root`) decoded each of the two hash texts alone, reversed each and appended them, and a side of odd length, which the `hex` crate refuses, contributed no byte. The reference's `hashPair` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `MerklePath.ts:30-32`) concatenates the two texts as text, adds one leading `0` when the total length is odd (`toArray`, `primitives/utils.ts:125-128`), decodes once, reverses the whole and hashes; its callers pass the sides the other way round (`nextCachedHash`, `:61-62`; `findOrComputeLeaf`, `:455-459`, `hashPair(leaf1.hash, leaf0.hash)`), so this crate's `hash_pair(left, right)` is its `hashPair(right, left)`. For two even-length texts the bytes hashed were already equal; with one odd side the reference pads the concatenation where this crate dropped the side, and with two odd sides it decodes across their boundary where this crate dropped both, so `compute_root` answered another root. Now `hash_pair` builds `right + left`, pads it with one `0` when its length is odd, decodes it once (a failure after the non-hex check, which stays ahead, is `Invalid hex string`), reverses it whole and keeps its tail (`merkle_parent` for 64 bytes, else `sha256d`). The `""` for an absent hash and the non-hex refusal are unchanged.

Reach: no reader builds such a hash (they read 32 bytes); `MerklePath::new`, `new_unchecked`, `from_coinbase_txid` and the public fields do. No wire byte moves.

The censuses: the vector's `signing` group holds three BEEF texts, two distinct and both V2, and the seed sweep (`tests/support/beef_seeds_817.rs`) reads every BEEF any JSON file under `tests/vectors` holds, so three pinned totals move, re-derived by running each: on `origin/beta` `43ee8c85` (after 0.8.8's `beef_tx_order.json`) the pre-pass census (`src/transaction/beef/prepass_621_tests.rs`) from 361 BEEFs to 363 under 17 states, 6,137 to 6,171 (2,443 to 2,467 `Ok`, 3,694 to 3,704 refused, 1,789 by the reader and 252 `RootNotCarried` unmoved), `SWEPT` in `tests/beef_v1_txid_only_writer_817.rs` from `(361, 126)` to `(363, 126)`, and `tests/beef_writer_refusals_817.rs`'s `6 * 361` to `6 * 363`.

Pinned by `tests/merkle_path_hash_pair_817.rs` against `tests/vectors/transaction_fold_817.json`, group `hash_pair` (`tests/support/transaction_fold_817.mjs`, Node v22.18.0, the bundle at the pin, two runs byte-identical): thirteen held paths, each `computeRoot()` and both constructors, every cell's root equal on `compute_root`, `new` and `new_unchecked`: a sibling of 63, 1 and 65 digits and a txid of 63 (`an_odd_length_sibling_is_paired_as_the_reference_concatenates_it_817`), both sides of 63 and a 63-digit txid beside a duplicate (`two_odd_length_hashes_are_read_across_their_boundary_817`), a computed node whose `leaf0` or `leaf1` has 63 digits (`an_odd_length_child_of_a_computed_node_is_paired_as_the_reference_817`), all three RED on `3e1ade84`; 62, 64 and 66 digits, the empty text and a computed node of 64-digit children (`an_even_length_hash_pairs_as_before_817`), green on both; and a count of the cells.

### Fixed: `rows_from_sources.py` writes back the rows it read: a pipe inside a code span is text, and the writer is held to the identity on the tree (the rows lane)

The fix-817 lane ran `python3 .github/scripts/rows_from_sources.py` without `--check` on 2026-11-12 and saw it rewrite two rows of `tests/CLAUDE.md` that `--check` passed: `shamir_backup_854.rs`'s two `||` inside backticks became `` ` |  | ` `` and `front_page.rs`'s `|` inside backticks became `` ` | ` ``. The splitter, `affected_tests.row_cells`, cut a row at every `|` not after a backslash (`re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", ..)`), so a pipe inside a code span was a cell boundary, and the writer joined the cells back with `" | "`. The Rust guard's twin (`cells` in `tests/arch_tests_claude_rows_name_modules_706.rs`) and the File-cell readers (`nightly_mutants.table_rows`, the guard's `table_rows`, both `line.split("|")[1]`) read the same way.

Now one splitter, `nightly_mutants.cell_spans` (`affected_tests.row_cells` and `cell_spans` are its names there), and its Rust twin read a boundary as a `|` outside a code span and not escaped: a code span opens at a run of n backticks and closes at the next run of exactly n (CommonMark 6.1), a run with no closer is text, and a backslash escapes the next character outside a code span and nothing inside one (so `\\|` is a backslash and a boundary, which the old lookbehind read as an escaped pipe). The writer changes only the Modules cell of a row whose cell moves, splicing that cell's text between its own edge white space (`with_cell`); every other byte of the row and every other row is as read, and the file is read and written as UTF-8 bytes, so a `\r\n` line end, irregular spacing and non-ASCII text come back unchanged (the old writer rebuilt every row from stripped cells and went through `read_text`'s newline translation). On a tree `--check` passes, the writer is now the identity.

Pinned by `.github/scripts/test_rows_from_sources.py` (10 tests), run by the Test Suite's plan step beside `rows_from_sources.py --check` (the line pinned by `tests/arch_ci_runs_every_test.rs`): the reader's cases (a pipe in a code span of one and two backticks, an escaped pipe, an escaped backslash before a pipe, an unclosed run, a backslash inside a span, the two rows the finder saw read as five cells each); a property over 2,000 generated rows (seeded; code spans of one to three backticks holding pipes, backslashes and backtick runs of other lengths, escaped `|`, `\\`, `` ` ``, `*`, `_`, `&#10;`, `&#124;`, `<br>`, non-ASCII text; no edge white space, which the reader strips) that `read(write(row)) == row` and `write(read(text)) == text`, and 500 rows with irregular spacing and a `\r` whose rewritten cell keeps every other byte; the writer run without `--check` on a copy of the tree, an empty diff required; a CRLF fixture with spacing and non-ASCII text in which only the cell that moves is written. RED on `5a87392e`: the identity test (`the writer rewrote 2 lines of a tree --check passes`, lines 224 and 264), the reader's cases (the finder's row read as nine cells, the description cut at each pipe of its code spans; `a\\| b` read as one cell), the CRLF fixture (`\r\n` written `\n`), and the base's reader and joiner failing the property on 914 of 2,000 rows, every one a pipe inside a code span. `a_pipe_inside_a_code_span_or_escaped_is_text_and_not_a_cell_boundary` pins the Rust guard's reading. Stated, not changed: GitHub's table renderer (GFM) splits a row at a `|` inside a code span unless it is escaped, so the two finder rows render on GitHub with more cells than these readers read; writing those pipes `\|` is a docs choice left open (`docs/lanes/fix-rows-script.md`). No crate code moves.

### Security: a transaction's BEEF ends with that transaction: the doors that write one from a transaction's own ancestry no longer sort it, so the read that names no txid takes the transaction back

- What was wrong. `Transaction::to_beef` and `to_beef_v1` collected the transaction's ancestry — each entry's sources above it, the transaction last, BRC-62's own rule for the form ("we must ensure that we end with the tx being evaluated, and its inputs are above, and their inputs are above that") — then handed the assembled `Beef` to `Beef::to_binary`, whose sort writes the dependency order a caller-assembled BEEF takes. A graph whose collected order is not that order — one holding a proven branch beside a branch resting on a missing source — got its subject written before the proven ancestor, and `Transaction::from_beef(&bytes, None)` (its target `txid ?? atomic_txid ?? the last entry`) answered the last entry: a proven root, not the transaction the caller serialized. Every published version reads this way — the doors are as old as the crate's first release (`0.2.0` through `0.8.7`, released without this fix, and the `0.9.0-beta` line; the fix ships in `0.8.8`).
- The reach. A caller that serializes a partial graph holding a proven branch beside a missing source and reads the bytes back without naming the txid: the door answers an ancestor of the transaction it was handed, real and valid, so it is a wrong-identity loss, not a validity loss (1,259 of 2,000 random such graphs misidentify, measured on every published version from `0.2.0` to `0.9.0-beta.7` — the served-without-a-tag `0.2.0` and `0.3.0` and the yanked `0.3.21` included, every one crates.io serves). A read that names the txid always took the transaction; a graph with no proven entry was never misread (the sort leaves its subject last); the atomic word's own read was never misled (it names its subject in the header, and its reader takes it back on every published version), and its BEEF portion, the closure sorted and the subject then moved last, ends with the subject as `0.8.7` and `0.9.0-beta.7` write it (on this line a change after `0.9.0-beta.7` dropped the move and left the subject among the entries resting on a missing input; this fix restores it), while a no-txid `from_beef` of its bytes, which took the header into account only from `0.3.20` on, misread before that the same way. Honest graphs whose collected order is the dependency order — the differential's 20,000 generated single-root trees among them — keep the same bytes: the bytes and the ids every read returns, one SHA-256 digest, are equal on `0.8.7` and on this fix, so whatever a published version writes still reads. A graph whose collected order is not that order — an honest merge of two independent branches among them — takes the Migration's change: 11,263 of 20,000 generated graphs of two or three roots, every root proven, write different bytes at the plain doors, and every read of them is unchanged (the subject, named or not); the atomic door's bytes are equal to `0.8.7`'s on all 60,000 generated graphs (the single-root trees, those, and as many with each root proven at odds of one half).
- The fix, in one place. The collected ancestry is written in the order the walk collects it: `Beef::hold_order` holds a BEEF a transaction door assembles as it stands, and `to_binary` writes it without the sort; the three transaction doors (`to_beef`, `to_beef_v1`, `to_atomic_beef`) reach it through one private helper — the atomic door onto the atomic writer's transaction-door form (`to_binary_atomic_subject_last`, `src/transaction/beef_atomic.rs`: the BRC-95 closure sorted as `Beef::to_binary_atomic` sorts it, then the subject moved last, the closure being the subject's ancestry alone, so no other entry moves and the bytes are those `0.8.7` writes; `Beef::to_binary_atomic` on a BEEF a caller assembles by hand keeps the closure's documented sort) — so every sibling door that shared the behavior is brought under the one piece of code. The doors that were already safe are pinned by their own cells: a BEEF a caller assembles by hand keeps the documented dependency sort (`Beef::new`/`with_version` then `to_binary`), `merge_beef` then `to_binary` keeps it, and the atomic word's read keeps the subject (the header names it, and the transaction door's atomic bytes end with it too).
- The tests. `tests/beef_tx_order.rs` (16): the finding's shape through both transaction doors and the atomic door, the bytes and the reads (the no-txid read, the named read, the parsed last entry, the atomic bytes pinned on the finding's shape, the plain doors' version words asserted, the held order asserted written through `to_writer`); a caller-assembled BEEF, a merged BEEF and a pre-fix version's bytes each keeping their documented order; the invariant as a property over generated graphs, 200 of the finding's population (156 the sort writes differently, 128 of them moving the subject off the last entry; the floors hold the corpus to the measured counts, so the property is never vacuous) and 200 of missing roots only (134 differ, none misread), the counts re-derived and pinned by a census cell in the same file (the 817 sweeps' form, so a silent generator degradation stays red with the floors gone); and 200 of the differential's honest trees, pinned as the boundary cell; the committed fuzz seed replayed through the no-txid read (the shape checked, so an emptied or vacuous seed is red); a witness of two proven roots under one BUMP (a level-0 multi-leaf path, a shape no cell had built: the BUMP-combine path and the closure's renumbered-index sharing), read back through every door; and the atomic door's order on 605 graphs (the four witnesses, two proven branches fully linked, the 400 property graphs, the 200 honest trees): the Beef-level door's sorted closure of the same graph with the subject moved last, never the collected order where the two differ (280 of them, counted, so the cell cannot go vacuous) and never the sort alone. `tests/vectors/beef_tx_order.json` (4 witnesses), recorded by `tests/support/beef_tx_order.mjs` by a run at the pin (`ts-stack@edf6e03`, Node v22.18.0): each witness's V1 bytes beside the dependency sort's bytes and the validity verdict. On a scratch copy of the base (`6bc872d7`, `origin/beta`) with the test file, the vector and the seed alone, nine of the sixteen cells were red — the no-txid read answered an ancestor, the door's bytes differed from the recorded bytes, both property floors and the census of their counts, the held order through `to_writer`, the replayed seed, the atomic byte pin and the atomic order cell (the closure's sort alone: the subject mid-list) — and the seven boundary cells green; all sixteen green on the fix; the honest-tree cell is green on the base by design (the sort leaves a single root's tree alone), which is what the differential measures. The atomic order cell is red on a tree whose atomic door writes the collected closure instead. The fuzz target `fuzz_beef_parser` now checks the round trip at both doors (a transaction read from a BEEF, re-serialized through the plain door and the atomic door, reads back as itself, and the atomic closure's last entry is it) and carries a seed for the shape (`fuzz/corpus/fuzz_beef_parser/tx-door-order`, written by `fuzz/corpus-gen`, which crashes a build of the base carrying the check and passes on the fix); two 60-second runs clean (41,499 and 28,154 executions). The vector's five distinct BEEFs (the door's, the recorded door's and the sorted, four witnesses, deduplicated by bytes, every one V1) move the sweeps that count the vectors' BEEFs: the pre-pass census of #621's differential (`src/transaction/beef/prepass_621_tests.rs`) to 361 read under its seventeen states (6,137: 2,443 `Ok`, 3,694 refused, 1,789 by the reader, 252 the judge's `RootNotCarried`), `tests/beef_v1_txid_only_writer_817.rs`'s sweep to (361, 126) and `tests/beef_writer_refusals_817.rs`'s to 6 × 361, every figure re-derived by the tests' own runs (363, (363, 126) and 6 × 363 since #817's transaction fold, its entry above); and the recursive reference of the 0.3.35 iterative equivalence (`beef.rs`'s `iterative_equivalence_tests`) carries the order hold alike at both doors, so the iterative doors and it still write the same bytes.
- Not in this patch. The Beef-level doors keep their documented dependency sort: a BEEF a caller assembles by hand, and one built by `merge_beef`, still write it, and a subject that sits before a proven ancestor in that order is still the last entry's to claim at a no-txid read — the documented behavior of those doors, unchanged since they landed, pinned here by its own cells.
- Migration. No signature moved. The bytes a transaction door writes change for graphs whose collected order is not the dependency order — the entries are the same, each entry's sources above it, the subject last — so a consumer that takes the last entry now takes the subject; a consumer that names the txid sees no change; a consumer of the atomic word sees no read change (the header names the subject), and the atomic door's bytes are those `0.8.7` writes. A BEEF any earlier version wrote still reads, at every door.


### Fixed: Shamir recovery takes one modular inverse where it took one per pair of shares; 255 of 255 in 12 ms where it took about a second (#880)

Since #854 a backup share's x coordinate is a 256-bit field element, and `Polynomial::value_at` interpolated as the reference's `valueAt` does, with one modular inverse per ordered pair of shares (64,770 at 255 shares), each a full-width extended Euclid: about a second for a 255-share recovery, a long time inside a Cloudflare Worker's CPU budget, and the common 3 of 5 about eighteen times its cost before #854. The answers were right; the cost was not.

`value_at` now takes one modular inverse per call. For each share it multiplies out the numerator `N_i = Π(j≠i) (x - x_j)` (by the products before and after i) and the denominator `D_i = Π(j≠i) (x_i - x_j)`, inverts the non-zero `D_i` together (Montgomery's batch inversion: the running products, one `mod_inverse`, the walk back) and sums `y_i * N_i * D_i^-1`, all modulo p. The field value is the pairwise loop's on every input the public door takes: a point whose x repeats another used point's (a `D_i` of 0, never multiplied into the batch) contributes 0, as the per-pair zero inverse did; no points answers 0 and one its `y` reduced; a threshold above the point count uses the points there are; any `x` and hand-built coordinates at or past p or negative are reduced as before. `interpolate`, `refuse_degenerate_xs` and both readers are untouched, so no key, refusal, refusal order or word moves. The function is not constant time and never was (`num-bigint` throughout); what it keeps is that every inverse's input, and its one data branch (`D_i == 0`), are functions of the x coordinates alone, a `y` entering only as a factor. Its rustdoc no longer says it panics (it did not).

| Release build, this host (Apple M5 Max), median of five | `3e1ade84` (one inverse per pair) | this change |
|---|---|---|
| Read and recover, 255 of 255 | 1.18 s | 12.3 ms |
| Read and recover, 10 of 20 | 1.74 ms | 0.092 ms |
| Read and recover, 3 of 5 | 0.130 ms | 0.043 ms |
| Read and recover, 2 of 3 | 0.060 ms | 0.036 ms |
| Split, 3 of 5 (not changed) | 0.025 ms | 0.025 ms |
| Legacy reader, 3 of 5 | 0.0089 ms | 0.0090 ms |
| Legacy reader, 255 of 255 | 47.8 ms | 6.0 ms |

(`tests/shamir_interpolation_880.rs` `figures_880`, release; "read and recover" is `from_backup_format` of exactly the threshold's shares and `recover_private_key`. What is left at small thresholds is the one inverse, the reader's re-read of each point and the tag's public key. The legacy reader's x are 1 to n, so its pairwise inverses were short; it gains at large sets alone.)

Pinned by `tests/shamir_interpolation_880.rs`, which keeps the pairwise loop (`src/primitives/bsv/polynomial.rs:259-297` at `3e1ade84`) as the oracle: `the_batched_interpolation_answers_as_the_pairwise_one_on_10000_sets_880` (10,000 seeded sets built by this crate's `split_private_key_with` and `to_backup_format`: 6,500 honest, 2,500 over twelve classes of altered sets (eleven refusals and f(0) in `[n, p)`, a key), 1,000 at the legacy door; thresholds 2 to 32, and 64 of 64, 128 of 128, 254 of 255 and 255 of 255; every key's bytes and every refusal's whole text equal to the oracle's through the same steps, 7,508 keys and 2,492 refusals, their SHA-256 `347d8607aeb7840404e7e85a13f2c543658b13d482b59b51b1361f044936ef48` on this change and on `3e1ade84` alike); `value_at_answers_as_the_pairwise_one_on_hand_built_points_880` (the public door's cells above and 2,000 seeded point lists, value for value); `recovery_at_128_of_128_costs_a_fraction_of_the_pairwise_oracle_880`, the test that was RED before the change (the oracle at least 5 times `value_at`'s time in one process, a ratio; on `3e1ade84` `value_at took 2.541130083s where the pairwise oracle took 2.526311458s`, here 34 ms against 2.47 s in a debug build); and by hand in release every threshold from 2 to 255, t of t, equal on all 254 (`every_threshold_from_2_to_255_answers_as_the_pairwise_one_880`). `tests/shamir_backup_854.rs` (16) and `tests/shamir_backup_refusals_854.rs` (27) pass with no cell changed and `tests/vectors/shamir_backup_854.json` is untouched. `benches/primitives_bench.rs` gains `recover_private_key (2 of 3)`, `(10 of 20)`, `(255 of 255)` and `recover_private_key_from_legacy_backup (3 of 5)`, `(255 of 255)`; `benches/baseline.json`'s entries do not carry the five rows yet (each machine's record is its own run).

Not in scope, as the issue says: the split and `to_backup_format` (the writer re-reads each point as the reference does). No public item changes: Migration: none.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#880)

The reference and go-sdk keep one inverse per ordered pair (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/primitives/Polynomial.ts:120-136`, `denominator.invm(P)` at `:129`, called from `PrivateKey.ts:615-616`; go-sdk@2ca481c `primitives/keyshares/polynomial.go:82-106`, `ModInverse` at `:92`, a missing inverse read as 0 at `:93-95`). The value is the same field element: equal on the differential's 10,000 sets and 254 thresholds against this crate's copy of that loop, and the #854 recording of the reference (`tests/vectors/shamir_backup_854.json`) is read as before, both directions. No answer moves; this is cost alone. ### Changed (breaking): the ECDH result is a `SharedSecret` whose `Debug` prints no secret; both `derive_shared_secret` doors and `reveal_counterparty_secret` return it (#843d6)

**What changed.** `PrivateKey::derive_shared_secret`, `PublicKey::derive_shared_secret`, `KeyDeriver::reveal_counterparty_secret`, `KeyDeriverApi::reveal_counterparty_secret` and its two impls (`KeyDeriver`, `CachedKeyDeriver`) return `Result<SharedSecret>`, where they returned `Result<PublicKey>`. `SharedSecret` (`src/primitives/ec/shared_secret.rs`, re-exported at `primitives::ec` and `primitives`) holds the point in one private field and offers three doors, each documented as revealing the secret: `to_compressed() -> [u8; 33]`, `x() -> [u8; 32]` and `to_point() -> PublicKey`; a hand-written `Debug` writing `SharedSecret { .. }`; `Clone`; `PartialEq` and `Eq` in constant time over the compressed bytes (`subtle`, as `PrivateKey`'s). It has no public constructor (only the doors make one), no `Display`, `Hash`, `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `Deref`, `AsRef`, `Default`, no conversion into a `PublicKey`, and its point is not wiped from memory on drop. The arithmetic, the errors and every byte are unchanged: `Schnorr::generate_proof` and `verify_proof` keep `&PublicKey` (a verifier holds a linkage revealed on the wire), and `PublicKey::mul_scalar` stays public, now documented as point arithmetic whose result, given a private scalar the caller names through `to_bytes`, is the ECDH secret as a `PublicKey`.

**Why the old type was wrong.** The ECDH point is secret material (BRC-42 keys its HMAC with its 33 bytes, `PrivateKey.ts:460` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`; its x is the wallet's and ECIES's symmetric key), and `PublicKey` prints it: its `Debug` writes the compressed hex (`public_key.rs:422-428` on `3e1ade84`), as do its `Display`, `Hash` input and `Serialize`, and its `==` is not constant time. So a `{:?}` of the result, or of a dependent's struct holding it, wrote the secret to a log line; the secret `Debug` lane stated this as its one exception.

**What pins it.** `tests/secret_debug.rs` `the_ecdh_shared_secret_is_not_printed_by_debug_843d6`: the five doors (both `derive_shared_secret`, the inherent `reveal_counterparty_secret`, the trait's through `KeyDeriver` and `CachedKeyDeriver`) and a struct deriving `Debug` over each result carry no run of four characters of the compressed hex (either case), of x's hex, or of the 33 bytes' decimal list; written through `to_compressed()` and `x()` alone, RED on `3e1ade84` at run time (`PrivateKey::derive_shared_secret: Debug carries a run of the shared secret`). `tests/arch_shared_secret_843d6.rs`: by signature over `src/`, no `fn` whose name holds `shared_secret` or `counterparty_secret` returns `PublicKey`, and `shared_secret.rs` derives no `Debug`, implements none of the printing or converting traits and has no `pub fn` beyond the three doors; RED on `3e1ade84` at the six signatures. Four `compile_fail` doc tests on the type: `format!("{s}")`, a `HashSet` insert, `serde_json::to_string(&s)`, `&s` where `&PublicKey` is wanted (each compiling on `3e1ade84`). `tests/shared_secret_bytes_843d6.rs` against `tests/vectors/shared_secret_843d6.json` (`tests/support/shared_secret_843d6.mjs`, Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical): five scalar pairs, the reference's 33 bytes from both doors and `revealCounterpartySecret`, and BRC-42's children from both sides for two invoice numbers, read byte for byte through every door here; green before and after, the proof that no byte moved, beside `ec_tests`, `cross_sdk_tests`, the three ECIES files, `messages_tests`, `wallet_specific_linkage_427` and `wire_linkage_calls_406`, whose counts are equal on `3e1ade84` and on the change. The fold after the three reads of PR #899 (tests and two doc-test blocks, no behaviour): a fifth `compile_fail` doc test builds `SharedSecret { point }` from outside the crate, with a compiling twin of its other lines; `tests/shared_secret_bytes_843d6.rs` asserts `!=` on different pairs and `==` on one pair both ways; the arch test reads every `pub` of the type's file (a field, `pub const fn`, `pub async fn`), refuses `From`, `TryFrom`, `LowerHex`, `UpperHex`, `ToString` and a derive of anything but `Clone`, wants `ct_eq` in the hand-written `PartialEq`, and counts exactly six `fn`s returning `SharedSecret`, by name; `secret_debug` asserts the exact text `SharedSecret { .. }`. The scan is lexical and its header states its bound (an alias, a return type written `Self`, a macro-built signature, a re-export under another name).

**The break, measured.** `cargo semver-checks --release-type patch --all-features --baseline-rev 3e1ade84` (0.51.0): 229 checks pass, 31 skip, no lint fires; a changed return type is not among its lints. The rustdoc JSON of base and change (nightly) differs in the six return types and the new type alone.

**Migration.** `s.to_compressed()` and `s.x()` compile unchanged. Where a `PublicKey` is wanted (a Schnorr proof, point arithmetic), call `s.to_point()`. `format!("{s}")`, `s.to_hex()`, serde and a hash key no longer compile: name `to_point()` or `to_compressed()`. An implementor of `KeyDeriverApi` returns from `reveal_counterparty_secret` what `derive_shared_secret` gave it.

### Fixed: the four wallet PushDrop lock sites judge the key text before any signature is asked (#816)

Four sites that build a signed PushDrop token from a wallet (the identity reveal's `identity_token`, `src/identity/reveal.rs`; the contacts manager's `contact_lock`, `src/identity/contacts_actions.rs`; the registry's `lock_definition`, `src/registry/token.rs`; the local key-value store's `create_locking_script`, `src/kvstore/local_token.rs`) asked the wallet's `getPublicKey`, then its `createSignature`, and only then read the key text (`wallet_key_lock`). A key answer that is no key was therefore refused after two wallet calls: a signature, and with it a permission prompt on a wallet that asks for one, that the reference never requests for a text that is not hex (for a text that decodes as hex and is no key the reference asks it too and pushes the text, #782's residue (a); the parity note below). The reference's `PushDrop.lock`, which all four counterparts call (`IdentityClient.ts:502`, `ContactsManager.ts:767`, `RegistryClient.ts:320,622`, `LocalKVStore.ts:487` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`), asks the key (`PushDrop.ts:155-163`), decodes its text (`toArray(publicKey, 'hex')`, `:166-172`, which throws on a text that is not hex) and only then asks the signature (`:173-185`).

Each of the four now locks through the one door, `PushDrop::lock_with_wallet` (#782), which has had the reference's order since #782's fold: the key asked, its text read, then the signature over the data fields, appended last. The wallet sees the same two requests (the same protocol, key ID, counterparty and `forSelf` on the key call, the same data on the signature call, the same originator on both) and the locking script is the same bytes; only a key text that is no key is refused one call earlier, in the same words (`PublicKey::from_hex`'s). `wallet_key_lock` keeps one caller, the global key-value store, and is compiled under `kvstore` alone.

Pinned by `tests/pushdrop_lock_key_order_816.rs` (4), each site through its public path over the #318 counting wallet answering `zz` for a derived key: `the_identity_token_refuses_a_key_text_that_is_no_key_before_any_signature_is_asked_816`, `the_contact_lock_refuses_a_key_text_that_is_no_key_before_any_signature_is_asked_816`, `the_registry_lock_refuses_a_key_text_that_is_no_key_before_any_signature_is_asked_816`, `the_local_kvstore_lock_refuses_a_key_text_that_is_no_key_before_any_signature_is_asked_816` (the error the parser's, the lock key's `getPublicKey` the last call, no `createSignature`, no `createAction`); and by the machine `tests/arch_pushdrop_wallet_key_order_816.rs`, `the_wallet_key_lock_helper_has_one_stated_caller_816`, which refuses `wallet_key_lock` named under `src/` anywhere but its definition and `src/kvstore/global_actions.rs`, and `read_wallet_key` anywhere but its definition's file and the door. Five of five RED on a scratch copy of `3e1ade84` (the four at the calls assertion, the words assertion ahead of it passing; the machine naming the four sites). The good-key path is held by the older witnesses, untouched (`tests/identity_reveal_rest_310.rs`, `tests/identity_contacts_envelope_544.rs`, `tests/registry_token_fields_543.rs`, `tests/kvstore_local_454.rs`, `tests/script_pushdrop_key_bytes_545.rs`).

Migration: none. No public item, no request byte, no locking script byte and no refusal text moves. What a wallet, or a test double of one, can see: one that answers `getPublicKey` with a text that is no key is no longer asked `createSignature` at these four sites, so a count of its calls drops by one, and where its `createSignature` would itself have failed the error returned is the key parser's, where it was the wallet's.

Tests alone, the same issue (its comment of 2026-11-10: two paths of the relaxed push-only rule had no test): `tests/script_push_only_default_816.rs` gains `the_two_pass_stream_judges_push_only_as_the_reference_default_816` (`verify_stream_two_pass`), `the_async_stream_judges_push_only_as_the_reference_default_816` (`verify_stream_async`) and `an_unproven_ancestor_is_judged_push_only_as_the_reference_default_816` (an unproven parent that is not the subject, at the cell's version with the cell's unlocking script, under a version-1 push-only subject; the BEEF by this crate's writer, read by the three stream doors and `Transaction::verify`), over the recorded grid's default-mode cells, the vector not edited: valid where the reference's default runs the cell, refused at the parent's input 0 in the reference's words at versions 0 and 1 (`Spend.ts:319-321,366-368,2060-2063`). They pin behaviour landed by PR #822; their RED is a mutation of the tip (`&& !relaxed_by_default(transaction_version)` removed from `Spend::new`'s `require_push_only`), under which the three fail at the version-2 cell that is not push-only. No `src/script/spend/` line changes.

### Changed: fee refuses inputs that cannot pay, an amount or a total past 21e14, an output with no amount and a missing source output, in the reference's words and order; get_fee refuses an output with no amount, a change output's included (#871)

- What was wrong. `Transaction::fee` answered `Ok` where the reference's `fee` refuses (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/transaction/Transaction.ts:770-862`): on inputs that could not pay the outputs and the fee the change saturated to 0 and the change outputs were removed, so an input of 1,000, an output of 950 and a fee of 100 gave a transaction paying 50, and outputs above the inputs gave `Ok` on a transaction no node accepts; amounts and totals were bounded only at `u64` where the reference bounds them at 21e14 satoshis (`MAX_SATOSHIS`, `requireSatoshiAmount`, `addSatoshiAmount`, `:65-86`; the node's `MAX_MONEY`); an output with no amount was read as 0 (`unwrap_or(0)`); a source output that did not exist, or held no amount, was named in the missing-source sentence. `get_fee` read an output with no amount, a change output not yet computed among them, as 0 where the reference's `getFee` refuses it (`:899-933`). Every row a caller's own values: no peer's bytes reach `fee`.
- The fix, the reference's checks in the reference's order (`fee`: the fee, then `#calculateChange`; one place for each bound, `transaction::amount`): the fee past 21e14 refused ahead of every other check (`Computed transaction fee must be a non-negative safe integer no greater than 21e14.`; `fee(None, ..)` judges its own `estimate_size` the same way); then each input in turn, no source transaction (the sentence unchanged), a source output that does not exist (`Input N references a source output that does not exist.`), a source output with no amount or one past 21e14 (`Input N source amount must be a non-negative safe integer no greater than 21e14.`), the input total past 21e14 (`Transaction input total exceeds the maximum valid monetary range.`); then each output that is not a change output, no amount or one past 21e14 (`Output N amount must be ...`), the output total (`Transaction output total exceeds ...`); then the inputs against the outputs and the fee (`Transaction inputs are insufficient for the requested outputs and fee.`). A change output's amount is not read by `fee` (the reference's neither; a preset one is overwritten). `get_fee` runs the same input checks under its own missing-source sentence and the amount and total checks over every output, change outputs included. `amount::add_amount` is the one place for a total's bound (21e14, where it was `u64`) and `amount::require_satoshi_amount` for an amount's. The transaction is unchanged on every `Err`.
- The reference's answers by a run. `tests/support/transaction_fee_refusals_871.mjs` (the SDK at the pin bundled with bun, Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical) records `fee` and `getFee` on 65 cells to `tests/vectors/transaction_fee_refusals_871.json`: each row at each side of its edge (inputs that cannot pay the outputs alone, the outputs and the fee, one satoshi short, exactly, one over, with and without change outputs, no input; an amount and each total at 21e14, at 21e14 + 1, at 2^53 - 1 and at 2^53, the fee among them; an output with no amount at output 0, 1 and 2 of three, a source output with none, a change output with none; an index one and seven past the source's outputs, a source with no outputs, the second input's; no fee given; both distributions), thirteen cells of two refusals at once (the fee before any input; an input before a later input and before any output; an amount before its total; an output with no amount before the insufficiency), and `getFee` on every cell.
- What pins it. `tests/transaction_fee_refusals_871.rs` (10): one test per row replaying its cells, `fee` and `get_fee`, every difference gathered before the assertion, the transaction unchanged on `Err`; `(e)` and `(f)` as stated below; an amount and a fee at `u64::MAX` in the amount words; the vector's census. On the base (`8e78516f`, a scratch copy, its own target) 9 of 10 RED, each by its message (`a_inputs_cannot_pay_the_outputs_and_the_fee fee: got {"ok":[{"satoshis":950,...}]}, reference {"err":"Transaction inputs are insufficient ..."}`; `c_no_amount_at_output_0_of_3 getFee: got {"ok":980}`; `d_index_one_past_the_source_outputs fee: got {"err":"Source transactions are required ..."}`), the census green on both. Ten plants on the tip, each new check removed in turn (the fee's bound, the insufficiency, an output's amount, a source output's existence, a source amount, a total's bound, `get_fee`'s change outputs) and three orders swapped (the fee after the inputs, the outputs before the inputs, a total before its amount), each RED by a named test. A differential of 20,000 seeded calls on the base and the tip (inputs with sources, without, past their source; outputs with and without amounts; change outputs, some preset; no fee, a small fee, an edge fee; both distributions): no `Ok` became another `Ok`, no `Err` became `Ok`; `fee`'s 3,528 well-funded, well-formed calls the same `Ok` to the satoshi (one SHA-256 over their answers on both sides, `014ca3e1...`); `docs/lanes/fix-871-fee-refusals.md` has the classes. Two older tests asserted the old reading and assert the reference's now: `tests/transaction_identity_843.rs`'s property funds its `fee` step before the call (a shortfall input, no draw from the seed) and its no-change cell asks a fee of 19,000 over 20,000 less 1,000 where it asked 50,000; `tests/transaction_fee_random_change_868.rs`'s three `u64` cells name the amount, refused ahead of its total.
- Migration. No signature moved; `fee` and `get_fee` already answered a `Result`. Each `Ok` that is now an `Err`, and what a caller does:
  - `fee` on inputs that cannot pay the non-change outputs and the fee: `Err` where the change outputs were removed and the shortfall taken from the fee. Fund the transaction, or lower the fee or the outputs, before calling `fee`.
  - `fee` or `get_fee` with an amount, a source amount, a fee or a total above 2,100,000,000,000,000 satoshis: `Err` where it was read. No valid transaction carries one; keep the amounts within it.
  - `fee` with a non-change output holding no amount (one built with `satoshis: None` through `outputs_mut()` or a literal; `add_output` refuses it already): `Err` where it was read as 0. Give it an amount or mark it change.
  - `get_fee` with a change output whose amount `fee` has not written yet: `Err` where it was read as 0. Call `get_fee` after `fee`.
  - `fee` or `get_fee` whose input names a source output that does not exist or holds no amount: the same `Err` in other words (a caller matching the missing-source sentence matches `Input N references a source output that does not exist.` and `Input N source amount must be ...` too).
- Not for the stable line: no class under `RELEASING.md`'s direction rule; 0.8.x keeps these answers, stated in its parity rows.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#815)

Ours: the reference's constructor, STEAK validation, discovery cache and answer readings at the pin, with these residues stated. The typed `Steak` cannot hold three of the states `validateSTEAK` checks (a value that is no plain record, an instruction with a field other than the three, an index that is no integer from 0 to `0xffffffff`): a custom facilitator cannot build them, and the HTTPS facilitator judges them on the JSON, in the reference's words, before it builds the type (the fold; until it, serde's typed read refused the non-record and the non-integer index in serde's words and took the instruction field). At that door, stated (`tests/overlay_ship_steak_door_815.rs`, `WORDS_STATED` and the file's header): five of the 79 recorded shapes are refused on both sides in other words (a non-2xx status `Broadcast failed with HTTP status: <status>` here, `Failed to facilitate broadcast` there; an index past the double range, an array nested 200 deep and a lone surrogate escape in a topic name `SHIP response is not valid JSON.` here, where the reference parses each and refuses the value); `{}` is handed back by `send` as the empty STEAK and refused by the broadcaster, in the reference's words; the JSON object's entries are walked in `serde_json`'s sorted order and the typed `Steak` is a `HashMap`, so where two entries break a rule the one named can differ from the reference's, which names the earlier in the body's order; the facilitator refuses a STEAK the reference's facilitator hands to its broadcaster to refuse, the same host failed either way. Not ported at that door, older than #815: the reference's refusal of a redirect (`redirect: 'error'`, `:371`), its 30 s timeout (`:378-385`), its `X-Topics` in the comma-joined form (`:347`) and its endpoint check (`shipEndpoint`, `:103-127`, read at the discovery and the constructor since #804, not at `send`). A caller waiting on a discovery that fails asks for itself after it, where the reference's waiters receive the leader's rejection (`:706-707`); the leader's `Err` is the leader's alone. The counting pass has no reference twin. Theirs: go-sdk@2ca481c checks the `tm_` prefix alone and a `nil` topic list, an empty one passing (`overlay/topic/broadcaster.go:66-73`), keeps no interested-hosts cache, and compares the content type exactly (`overlay/lookup/facilitator.go:60`), so a type with parameters goes to its JSON reader; not filed.

### Tests: the wallet error family's derives and #[non_exhaustive] are pinned (#819)

`AbortKind` (#604) derives `Hash` and is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and so are `WalletFaultFamily` (#439) and `WalletRefusalClass` (#137); `WalletFault` and `AbortAcceptance` (#439) are `#[non_exhaustive]` structs. Nothing held any of it: dropping the derive or the attribute passed every test. A host may key a map by these enums, and `#[non_exhaustive]` is what keeps a later variant or field additive within 0.x (root `CLAUDE.md` rule 9); removed, the next variant breaks every exhaustive match downstream. Held by the compiler, in a form an addition cannot make stale:

- The enums (`WalletFaultFamily`, `AbortKind`, `WalletRefusalClass`): each is defined inside `non_exhaustive_enum!` (`src/util/non_exhaustive.rs`, crate-private), which passes the definition through token for token and appends two doc tests written from it: a `compile_fail` match with one arm per variant and no wildcard, and the same match with a wildcard arm, which must compile (so a wrong path or a block broken in another way fails there). The arms are the definition's variants by construction, so a variant added later is in the block without a hand.
- The structs (`WalletFault`, `AbortAcceptance`): a `compile_fail` functional update that names no field (`fn rebuilt(value: T) -> T { T { ..value } }`) beside a compiling twin of the same path. With the attribute no struct expression is allowed outside the crate; without it this one compiles whatever the fields are, each being `pub`.
- `tests/wallet_fault_shapes_819.rs` (6): the three enums each a distinct entry in a `HashSet` and answered by key in a `HashMap` (the SDK's seven classes by `from_code(2..=8)` and `ALL`), `ALL`'s twenty classes distinct and each found by its name, the enums' value derives held by a generic bound (`Copy + Eq + Hash + Default + Debug` for `AbortKind`, less `Default` for the other two), and the two structs' by `std::error::Error + Clone + Eq + Debug`.
- `ALL` against the definition, in the crate: `all_holds_every_variant_once_in_the_definitions_order_819` beside `WalletRefusalClass` and beside the stream's `Kind`: a match with no wildcard gives each variant its position (a variant added does not compile there until it has one), and `ALL`'s names equal `VARIANT_NAMES`, which the macro writes from the definition under `cfg(test)` (a variant left out of `ALL` fails). `ALL`'s array type is unchanged.

The class (root `CLAUDE.md` rule 11), since the fold of the three reads of `c7dbf729`. A hand-written block that names every variant or field judges the attribute only while it does: stable rustdoc checks no error number, so after an addition the block fails to compile for the missing arm or field, with the attribute or without it, and reads `ok`. It had happened here: #167 added `LeftDuplicateBelow` to the stream's `Kind` and `Reason` and left both blocks short, so neither judged anything since. `tests/arch_non_exhaustive_pins_819.rs` (8 at the fold; 10 since the third, one of them the log's reader, run by CI's step) finds every `#[non_exhaustive]` under `src/` (27 types), refuses a spelling it cannot read, a hand-written `compile_fail,E0004` match and an `E0639` block that is not the functional update, and requires for each type one of the two forms above or an entry in its list with the reason: 21 are pinned (the thirteen enums `WalletFaultFamily`, `AbortKind`, `WalletRefusalClass`, `Kind`, `Reason`, `TransportFault`, `ChainTrackerError`, `NotJudgedCause`, `HmacKeyEncoding`, `HmacVerifyPolicy`, `DifficultyError`, `ActivationHeightsError`, `PowError`; the eight structs `WalletFault`, `AbortAcceptance`, `WorkBudget`, `Contact`, `Certificate`, `LookupLimits`, `LookupRequestOptions`, `ChainParams`, the literal blocks of `WorkBudget`, `Contact` and `Certificate` converted), 6 are listed with no pin yet (`Error`, whose variants stand under `cfg(feature)`; `Stop`, `Verdict` and `AsyncVerifyError` of `src/transaction/beef_stream.rs` and `InputVerified` and `InputRefusal` of `src/transaction/spending.rs`, files at their ratchet line ceilings). ### Fixed: the documented door reads a transaction as the node's script door does; an amount is checked in the reference's default mode alone (#874)

`SpendingTransaction::from_bytes` (#855) read the spending transaction with `Transaction::from_binary`'s strict reader, which since #844 refuses an output amount of 2^53 satoshis or more, the reference's bound. The node's consensus library deserializes an amount as any 64-bit value and checks none (bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `bitcoinconsensus.cpp:88-122`, `primitives/transaction.h:190-194`, `amount.h:111`): the amount rules are `CheckRegularTransaction`'s, a transaction check, never the script door's. So under a node's word the door refused at the read a transaction the node's door judges: the node oracle's entry `tx/tx-00026` (an output of 2^63, bsv-script-lean@1c051eae `corpus/tx/tx.jsonl`) answered `InputRefusal::Transaction(Number can only safely store up to 53 bits)` under every word, where GoBDK judges it valid in both columns. Decided by three design reads, 3 of 3 (`docs/lanes/fix-874-door-reads-as-node.md`).

Now `from_bytes` reads exactly one transaction as the node's deserializer does: an output amount is any 64-bit value, and every other refusal is `from_binary`'s, in its error (one reader: the amount rule is a crate-private parameter of `Transaction::from_reader`'s body, `amount::AmountRule`). Where an amount of 2^53 or more precedes another refusal, the door answers the amount's error, as `from_binary` stops there. `verify_input` under a word applies no amount check; in the reference's default mode (`InputRules::reference_default*`) a transaction holding such an amount is refused before the index check and before evaluation as `InputRefusal::Transaction`, in `from_binary`'s words. `tx-00026`: the block and standard words of both eras `Ok(InputVerified)`, the default mode the reference's refusal. `Transaction::from_binary` and its family keep the reference's bound (#844 stands); `Transaction::verify` and the streaming reader read through their own readers and never reach the cell. The door's documentation says it is the node's script check and never its transaction check: a caller accepting a transaction on its answer still applies the node's transaction rules.

Pinned by `tests/verify_input_door_amount_874.rs` (7): tx-00026 built by this crate's writer to the corpus's bytes, valid under the four words and refused in the default mode and its three overrides, before the index (at 1, 7 and `usize::MAX`) and before evaluation (a lock that fails, under a work limit of 0); a seeded property over transactions this crate's writer builds, every amount class (0, 1, 2^53 - 1, 21e14 + 1; 2^53, 2^53 + 1, 2^63 - 1, 2^63, 2^64 - 1) at an output's first, middle and last place, whole, with a byte after the lock time, cut after and cut before the amount, each of the 108 cells judged six times and what it is asserted (read by both, refused by both in one error, read by the door alone); an amount behind a later refusal answered in the amount's words; `from_binary`, `from_hex` and `from_reader` keeping the bound. `tests/verify_input_door.rs`' agreement over the vectors' transactions and their single-byte changes now admits the door-alone cell only where every such amount made 0 reads by `from_binary` and the default mode answers its error. `fuzz_verify_input` asserts the same invariant (its `(Err, Ok)` arm: the amount's words, the bytes with every such amount made 0 read by `from_binary`, the default mode answering the error at any index, a word judging the input). RED on a scratch copy of `8e78516f`: 5 of the 7 (tx-00026 refused under each of the four words, by name; the property's door-alone cells `refused by both`; the order and evaluation tests at the read). Plants on the tip, each RED: the door given the reference's rule (5 of 7); the default-mode check moved after the index check (2 of 7, and `fuzz_verify_input` within its first second, `InputIndex` where the amount's error was asserted); `from_binary` given the door's rule (8 of `tests/transaction_numbers_844.rs`). The node's oracle through the door (the sibling's harness at its pin with its adapter judging through `from_bytes` and `verify_input`): on the base RED at `tx-00026` alone, under its three words; on this tree `VERDICTS: 13765 entries, 0 divergences`, `REASONS: 13765 equal`, as the pinned adapter's run.

No public item changes and no signature: Migration: none. A caller that matched `from_bytes`' refusal of such an amount now meets it at `verify_input` in the default mode, and not under a word (the door is on `beta` alone, in no release).

### Tests: the stream's flat-memory pin judges the least of three windows at each depth, equal across depths, with at most two of the nine windows above the least, so a stray allocation in one window cannot fail it and a cache the stream fills once still does (#873)

`test_beef_stream_memory_is_flat_per_element` compared one window per depth by exact equality, so on PR #872 and PR #883 a 138-byte allocation in the opening window alone (17,150 B against 17,012 at every other depth, a Linux runner, one window of one process each time; every window 17,004 B here) failed a required check the stream did not move. It now measures each depth three times, round by round, and judges two things: the least of each depth's windows, equal across the depths to the byte, every differing depth named; and at most two of the nine windows above the least of all nine, every high window named with its round, depth and bytes. An allocation that is not the stream's can only raise a window's peak. The count is the cold read's finding: a cache inside the stream that fills once per process and keeps its capacity raises only the windows of the round that grows it (three, one per depth), which the minima alone did not see and the one-window form did. What the form cannot see, stated: three or more stray allocations in one process fail it, and a cache grown in fewer than three windows passes it. The cause on Linux is a likely one (libtest's main thread registering its receive waker late), not a confirmed one. RED in a scratch copy: 138 bytes planted in one window (the opening one, a middle one, the last) or in two windows of different depths pass; in three windows, one per depth, fail on the count; in the three windows of one depth, fail on the minima; the retained cache fails on the count (it passed the form of a pre-squash commit of `8e78516f`); 8 bytes per element fail at N=4000 and N=16000. No public item moves.

### Changed (breaking): a Transaction owns its four serialized fields; id(), to_binary() and to_hex() are always those of its current fields (#843)

**What changed.** `Transaction`'s `version`, `inputs`, `outputs` and `lock_time` are private. They are read through `version()`, `lock_time()`, `inputs() -> &[TransactionInput]` and `outputs() -> &[TransactionOutput]`, and written only through `&mut` doors, each of which empties every cache before it lends or sets: `set_version(u32)`, `set_lock_time(u32)`, `inputs_mut() -> &mut Vec<TransactionInput>`, `outputs_mut() -> &mut Vec<TransactionOutput>`, and `parts_mut() -> TransactionPartsMut<'_>` (the six fields, the four, `metadata` and `merkle_path`, lent at once, for a caller that writes one while it reads another). `Transaction::from_parts(TransactionParts)` and `into_parts(self) -> TransactionParts` build and take apart a transaction by six named fields, so `Transaction::from_parts(tx.into_parts())` is `tx` in every field, its merkle path and metadata included; `TransactionParts`'s `Default` is `Transaction::new()`'s parts (version 1, lock time 0, the rest empty, as the reference's constructor defaults them, `ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:581-595`; a derived `Default` gave version 0 until #869's second fold, so a `..Default::default()` literal could build a version-0 transaction by omission) and it is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a caller writes `TransactionParts { version, inputs, outputs, lock_time, ..Default::default() }` (#869's fold: `into_parts` dropped `metadata` and `merkle_path` until then, so the round trip lost a proof while `==`, which compares the bytes, still answered true). `invalidate_caches` is removed. The three caches (`hash`, bytes, hex) are `std::sync::OnceLock`s, filled through `&self` and emptied only through `&mut self`, so clearing a cache from `&self` cannot be written. `metadata`, `merkle_path` and every field of `TransactionInput` and `TransactionOutput` stay public (nothing is derived from them, and an input or output is reachable mutably only through its owner's door). The four fields and the three caches live together in `Fields`, a struct declared in the inline module `sealed` of `src/transaction/transaction/fields.rs` with every field private to that module (#869's sixth fold; private to `fields.rs` from #869's fold until then, where the narrow read's plants wrote a field past the clear through a trait method named `clear_caches`, a struct update and a closure in a `const` or a `static`, each now a compile error): its one exclusive door, `Fields::write`, empties every cache before it lends `&mut` to the four fields; `Fields::replace_source` links a source and keeps the caches only where the input's `source_txid` is 64 hex digits (the serializer then never reads the source); `Fields::copy_relinked` (`Clone`'s step) and `Fields::copy_named` (`clone_for_beef`) copy the caches only where the copy writes the same bytes; `transaction.rs`, whose mutators (`add_input`, `add_output` and its family, `sign`, `fee`, `Drop`) write through the doors, and the rest of `fields.rs` cannot write a field past them (E0616, E0451). The serializer, the cache fills, `clone_for_beef`, `Clone` and `Debug` live in `fields.rs` beside the doors. `Debug`'s output, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Default` and every public item but the parts' new fields and `TransactionParts`'s `Default` are unchanged by the move (the rustdoc JSON against a pre-squash commit of `1a3e4c5a`). `Transaction::with_cached_bytes_for_test`, the crate's test door that plants a cache, is built for the crate's own tests and under `internal-test-doors`, a feature that names itself internal, no part of the API, which this repository's fuzz crate turns on; until the fold it was under `cfg(fuzzing)`, which cargo-fuzz sets for every crate of a build, so a dependent's fuzz harness could call it (a scratch crate on a pre-squash commit of `1a3e4c5a` built with `--cfg fuzzing` called it; on the tip it is E0599). `Transaction` is not `Sync` by this change: every input and output holds a `Script`, whose chunks and caches are `RefCell`s, and `Script` is its own later change.

**Why the old contract was wrong, even when obeyed.** Until this change the fields were public and `invalidate_caches()` was the caller's duty after a hand edit. On `7ab65f65`, the lane's base before its rebase (the lane record's RED, `docs/lanes/break-tx-fields.md`; the cold read confirmed it on `f97e94f6`): after `tx.lock_time = 7`, `id()`, `to_binary()` (last four bytes `00 00 00 00`) and `to_hex()` answered the bytes before the edit; `a == b` stayed true against an unedited twin (`PartialEq` compares `to_binary()`); `to_json` wrote `"lockTime":7` beside the stale `hex`, so `from_json` read back `lock_time` 0; a `Clone` copied the stale cache. And the duty could not be met: a linked parent edited through `child.inputs[0].source_transaction`, then `child.invalidate_caches()` called, left `child.id()` unchanged, because the child's serializer reads the parent's own cached hash, which the child's `invalidate_caches` never reaches (the adversary read's probe A). Since this change a stale identity does not compile: a cache is refilled only through `&self`, the borrow checker forbids that while a door's `&mut` borrow lives, and a linked source is reachable mutably only through its child's `inputs_mut()`, which has cleared the child. `Transaction::sign` emptied the caches before it serialized the transaction its templates sign, and the interpreter reads the fields, so no signature made by `sign` and no verdict was ever affected, and after #840 wire bytes alone could not reach a stale cache; every instance needed a caller's own edit. Decided by five independent design reads and the owner's word (`docs/design/843-identity-and-framing.md`, section 3, ensemble 3).

**What pins it.** `tests/transaction_identity_843.rs`: the law as a property, 10,000 seeded sequences of 12 edits through every public door that writes a serialized field (the four writers, `parts_mut`, `from_parts`/`into_parts`, `add_input`, `add_output` and its family, `add_input_from`, `add_inputs_from_utxos`, `sign`, `fee` under both distributions, `Random` over two or more change outputs among them since #868's fix, a linked parent's, grandparent's and great-grandparent's edit through the child's `inputs_mut()`, a `Clone`, a JSON round trip, a re-read from hex in either case), each step judged against the file's own serializer of the fields (`id()` is the display hex of `sha256d(to_binary())`, `to_hex()` its hex, a fresh parse and a clone equal with the same id); what the sequences did is counted and each count has a floor of 200, printed with the seed when one falls short (#869's fold, the strength read: the 4,976 "signs" were picks of the step; at the seed, 1,033 `sign` calls over a templated input, `fee` 2,436 times `Equal` and 2,550 `Random`, 1,377 of those over two or more change outputs, 13,072 steps ending at depth two and 7,452 at depth three, 841 grandparent and 242 great-grandparent edits, every other door at least 2,450 times;
