**Migration** (a dependent reads this; the compiler finds every site). The codes a dependent's build prints, compiled on 2026-11-12 in a scratch crate that depends on this tree by path (rustc 1.98.1): a read or a write of one of the four fields is E0615 (`attempted to take value of method`), a struct literal that names one is E0560 (`has no field named`), with or without a `..` rest, and a pattern that names one is E0026. E0616 and E0451, named above, are what code inside this crate gets when it reaches past the doors:
- a read of a field: `tx.inputs` becomes `tx.inputs()`, `tx.outputs` `tx.outputs()`, `tx.version` `tx.version()`, `tx.lock_time` `tx.lock_time()` (`&tx.inputs` becomes `tx.inputs()`; `tx.inputs.clone()` becomes `tx.inputs().to_vec()`);
- a write of a collection: `tx.inputs.push(x)` becomes `tx.inputs_mut().push(x)`; `tx.outputs[i].satoshis = s` becomes `tx.outputs_mut()[i].satoshis = s`; `&mut tx.inputs` becomes `tx.inputs_mut()`; a linked source is edited through its child, `tx.inputs_mut()[0].source_transaction.as_mut()` then that source's own doors;
- a write of a number: `tx.lock_time = n` becomes `tx.set_lock_time(n)`, `tx.version = v` `tx.set_version(v)` (the setters return `()`);
- a write of one field while reading another: `let p = tx.parts_mut(); *p.lock_time = p.inputs.len() as u32;`;
- moving the fields out or in: `tx.into_parts()` gives `TransactionParts { version, inputs, outputs, lock_time, metadata, merkle_path }`, `Transaction::from_parts(parts)` builds one, the six fields as given; a literal names the four and takes the rest from `Default`: `Transaction::from_parts(TransactionParts { version, inputs, outputs, lock_time, ..Default::default() })` (as `with_params`, which stays); a pattern names the six or ends in `..`;
- delete every `invalidate_caches()` call: there is nothing left to repair.
- `internal-test-doors` is no part of the public API: it is turned on only by this repository's fuzz crate and may change or vanish in any release, a patch included, so a `cargo semver-checks --all-features` report of `feature_missing` against it is expected and no break;
A read never goes through a `_mut` door: each call clears the cached id, so a walk that reads through `inputs_mut()` re-hashes on every step. `cargo semver-checks` 0.51.0 against `origin/beta` (`18ff3307`) names exactly these breaks, in two lints: `inherent_method_missing` (`Transaction::invalidate_caches`) and `struct_pub_field_missing` (the four fields), each at its three re-export paths; `struct_pub_field_now_doc_hidden`, a third lint on the shape of a pre-squash commit of `1a3e4c5a` (the four fields a struct's private fields), no longer fires since they moved into `Fields`. `TransactionParts` and `TransactionPartsMut` are new on this line, so their fields name no lint against `beta`.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#843)

The reference keeps `Transaction`'s fields public and notices an edit by comparing a state captured at its last serialization at every read (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:610-690`, `#captureSerializationState`; `:1097-1103`, `#getSerializedBytes`), which it can because JavaScript compares object identity; this crate's design read measured the same check here at about one serialization per read (1.98 ms recomputed against 93 ns cached at 10,000 inputs), recursive through every linked source, which makes the linear-time walks quadratic (the record's rejected I1). go-sdk@2ca481c keeps the fields public with no cache it fills itself; its one cache, `cachedTxID`, is set only by the caller's `SetTxHash` and returned by `TxID` until the caller clears it (`transaction/transaction.go:27-32,301-319`), the caller's duty this change removes here. The wire bytes, the ids and every verdict are the same on all three; the difference is the API's shape alone: a public field there, an accessor and a door here. Two cells of the BEEF linker are stated, not followed (#869's fourth fold): the reference's `mergeTransaction` writes each linked source's id into the input's `sourceTXID` across the caller's graph (`materializeSourceTXIDs`, `Beef.ts:883`, `Transaction.ts:254-271`), where `merge_transaction` stores the transaction as given, as go-sdk@2ca481c's `MergeTransaction` does (`transaction/beef.go:870-915`), so the input comes back naming no txid with the reference's source, path, id and verdict; and an input that links nothing and names nothing is refused by the reference before any BEEF door (`sourceTransaction is undefined`, at `id` and at `mergeTransaction`), where here it is merged and left as it is. No reader builds either (`tests/beef_input_without_txid_869.rs`; `tests/vectors/beef_input_without_txid_869.json`).

### Changed: the front pages follow each release: the README says why to choose the crate, each sentence pinned; the manifest owns the crates.io and docs.rs pages; the release run makes and checks the GitHub Release page (#883, the design reads of 2026-11-11)

- What changed. The README's first screen (everything before `## Install`) says what the crate is, why to choose it and its limits, and names no version; the install line is `cargo add bsv-rs --features transaction,wallet`; five badges that showed no status are gone; each sentence says no more than its producer: the semver sentence says the check judges a pull request into `main` and nothing on `beta` (cargo-semver-checks 0.51.0 run by hand on 2026-11-11 with a public function removed: `0 checks` on a prerelease, equal to its tag or stepped, `1 fail` on a stable version, equal or bumped by a patch), the private channel speaks of a new row (rule 1's exception), and the fuzzing headline makes no absolute claim. `Cargo.toml` gains `documentation`, `readme`, the categories `cryptography::cryptocurrencies` and `wasm`, and `[package.metadata.docs.rs]` (`all-features`, `--cfg docsrs`), with `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]` in `src/lib.rs`, so docs.rs shows every module, each item labelled with its feature; `homepage` is dropped (it repeated `repository`) and `HANDOFF.md` is excluded from the package. `SECURITY.md` says the crate has had no third-party audit. `Cargo.toml`'s description says the crate is ported from the TypeScript SDK (it said "Reference parity"); the repository's About description follows it in the sitting of the stable tag that ships it. `release.yml`'s `version` job refuses a tag of any form but `vX.Y.Z` and `vX.Y.Z-beta.N` (`-rc.1`, `-alpha`, a build suffix), and a tag whose `CHANGELOG.md` has no `## [X.Y.Z]` heading, or an empty one, before anything is published; after `Publish to crates.io` the `page` job (the workflow's only `contents: write`) writes the notes with `.github/scripts/front_pages.py notes` (the kind of release and how to take it, true for a stable patch, a back-patch, a prerelease and a minor; the tag's hand-written `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` when it has one; one bullet per `### ` heading; every Migration line; the PUBLISHED advisories of this repository the version fixes or is affected by, each with the patch of the range that holds the version; a "Measured at this tag" block read from the run, an input it cannot read, the run itself included, written "not recorded" and raised as a warning of the run; a tag without hand notes one warning, the step going on), then creates the page, or edits one that exists, with `front_pages.py flags`'s marks read on a line of their own (`--prerelease` on a `-` version, `--latest` only on the highest stable). ### Security: a Shamir backup set that carries a share at x = 0 substituted the recovered key for the holder's; every door now refuses it before interpolating (#854)

- What was wrong. The rewritten reader checked every field's grammar but the x values of a set only where the interpolation reads them: a share standing at x = 0 was read — its y is the secret itself, the interpolation answering that share alone, so a set whose zero-x share holds another key recovers that key, its tag agreeing when the tag is that key's own — and a repeated x was refused only among the leading `threshold` points, so a set of more shares than the threshold passed with one repeated past them. Every door read this way: `KeyShares::from_backup_format`, `recover_private_key` (a hand-built set) and `recover_private_key_from_legacy_backup`.
- The reach. A caller that reads a backup set it did not write itself: a custodian's medium, a share pasted by hand, a set restored from another writer. A set this crate's own writer produces never trips the new refusals — `split_private_key` draws every x non-zero and distinct — and no door outside `primitives::bsv::shamir` reads a share set.
- The fix, before interpolating, at all three doors: one scan of the whole set, past the threshold window (`refuse_degenerate_xs`). An x of zero is refused (`Zero x coordinate in share N`, the legacy door's `Zero x coordinate in legacy share N`); a repeated x is refused in the reference's words (`Duplicate share detected, each must be unique.`, the legacy door's `Duplicate legacy share detected, each must be unique.`). The grammar refusals the rewrite added (the point's canonical round trip, the 64-character fields, the counts) already close the non-canonical zero — the field prime as an x field reduces to zero on read — an at-or-above-prime coordinate and an overlong field at both doors; nothing is done twice. The writer is unchanged.
- The tests. `tests/shamir_backup_refusals_854.rs` (27): the finding's set refused at both doors of the new form and at the legacy door, as backup strings and as hand-built points, the forged share first, second and third of three, at recovery first, second and last of four, and a zero-x point built by `PointInFiniteField::from_string` composed into the set; the non-canonical zero x (the field prime); a repeated share at the backup door, and a repeated x past the window at recovery and at the legacy door, each in three shapes — the same share twice, twins not adjacent to each other, and one x carrying another y; the overlong, non-canonical and at-or-above-prime coordinate fields, and a 400,000-character field refused in under a second (pins of the rewrite's own refusals and its cost), the canonical and the legacy zero-x refusals' words pinned by their cells; beside them, honest sets at thresholds (2,3), (3,5), (5,10) and (10,10) round-tripped whole, from the first and the last `threshold` shares, in several orders and from a scattered subset, an honest legacy split recovered, and an honest boundary set (x = 1 and x = p − 1) recovered at every door, its legacy share inside the 65-byte bound. On a scratch copy of the fix's parent (`842562fd`; the first read ran on `4f6e82f2`) with the test file alone, the 18 zero-x and duplicate cells RED (every door answered `Ok`, the recovery returning the forged key) and the 4 honest controls green, the boundary set among them; the 5 pins green on both. `tests/shamir_backup_854.rs`'s reader test now holds this crate's verdicts for the four vector cells whose sets carry a share at x = 0 or a repeated x (`same_share_twice`, `duplicate_past_the_threshold`, `x_zero`, and `shares_255_leading_distinct`, whose 255 shares repeat one past the threshold window: refused at the door, the vector as recorded), and its 255-share legacy cell is rebuilt on 255 distinct x (the line f(x) = 1). `src/primitives/bsv/shamir_tests.rs`'s duplicate-shares test reaches its refusal at the door. `fuzz_shamir_backup` asserts that a set either reader takes holds no share at x = 0 and no repeated x.
- Parity. The vector's recorded verdicts stand as recorded (it is read, never edited): this crate's reader refuses the four cells named above, where the recording reads them, and its own verdicts for those cells are pinned in the reader test. Everything else the recording holds, this crate holds with it.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller that fed a set carrying a share at x = 0 or a repeated x — through any of the three doors — now gets an `Err` where it got a key: take the shares as the writer that made them wrote them, or re-split the key (`split_private_key`). A set this crate wrote reads as before.

### Changed (breaking): backup shares are BRC-140's; a backup written by an earlier release is recovered by a named function (#854)

- What changed. The Shamir backup is BRC-140's (`key-derivation/0140.md` at `bsv-blockchain/BRCs@f7f1520`), written and read as the reference writes and reads it (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/primitives/PrivateKey.ts:12-118,478-623`, `Polynomial.ts:32-49`). The integrity tag is the leading 8 hex digits of HASH160 of the compressed public key (`751e76e8` for the key 1), where this crate wrote the leading 4 base58 characters of SHA-256 of the key's bytes (`GuMr`). Each share's x is drawn by BRC-140's procedure, as `toKeyShares` draws it (`PrivateKey.ts:513-531`): a 64-byte seed per split, `x = HMAC-SHA-512(seed, [i, attempt, 32 fresh bytes]) mod p`, drawn again when 0 or already used, at most 5 attempts; this crate wrote x = 1, 2, ..., n, so two splits of one key shared every x. The split takes the reference's bounds and words (`threshold must be at least 2`, `totalShares must be at least 2`, `threshold should be less than or equal to totalShares`, `threshold and totalShares cannot exceed 255`; a total above 255 was accepted). `KeyShares::from_backup_format` is the reference's `fromBackupFormat` cell for cell, in its words: 1 to 255 shares; a share over 256 UTF-16 code units refused (`Invalid share format in share N`); four fields; x and y 1 to 64 base58 characters, the threshold 2 to 255 with no sign or leading zero, the tag 8 lowercase hex digits (`Invalid canonical share data in share N`); `Threshold mismatch in share N` before `Integrity mismatch in share N`; the point read by `PointInFiniteField::from_string`, which now takes the reference's 129-character bound and its canonical round trip (a leading `1`, a coordinate at or above p: `Finite-field point must use a bounded canonical Base58 representation`). `recover_private_key` is `fromKeyShares`: the collection checked, `At least T shares are required to reconstruct the private key`, `share coordinates must be canonical field elements`, `Duplicate share detected, each must be unique.` among the leading T (a duplicate reached the interpolation's zero inverse and failed as `invalid private key` until now), the secret read modulo n, `Integrity hash mismatch`. `to_backup_format` returns `Result<Vec<String>>` and refuses, before any string, a state the reader refuses, as `toBackupFormat` does (`PrivateKey.ts:104-118`). New: `shamir::recover_private_key_from_legacy_backup(shares: &[String]) -> Result<PrivateKey>` reads only what the old writer wrote (1 to 255 shares, each at most 65 bytes and of four fields, canonical base58 x and y, a threshold of 2 to 255, a tag of exactly 4 base58 characters), checks the old tag, refuses duplicates, too few shares and a BRC-140 share (in words naming `KeyShares::from_backup_format`), and returns the key, never a `KeyShares`, so the old form is never written again. It is kept, not deprecated. `split_private_key_with` takes the coordinate draws too (`seed: &[u8; 64]`, `draws: &[[u8; 32]]`, one draw per attempt; running out is `Shamir coordinate draws exhausted`), so the corpus stays reproducible (#180).
- Why it was wrong. A key backed up with one SDK could not be restored with another: the reference's and go-sdk's shares failed here (`Integrity check failed: computed 'GuMr', expected '751e76e8'`), and this crate's were refused by the reference (`Invalid canonical share data in share 0`) and by go-sdk (`integrity hash mismatch`). The reader also read what the reference refuses (a share over 256 characters, a leading `1`, thresholds `+2`, `02`, `0`, `1`, `256`, a tag of any shape), and the writer broke BRC-140's MUST on the coordinates. Every published release from 0.2.0 to 0.8.5 wrote the old form (share sets written by the published 0.2.0, 0.3.1, 0.5.0 and 0.8.5 recovered by the legacy function, the cold read of PR #876); no published dependent calls these functions (the holders read, 2026-11-10).
- What pins it. `tests/shamir_backup_854.rs` (16 tests since the second fold) against `tests/vectors/shamir_backup_854.json`, recorded by `tests/support/shamir_backup_854.mjs` under Node v22.18.0 from the reference bundled at the pin: the reference's shares for the keys 1, n - 1 and SHA-256 of a label at 2 of 3 and 3 of 5, each key recovered from every threshold-sized subset in both orders (78 cells) and from all its shares; 46 reader cells, each the reference's parse and recovery verdict in its words; the writer's and `fromKeyShares`' refusals of six and three hand-built collections; this crate's shares, written by `split_private_key_with` with fixed draws, byte for byte as recorded and recovered by the reference from all 39 threshold-sized subsets; BRC-140's example shares recovered. The legacy door: six share sets written by the published `bsv-rs` 0.8.5 (a scratch project against `=0.8.5` from crates.io, pasted as a constant with its provenance), each recovered from every window and refused by the standard reader; its own refusals one by one. On `origin/beta` (`18ff3307`), 117 of the vector's 124 recovery and read cells differ, the reference's shares failing at `Integrity check failed`; the test file does not compile there (the legacy function and the draws absent). `fuzz_shamir_backup` asserts the standard reader is canonical (what it reads it writes back as the very lines given) and the two forms disjoint.
- The fold (the three reads of PR #876). A secret of 0 modulo n (shares on the zero line, on y = x and at y = n at a threshold of 2, and on the zero line at 3) is refused with `Integrity hash mismatch`, the reference's words in the recording, where this crate said `invalid private key: Invalid key bytes: crypto error`; a key of 0 is never returned. A recovery whose f(0) lies in [n, p) is read modulo n (the key 1 from y = n + 1), a y at or above p among the leading T refused (`share coordinates must be canonical field elements`) and one past T not read, 256 points refused on the count, each the reference's answer. BRC-140's coordinate procedure is cross-recorded: the recorder's `--fold` mode runs the reference's `toKeyShares` with `globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues` (the platform source the bundle's `Random` reads) fed fixed bytes, the reference's code otherwise as shipped, and `split_private_key_with` given the same key, seed and draws and the coefficients of the reference's polynomial writes its shares byte for byte (2 of 2, 2 of 3 and 3 of 5); a counter with the index and the attempt swapped is RED there, where the self-recorded test would pass after a re-record. No input through the public split forces a second attempt (an x of 0 or a repeat needs an HMAC-SHA-512 value the draws cannot choose), so the recording pins the attempt byte at 0 alone; the attempts after it are pinned at the private `coordinate`, which takes the used points (the second fold, below). The legacy reader refuses a share longer than 65 bytes, the longest the old writer could write (x at most 11 base58 characters for its `usize` total, y at most 44, a threshold of 3 digits, a 4-character tag, three dots), on its length before it splits it, in words that say what to check before they name `KeyShares::from_backup_format` (`Share N is longer than any legacy share (65 bytes): check it for spaces or a line break around or inside it; a share with an 8-hex-digit tag is BRC-140's, read with KeyShares::from_backup_format`; the second fold, where the words said `(65 characters)` of a bound judged in bytes and sent a padded old share to the reader that refuses it too); a share the old writer wrote with whitespace that keeps it within 65 bytes (a trailing newline, twelve spaces on a 53-byte share) is refused as `Invalid legacy share data in share N`, as before the fold; its share words carry the share's index at every index. A mutation pass over the three files (155 mutants) left ten survivors; six are equivalent, each named with its argument: `polynomial.rs:98` (four; the 129-unit bound, which a canonical point never reaches, its longest 89 characters, the round trip refusing first), `polynomial.rs:105` (`||` to `&&`; a field outside the grammar fails the base58 read or the round trip, in the same words), `shamir.rs:131` (`||` to `&&`; a threshold of four or more digits without a leading zero is above 255, refused by the range); the coordinate's four retry arms (the pass's `:542` `+=` to `*=`, `:543` `>` to `>=` and `==`, `:548` `&&` to `||`; `shamir.rs:541`, `:542` and `:546` at the tip) are killed since the second fold at the private seam; the others it found are pinned: both readers' share counts at 255 and past it (300 shares refused on the count before a malformed share 256, the reference's recording), a split of 2 of 2, a point's `Display` and the three `Debug`s' fields. The vector's cells are added in `fold_854` without re-rolling the reference's random shares (every earlier member as recorded). The second fold (the three re-reads of PR #876): `coordinate`'s retry arms pinned at its seam (a unit cell in `src/primitives/bsv/shamir_tests.rs`: with x(0..3) used, x(k) = HMAC-SHA-512(seed, [0, k, draw k]) mod p computed in the test, the fifth attempt answers x(4); with x(0..4) used and six draws the sixth attempt is refused in `Failed to generate unique x coordinate after 5 attempts`, the reference's order, `PrivateKey.ts:513-528`); one coordinates case of counting bytes recorded by the `--fold` mode as the vector's new member `fold2_854` (the seed the bytes 0 to 63, each draw and random point counting; every earlier member byte for byte, 41 insertions), where the fold's four repeat one byte; the legacy reader's zero secret (old-form shares on y = 5x at 2 and 3 shares and on y = n + x) refused in its own words, `Legacy integrity check failed`. No behaviour of the standard reader or writer moved. The cost the cold read measured (release, 255 shares, median of five): `to_backup_format` 0.38 ms to 2.05 ms and the split 8.1 ms to 10.8 ms, because the writer now re-reads each point as the reference does. Read and recover (`from_backup_format` then `recover_private_key`), measured by the second fold on `18ff3307` and on its tip (release, median of five, two runs): 45 to 47 ms before and 0.99 to 1.07 s after at 255 of 255, one modular inverse per pair of 256-bit coordinates, the reference's `valueAt` (x was 1 to n before); at 3 of 5, the common case, 0.007 ms before and 0.12 to 0.13 ms after (the split 0.005 ms and 0.025 ms, `to_backup_format` 0.006 ms and 0.04 ms).
- Migration. A backup whose shares end in a 4-character tag after the last `.` (`...2.GuMr`) was written by bsv-rs 0.8.5 or earlier (the crate `bsv-sdk` on crates.io is another project, whose shares carry BRC-140's tag and are read by `from_backup_format`); `from_backup_format` refuses it as `Invalid canonical share data in share 0`. Recover the key with `shamir::recover_private_key_from_legacy_backup(&shares)`, split it again with `split_private_key`, write the new shares with `to_backup_format()?`, and replace the paper copies: the new shares are read by `@bsv/sdk` and go-sdk; no other SDK ever read the old form. `to_backup_format()` returns `Result<Vec<String>>`: add `?` or `.expect(..)` (a collection `split_private_key` returns always writes). `split_private_key_with(key, t, n, &coefficients)` takes `&seed, &draws` after the coefficients (`total` 32-byte draws suffice unless an attempt is drawn again). A caller that matched the old error texts (`Threshold must be at least 2`, `Insufficient shares: ...`, `Integrity check failed: ...`, `Threshold mismatch: share 0 has ...`) reads the reference's.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#854)

BRC-140 at `f7f1520` specifies the tag (`hex(HASH160(compressedPublicKey))[0:8]`), the coordinate procedure (MUST, `counter = [i, attempt, r0..r31]`, at most 5 attempts), the four-field text and a reader that rejects other than four fields, unequal thresholds or tags and duplicate x among the shares used; the reference's `PrivateKey.ts` at `ts-stack@edf6e03` is its implementation and this crate's reader and writer now agree with it on every recorded cell. go-sdk, by a run on 2026-11-11 (go1.27.0 darwin/arm64) at `2ca481c` and at master `0503af8`, the same counts at both: its backup reader (`PrivateKeyFromBackupShares`, `primitives/ec/shamir.go:150-156`) recovered the key from 108 of 108 subsets (the leading threshold and the trailing one, reversed where the threshold is every share) of 54 sets this crate's `split_private_key(..).to_backup_format()` wrote (12 each at 2 of 2, 2 of 3, 3 of 5 and 5 of 9, three at 255 of 255, the vector's three keys at 2 of 3), read the reference's six recorded sets and this crate's six, and refused the six sets 0.8.5 wrote (`integrity hash mismatch`); this crate's reader recovered 102 of 102 subsets of 51 sets go-sdk's `ToBackupShares` wrote at the same thresholds, so they carry the same tag (the reader checks it; `:107`), and `recover_private_key_from_legacy_backup` refused all 51. By reading, not run: `ToKeyShares` draws x by HMAC-SHA-512 of the seed over a counter of `i` and the attempt as 4 big-endian bytes each with 32 random bytes (`:59-105`), a counter shape of its own that no reader sees. `recover_private_key_from_legacy_backup` is this crate's addition, with no counterpart in any SDK; the old form exists only in this crate's earlier releases.

### Changed: fee's equal change distribution gives the remainder to the last output, as the reference does (#868)

- What changed. `fee(.., ChangeDistribution::Equal)` writes `floor(change / n)` to each change output and the remainder to the last, as the reference's `#distributeChange` does (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:886-892`): 5 over 3 is `[1, 1, 3]`, where this crate gave one satoshi more to each of the first `change % n` (`[2, 2, 1]`). Nothing was broken: the sum was the change before and after; the amounts a caller sees move. On `beta` alone (no class under `RELEASING.md`'s direction rule; the random arm's fix below is the stable line's).
- The tests. `tests/transaction_fee_random_change_868.rs`'s `equal_change_writes_the_floor_to_each_and_the_remainder_to_the_last_868` (five cells), RED on the random arm's commit (`left: [2, 2, 1]`, `right: [1, 1, 3]`), green after; `tests/transaction_tests.rs`'s `test_change_distribution_equal_multi_output` asserted this crate's spread (every amount within one satoshi); it asserts the reference's remainder-to-last now.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller that pinned the amounts of an uneven equal split sees them move (the remainder on the last change output, not one satoshi on each of the first); the sum does not.

### Fixed: fee(.., ChangeDistribution::Random) over two or more change outputs: a debug panic, and in release every change output but the last written 0 (a change of 2 or more; a change of 1 went to the first change output, save a debug panic over three or more) (#868)

- What was wrong. `Transaction::benford_number` computed `(1.0 + 1.0 / d).log10() / 1_f64.log10()`, a division by zero: the factor infinite, `(range * factor) as u64` saturating to `u64::MAX` for any range above zero, then `min + u64::MAX` with `min` 1. The reference divides by `Math.log10(10)`, one (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:894-897`). Every tag from `v0.3.1` to `v0.8.5` carries it. `fee(.., ChangeDistribution::Random)` reaches it with two or more change outputs (with one, `distribute_change` writes the change to it without the call). The reach is a caller's own choice; no peer's bytes reach it.
- What a run showed, on `origin/beta` (`460e6201`, and again at `f97e94f6`) and on the published `bsv-rs = "=0.8.5"` from crates.io (a scratch project, its own target), the same: in a debug build an overflow panic at the add (`attempt to add with overflow`, `src/transaction/transaction.rs:1676:9` on beta, `bsv-rs-0.8.5/src/transaction/transaction.rs:1549:9` published); in a release build the add wraps, `1 + u64::MAX` is 0, so every change output but the last is written 0 and the last takes the whole change (`n 2, change 12345: output 0 holds 0, not a Benford portion of 12345 ([0, 12345])`): no output of `u64::MAX` reaches the transaction, the sum is the change, and the distribution is no distribution. The issue's "u64::MAX" is the cast's value before the wrap.
- The fix, the random arm of the reference's `#distributeChange` (`Transaction.ts:864-897`) line by line (`docs/lanes/fix-868-benford.md` has the table): the divisor `log10(10)`; the minimum 0, where it was 1 (so a change below the output count leaves outputs at 0, as there: change 1 over 3 is `[0, 0, 1]`; with a minimum of 1, `benford_number(1, 0)` would have underflowed at `max - min` once the change ran out); `floor` as `Math.floor`; each change output but the last a portion of what remains, the last what is left. The random digit is drawn by `rand`'s `gen_range(1..=9)` where the reference takes `Random(1)[0] % 9 + 1`, by necessity. The equal arm is unchanged here (its remainder is the parity note's).
- The class (rule 5): `fee`'s and `get_fee`'s input and output totals were unchecked `+=` on a caller's amounts (a debug panic past `u64`; in release a wrap, so `fee` saw a change of 0 and removed the change outputs, `get_fee` answered a wrapped fee); they are refused now as `TransactionError` in the reference's `addSatoshiAmount` words, `Transaction input total exceeds the maximum valid monetary range.` and `Transaction output total exceeds the maximum valid monetary range.` (`Transaction.ts:80-86`; one helper, `transaction::amount::add_amount`). `total_output_satoshis` returns a `u64` and saturates where `.sum()` panicked in a debug build.
- The tests. `tests/transaction_fee_random_change_868.rs` (6): the random distribution over 2, 3 and 5 change outputs, 2,000 runs per cell at changes of 12,345, 2e15, the count, 2, 1 and 0: no panic, every amount within the change, the amounts summing to the change (inputs less the other outputs less the fee), each but the last the reference's `floor(remaining * log10(1 + 1/d))` for some digit, the last what remains, `get_fee` the fee; no change removing the change outputs; a change below the output count fixed at the reference's answer; the four overflow cells. On `origin/beta` (`f97e94f6`) 6 of 6 RED in debug (five tests panic in the crate, `attempt to add with overflow` at four sites, `transaction.rs:1676:9`, `:1591:13`, `:1598:17`, `:1693:13`, and one fails an assertion, `left: [1, 0]`, `right: [0, 1]`) and 5 of 6 in release (the no-panic sum test passes there: the wrap keeps the sum); the published 0.8.5 the same in both.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller of `Random` gets a distribution (it got a debug panic, or zeros and the whole change last, or with a change of 1 the whole change first); a caller of `fee` or `get_fee` whose input or output total passes `u64` gets `Err(TransactionError)` where it got a debug panic or a wrapped total: keep the amounts within `u64` (no valid transaction comes near it).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#868)

`distribute_change` is the reference's at the pin, both arms (the equal arm since the `Changed` entry above), with the random digit's source the one difference (the reference's `Random(1)[0] % 9 + 1` weights the digits 1 to 4 at 29/256 and 5 to 9 at 28/256, `gen_range(1..=9)` uniform). Stated, older than #868 and not changed here (the fix kept to the distribution): the reference's `fee` refuses inputs that cannot pay the outputs and the fee (`Transaction inputs are insufficient for the requested outputs and fee.`, `Transaction.ts:812-814,858-860`) where this crate's saturates the change to 0 and removes the change outputs, so `fee` answers `Ok` on a transaction that pays less than the fee asked or whose other outputs exceed its inputs (`get_fee` then 0), and bounds every amount and total at 21e14 satoshis (`requireSatoshiAmount`, `addSatoshiAmount`, `:68-86`) where this crate refuses a total only past `u64`; its `getFee` answers a negative fee where this crate's saturates to 0. go-sdk at `2ca481c` (`transaction/fees.go:21-63`) answers `not-implemented` for its random distribution, writes `change / n` to every change output with the remainder left to the fee, removes every change output when the change is below their count, and refuses insufficient inputs (`ErrInsufficientInputs`). (The insufficiency, the 21e14 bounds and the negative `getFee` are #871's, above: the insufficiency and the bounds conformed, the negative `getFee` stated.)

### Added: a door that verifies one input of a transaction held as bytes; Transaction::verify and the streaming reader judge every input through the same core (#855)

**What it is.** `bsv_rs::transaction` (feature `transaction`,
`src/transaction/spending.rs`) gains the node's consensus-library shape for one
input: `SpendingTransaction::from_bytes(&[u8]) -> Result<SpendingTransaction>`
reads exactly one transaction, by `Transaction::from_binary`'s strict reader
(#840) and no second reader, once, and keeps it with its sighash midstates;
`input_count()`; `verify_input(&self, input_index, locking_script: &[u8],
source_satoshis: u64, rules: &InputRules) -> Result<InputVerified,
InputRefusal>` judges one input against the output it spends. One parse and one
set of midstates serve every input; the type is `Send + Sync` (a static
assertion) and holds no `RefCell`. The one-shot
`transaction::verify_input(locking_script, source_satoshis, spending_tx,
input_index, rules)` takes the node's argument order and is `from_bytes` then
the method, nothing else; its rustdoc sends a caller with more than one input to
the prepared form.

**The rules.** `InputRules` has private fields and a constructor per mode:
`reference_default()` (also `Default`), the reference SDK's `Spend` without
flags exactly as `Transaction::verify` runs it when no chain parameters are
given; `reference_default_with(DefaultMode)`, the default mode with its three
overrides (`with_require_push_only`, `with_require_minimal`,
`with_utxo_after_chronicle`; an overlay that refuses a non-push unlocking script
at every version passes the first); `under(ScriptFlags) -> Result<InputRules,
ScriptFlagsError>`, a node's word, typed (go-sdk's flag bits are btcd's layout,
the node's another: a bare number means two things), refused when the rules are
built if `ScriptFlags::check` refuses it, before any input is judged, as the
node refuses invalid flags before it reads the transaction; a judge holding a
number writes `InputRules::under(ScriptFlags::from_bits(n)?)?`, which refuses an
unknown bit first. Under a word the word alone decides: the overrides live on
`DefaultMode`, which only `reference_default_with` takes, so a word with an
override does not compile (a `compile_fail` doc test on `DefaultMode`). The
budgets are setters on the rules, `with_memory_limit(usize)` and
`with_work_limit(u64)`, each a LOCAL budget; every setter commutes (a test).
A node operator's own figures are a value of their own, `NodeFigures`
(`with_stack_memory_policy`, `with_stack_memory_consensus`,
`with_script_num_length_policy`, the three `Spend` setters of those names;
`new()` the node's defaults: 100,000,000, 0, 10,000), taken only by
`under_with(word, figures)`, so by type never by the default mode, which reads
none of them; `under(word)` is `under_with(word, NodeFigures::new())`. Under the
block word a stack past 100,000,000 bytes is a decline with the defaults and
judged by a node run with a consensus figure of 0 (`with_memory_limit(
usize::MAX)` beside it); a figure of `X` is a verdict past `X`.
Getters: `word()`, `default_mode()`, `node_figures()`, `memory_limit()`,
`work_limit()`, `DefaultMode`'s three and `NodeFigures`' three.

**The answer.** `Spend::validate` never answers `Ok(false)`, so the door returns
no `bool`: `InputVerified { work_spent }` (`#[non_exhaustive]`; the work the
evaluation spent, always counted, with or without a work limit: one unit per
opcode reached and per byte hashed, the work budget's unit, a preparation's
BIP143 midstates charged once, to the input that computes them; for a caller
charging a transaction's inputs to one total through `WorkBudget::charge`) or `InputRefusal` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Invalid`
(a verdict, the `ScriptEvaluationError` in the interpreter's words), `Declined`
(a local budget stopped it, the same error with its `resource_limit`: a caller
cannot read a decline as invalid without writing that arm), `InputIndex {
index, inputs }` (refused before evaluation, in `Spend::with_transaction`'s
words, `input index N out of range (transaction has M inputs)`) and
`Transaction(Error)` (the one-shot's bytes that are not exactly one transaction:
the reader's own error, before the index is read). `InputRefusal` implements
`std::error::Error` (its `Display` the interpreter's message, the index
sentence or the reader's error) and `PartialEq`/`Eq` by every field of the
interpreter's error (an exhaustive destructure, so a field added to
`ScriptEvaluationError` fails to compile there; `ScriptEvaluationError` itself
is unchanged); `evaluation()` and `resource_limit()` read it. It converts into
no `crate::Error` variant: the mapping into the crate's error is
`Transaction::verify`'s, with the txid and the input, and a generic `From` would
fold a decline into a verdict's variant. `InputRules`, `DefaultMode` and
`InputVerified` are `Copy`, `Eq` and `Hash`.

**One core.** `spending::judge_input` (crate-private) is the only place outside
`src/script/` that builds a `Spend` for an input: the door,
`Transaction::verify`'s per-input code (`src/transaction/verify.rs`) and the
streaming reader's (`src/transaction/beef_stream/spends.rs`) call it, and
`tests/arch_one_input_core.rs` refuses a third site by its `file:line` (RED on
`842e5cc4`, naming `verify.rs:318` and `beef_stream/spends.rs:176`).
`Transaction::verify`'s and the stream's public errors, verdicts and words do
not move: each maps the core's answer through its own code as before
(`verify_refusal::script_refusal`, `execution_result`), a word left for
`Spend::validate` to check on those paths so its refusal keeps their words, and
the stream still charges a refused input's work to its total.

**What does not move.** `Spend`, `SpendParams`, `TxSpendParams`,
`Spend::with_transaction` and `SpendValidation` keep their shape and stay
undeprecated (what becomes of them is the break program's, #843).

**The tests.** `tests/verify_input_door.rs` (14): the door equals a `Spend::new`
built by hand, verdict, words and resource fields, on all 1,488 spends of
`vectors/spend_valid.json`, `script_valid.json` and `script_invalid.json` at
versions 1 and 2, in the default mode and under `ScriptFlags::block(era)` and
`standard(era)` of both eras (14,880 runs, the one-shot equal to the prepared
form on each), and again under a 48-byte memory and 12-unit work budget; the
door equals `Transaction::verify`'s class on every input of every vector BEEF's
unproven transaction whose sources the BEEF carries and of signed P2PKH spends
of 1, 3 and 10 inputs (two with a broken signature), in the default mode and
under the chain parameters' word (56 transactions, 78 inputs, both modes);
`from_bytes` agrees with `Transaction::from_binary` on 556 transactions and
their single-byte changes, truncations and extensions (268,708 inputs); each
refusal before evaluation (an index at and past the count, a byte after the
transaction, a truncated transaction, no bytes, an unknown flag bit, a word
without SIGHASH_FORKID, GENESIS or UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS, the zero word); a memory
and a work decline `Declined` in every mode, judged under a larger budget; the
three overrides; a word carrying no default mode; the setters commuting; a
prepared transaction judged on four threads. `tests/conformance_scripts.rs`
gains the door as a second runner over the evaluation corpus
(`conformance_scripts_through_the_door_855`: 2,922 `node-script` vectors and
134 `node-transaction` inputs answer what the `Spend` runner answers, the
pinned totals unmoved). Seven faults planted in a scratch copy each turn a test
RED (a decline read as invalid, the Chronicle override dropped, the version
forced to 1, the unlocking script of input 0 for every input, a prefix reader
for `from_bytes`, an override under a word, the one-shot dropping the word);
the API is absent on the base (compile-RED). `fuzz_verify_input` (in the
nightly's matrix, 653 seeds from `fuzz/corpus-gen --door-only`): arbitrary
transaction bytes, locking script, amount, index and flag bits, never a panic;
`from_bytes` accepts exactly what `from_binary` accepts; the prepared form
answers what the one-shot answers; a refusal before evaluation never reaches
the interpreter; two runs of 60 s, 983,154 and 826,155 executions, no failure.
`examples/verify_input.rs` is a README block (`tests/readme_examples.rs`).
`tests/verify_input_door_fold_855.rs` (11, the fold of the three reads): a
valid input reports its work with no limit set; the count with no limit equal
to the count under `u64::MAX` on every vector spend in every mode and on
signed P2PKH inputs; a work decline's count; `NodeFigures` through the door
equal to a hand-built `Spend` with the same setters on every vector spend
under the four words and three figure sets (35,712 runs), and on a script
crossing each bound (a verdict past the policy and the consensus figure, a
decline below them, a node run with 0 judging a 100,000,001-byte element, the
number length policy on an operand); `InputRefusal`s differing in the index,
the input count, the message, each resource field, the arm and the reader's
error unequal. `tests/arch_door_says_what_spend_says_855.rs` (2): every public
`set_*` of `Spend` and field of `SpendParams` has a counterpart on
`InputRules`, `DefaultMode` or `NodeFigures`, or an allowance with its reason.
RED on a pre-squash commit of `f5a12929` (compile, and the counterparts undeclared) and under nine
faults planted in a scratch copy of the tip.

**Cost.** Release, five runs each after a warm-up, base `842e5cc4` against the
tip, run twice interleaved: `Transaction::verify` of 1, 10 and 1,000 P2PKH
inputs 0.034-0.036, 0.305-0.326 and 30.4-33.0 ms on the base against 0.034,
0.311-0.317 and 30.5-32.4 ms on the tip; the streaming reader on the largest
vector BEEF (713 bytes) 0.037 against 0.034-0.036 ms and on a 1,000-input BEEF
32.0-32.2 against 30.2-32.0 ms: within the runs' noise. The door's prepared form
judges 1,000 inputs in 30.0-30.8 ms where a `Spend::new` built per input, as both
callers build it, takes 158-173 ms. Counting the work without a limit, at the
door alone: 32.24-32.71 ms without the count against 32.25-32.85 ms with it
over the same 1,000 inputs, five interleaved rounds, within the noise.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#855)

The node's library gives the call's shape and its refusals before evaluation:
bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `bitcoinconsensus_verify_script_with_amount`
(`src/script/bitcoinconsensus.h:90-98`) takes the locking script, the amount,
the transaction's bytes, the index and a flag word, and refuses invalid flags,
then a transaction that does not deserialize, then an index past its inputs,
then bytes after it (`bitcoinconsensus.cpp:88-97`; its codes
`bitcoinconsensus.h:41-49`), a failed script a return of 0, never an error code.
Three cells differ, stated: its flag mask (`VERIFY_ALL`, `bitcoinconsensus.h:
69-74`) excludes SIGHASH_FORKID and GENESIS, so it refuses every post-Genesis BSV
word, where this door takes the interpreter's full word and refuses what
`ScriptFlags::check` refuses; an index past the inputs with bytes after the
transaction is the reader's refusal here (`Transaction`), the node's
`TX_INDEX` there (both refuse); and its budgets come from its `Config`, not the
word, where this door's are the rules' local budgets. The reference has no
public twin (`ts-stack@edf6e03`): its `Spend` gives the default mode
(`packages/sdk/src/script/Spend.ts:296`, `memoryLimit` uncapped by default),
the words and the split of a verdict from a budget refusal (`validate` throws
`ScriptEvaluationError` or `ScriptResourceLimitError`, `Spend.ts:2017-2026`), and
its `Transaction.verify` builds one `Spend` per input (`Transaction.ts:1441-1456`);
its index refusal reads `Spend input index is out of range` (`Spend.ts:2214`),
where this door keeps `Spend::with_transaction`'s sentence. go-sdk@2ca481c's
`Execute(WithTx(tx, idx, prevOut), WithFlags(f))` (`script/interpreter/options.go:15,168`)
refuses an index past the inputs before running (`ErrInvalidIndex`,
`thread.go:135-145`), its flag bits btcd's layout (`script/interpreter/scriptflag`),
which is why the word here is typed. A fourth cell, the fold's: `NodeFigures` takes
any three figures, where the node's configuration refuses a stack memory policy
above its consensus figure (`configscriptpolicy.cpp:269-305` at v1.2.2, 0 read as
`INT64_MAX` for either, `consensus/consensus.h:82`) and a script number length
policy of 1 to 3 (`:192-214`, under `MAX_SCRIPT_NUM_LENGTH_BEFORE_GENESIS`, 4,
`consensus/consensus.h:62`); here each figure is read on its own path (the policy
under a mempool word, the consensus figure under a block word), so such a pair
judges as the two `Spend` setters do. Ours: the typed word, the default mode as a
mode, the decline as its own arm, the figures unchecked against each other.

### Fixed: the ratchet's library lock no longer goes stale when the crate's own version moves; a release commit is Cargo.toml and CHANGELOG.md alone on both lines

- What contradicted what. `RELEASING.md` steps 3 and 17 and the `beta-born` job (`release_commit()` in `ci.yml`) admit a release commit of `Cargo.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md` alone. The ratchet's compiler counters build a scratch copy of the library with `tools/ratchet/library.Cargo.lock` in place and run cargo `--locked`; that lock records the crate's own version (`0.8.3` on `main`, `0.9.0-beta.7` on `beta`), so the version line of a release made it stale and the `ratchet` step stopped (`cargo clippy (pedantic, cognitive complexity >25) failed (exit status: 101); no measurement was recorded ... the library lock is stale`), and `docs/RATCHETS.md` asked for the lock's refresh in the same pull request, which the release-commit rule forbids. Met on PR #858, the 0.8.4 release commit on `main` (2026-11-10 18:49Z); beta's prerelease commits had touched the lock as a third file for the same reason, where `beta-born` does not run.
- The fix, in the tool. Where the scratch copy receives the lock (`tools/ratchet/src/tree.rs`, `lock_for_manifest`), the root package's `version` line is set to the version the scratch copy's `Cargo.toml` declares: the one `[[package]]` entry whose `name` is the manifest's package name and that carries no `source` line. None, or more than one, and the run stops naming what it found (`... has no root package bsv-rs (a [[package]] named bsv-rs without a source line) ...`; `... has 2 root packages bsv-rs (entries without a source line at lines 3, 7); exactly one is required`). Every other byte is the committed lock's, which this change does not edit; its own-version line is whatever it was at the last dependency refresh and is not read. A dependency added, removed or bumped still makes the lock stale and still stops with the message it did.
- The tests. Six in `tools/ratchet/src/tree.rs`: the own version moved (a patch, a prerelease, a longer string with build metadata) differs from the committed lock in that one line alone; no root entry and two root entries stop in the words above; an entry named `bsv-rs` with a `source` line is left alone (either order); a planted dependency moves no other line; the manifest's version read from its `[package]` table alone. Five RED with the change removed (the committed lock written as is), two RED with the `source` condition dropped. Live, from `git archive` copies: `0.9.0-beta.8` in `Cargo.toml` on the base stops stale and on the tip passes and records what the unedited tip records; a planted `semver = "1"` on the tip still stops stale.
- The follow-up (the cold reads of PR #859 and of PR #865). A planted fault, `materialize` writing the committed lock as it is, left the six tests above green: they call the lock function, not the line that uses it. The manifest's name and version are now read by cargo: `package_of` runs `cargo +1.95.0 metadata --no-deps --offline --format-version 1` on the scratch copy's `Cargo.toml` and takes the package whose `manifest_path` is that manifest, read with the `serde_json` the tool already pins (no dependency added, `tools/ratchet/Cargo.lock` unchanged, about 10 to 50 ms a run), and `lock_for_package` (`lock_for_manifest` above) sets the root entry's version line. The line scanner of `Cargo.toml` is deleted, and the sixth test above with it: as the follow-up had extended it, it stopped on valid TOML and took an array element `["package"]` for the header (the cold read of a pre-squash commit of `f97e94f6`), and on both lines it misread four older shapes. What cargo reads, the tool reads: a version inherited from `[workspace.package]` is read, and a manifest with no `version` is cargo's `0.0.0`. What cargo (or rustup) refuses stops as `cargo metadata failed on the measured tree at <commit>: <cargo's words>`, the words its `error:` line and every line after it up to the next blank line (a foreign workspace's path lines, rustup's `help:` line for a toolchain it lacks), then each `Caused by:` block (``unclosed table, expected `]` ``; `duplicate key`); the prefix blames no manifest, since an absent toolchain fails the same call (the cold re-read of a pre-squash commit of `f97e94f6`: its stop said `cannot read the measured tree's Cargo.toml` for a toolchain not installed, and cut a foreign workspace's stop before the line naming its `Cargo.toml`); a tree without a `Cargo.toml` stops as `the measured tree at <commit> has no readable Cargo.toml: ...`; a lock with no root entry or two stops as above. `Cargo.lock`, cargo's own writing in one fixed form, is still read by lines. The tests (30 in the tool, 17 in `tree.rs`): `materialize` run on a Git repository the test builds (a commit by `git archive`, and the working-tree copy) writes a scratch `Cargo.lock` that differs from the committed lock in the root's version line alone (`99.0.0`, `0.9.0-beta.8`, an inherited `4.5.6`, `0.0.0`) or is byte for byte the committed lock (the versions equal), and the planted dependency still leaves it stale; real minimal packages read by cargo offline: the eight shapes the scanner misread (each RED on a pre-squash commit of `f97e94f6` by its message) and eleven it read right (`[[bin]]`, `[[example]]`, `[[bench]]` with their files, a `target.'cfg(...)'` header, `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`, `[workspace.package]`, a trailing comment, `[ package ]`, `["package"]`, a quoted dotted table name, leading spaces or a tab), each read as `cell 1.2.3`; five refusals in cargo's words and the cause chain of a version inherited from no workspace, each sentence asserted by `contains` of its core (a toolchain that rewords the rest of cargo's message fails none; a tool that drops or rewords cargo's line fails each, planted), and the tool's prefix exactly; a package under a foreign `[workspace]` stops naming that workspace's `Cargo.toml` (RED on a pre-squash commit of `f97e94f6`); rustup's two lines for an absent toolchain kept whole; the cargo call's arguments asserted exactly, toolchain selector, `metadata`, `--no-deps`, `--offline`, `--format-version 1`, `--manifest-path` (RED with `--offline` dropped); a workspace whose root `middle` cargo lists after its members `alpha` and `zulu`, each package read by its own manifest (RED when the `manifest_path` match is removed: the root read as `alpha 2.0.0`); this repository's three manifests at `HEAD`. Under the plant three go red: `materialize_writes_the_manifests_version_into_the_scratch_lock`, `a_dependency_moved_is_still_a_stale_lock` and `materialize_stops_on_what_it_cannot_read_and_names_it`. The shared test fixture named its folder by the clock (microsecond steps on macOS) and failed 2 runs in 60 (`AlreadyExists`); every test folder is now named by the process id and a process-wide counter: 60 runs in a row, none failed. The live ratchet's output on this tree is byte for byte what it was before.
- Nothing under `src/` moved.

### Fixed: the transaction readers refuse an amount of 2^53 satoshis or more, as the reference does; from_json refuses an input txid that is not 64 hex digits (#844, #845)

- What was wrong. `Transaction::from_binary`, `from_hex`, `from_reader`, `from_ef` and `from_hex_ef` read an output's amount, and `from_ef` an input's source amount, as a `u64` and answered `Ok` for any value, where the reference reads each through `readUInt64LEBn().toNumber()` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:388,409,497`) and refuses one of 2^53 or more in `Number can only safely store up to 53 bits` (`BigNumber.ts:624-628`): bytes that were a transaction with an id here and no transaction to the reference (stated by #840's fold, older than #840). `Transaction::from_json`, for a document with no `hex` member, held each input's `txid` member as given, so a text the writer cannot read (`"zz"`, `"abcd"`, `""`) was written as 32 zero bytes: three documents, one transaction, spending an outpoint nobody named; an upper-case txid was held as a second string for the same txid (the BEEF index keys on the text).
- The reach. Any door handing outside bytes to the five readers, `from_json`'s `hex` member among them, and through them `Beef::from_binary`, `from_reader`, `BeefTx::from_reader`, `Transaction::from_beef` and `from_atomic_beef` (their entries are parsed by `from_binary` and `from_reader`), `merge_raw_tx` and `BeefTx::from_raw_tx` (the raw-entry scan), and `merge_beef` (the writers' check). No such output is valid at the node: an amount above `MAX_MONEY`, 2.1e15 satoshis and below 2^53, is `bad-txns-vout-toolarge` (bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `validation.cpp:548-551`, `amount.h:130`), so no node verdict moves. In the dependents (`docs/lanes/fix-844-amount.md`) no production site calls `Transaction::from_json` and none matches a text this change moves.
- The fix. One judgment, `src/transaction/amount.rs`: `read_amount` at the three output sites and the EF source site of `transaction.rs`, refusing an amount above 2^53 - 1 as `Error::TransactionError("Number can only safely store up to 53 bits")`, the reference's words. `parse_script_offsets` skips the eight bytes unread, as the reference's `parseScriptOffsets` does (`br.read(8)`, `Transaction.ts:456`, recorded: it takes 2^64 - 1), and is unchanged. The raw-entry scan (`beef_raw_frame::one_transaction`) refuses the same amounts in the same words (as `Error::BeefError`, its variant), so the scan and `from_binary` still take the same bytes, and the writers' check judges the fields of every entry holding a transaction (`BeefTx::amount_refusal`, every output read, ahead of every other writer refusal; the cold read's FIX of PR #856: in the reader's words, from `BeefTx::own_refusal`, until the fold, and since in the reference's writer's, below): before this change it took such an entry on trust (its fields' bytes one transaction by construction), and `fuzz_beef_parser` found the state on its seeds once the reader refused the amount (a transaction built by hand, pushed into `txs` without being hashed: the check passed, the round trip refused it `ValueOutOfRange`, the pre-pass of #621 then disagreed with its oracle), kept as found (`fuzz/corpus/fuzz_beef_parser/issue-844-hand-pushed-entry-amount-unchecked`). `from_json` refuses an input's `txid` member of other than 64 hex digits as `TransactionError("Invalid txid of input N: expected 64 hex digits")`, naming the index and none of the text, and holds one in upper or mixed case in lower case.
- The BEEF doors. The reference's BEEF reader scans a raw transaction without reading its amounts (`BeefTx.ts:16-48`), so its `Beef.fromBinary`, `fromBinaryStrict`, `verifyValid` (valid), `isValid`, `mergeRawTx` and `mergeBeef` take a BEEF whose transaction carries a 2^53 output, which its `Transaction.fromBEEF`, `fromAtomicBEEF` and the entry's `tx` getter refuse in the amount's words (recorded). ### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#844, #845)

The reference refuses each amount cell this crate now refuses, in the same words (recorded at `fromBinary`, `fromHex`, `fromReader`, `fromEF` and `fromHexEF`), and its `parseScriptOffsets` reads none, as here. Stated, the BEEF path: the reference's BEEF reader and its merges take a 2^53 output that this crate's BEEF readers and merges refuse (the root `CLAUDE.md` row). Stated, the counts and lengths: a varint in a longer form than its value needs is `non-canonical varInt` there and `NonCanonicalVarInt` here, and a count or length of 2^53 or 2^64 - 1 is `number too large to retain precision - use readVarIntBn` there and a read past the bytes here (60 cells, refused on both). Not conformed and reported, two cells of the BUMP reader, outside the transaction readers: a block height of 2^32 is read there and refused here (#167's stated row: the height is a `u32`), and a leaf offset of 2^53 in a 54-level path is refused there (`readVarIntNumStrict`, `MerklePath.ts:125`) and read here, BRC-74 carrying an offset to 2^64 - 1. go-sdk at `2ca481c` reads every amount as a `uint64` (`transaction/output.go:29,53`; an EF source amount the same) and answers the well-formed transaction at 2^53 with its id, as this crate did until #844; its `UnmarshalJSON` (`transaction/txjson.go:49-66`) reads a document with `hex` from the hex, its top-level `txid` member unread, as `from_json` does, and from a field-built one sets the `version` and `lockTime` alone, its inputs and outputs not carried into the transaction.

The writer doors on a transaction built by hand with an output of 2^53 (the recorded `writer_cells`; the amount in the first, the middle or the last of three outputs alike; at 2^53 - 1 every door writes on both sides, its bytes the reference's save `toAtomicBEEF`'s V1 body, the older #798 row):
