### Changed: MerklePath's writers return Result and refuse what they cannot write faithfully (#817)

**Migration:** `path.to_binary()`, `path.to_hex()` and `path.to_writer(w)` now return
`Result<Vec<u8>>`, `Result<String>` and `Result<()>`: add `?` (or `.ok()?` where the
caller returns an `Option`). A survey of the dependents (each grepped by its own path)
counts 131 call sites on a `MerklePath`: `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs` 19 (5 in production),
`bsv-overlay-cloudflare` 112 (10 in production), `bsv-wallet-cli` and `rust-message-box`
none; no dependent calls `MerklePath::to_writer`. `Beef`'s writers are unchanged here.
No signature moves at `MerklePath::new`, `new_unchecked`, `compute_root` or `verify`, but
each now answers `Err(MerklePathError("Invalid hex string"))` for a path whose walk pairs a
hash with a non-hex character, where through 0.9.0-beta.7 it answered `Ok` (a root hashed
from the text with that hash dropped; `verify` then `Ok(false)` from the tracker): a caller
that read that `Ok` as a verdict now reads the `Err`.

What was wrong: the writer wrote some states it cannot carry without a word. A leaf not
flagged duplicate with no hash, or with a hash that was not hex, was written as its flag
and nothing more (`from_hex(..).unwrap_or_default()`), so the next leaf was read from the
bytes meant for this one's hash; a hash of another length was written at its length; more
than 255 levels were written `as u8`. None of these reaches the writer from a reader (the
readers hold 32-byte hashes and 1 to 64 levels), but every one does through the public
`path` field, `from_coinbase_txid` (which checks nothing) and `new` with a lone leaf (whose
root is its text, unread). The reference's `toWriter` throws on a non-hex hash
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `MerklePath.ts:289`, `hex.ts:6-17`).

The rule (decided on #817 by eleven design reads, three of three in round 2 for this cut):
a writer refuses only a state it cannot write faithfully (bytes that would not frame, or
would read back as another path) and writes every other state, valid or not, as the
reference writes it; validity is the readers' and `verify`'s. Its words are the
reference's where the reference refuses; where the reference writes bytes no reader reads
back as written, this crate refuses in its own words and states the row.

One read-only check runs before any byte, so a caller's `Writer` is untouched on `Err`;
each refusal is `Error::MerklePathError`. A non-hex hash on a leaf not flagged duplicate
is looked for over the whole path first, so a path holding one is refused in the
reference's words whatever other state it holds (the reference's writer throws at that
leaf, whatever it wrote before it); the other refusals follow in written order:

| State | Refused in | The reference |
|---|---|---|
| a hash with a non-hex character | `Invalid hex string` | throws the same |
| a leaf not flagged duplicate with no hash | `Missing hash at height H, offset O` | writes the flag alone |
| a hash of other than 64 hex digits | `Invalid hash at height H, offset O: expected 64 hex digits, got N` | writes it at its length; pads 63 digits to another text |
| more than 255 levels | `Invalid tree height: N, over the 255 levels a BUMP's tree height byte writes` | writes `n & 0xff` |
| a leaf flagged duplicate carrying a hash | `Duplicate leaf at height H, offset O carries a hash, which a BUMP's duplicate flag cannot write` | writes the flag alone, the hash lost |
| a leaf flagged duplicate and txid | `Duplicate leaf at height H, offset O is flagged txid, which a BUMP's duplicate flag cannot write` | writes `03`, read back as a plain duplicate, the txid flag lost (this crate's readers refuse `03`) |

Written as before, valid or not, as the reference writes them: no level, 65 to 255
levels, an empty level 0, a repeated offset, an illegal offset, mismatched roots, an
upper-case hash, leaves out of offset order, a txid flag above level 0, a lone leaf at
offset 1. `combine` can produce the duplicate flagged txid from two paths `new` accepts (a
held duplicate at offset 1 and the other path's txid leaf there, both holding the hash at
offset 0: a level whose txid equals its sibling's, no honest block's); its writer now
refuses the result. `combine` is unchanged: the reference's `combine` makes the same leaf
(`MerklePath.ts:508-536`, `existingLeaf.txid = true` on a held duplicate) and writes it `03`.

The constructors and the root: `new`, `new_unchecked` and `compute_root` refuse a hash
that a walk pairs and that has a non-hex character, in `Invalid hex string`, as the
reference's `hashPair` throws (`MerklePath.ts:30-32`); through 0.9.0-beta.7 `hash_pair`
dropped the text and hashed the rest. A lone leaf's text (returned unread) and a leaf no
walk reads are not refused there, on either side. No signature changes there.

`Beef::to_binary`, `to_hex`, `to_writer` and the atomic writers keep their signatures and
bytes in this cut: they write each BUMP through a crate-private lenient writer
(`MerklePath::to_writer_lenient_until_beef_817`), which the second change of #817 removes
when the BEEF writers and `merge_beef` become fallible.

Tests: `tests/merkle_path_writer_refusals_817.rs` (32), one per cell, each against the
reference's recording `tests/vectors/merkle_path_writer_refusals_817.json` (30 cells,
`tests/support/merkle_path_writer_refusals_817.mjs`, Node v22.18.0, two runs
byte-identical: 20 cells equal, 10 stated), and a sweep: 601 merkle paths held by
`tests/vectors/` and `tests/transaction/vectors/` written `Ok` and read back equal.
Compile-RED on `cebd819a` (the writers return bytes); on that base every refused cell is
written and the non-hex sibling is accepted by `new`. The equivalence entries of
`.cargo/mutants.toml` move from `merkle_path_walk.rs:141` to `:142`. The fold (the reads
of 2026-11-09): six cells added (a non-hex hash after 256 levels, after a hashless leaf at
level 0 and at level 1, after a 62-digit hash; a duplicate carrying a non-hex hash; a
computed node pairing a non-hex hash), the non-hex scan moved ahead of every check, and
the duplicate flagged txid refused; on a pre-squash commit of `b76114a7` five tests RED, the four cells' and the
recorded-cell sweep (`left: "Missing hash at height 0, offset 0"`, `"Invalid hash at height 0, offset 0: expected 64 hex digits, got
62"`, `"Invalid tree height: 256, ..."` for `right: "Invalid hex string"`; the `03` cell
written; the cell census), the two shared pins RED on planted mutations of the tip. The lane record is
`docs/lanes/fix-817-merkle-writers.md`.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#817)

The reference (`ts-stack@edf6e03`) throws for one of the six refused states, a non-hex
hash, in the words this crate now uses, wherever it sits in the path. It writes the other
five as bytes no reader reads back as the path written: a hashless leaf and a hash of the
wrong length misframe the BUMP, 256 levels are written as a height of `00`, a duplicate's
hash is dropped, and a duplicate flagged txid is written `03`, which its reader reads as a
plain duplicate (`MerklePath.ts:133-140`); these are five stated rows in `CLAUDE.md`, drafted for upstream as row 58 of the #375 queue
(`docs/lanes/375-filings/merkle-path-writer-unframed-states-ts-stack.md`; unfiled). Its
writer also flags a leaf as a txid when its `txid` member is present, `false` included
(`MerklePath.ts:284-286`), so `{ txid: false }` is written `02`; this crate writes its
`false` as `00` (row 59, `merkle-path-writer-txid-false-ts-stack.md`; unfiled). go-sdk at
`2ca481c` holds a hash as a 32-byte array, so it has no non-hex or wrong-length state; its
`Bytes()` is infallible, panics on a nil hash (`transaction/merklepath.go:311`), writes
`byte(treeHeight)` (`:297`) and a duplicate's flag alone (`:310`).

### Fixed: Beef::merge_beef leaves an entry the target holds alone, as the reference does, and files a raw source entry under the txid it holds, one hash less per entry (#621)

From bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs's A8 cycle 1 (issue #621, its opening slice) and
its fold (the reads of 2026-11-09). Two changes in `merge_beef`'s per-entry
merge, now one crate-private door, `merge_beef_entry`
(`src/transaction/beef/merge_entry.rs`):

1. **A held entry is left alone.** The reference's `mergeBeef` merges a
   source entry through `#mergeBeefTxEntry` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
   `packages/sdk/src/transaction/Beef.ts:950-967`): a txid-only entry is
   appended only where the target holds nothing under its txid, a raw or
   parsed one only where it holds nothing or the txid alone (that entry
   upgraded in its place). `merge_beef` replaced an entry the target held raw
   or parsed (`replace_or_append`, #764) and rescanned its BUMP index to the
   last BUMP holding it, so a target holding T raw under BUMP 0 and merging a
   source with T raw and a BUMP at another height that also holds T wrote
   index 1 where the reference keeps 0; and an entry `merge_transaction`
   stored with its source links lost them. Both now stay. The source's BUMPs
   still merge before its entries, and the BEEF is marked for a sort whatever
   the source holds (`#markMutated(true)`, `:978`).
2. **No second hash.** A raw source entry is filed under the txid it holds
   (the crate-private `BeefTx::held_txid`: the decoder's hash of the bytes it
   read, or `merge_raw_tx`'s), where `merge_raw_tx(raw, None)` hashed its
   bytes again (one `sha256d` and one clone of the body per entry; on beta
   nothing is re-serialized, the parse keeps the bytes). An entry holding no
   txid (the public `BeefTx::from_raw_tx`, or one whose `tx_mut` borrow
   cached a stale serialization before `raw_tx_or_compute`) is filed under
   the hash of its bytes, never under `txid()`'s reading of its fields: the
   opening slice filed the stale-cache entry's old bytes under the edited
   fields' hash (the strength read's FIX).
3. **The source is merged as its snapshot** (the second fold, the rule
   read's FIX). The reference's `mergeBeef` merges
   `Beef.fromBinaryStrict(beef.toBinary())` (`Beef.ts:971-990`), so it walks
   the source's entries in the order that `toBinary` writes them and sees each
   one as its bytes or its txid alone. Its snapshot holds every entry raw
   (`BeefTx.fromReader`, `BeefTx.ts:288-311`), so the `_tx` branch of
   `#mergeBeefTxEntry` is never reached from `mergeBeef`. `merge_beef`
   walked the source in held order and cloned a parsed entry's transaction
   with its source links and merkle path. It now walks the source in the
   order the reference's `#getSerializedBytes` writes it (`:360-373`), the
   source unchanged:
   - **A source read from bytes and not touched since** keeps the order it
     was read in: the reference returns the bytes `fromBinary` read
     (`:363-364`, `:1268-1270`), unsorted. A crate-private mark, `wire_order`,
     is set by the reader and cleared by every merge door, `merge_bump`
     included (`#markMutated(false)`, `:690`, which invalidates the cache),
     and by the sort.
   - **A source that needs a sort** is walked in that sort's order,
     computed on a list of positions (`dependency_order` in `beef.rs`, the one dependency
     order `sort_txs` reorders by). An entry mutated through `tx_mut` counts
     as needing a sort, read with the input txids its refresh would give it,
     as `synchronizeNestedTransactionMutations` makes it (`:342-352`).
   - **Otherwise** the source is walked in held order.

   Each entry is merged as the bytes the writer writes for it
   (`BeefTx::written_tx_bytes`: the held bytes, else the transaction's
   serialization), filed under its held txid or its bytes' hash. It carries
   no transaction object, no link, no path of its own, and its linked
   sources that are not entries are not walked. The source's BUMPs merge
   with every level sorted by offset, as the snapshot's reader sorts them
   (`MerklePath.ts:148-149`), the source's own BUMPs unchanged (the third
   fold, the rule read's FIX; merged as held until then, so a source BUMP
   built in memory with its level 0 out of offset order was written so in
   the target). The cost against the opening slice's claim (one hash and one body
   clone less per raw transaction):
   - **A raw entry** still costs one body clone and no hash.
   - **A parsed entry** costs one serialization (cached in the transaction)
     in place of a `Transaction` clone, and a hash when it holds no txid.
   - **The order** costs nothing for a source read from bytes. A source
     built in memory pays one pass over its entries and one dependency
     order over a copy of the position list. Nothing is serialized whole and
     nothing is parsed back.

Pinned by `tests/beef_merge_beef_held_621.rs` (fourteen cases since the fourth fold, twelve since the third, nine since the second
fold, six before, against
`tests/vectors/beef_merge_beef_held_621.json`, recorded from the reference's

- a source BUMP built by `MerklePath::new` with T at offset 1 before U at

The fourth fold (the rule read of the third): `merge_beef` re-keys the
TARGET before it merges (`refresh_mutated`, then the mark), as the

own staleness, stated and not followed: the synchronization invalidates

Migration: no public item is added or changed. A caller of `merge_beef`
whose target already holds a txid raw or parsed now keeps that entry: its

last BUMP holding it. The written bytes move only where two BUMPs of
different height or root prove that txid (a reorg, two roots at a height);
there the earlier entry's index is written, the reference's. Since the
second fold there are two more changes. A caller passing a source built in
memory whose parsed entries carry links (or a merkle path) no longer gets
those objects or links in the target: each entry arrives as its bytes, and a
linked source that is not an entry of the source is not merged. A caller
relying on the held order among ties gets the source's serialized order
instead: the sort when the source needs one, the order read for a source
fresh from bytes. Verdicts do not move: a BEEF is valid in any order
(#240). A caller wanting
the source's entry to win calls `make_txid_only(txid)` before the merge (the
held entry is then upgraded in its place) or `merge_raw_tx` after it. The
survey: in this crate `src/kvstore/token_spends.rs:79` merges into an empty

`~/bsv/bsv-overlay-cloudflare` `overlay-cloudflare/src/routes.rs:3020`,
`low-app-layer/src/credit_beef.rs:120`, `compaction.rs:229` (a test),
`overlay-engine/src/gasp_overlay.rs:1363` and `engine.rs:4032`; none in
`~/bsv/bsv-wallet-cli` or `~/bsv/rust-message-box`. Every source there is
read from bytes, so part 2's no-second-hash moves nothing; the held-entry
rule moves an index only on the two-BUMP shape above. The issue's second half
(a public shape for judging bytes already in hand: `StreamVerifier` over a
slice, a public `Judge`) has no reference shape and is the owner's question,
not this entry's.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#621)

Conformed. `merge_beef` takes `#mergeBeefTxEntry`'s three branches as written
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Beef.ts:950-967`, `mergeBeef` `:971-986`); go-sdk@2ca481c
takes the same conditions (`MergeBeefTxWithTxid`, `transaction/beef.go:984-1000`,
called from `MergeBeef`, `:1010-1017`) and keeps the map's txid, the shape of
the no-second-hash change. The reference snapshots the source through its
bytes (`fromBinaryStrict(beef.toBinary())`) and hashes each raw entry twice
(`:842-846`, `BeefTx.ts:105-115`). The opening slice and its fold merged
the source as held and said the vector showed that writes the same on both
readings. That was false: the vector's "as built" merge serialized the source
first, which sorted it in place, and so hid the order. A source built in
memory and never serialized was walked unsorted here and sorted there, and
the sort breaks ties by position, so the written bytes differed. A parsed
entry was also merged as its object. Since the second fold `merge_beef` walks
the snapshot's order and form (part 3) without serializing the source, and
since the third fold its BUMPs with each level sorted by offset. Eight
residues are stated:
- An edit made straight through the public `txs`, `bumps` or `version`
  fields, or through `find_txid_mut(..).set_bump_index`, to a BEEF read from
  bytes leaves it read as unchanged, where the reference's cache check sees
  the change and sorts.
- This crate's `to_binary` sorts such a BEEF before writing, where the
  reference's `toBinary` returns the bytes read. That is a writer
  difference, older than #621 (a finding for the captain). `merge_beef`
  does not call it, but a caller can: a source read from bytes and then
  written with `to_binary` or `to_hex` is sorted in place and loses its
  mark, so a merge after that walks the sort's order where the reference
  walks the bytes read (the vector's `read_source_merged_in_its_wire_order`
  source: X, T there, T, X here; the review of the second fold, a scratch
  probe). `verify_valid`, `is_valid` and `sort_txs` sort on both sides and
  leave no difference when they pass (but see the `verify_valid` refusal
  below).
- The source is not sorted in place, where the reference's `toBinary`
  sorts a source needing a sort (`#ensureSortedForSerialization`,
  `:354-358`), so its held `txs` order moves there and not here.
- A V1 source holding a txid-only entry (`Beef::with_version(1)` then

### Changed: the default mode requires a push-only unlocking script only where the reference's default does (a version of 1 or below); a version above 1 runs it, as the reference and the node do (#816; the owner's word)

Without a flag word, `Spend` required a push-only unlocking script at every
transaction version (`REQUIRE_PUSH_ONLY_UNLOCKING`, the check at the head of
`Spend::validate`), an older choice of this crate (the 0.3.16 entry's "the
default remains enforced"), while the contract named the default mode the
TypeScript default and so was stricter than it. `ts-stack@edf6e03`'s default
requires it at version 1 alone: `Spend.ts:319-321`, `#isRelaxed()` is
`this.isRelaxedOverride || this.transactionVersion > 1`; `:365-369`,
`#shouldEnforceSigPushOnly()` is `!this.#isRelaxed()` without flags; the check
at `:2059-2063`. bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 under `SIGPUSHONLY` requires it before
Chronicle at every version and after Chronicle at a non-malleable version
alone (`interpreter.cpp:2321-2334`: `(IsGenesis(flags) && !IsChronicle(flags))
|| (IsChronicle(flags) && !IsMalleableTxnVersion(checker.Version()))`), the
reading this crate's words already follow (`ScriptFlags::requires_push_only`,
unchanged). The owner, 2026-11-09 23:5xZ, on the question the stated lane put
(PR #822): "yeah relax it".

Now `Spend::new` derives the switch from the version as the reference does
(`src/script/spend/mod.rs`, `require_push_only: REQUIRE_PUSH_ONLY_UNLOCKING &&
!relaxed_by_default(transaction_version)`): the four bytes read unsigned, as the
reference's `readUInt32LE` number is, so version 0 is strict and 2^31 and
2^32 - 1 are relaxed (#418's `relaxed_by_default`, now the one reading of the
version at `Spend::new`'s five rules). `Transaction::verify` and the streaming
readers build their spends through `Spend` and move with it. Under a word
nothing moves: `set_flags` re-derives the rule from the word, the node's
`int32_t` reading kept.

Scenario: `<sig> OP_DUP OP_DROP` (or `OP_1 OP_DROP <sig>`) over a lock that
succeeds, at version 2: refused until now in `Unlocking scripts can only
contain push operations, and no other opcodes.` by `Spend`, by
`Transaction::verify` (`Script validation failed for input 0: ...`) and by the
stream (`SpendRefused`, `SpendRefusal::Script`); now valid at all three, as
the reference's default and the node under Chronicle judge it. At version 1
(and 0) all refuse it in the same words, as before. At a version at or above
2^31 the default mode runs it, as the reference's default does, where the
node under Chronicle refuses it (its `int32_t` version is negative, so not
malleable: bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `interpreter.cpp:34-44,2321-2334`); under a word
this crate keeps the node's reading and refuses it (#418's stated reading,
now reaching this rule too).

Pinned by `tests/script_push_only_default_816.rs` (7 tests) against
`tests/vectors/script_push_only_default_816.json`: the stated lane's 24 cases
unchanged and 9 `version_edges` added (the default mode at versions 0, 2^31
and 2^32 - 1, recorded by `tests/support/script_push_only_default_816.mjs` at
ts-stack@edf6e03 under Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical). Every
default-mode cell is the reference's verdict at `Spend`, `Transaction::verify`
and the stream; `set_require_push_only` overrides both ways; the words' cells
unchanged. RED on a pre-squash commit of `cc2bcd5f` with the test overlaid: 3 of 7 (`v2
op1-drop-then-push`, `left: Err("Unlocking scripts can only contain push
operations, and no other opcodes.")`, `right: Ok(true)`; the same at
`Transaction::verify` and the stream); with the version read signed, 3 of 7 at
`v2147483648`. Moved with the rule: `spend::flag_tests::push_only_is_derived_from_the_word_and_the_version`
(the default at version 2 now valid, at version 1 refused); the
`sighash_scriptcode_654.json` vector's `default` column at version 2 (nine
cells: U1, U2 ×3, U3, M2 ×2, P1 ×2, now equal to its `default_no_push_only`
column, written by the file's own recorder; the TypeScript and Lean columns
unchanged; seven of the nine now differ from its `ts_default` column, P1's two
agreeing, and with L1, which did not move, eight of the ten version-2 cells
differ); the conformance census: `node.tx-valid.shared.0168` (version 2,
unlocking script `51 b2`, `OP_1 OP_NOP3`, expected valid) leaves the
unsupported class "bsv-rs always enforces SIGPUSHONLY" (319 to 318, renamed
"the default mode enforces SIGPUSHONLY at version <= 1") and runs and passes:
4,120 run, 4,109 passed, 959 unsupported before; 4,121, 4,110, 958 after;
37 skipped, 11 known failures, 0 unexplained, 0 panics both.

Migration: a caller of the default mode (`Spend` without a flag word,
`Transaction::verify`, `verify_stream` and the asynchronous and two-pass
readers without chain parameters) now accepts a spend whose unlocking script
is not push-only at a version above 1 when the scripts succeed. The overlay
engine's submit door is not such a caller, and nothing moves there: it builds
a `Spend` per input itself and refuses a non-push-only unlocking script at
every version in its own static checks before any `Spend` runs
(`bsv-overlay-cloudflare` `crates/overlay-engine/src/script_door.rs:557,649,857`,
read at `9a0f3c29`), so that door is now stricter than the default mode above
version 1. A caller that
wants the old refusal sets a flag word (`ScriptFlags::block(era)` or
`standard(era)`, which require it before Chronicle, and after Chronicle at
version 1), or calls `Spend::set_require_push_only(true)`. No public type or
error text changes.

### Fixed: the topic broadcaster's acknowledgment requirements as the reference has them: the requirement topics checked at construction, every interested host seeded, the three failure codes

The overlay bucket's blocking lines 3, 4 and 5 of 2026-11-09 (the reads of
PR #813). `TopicBroadcaster` now reads its acknowledgment requirements as
`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/SHIPBroadcaster.ts` does
(`src/overlay/topic_broadcaster/requirements.rs`):

- **The requirement topics checked at construction** (`:182-193`, called at
  `:430-444` and per specific host at `:212-216`). A topic list in
  `require_ack_from_all_hosts`, `require_ack_from_any_host` or a specific
  host's requirement that names a topic outside the broadcast's, repeats
  one, holds a name that is not a canonical `tm_` topic, or names more than
  64, now refuses `TopicBroadcaster::new` in the reference's words
  (`All-host acknowledgment requirement may only reference topics included in
  this broadcast.`; `Any-host ...`; `Acknowledgment requirement for <origin>
  ...`; the canonical and bounded refusals `... must contain unique canonical
  tm_ topic names.`, `... must be a bounded array of canonical topic names.`),
  all-host, then any-host, then each specific host after its key. It
  was wrong because `new` accepted the requirement, the transaction was then
  sent to every interested host and the broadcast reported it failed: a
  transaction sent under a configuration the reference never sends under.
  `All`, `Any` and `None` carry no list and are not checked (the reference's
  `'all'` and `'any'` return as given; `None` has no reference form and reads
  as its empty list, which passes).
- **Every interested host seeded** (`:511-512`). The acknowledgment map holds
  every interested host, an empty set before any answer is read, so a host
  that failed or answered no topic acknowledged nothing. It was wrong because
  only the successful hosts entered the map: an all-hosts requirement passed
  with an interested host failing (a false success at a public door), and a
  specific host that failed under an empty list failed where the reference
  passes it.
- **The three failure codes** (`:572`, `:596`, `:615`), checked in the
  reference's order: `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FROM_ALL_HOSTS_FAILED` (`Not all hosts
  acknowledged the required topics.`), `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FROM_ANY_HOST_FAILED`
  (`No host acknowledged the required topics.`) and
  `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FROM_SPECIFIC_HOSTS_FAILED` (`Specific hosts did not
  acknowledge the required topics.`), where this crate answered one code,
  `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FAILED`, with its own words behind the `overlay error: `
  prefix. Two readings in the same checks follow the reference with them: an
  any-host topic list asks one host for every listed topic (`require: 'all'`,
  `:584`; it asked any one topic here), and an empty any-host list is no check
  (`:592`; it failed every broadcast here).

On the reference's recording of 120 broadcasts the base differed in 27
verdicts (7 false successes, 20 false failures) and 45 more in words; none
differs now. Pinned by `tests/overlay_ship_requirements_tb.rs` (five tests,
each RED on a scratch copy of `c96f3c7e`) against
`tests/vectors/ship_requirements_tb_acks.json`, recorded by
`tests/support/ship_requirements_tb_acks.mjs` from the reference's own
`TopicBroadcaster` under Node v22.18.0 (20 constructions, 120 broadcasts; two
runs byte-identical); `tests/overlay_ship_discovery_804.rs` now asserts the
recorded code. The #804 row's two stated residues are closed.

**Migration.**
- `TopicBroadcaster::new` (and `SHIPBroadcaster::new`, `SHIPCast::new`) now
  returns `Err(Error::OverlayError(..))` for a `RequireAck::Some` list naming
  a topic outside the broadcaster's topics, a repeated or non-canonical topic,
  or more than 64; a configuration that broadcast and then failed is now
  refused before anything is sent. Name only the broadcast's topics.
- The failure code `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FAILED` is replaced by
  `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FROM_ALL_HOSTS_FAILED`,
  `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FROM_ANY_HOST_FAILED` and
  `ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_FROM_SPECIFIC_HOSTS_FAILED`, the description the
  reference's words without the `overlay error: ` prefix. A caller matching
  the old code matches the three (`code.starts_with("ERR_REQUIRE_ACK_")`
  holds for both). No dependent read here matches it: `bsv-overlay-cloudflare`
  names `TopicBroadcaster::broadcast_tx` in one doc comment
  (`crates/overlay-cloudflare/src/mainnet_fanout.rs:19`);
  `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs` and `bsv-wallet-cli` name neither.
- A broadcast with an interested host failing now fails an all-hosts
  requirement, and an any-host topic list now asks one host for every topic.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity

go-sdk@2ca481c answers the reference's three codes and descriptions
(`overlay/topic/broadcaster.go:205-244`) but checks no requirement topic at
construction (`NewBroadcaster`, `:64-75`, the `tm_` prefix alone) and keys its
acknowledgment map by the successful hosts alone (`:174-182`), so an
all-hosts requirement passes there with a failed host; this crate follows the
reference. Theirs: go-sdk, not filed.

### Fixed: a freeform answer from one host no longer blanks a lookup; LookupResolver::query answers the merged output list, as the reference does (#815)

From the overlay bucket's blocking line 2 (review-strength-fix-804, PR #813,
and review-strength-fix-796, PR #808, merged).

**What was wrong.** `LookupResolver::query` merged every host's output list
and then, if any host had answered freeform, returned the earliest freeform
answer in place of the merge (`src/overlay/lookup_resolver/query.rs`, the
`first_freeform` slot). One discovered host answering freeform (any SLAP- or
SHIP-advertised stranger) blanked the lookup for every consumer: the
kvstore's global store read no entry, the registry and the identity client
no record, and since #804 every SHIP discovery was refused in `SHIP answer is
not a bounded output list.`, so a broadcast found no interested host. The
lists the other hosts gave were discarded, and the #796 hint contradictions
counted on them described an answer nobody received.

**The reference.** No path of its `query` returns a freeform answer
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/LookupResolver.ts`):
`query` is `return (await this.queryDetailed(question, timeout, options)).answer`
(`:1374`), and `queryDetailed` answers
`{ answer: { type: 'output-list', outputs: progress.outputs }, progress }`
(`:1445-1450`), its other exits are throws (`:1431`, `:1437-1443`). A host's
freeform answer is counted and nothing else: `recordLookupHostAnswer`
(`:1493-1514`) sends an output list to `session.recordOutputAnswer` and
anything else to `session.recordFreeformAnswer()` (`:1512`), which is
`if (!this.closed) this.freeformHosts++` (`:1085-1087`); the session's
`snapshot` is always `type: 'output-list'` (`:1123-1135`). For the host's
reputation a freeform answer is neither a success nor a failure (`:2399-2402`,
`if (isFreeformAnswer(normalizedAnswer)) return normalizedAnswer`), as this
crate already had it (#760).

**The fix.** `query` answers the merged output list in every case, empty when
no host answered one; a freeform answer contributes nothing (a formula answer
stays a recorded failure that contributes nothing). The #796 merge (the hint
compare, `txid_hint_contradictions`, the displacement), #760's accounting and
#775's budgets run unchanged on the lists kept. No public type or signature
changes; `LookupAnswer::Freeform` stays (a facilitator still returns it, and
`find_competent_hosts` still reads it as a tracker's neutral answer).

**The tests.** `tests/lookup_freeform_precedence_815.rs` (6) replays
`tests/vectors/lookup_freeform_precedence_815.json`, recorded by
`tests/support/lookup_freeform_precedence_815.mjs` against the reference's own
`LookupResolver.queryDetailed` and `query` (Node v22.18.0, a scripted
facilitator, `.invalid` hosts never dialled, BEEFs by this crate's writer;
seven shapes: one host freeform and one an output list in both orders, every
host freeform, a lone freeform host, a freeform host beside an empty list,
three hosts mixed, and a freeform host beside a liar and an honest host),
each answer the reference's, the hint merge's count 1, and each host's
successes and failures the reference's tracker's. All six RED on `71202e33`
(`left: {"type": "Freeform"}`). `tests/overlay_ship_discovery_804.rs`:
`a_freeform_ls_ship_host_beside_an_advertising_one_admits_the_advertised_host_815`
(both rank orders) and `a_freeform_ls_ship_host_admits_no_host_and_refuses_nothing_815`
(replacing `an_answer_that_is_no_output_list_refuses_the_discovery_804`), both
RED on `71202e33` (`SHIP answer is not a bounded output list.`); the
recording's `not_output_list` case, which the reference reached through a
stub resolver, now replays as no host here and its refusal is pinned at the
reader, `topic_broadcaster/discovery.rs`'s
`a_freeform_answer_handed_to_the_reader_is_refused_815`. Three older pins
that asserted the freeform answer through the resolver now assert the empty
list (`overlay_mock_tests.rs`' `test_lookup_resolver_with_mock` and
`test_lookup_resolver_multiple_hosts`, `lookup_tracker_accounting_762.rs`'
`a_freeform_answer_with_a_null_result_is_an_answer_762`, whose facilitator
half is unchanged).

**Migration.** A caller that read a freeform answer from
`LookupResolver::query` (or through `TopicBroadcaster::find_interested_hosts`,
which refused it) no longer receives one: the answer is the merged output
list, empty when every host answered freeform. So a `TopicBroadcaster::broadcast_tx`
whose `ls_ship` hosts all answer freeform fails `ERR_NO_HOSTS_INTERESTED`
where it failed `ERR_HOST_DISCOVERY`, the code the reference's broadcaster
answers with its own resolver (`SHIPBroadcaster.ts:475`); a caller matching
the old code on that shape matches the new one. Inside this crate no caller
depended on it (`GlobalKVStore`'s freeform arm and the identity, registry and
storage readers' non-list arms read nothing, as an empty list reads nothing);
in the dependents read (`~/bsv/bsv-overlay-cloudflare`,
`~/bsv/bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs`, `~/bsv/bsv-wallet-cli`, `~/bsv/rust-message-box`)
none reads a freeform answer from `LookupResolver::query`: the
overlay-cloudflare matches on `LookupAnswer::Freeform` are its own lookup
services' answers and its engine's, and the toolbox's `parse_overlay_answer`
reads any non-list answer as no certificate. A caller that needs a host's
freeform result asks that host through an `OverlayLookupFacilitator`
directly.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#815)

The answer is the reference's on every recorded shape, and each host's
reputation counts are its tracker's. The reference's `queryDetailed` also
reports the hosts' tally (`freeformHosts`, `successfulHosts`, `emptyHosts`,
recorded in the vector); this crate has no `queryDetailed` and no tally, older
than #815. go-sdk at `2ca481c` returns a freeform answer when the response
that reached its channel first is one (`overlay/lookup/resolver.go:122-124`,
`if successfulResponses[0].Type == AnswerTypeFreeform { return
successfulResponses[0], nil }`), so a freeform host that answers fastest
blanks its lookup as this crate's did, and otherwise drops freeform answers
from the merge (`:128-130`); with no successful response it errs
`no-successful-responses` (`:118-120`), where the reference and this crate
answer the empty list. Theirs: go-sdk, not filed (the witness:
tests/lookup_freeform_precedence_815.rs; tests/vectors/lookup_freeform_precedence_815.json).

### Fixed: the default mode reads the transaction version unsigned, as the reference does; a word keeps the node's `int32_t` (#418)

From the #397 re-review's observation (2026-10-28). `Spend`'s default mode
(no word) compared the `i32` it holds, so a version whose four bytes are at or
above 2^31 (`0x80000000`, `0xFFFFFFFF`) read as negative and every version
rule judged it strict: MINIMALDATA, LOW_S, CLEANSTACK and NULLDUMMY enforced,
the Chronicle hash type refused in the DER wrapper's words. The reference
reads the version with `readUInt32LE` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/transaction/Transaction.ts:471`, passed as
`transactionVersion: tx.version` at `:1446`), and its default
`#isRelaxed()` is `transactionVersion > 1` (`Spend.ts:319-321`; the Chronicle
hash type's `#isAfterChronicle()` the same without flags, `:338-341`,
`:586-591`): 2147483648 and 4294967295 are relaxed there. The default mode now
reads the bits as `u32` through one crate-private helper,
`relaxed_by_default` (`src/script/spend/hash_type.rs`), at its four sites:
the four rules and the coin-era switch at `Spend::new`
(`src/script/spend/mod.rs`), the Chronicle hash-type gate (`hash_type.rs`)
and #417's version-1 wrapper (`signature_encoding.rs`). Under a word nothing
moves: the gates read the node's `int32_t` (`ScriptFlags::gates`,
`src/script/flags.rs`), so those versions stay strict under a Chronicle word,
as at the node and in go-sdk. `OP_VER` and `OP_VERIF` write the four bytes in
every mode, unchanged.

`tests/script_transaction_version_sign_418.rs` (nine tests) against
`tests/vectors/script_transaction_version_sign_418.json`, recorded from the
unmodified reference under Node v22.18.0 by
`tests/support/script_transaction_version_sign_418.mjs`: versions 1, 2,
`0x7FFFFFFF`, `0x80000000`, `0xFFFFFFFF` with and without the reference's
explicit flags (the names of `ScriptFlags::standard(PostChronicle)`), six
rules each (a non-minimal push, two items left, a non-empty CHECKMULTISIG
dummy, a high-S signature, an `ALL|FORKID|CHRONICLE` signature, `OP_VER`'s
bytes), and `Transaction.fromHex`'s unsigned read of `00000080` and
`ffffffff`. The default mode equals every recorded verdict, word and stack;
under `ScriptFlags::standard` and `ScriptFlags::block` (post-Chronicle) the
versions at or above 2^31 give the version-1 verdicts and words, 2 and
`0x7FFFFFFF` relaxed; a transaction at `0x80000000` built, written, read back
and verified through `Transaction::verify` beside the direct `Spend`.
`a_version_at_or_above_2_31_is_relaxed_in_the_default_mode_as_the_reference_reads_it_418`
and the `Transaction::verify` test RED on `7a047467`
(`This data is not minimally-encoded. (PC: 0)` at `0x80000000`; `The
signature format is invalid.` through `verify`); the word pin
(`a_version_at_or_above_2_31_is_strict_under_a_word_as_the_node_reads_int32_418`)
and the three agreement tests green there.

The fold (the strength read of 2026-11-09): three pins of behaviour the tip
already had, recorded apart in the vector's `fold_cases` (24 cells, the 60 of
`cases` unchanged; the recorder's two runs byte-identical under Node v22.18.0).
`a_version_of_0_is_strict_in_every_mode_as_at_1_418`: the six rules at version
0, the default mode equal to the recording, a word giving the version-1
verdicts (`OP_VER` its own falsy push). `an_undefined_hash_type_at_or_above_2_31_is_refused_in_the_version_2_words_418`:
a scope-0x44 signature in the default mode refused in the reference's DER
wrapper at 0 and 1 and in #23's sentence, `The signature's hash type (0x44)
has no defined base type.`, at 2, `0x7FFFFFFF`, `0x80000000` and `0xFFFFFFFF`
(the reference's wrapper at every version: #417's stated row, the same above
2^31 as at 2). `a_non_push_only_unlocking_script_at_or_above_2_31_is_refused_under_a_word_418`:
`OP_1 OP_DROP` before `OP_1` under the post-Chronicle mempool word refused at
0, 1, `0x80000000` and `0xFFFFFFFF` (`ScriptFlags::requires_push_only` on the
`int32_t`), run at 2 and `0x7FFFFFFF`, the reference's flags relaxing at and
above 2^31 (this entry's parity note). Each RED on a scratch copy of the tip
with one line planted: `relaxed_by_default`'s `> 1` as `!= 1` (2 of 9),
`signature_encoding.rs`'s arm back to the signed `transaction_version <= 1`
(1 of 9), `requires_push_only`'s `tx_version as u32 <= 1` (1 of 9).

Behaviour: in the default mode a spend of a transaction whose version is at
or above 2^31 moves from strict to relaxed (a refusal under the four rules or
a version-1 Chronicle hash-type refusal becomes the version-2 verdict). Under
a word, no verdict moves. No public type changes (`SpendParams::transaction_version`
stays `i32`, its bits the wire's four bytes; `Transaction::version` stays
`u32`); no migration. The same reading reaches the streaming reader's default
mode (`src/transaction/beef_stream/spends.rs:246`, the version's bits cast to the
`i32` as `src/transaction/verify.rs:365` casts them, both into
`Spend::with_transaction`), and a caller handing `Spend` a negative
`transaction_version` directly (`-1`) is now relaxed as `0xFFFFFFFF`, where the
reference's `new Spend({ transactionVersion: -1 })` is strict: the parameter
holds the wire's bits, not a signed number.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#418)

The default mode is the reference's (`Spend.ts:319-321` on `readUInt32LE`'s

The reference's explicit flags apply the same `transactionVersion > 1` to the

### Fixed: an attribute question keeps only the certificates matching it, as the reference wallet does (#751)

`IdentityClient::query` sent `attributes` to `ls_identity` and checked none
of them on the certificates it read, and `resolve_by_attributes` kept every
certificate the parser admitted, so a host could answer an attribute question
with any certificate (the injection class #746 closed for the subject, the
type and the certifier). The reference wallet re-binds the answer to the
question it asked: `discoverByAttributes` filters through
`filterCertificatesByAttributes` before its trust step and its page
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/Wallet.ts:1069-1082`;
the matcher `packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/utility/identityUtils.ts:140-293`).
The matcher is ported function for function (`src/identity/client_attributes.rs`)
over each certificate's decrypted fields (the anyone wallet's): `userName`
equal to the asked value after `normalizeIdentitySearch` (`:141`, `:214-215`),
every other named field by `identityFuzzyMatches` (`:145-162`: the tokens in
order on one line, each a literal under JavaScript's `gi` without `u`, its
`Canonicalize` written out), `any` across every string field but
`profilePhoto` and `icon` (`:229-244`: two UTF-16 units fuzzily, three or more
by `identityTextMatches`, `:166-223`: NFD, `\p{Mn}` removed, lower case, the
English stop words, `-term`, a quoted phrase; the fields joined in the order a
JavaScript object walks them, array-index names ahead), the other names unread
beside `any` (`:275`), and nothing kept when no attribute is usable
(`:257-265`, `:291`). It runs at `query` when `attributes` is set and at
`resolve_by_attributes` over the map sent, so that door's lone attribute is
judged by the `any` rule, the search the overlay ran. A certificate whose
revealed field does not decrypt carries no field and matches nothing.

Pinned by `tests/vectors/identity_attributes_751.json` (42 cases, recorded by
`tests/support/identity_attributes_751.mjs` from the exported
`filterCertificatesByAttributes` under Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical),
judged case for case by the unit module
`src/identity/client_attributes_751_tests.rs`, and by
`tests/identity_query_attributes_751.rs`: a host answering with another
certificate not believed at `query` nor at `resolve_by_attributes`, the asked
one kept, an undecryptable one dropped, nothing usable keeping nothing, a type
beside attributes filtering by both. 5 of 6 RED on `545eb36f` (every
certificate kept; the no-attributes control green); the unit module
compile-RED there (the matcher absent). Two older pins read their certificates
through `resolve_by_attributes` with values the certificate does not carry:
`src/identity/client_field_value_261_tests.rs` asks the certificate's own
email (`alice@example.com`, where it asked `x`), and
`tests/identity_certificate_record_553.rs` reads through `query` with no
filter, the same parser (its `fields_at_bound` certificate carries no
`alice`).

Migration: an attribute question through `query` or `resolve_by_attributes`
now returns only the certificates whose decrypted fields match it; code that
read every certificate a host answered reads fewer. No public type or
signature changes.

### Added: an `IdentityQuery` the overlay would refuse is refused locally in the overlay's words, never sent (#756)

The reference overlay's identity lookup service refuses the whole question for
a `limit` outside 1 to 100, an `offset` above 100000, an `identityKey` or a
`certifiers` entry that is no compressed key, a type that is not base64 of 32
bytes, an `attributes` map of 0 or more than 32 fields, an unsafe name or a
value over 500 bytes (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/overlays/topics/src/identity/IdentityLookupService.ts:83-123`; the
words `packages/overlays/topics/src/shared/queryValidation.ts:9,58,72,126,174-178,188,247-256`).
`IdentityClient::query` sent such a question, and `LookupResolver::query`
read the overlay's refusal as an empty answer and charged the host's
reputation for the caller's input. `query` now checks what it would send
before the network, in the overlay's order (`limit`, `offset`, `identityKey`,
a set certifier as `certifiers[0]`, a set type as `certificateTypes[0]`,
then `attributes`: the count, then per entry the name and the value, the
entries in the order the overlay walks them, `Object.entries` of the text
`query` sends: array-index names ahead, ascending, then the rest as
inserted), and refuses
with `Error::IdentityError` carrying the overlay's whole message (`Invalid
lookup query: limit must be an integer from 1 to 100`, `... identityKey must
contain 1-66 UTF-8 bytes`, `... certifiers[0] must be a non-empty bounded
string`, `... certifiers[0] must be a compressed public key`, `... must be a
valid compressed public key`, `... certificateTypes[0] must be a non-empty
bounded string` (empty or past 44 bytes), `... certificateTypes[0] must be a
32-byte base64 value` (`IdentityLookupService.ts:97-100`,
`queryValidation.ts:183-190`: `validateBase64String` of 32 bytes, trimmed,
padding required, read by the port of it `publicly_reveal_attributes` already
uses), `... attributes must contain 1-32 fields`, `... attribute names must
be safe MongoDB field segments of at most 50 UTF-8 bytes`, `... attribute
values must be strings of at most 500 UTF-8 bytes`); the key's point is read
by `PublicKey::from_hex`, the reference's `PublicKey.fromString` reading
(#498: an upper-case key and `02`+(p+1) admitted, an x of no point refused).
`src/identity/query_bounds.rs`; the bounds named on `IdentityQuery`'s fields,
`with_limit`, `with_offset` and `query`. One older pin of this crate's own
follows the row (the captain's ruling of 2026-11-09): the last assertion of
`a_query_by_type_keeps_only_the_asked_types_certificates_746`
(`tests/identity_query_filters_746.rs`), which asked `query` with the
unpadded type and read an empty list, now reads the refusal in the overlay's
words; its assertions on a well-formed type are unchanged. No vector moved.

The rule read's fold: `query` sent its attributes as a `serde_json::Value`
writes them, sorted by bytes, while the check walked them as inserted, so a
question with two attribute faults was named here by one and refused by the
overlay by the other (`[email: 501 bytes, a.b]`: the value here, the name
there). `query` now sends the attributes in insertion order, as
`resolve_by_attributes` has since #394 (`LookupResolver::query_ordered`; the
question's other members keep their sorted bytes), and the check walks them in
JavaScript's order over that text (`client_attributes::js_order`), so the
recorder's question is the one sent and judged. Pinned by the recorded
`two_faults_index_value_then_name` (`a.b`, then `7` with a 501-byte value: the
overlay holds `7` ahead and names the value; RED on a pre-squash commit of `4e57b23f`, the name named)
and `query_sends_its_attributes_in_insertion_order_751` in
`tests/identity_lookup_attribute_order_394.rs` (RED on a pre-squash commit of `4e57b23f`,
`{"alpha":"a","zeta":"z"}`).
Stated, the scoped cold re-read: an array-index name is written where it was
inserted, where the reference wallet's `JSON.stringify` writes it ahead
(`stringifyBRC100`, `LookupResolver.ts:787,797` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`)
(`{"7":..,"a.b":..}` there, `{"a.b":..,"7":..}` here, Node v22.18.0); the
overlay's `JSON.parse` holds it ahead either way, so the walk and the verdict
are the same and only the bytes differ (#385's integer-like residue).

Pinned by `tests/vectors/identity_query_bounds_756.json` (68 questions,
recorded by `tests/support/identity_query_bounds_756.mjs` from
`IdentityLookupService.lookup` over a stub storage manager, Node v22.18.0, two
runs byte-identical) through `tests/identity_query_bounds_756.rs`: each
refused question refused in the recorded message with nothing sent on #752's
recording facilitator, each admitted edge sent (limit 1 and 100, offset
100000, 32 attributes, a 50-byte name, a 500-byte value), two faults at once
named in the overlay's order (a type fault named before an attribute fault),
the type beside attributes sent with both. 6 of 9 RED on `545eb36f` before the
type check (every question sent; the case count, the type-beside-attributes
pin and the type group, then held back, green); with the type check, the type
group and the type-then-attributes fault RED on a pre-squash commit of `4e57b23f` (each type case
`Ok([]), 1 sent`; the pair named in the attributes' words), and #746's moved
assertion RED there (`unwrap_err()` on `Ok([])`).

Migration: a question outside these bounds is an `Err` where it was an empty
list (`Ok(vec![])`) after a network round trip.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#751)

Two rows. #751 is parity: the matcher is the reference wallet's at both doors
that send attributes. Kept and stated, not changed: `resolve_by_attributes`
rewrites a lone attribute to `any` (pinned by
`tests/identity_lookup_attribute_order_394.rs`; the reference's SDK client
sends its caller's `args` as given, `IdentityClient.ts:614`); `limit` and
`offset` go to the overlay before the local filter, so a host padding its

(the reference's either, `identityUtils.ts:190-194`). The case tables are

its page are not ported at the attribute doors (#737's record). The keeper's

answer. #756 is hardening, not parity: the reference's SDK client validates

(`identity/client.go:258-273`) and filters nothing in the client.

### Fixed: the lookup response bounded at 32 MiB and an output list at 4096 on both paths, neutral for host reputation; the discovered hosts in the trackers' order within the reference's bounds (#775, #785)

From the rule read of PR #774 (#775) and the rule and strength reads of PR
#783 (#785).

**The bounds (#775).** `HttpsOverlayLookupFacilitator` read a lookup response
with reqwest's `.json()` and `.bytes()`, unbounded, and neither path counted an
answer's outputs: an allocation a hostile host chose (on wasm32 a failed
allocation is an abort, rule 5), and a 4,097-output answer was its host's
success. The reference bounds both (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/LookupResources.ts:16-27`,
`DEFAULT_LOOKUP_LIMITS`):

| Limit | Default | Where the reference applies it | Here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxResponseBytes` | 32 MiB | the body as read (`LookupResponseReader.ts:150-214`: a declared length before the read, then chunk by chunk), the binary path's extracted outputs (`LookupResolver.ts:929-932`), a returned answer's BEEF and context bytes (`:2351-2364`) | `LookupLimits::max_response_bytes` |
| `maxOutputs` | 4096 | the JSON answer (`:859-860`), the binary outpoint count (`:877-883`), a returned answer (`:2366-2375`) | `LookupLimits::max_outputs` |
| `maxTotalBytes` | 64 MiB | a query's hosts together (`:1624-1631`, retained `:1734-1743`), a discovery's trackers together (`LookupDiscovery.ts:21-29`) | `LookupLimits::max_total_bytes` |
| `maxHosts` | 256 | the discovered list (`:2006-2009`), a query's admission (`:1842-1849`) | `LookupLimits::max_hosts` |
| `maxHostsPerTracker` | 64 | a tracker's share (`LookupDiscovery.ts:62-78,105-108`) | `LookupLimits::max_hosts_per_tracker` |

A limit reached is the new `Error::OverlayResourceLimit(<limit>)`, the
reference's `LookupResourceLimitError` in its words, `Lookup resource limit
reached: maxResponseBytes` (`LookupResources.ts:29-34`), and is neutral for
host reputation on the host path and the tracker path: the resolver records
neither a success nor a failure (`LookupResolver.ts:2415`, the tracked call
rethrowing it before `recordFailure`; `:1764-1767`). The facilitator reads the
body with `Response::chunk` under the bound (a `Content-Length` past it refused
before any read; a body with no length stopped at the chunk that passes it),
charges each chunk to the request's budget, and counts the outputs at the
parse. The resolver hands each request its limits through the new provided
trait method `OverlayLookupFacilitator::lookup_bounded` (the reference's
`options?: LookupRequestOptions`, `:740-746`), whose default ignores them and
calls `lookup_ordered`, and checks every returned answer itself, so a custom
facilitator is bounded too, after its answer is in memory.

**The order (#785).** `find_competent_hosts` gathered the advertised hosts
into a `HashSet` and returned its order, unbounded, so the hosts asked and
cached differed from run to run. It now takes the trackers as they answer,
each answer's hosts in its own order, deduplicated and cut to the tracker's
share (the lesser of `maxHostsPerTracker` and `maxHosts` divided by the
trackers asked), the whole deduplicated by earliest occurrence and cut to
`maxHosts`; the cache holds that list and `query` admits the discovered (or
overriding) hosts and then the additional ones the same way.

Additions (semver, rule 9): `overlay::{LookupLimits, LookupRequestOptions,
LookupByteBudget}` and the five `DEFAULT_LOOKUP_MAX_*` constants,

### Added: `AbortAcceptance` carries a `kind`, so a host tells the abort-on-chain refusal by type, not text (#604)

From bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs #528, the owner's word of 2026-11-01 14:4xZ (a
field on the existing payload, not a new `Error` variant). Until now a host
that wanted to tell "the transaction is already on chain" from the other
abort refusals (the store's accepting word, toolbox #165; the status guard)
matched `AbortAcceptance::message` (bsv-wallet-cli#386). `AbortAcceptance`
now carries `pub kind: AbortKind`, a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum
(`src/error/wallet_fault.rs`, re-exported at `bsv_rs::error::AbortKind` and
`bsv_rs::AbortKind`): `OnChain` (the transaction mined or known to the chain,
the toolbox reference's predicate), `AcceptedInStore` (the store's accepting
word refused the abort) and `Other` (every other guard refusal). The default,
and the value `AbortAcceptance::new` leaves, is `Other`: an unset record
claims no fact its guard did not set. The kind is set by the guard that
knows it, never derived from text. The wire class and code, the `Display`
text, `class` and `size_of::<Error>()` (56) are unchanged.

Pinned by `tests/abort_kind_604.rs` (four tests: the default, a mined
transaction told by kind with its text unchanged, every kind's abort frame
equal to `Other`'s and to the `WalletRefusal` of the same class and message
under `InvalidOperation` and `InvalidParameter`, the kind in equality and the
size); compile-RED on `e228c61a` (`AbortKind` and the field absent).

Semver: additive within 0.9. A new public field on a `#[non_exhaustive]`
struct (no literal outside the crate can build it) and a new public enum. A
downstream reading the record needs nothing; the toolbox's abort door sets
`kind` at its two refusal sites (`OnChain` at the on-chain guard,
`AcceptedInStore` at the accepting-word guard) by assignment after `new()`.
The record's derived `Debug` text gains `kind: ..`; no test here matches it.

The record's meaning, aligned at every site by the fold of the three reads
(2026-11-09): its presence affirms that an abort guard refused the abort
(stored acceptance, the chain or another guard), `kind` naming which; until
#604 the docs said it affirmed stored acceptance alone. The wording moved in
`src/error/wallet_fault.rs`, `src/error.rs` and the root, `src/wallet/` and
`src/wallet/wire/` `CLAUDE.md`; no behaviour moved.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#604)

The reference has no acceptance record and no kind: its `WalletError` is a
string and a code (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/wallet/WalletError.ts:7,79`), and its toolbox's on-chain
refusal is not a throw but `{ aborted: false }`
(`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/storage/StorageProvider.ts:878,889,927-932`:
`chainStatus === 'mined' || chainStatus === 'known'`, the predicate
`AbortKind::OnChain`'s doc follows, asked there only of a `nosend` action
with a txid and no expiry state, `:870`); that `{ aborted: false }` answer is
framed by this crate's processor as code 8 (#206), while an
`Error::AbortAccepted` record is framed by its class as the `WalletRefusal`
of that class and message, whatever its kind (`OnChain` under
`InvalidOperation` as code 1). go-sdk@2ca481c has no acceptance record. The record and its kind
stay in Rust; no byte on the wire moves. A port extension like #439's, not a
divergence.

### Fixed: a lying host's copy of a lookup output no longer shadows an honest host's at the resolver's merge (#796)

`LookupResolver::query` deduplicates the outputs of every host's answer by
the BEEF subject's txid and the output index, walking the answers in the
hosts' rank order and keeping the earlier copy of a key. Since #735 an
output carries its host's `txid` hint, and the owner's word on #735
(2026-11-04 13:5xZ) keeps a disagreeing hint carried and counted, never
refused. Until #796 the merge never read the hint: a lying host ranked ahead
of an honest one had its copy kept, its lying hint and its own `context`
included, and the honest copy discarded as the duplicate, where the
reference drops the lying copy and returns the honest one.

The merge now compares each output's hint with its subject's txid, ASCII
lower-cased, as the reference's `resolveTxIdForOutput` does
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/LookupResolver.ts:2229`,
`:2235`). A disagreeing output is counted, every one received, kept or not.
On a key already held, an agreeing (or hintless) copy displaces a held
disagreeing one and stands where it arrived; otherwise the earlier copy
stays, as `:1107`. The reference drops the lying copy and keys the agreeing
one on arrival (`:1104-1112`), so this crate's answer less its kept lying
outputs is the reference's copies, and its order too while the hosts answer
in their rank order: this crate merges the answers in rank order once every
host has answered (`futures::future::join_all`), the reference each answer
as it completes (`recordLookupHostAnswer`, `:1501-1502`, into
`recordOutputAnswer`, `:1065-1072`), so where the honest host answers before
a liar ranked ahead of it the reference answers `[A honest, B]` for the
vector's `replaced_keeps_place` and this crate `[B, A honest]` (the cold
read's probe: the recorder with the host ranked ahead delayed 50 ms). The
copies agree in every completion order; the order of outputs from different
hosts is the reference's completion order and this crate's rank order, older
than #796 and a row of its own. Where every copy of a key
disagrees, the reference returns none and this crate the earliest, hint as
given (the parity note below). The host's reputation is not touched, as the
reference's merge touches none (`mergeAnswer`, `:1101-1115`; the success
recorded for any output list at `:2395-2397`).

Additive: `LookupResolver::txid_hint_contradictions(&self) -> u64`, the
twin of `IdentityClient::txid_hint_contradictions`. The two counters are
separate: an identity lookup that keeps a lying output counts it at the
merge and again at the evidence check. A lying copy the merge displaces for
an agreeing one never reaches the evidence check, so it is counted by the
resolver alone: on an identity lookup answered liar then honest
`IdentityClient::txid_hint_contradictions` reads 0, where it read 1 before
#796, and `LookupResolver::txid_hint_contradictions` reads 1; a caller that
watches the identity count alone reads 0 for a displaced liar, and reads
the resolver's count beside it to see one (#818,
`tests/identity_hint_displaced_818.rs`).

Pinned by `tests/lookup_hint_merge_796.rs` against
`tests/vectors/lookup_hint_merge_796.json` (recorded by
`tests/support/lookup_hint_merge_796.mjs` under Node v22.18.0, the
reference's own `LookupResolver.query` with a scripted facilitator; two
runs byte-identical; the BEEFs this crate's writer's): ten shapes, the
reference's answer on eight, the lone liar and the two liars stated. On the
base `545eb36f` (the count's assertions held aside) 4 of the 8 tests then
written RED:
`a_lying_hint_ahead_of_an_honest_copy_does_not_shadow_it_796`,
`an_agreeing_copy_displaces_a_liar_and_stands_where_it_arrived_796`,
`an_agreeing_hint_in_upper_case_and_an_absent_hint_are_no_contradiction_796`
and `every_shape_is_the_references_answer_save_the_stated_796`; the same 4
on the tip with the displacement removed, and 2 (the place and the shapes)
with the agreeing copy written into the liar's slot. The reads' fold
recorded four more shapes, each pinning a stated rule against a one-line
mutation of the merge, every one RED on a copy of the tip: `honest_honest`
(two agreeing copies, the earlier kept by both; a later agreeing copy
replacing an earlier one turns
`an_earlier_agreeing_copy_stays_against_a_later_one_796` RED),
`liar_liar` (two different lies, a stated cell: the earliest kept here and
both counted, nothing there; the latest liar kept turns
`two_lying_copies_keep_the_earliest_and_count_both_796` RED),
`liar_honest_honest` (one displacement per key, the earlier agreeing copy
standing; a second displacement turns
`a_key_is_displaced_once_the_earlier_agreeing_copy_standing_796` RED) and
`liar_liar_honest` (the agreeing copy displaces the held liar, both lies
counted; a lying copy after the first left uncounted turns
`an_agreeing_copy_displaces_the_held_liar_after_two_lies_796` RED, `left: 1`,
`right: 2`).

The brief's residue, a binary aggregated answer whose every output carried
the whole BEEF so that outputs of other transactions keyed to one subject,
is closed already by #735's fold (`facilitators/binary_answer.rs`: each
output the Atomic BEEF of its own outpoint's txid, that txid its hint). A
JSON host serving one BEEF of several transactions for outputs of a
transaction other than its subject is judged by the subject on both sides
(`Transaction.fromBEEF(output.beef)`, `:2233`): an honest hint naming the
other transaction disagrees there and here, dropped there, kept and counted
here, the stated cell below.

### Fixed: the SHIP discovery admits a host as the reference does: the answer and BEEF bounds, the txid hint, 1 satoshi, the endpoint's origin, 32 hosts (#804)

`TopicBroadcaster::find_interested_hosts` parsed every output of the
`ls_ship` answer, took the output at its index, authenticated the
advertisement (since #544, the reference's `SHIPBroadcaster.ts:775`, the one
rule ported before) and matched the topic, keying the host by the token's
domain text; a non-output-list answer was no hosts. The reference's
`#fetchInterestedHosts` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/SHIPBroadcaster.ts:725-789`) reads more:
an answer that is no output list or carries more than 256 outputs throws
`SHIP answer is not a bounded output list.` before any output is read
(`:737-744`); an output whose BEEF is empty or over 16 MiB or whose `txid`
hint is not 64 hex digits is skipped before it counts (`:752-764`); the
BEEF lengths are summed and past 64 MiB the output is refused (`:765-768`);
a hint that, lower-cased, is not the BEEF subject's txid skips it (`:771`),
as does a selected output of other than exactly 1 satoshi (`:773`); the host
is `shipEndpoint(domain, false).origin` (`:779`, `:103-127`), and the loop
stops at 32 hosts (`:782`). So a host advertised at 0 or 2 satoshis, under
another transaction's hint, by an `https+bsvauth://` or `wss://` URI, or as
the 33rd was asked here and never there, and one host written two ways
(`https://Host.example:443/`, `https://host.example`) was two. The
discovery now reads in the reference's order (`src/overlay/topic_broadcaster/discovery.rs`,
the four bounds crate-private constants named as the reference's); a
refused answer is `ERR_HOST_DISCOVERY` at `broadcast_tx`, this crate's form
of the rejected promise.

Two readings the reference's code makes and this port keeps: (a) the throw
at `:767` is inside the per-output `try` (`:747`) and swallowed at `:783`,
so the output that crosses 64 MiB is skipped and, the total staying over,
every later one; the hosts admitted before stay and the discovery returns
normally. (b) `shipEndpoint` refuses every advertisement URI but plain
`https://` without a query, so an advertisement the token admits under the
`https+...` family, `wss://`, `js8c+bsvauth+smf:` or an `https://` with a
query is skipped; the key is the WHATWG origin (the host lower-cased, a
default port dropped, no trailing slash).

`TopicBroadcaster::new` takes `require_ack_from_specific_hosts` as the
reference's constructor snapshots it (`:195-219`): more than 32 entries
refused in `Specific-host acknowledgment requirements contain too many
hosts.`, each key held as `shipEndpoint(key, allowHTTP).origin` (`http:`
allowed under `NetworkPreset::Local` alone, `:426`), refused in its words
when it is no such URL, and a second key of one origin refused in
`Specific-host acknowledgment requirements contain a duplicate host.`, so a
key matches the origin the discovery admits.

Pinned by `tests/overlay_ship_discovery_804.rs` (15 tests, the answer
through a real `LookupResolver` on an `.invalid` host override and a
scripted facilitator, the advertisements this crate's writer's): 0 and 2
satoshis, a disagreeing, a 63-digit and a non-hex hint, `https+bsvauth://`,
`wss://` and a query admit nothing; an upper-case agreeing hint admits;
`https://Host.ship-discovery-804.invalid:443/` is admitted as
`https://host.ship-discovery-804.invalid`; 33 hosts admit the leading 32;
257 outputs and a freeform answer refuse; an advertisement, four 16 MiB
BEEFs, an advertisement admit the leading one alone; a 16 MiB plus 1 BEEF
is skipped before it counts; a specific-host key with a trailing slash or
upper case and `:443` matches its discovered origin, 33 keys and two of one
origin refuse `new`; and the reference's 17 discovery and 8 constructor
verdicts of `tests/vectors/ship_discovery_admission_804.json` (recorded by
`tests/support/ship_discovery_admission_804.mjs`: the reference's own
`TopicBroadcaster` on a stub resolver and a recording facilitator, its
advertisements by its `OverlayAdminTokenTemplate`, Node v22.18.0) are this
crate's. 13 of 15 RED on a scratch copy of `167c56ae` (beta, the PR's base)
with the tests and vector overlaid; the upper-case agreeing hint and the 16 MiB plus 1 pin green
on both.

Migration: `TopicBroadcaster::new`'s signature is unchanged, but a
`require_ack_from_specific_hosts` key that is no `https:` origin (an
`http:` key outside the local preset, a bare host name, a path or a query)
is refused at construction where it went unmatched at broadcast; write the
host's URL (`https://host.example`), and keep at most 32. A host advertised
at a value other than 1 satoshi, under a mismatched hint, or by a URI other
than plain `https://` is no longer discovered; the reference's advertisers
write 1 satoshi and an `https://` origin. Two codes move with it (#815, the
strength read of PR #813): an `ls_ship` answer that is no output list is
`ERR_HOST_DISCOVERY` where it was `ERR_NO_HOSTS_INTERESTED`, and hosts
advertised only as `https+...`, `wss://` or with a query give
`ERR_NO_HOSTS_INTERESTED` where they gave `ERR_ALL_HOSTS_REJECTED`.

Ours: the reference's discovery and constructor at the pin, the residues

types', the resolver dropping a BEEF that does not parse before the count

host cap and keying a host by the domain's text (`:290-293`); not filed.

### Fixed: the atomic writer writes a raw entry whose index names no matching BUMP with no BUMP and stops the walk at it, as the reference does (#798)

From PR #797's rule and strength reads of `lane/fix-766`.
`Beef::to_binary_atomic`'s closure (`atomic_closure`,
`src/transaction/beef.rs`) gave a raw entry whose BUMP index, set by hand
(`find_txid_mut` and `set_bump_index`, `tx_mut`), names a BUMP that does not
hold its txid that BUMP and that index, so the BEEF written failed this
crate's own readers with `TxidNotInBump`; an index past the BUMPs was an
`Err` (`<txid> names BUMP 5 of 1`); and the walk descended such an entry,
writing its ancestors and their BUMPs. The reference's `bumpIndex` setter
empties an entry's `inputTxids` whenever it carries an index
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/transaction/BeefTx.ts:90-92`,
`:219-221`), so its walk (`Beef.ts:427-431`) descends no entry with an index,
matching or not; `#copySelectedTransactions` builds its BUMP map from the
included entries `#hasMatchingBump` proves alone (`:453-456`, `:436-446`) and
maps every entry's index through it (`:462`), the copy keeping the source's
`inputTxids` (`:465`). Now the walk stops at a txid-only entry and at any
entry with an index; the BUMPs are those of the included entries a BUMP of
this BEEF proves, in entry order; each entry's index is mapped through them,
dropped where they do not hold it, kept (renumbered) where another included
entry's matching BUMP is the one it names; the copy keeps the source's
`input_txids`. #766's txid-only bytes stay; the readers' graph rule,
`from_atomic_beef` and `to_binary` do not move.

`tests/beef_bump_index_757.rs` on four cases the #757 recorder now writes
(`support/beef_bump_index_757.mjs`, `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0;
two transactions added, `uncle` and `join`):
`a_raw_entry_whose_index_names_no_matching_bump_is_written_without_a_bump_798`
(`raw_naming_a_bump_without_its_txid_with_child`: the reference writes
`...0200beef0002000100...`, the parent as format `00`, where this crate wrote
the grandchild's BUMP and `01 00`; `raw_naming_no_bump_with_child`: the same
bytes, where this crate erred), `the_atomic_walk_stops_at_an_entry_carrying_an_index_798`
(`raw_child_naming_a_bump_without_its_txid`: the grandchild's atomic BEEF
carries the child as format `00` and no parent, where this crate reached the
parent and carried BUMP 0), both RED on `e228c61a`;
`a_raw_entry_sharing_a_matching_entrys_bump_keeps_the_mapped_index_798`
(`raw_sharing_a_matching_entrys_bump`: the uncle keeps index `0`, the parent's
BUMP), green on both, the guard against dropping too much; and
`a_stub_read_from_bytes_written_atomic_is_refused_as_stub_not_proven_798`, an
agreement pin (a stub read by `Beef::from_binary` carries no index, written
atomic with no BUMP, refused `StubNotProven` by `verify_stream_structure` and

unchanged.

The fold (PR #809's three reads): the copy follows both of the reference's
branches (`#copySelectedTransactions`, `Beef.ts:464-467`): an entry held raw
keeps the source's `input_txids` (`:465`), one held as a transaction alone,

`a_transaction_entry_naming_no_bump_is_copied_with_its_inputs_rescanned_798`

(the same merged entries after `toHex`: the reference's parent, uncle, join;

The second fold (PR #809's re-reads of a pre-squash commit of `b91c487d`): `to_binary_atomic` no

(`BeefTx.ts:160-169`) and copies it through the raw branch with the inputs
its index emptied (`Beef.ts:465`); `tx_mut` drops the bytes here, and the copy
re-scanned them. Two cases the recorder adds (a `mut:<tx>=<lockTime>` step,

`a_raw_entry_mutated_through_tx_mut_is_copied_through_the_raw_branch_798`
(BUMP `alone_800000`, `raw:parent`, `raw:uncle`, `index:uncle=5`,
`mut:uncle=1`, `raw:join_mut`: parent, uncle, join; RED on a pre-squash commit of `b91c487d`
and on a pre-squash commit of `b91c487d` with the sort removed alone, uncle, join, parent) and
`an_index_read_from_bytes_naming_no_matching_bump_is_written_atomic_as_the_reference_798`
(green on a pre-squash commit of `b91c487d`; RED on its tests over `b9d048e7`'s `beef.rs`,
`names BUMP 1 of 1`). The test helper takes a case's atomic BEEFs before
`to_hex` where the recording did (`atomic_before_hex`).

Semver: no public shape changes. Migration: the streaming reader and
`verify_structure` refuse both shapes (`beef_stream.rs:2068-2077`), but
`Beef::from_binary` collects an entry's index unjudged, as the reference's

(`tests/vectors/beef_of_any_size/bad_index.bin`, an `Err` until #798, and
`not_in_bump.bin`, its BUMP kept until #798, now written as the reference's
`toBinaryAtomic` writes them at the pin; #809's cold re-read).
`to_binary_atomic` no longer errs on an out-of-range index, and an
entry whose index names no BUMP holding its txid is written as an
unproven raw entry with its ancestors not written: give it the index of the
BUMP that proves it, or clear the index, before writing. The same state is
reached without `set_bump_index` by an index the caller passes unchecked
(`merge_raw_tx(raw, Some(n))`, `BeefTx::from_raw_tx` and `from_tx` with
`Some(n)`: `try_to_validate_bump_index` leaves a given index as it is) and by
an edit of the public `bumps` under an entry's index; an index taken from
`merge_bump`'s return for the BUMP that holds the txid is unaffected. A
txid-only entry whose hand-set index names a BUMP another included entry is
proven by now keeps the mapped index in memory too (its bytes carry none;
the sort places it with the proven entries, as the reference's does), the one
txid-only shape whose entry order can move from #766's; by reading, no
recording.

Behaviour change, no hand-set index needed (the fold's removal of the
subject-last move; by reading, no recording): an atomic BEEF of a PARTIAL
closure changes its entry order. When the subject, or an unproven ancestor
it rests on, spends a txid this `Beef` does not hold
(`Transaction::to_atomic_beef(true)` with a source missing; a `Beef` read
from an input BEEF that lacks a parent, the subject merged and
`to_binary_atomic` called, as a wallet builds `signableTransaction.tx`), the
sort leaves those entries ahead of the txid-only and proven ones
(`sort_txs`: missing inputs, not valid, txid-only, proven, linked), so a
subject with a missing source and one proven parent is now written subject,
parent, where it was written parent, subject since 0.8.1. A closure whose
every input is held or proven is written as before, the subject last. No
reader on record judges that order: each finds the subject by the atomic
header's txid (this crate's `from_atomic_beef` at every release since 0.4.5,
`Transaction.fromAtomicBEEF` in `@bsv/sdk` 2 and 3, go-sdk's
`NewBeefFromAtomicBytes`), and each verifying reader refuses a missing input
in either order (`InputNamesNoElement` here, at 0.8.0 and earlier too).
Migration: a consumer that takes the last entry of an atomic BEEF as its
subject must read the header's txid (`Beef::atomic_txid`) in its place. The
reference's `Beef.toBinaryAtomic` writes the same order (`Beef.ts:385-389`,
`:1390`); its `Transaction.toAtomicBEEF` does not pass through it (a V1 BEEF
in collection order, the subject last, `Transaction.ts:1787-1789,1978-1983`),
where this crate's `to_atomic_beef` writes V2 through the closure: older
than #798, a row for the captain.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#798)

The reference's bytes at the pin, the root `CLAUDE.md` row closed. The
reference's own shape is kept where it gives a BEEF the readers refuse: an
entry whose index names a BUMP another included entry is proven by keeps the

One order differs, stated by the fold of PR #809: the reference's `toHex`
(and every other serialization of an entry, `BeefTx.getRawTxBytes`) fills the
entry's `_rawTx`, so an entry held as a `Transaction` and serialized once is

branch there depends on its serialization cache; this crate's does not. An
entry held raw and mutated through `tx_mut` is not this case: it copies
through the raw branch on both sides since the second fold. Ours: the copy by the entry's held form alone (the witness:
`a_transaction_entry_after_to_hex_keeps_the_never_serialized_order_stated_798`,
the recorded `transaction_uncle_naming_no_bump_after_to_hex`).
