### Fixed: an offset-0 proof under 100 blocks deep is refused by `Transaction::verify`, as the reference does (#734)

From the #730 lane's recording (2026-11-04 02:1xZ), the keeper's word of
02:2xZ: follow the reference where the verify door is this crate's. The
reference's `MerklePath.verify` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/transaction/MerklePath.ts:476-500`) computes the root, reads
the txid's level-0 offset (`indexOf`, `:327-333`) and, at offset 0 alone (a
coinbase's place; a transaction alone in its block, the lone leaf, is one
case), asks the tracker's `currentHeight` and answers `false` when
`blockHeight + 100 > height`, before the root is asked; `Transaction.verify`
throws `Invalid merkle path for transaction <txid>` on that `false`
(`#completeVerificationFromMerklePath`, `Transaction.ts:1298-1316`) for every
proven transaction it reaches, the subject included (`#verifySnapshot`,
`:1747-1771`). This crate's `proven` (`src/transaction/verify.rs`) asked the
root alone, so a proof 0 to 99 blocks deep at offset 0 verified here and not
there. New, additive: `MerklePath::verify(txid, tracker)`, the reference's
method (the root, the offset, at offset 0 the height with `u64` arithmetic, no
overflow at `u32::MAX`, then `is_valid_root_for_height`), which `proven` now
calls behind all six doors of `Transaction::verify`; the refusal keeps its
words, a tracker's error its class (`Chain tracker error: ...`, a transport
fault `Error::TransportFault`). `Beef::verify_valid` and the streaming reader
do not move (the reference's `Beef.verify`, `Beef.ts:1020-1035`, has no depth
rule). Pinned by `tests/transaction_coinbase_depth_734.rs` against
`tests/vectors/coinbase_depth_734.json` (`tests/support/coinbase_depth_734.mjs`,
Node v22.18.0, 56 cells: verdicts or words and the tracker's calls in order),
5 of 7 RED on `e228c61a`; the strength read's fold adds 24 cells of a tip
below the proof (80 in all).

The sites that verified a spend of `MerklePath::from_coinbase_txid(.., 800_000)`
against a tracker at 800,000 (or 800,010) keep their verdicts with the tracker
100 or more blocks above the proof, where no era is read from that height: the
`transaction` and `beef_spv` examples (README pasted),
`benches/transaction_sign_verify.rs`, `tests/support/fixtures/binary.rs` (its
recipe guard's two hashes; no fixture byte moves), two `src/transaction/beef.rs`
unit tests and ten `tests/` files (`docs/lanes/fix-734.md` lists them).

Migration: a `ChainTracker` whose `current_height` is a placeholder, or under a
proof's block height plus 100, now refuses every proof whose txid sits at
level-0 offset 0 (`Err(TransactionError("Invalid merkle path for transaction
<txid>"))`); answer the real tip, or set a mock's height 100 above its proofs.
`current_height` is now asked by `Transaction::verify` (at offset 0 alone).
A test or a caller that verifies an offset-0 (lone-leaf or coinbase) proof
against a tracker fewer than 100 blocks above the proof now reads `false`, a
tip below the proof included (a placeholder 0 or 1, pinned since the strength
read's fold by `a_tip_below_the_proof_refuses_an_offset_0_proof_734`, 24 cells
more, 80 in all); the overlay engine's
`crates/overlay-engine/tests/script_verification.rs:785` (a funding proof 10
blocks under its tracker) is such a test and sets its tracker to the proof's
height plus 100 when it takes this release; no production door of the overlay
engine, the toolbox or the CLI calls `Transaction::verify` with a tracker (the
strength read's table).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#734)

The rule is the reference's, read from the offset; two cells where it is
stricter than the node are followed and stated, not silent. The node refuses a
coinbase spend when `nSpendHeight - coinHeight < COINBASE_MATURITY` (100;
bitcoin-sv v1.2.3 `validation.cpp:2618`, `consensus.h:75`), the spend height
the tip plus one: at a tip of `h + 99` the node admits the spend in the next
block, the reference and `Transaction::verify` refuse it. And a proven
offset-0 transaction no input spends (the subject itself) is refused under
depth, where the node has no rule. The streaming reader keeps the node's
reading, a coinbase by its null input against the mining tip
(`beef_stream/spends.rs`, `tip + 1 - height < 100`), so on one BEEF the two
doors part at `h + 99` for a coinbase (a null input), and at every tip under
`h + 100` for an offset-0 transaction with a non-null input, which the stream
does not read as a coinbase, and for a proven offset-0 subject no input spends
(the second pinned by
`the_stream_keeps_its_verdict_on_the_same_beef_at_the_four_tips_734`, whose
parent carries a non-null input: the stream valid at `h` and `h + 99`, where
`Transaction::verify` refuses both; a block's offset 0 is its coinbase, so no
honest tracker carries that root).
go-sdk@2ca481c's `MerklePath.Verify` has no depth rule
(`transaction/merklepath.go:423-429`); its `spv.Verify` applies the node's
figure to a coinbase source by its inputs (`spv/verify.go:674-714`,
`coinbaseMature`). An upstream filing is the keeper's.

### Fixed: the SLAP discovery admits a host only from a 1-satoshi output whose txid hint agrees (#786)

`LookupResolver::find_competent_hosts` read every output of a tracker's
answer through `parse_slap_token` (`src/overlay/lookup_resolver.rs`), which
authenticated the advertisement and compared the service but read neither
the selected output's value nor the output's `txid` hint. The reference's
`extractHostsFromAnswer` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/LookupResolver.ts:2194-2216`) skips an output
whose hint is present and, lower-cased, is not the BEEF subject's txid
(`:2201`), and one whose selected output does not carry exactly 1 satoshi
(`:2203`), each a `continue`: no throw, the tracker's other outputs still
read, the tracker a success (its call at `:1974` returned). So a host
advertised from an output of 0 or 2 satoshis, or under a hint naming another
transaction, was admitted here and asked by `query`, where the reference
never asks it. `parse_slap_token` now reads in the reference's order: the
BEEF's subject, the hint (`OutputListItem::txid`, #735) when present, the
output at the index and its `satoshis` (`Some(1)` alone), then the token and
the service as before; a refusal is the skip it always was, the tracker's
accounting unchanged. An empty domain cannot be admitted, as at `:2208`: the
admin token's URI check refuses it (`admin_token_validation.rs`,
`advertisement_uri`).

Pinned by `tests/lookup_slap_admission_786.rs` (seven tests on a scripted
facilitator and `.invalid` trackers): 0 and 2 satoshis admit no host; a
tracker naming one host at 1 satoshi and one at 2 admits the one and is
recorded a success, not backed off; a disagreeing hint admits no host; an
upper-case agreeing hint and an absent hint admit the host; and the seven
cases of `tests/vectors/lookup_slap_admission_786.json` (recorded by
`tests/support/lookup_slap_admission_786.mjs`: the reference's own
`LookupResolver.query` on a scripted facilitator, its advertisements written
by its `OverlayAdminTokenTemplate`, Node v22.18.0) served here to the hosts
the reference asked. 5 of 7 RED on a scratch copy of the tip with the
reader's change removed (the host admitted), the two agreeing-hint controls
green.

Migration: a host advertised from an output of a value other than 1 satoshi,
or served under a `txid` hint that is not its BEEF's subject, is no longer
discovered. The reference's advertisers write 1 satoshi
(`WalletAdvertiser.ts`' `AD_TOKEN_VALUE`), as `bsv-overlay-cloudflare`'s does.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#786)

Ours: the reference's skip followed on both checks (`LookupResolver.ts:2201`,
`:2203` at `edf6e03`), closing the SLAP half of #735's stated residue; the
owner's word on #735 (a disagreeing hint read and counted) is the identity
evidence check's and does not reach this site, which admits a host and
proves no subject. A binary aggregated answer's outputs each carry the
Atomic BEEF of their outpoint's txid and that txid as their hint since

skips none of them; read, not changed. Theirs: go-sdk at `2ca481c`

(`src/overlay/topic_broadcaster.rs`), a row of its own.

### Added: PushDrop's wallet-aware lock, PushDrop::lock_with_wallet, the sdk's PushDrop.lock (#782)

`PushDrop::lock_with_wallet(wallet, originator, fields, protocol_id, key_id,
counterparty, for_self, include_signature, position) -> Result<LockingScript>`
(`src/script/templates/pushdrop_wallet.rs`, under the `wallet` feature) is the
reference's `new PushDrop(wallet, originator).lock(fields, protocolID, keyID,
counterparty, forSelf, includeSignature, lockPosition)` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/script/templates/PushDrop.ts:130-202`), in its order: the
wallet's `getPublicKey` for the protocol, key ID, counterparty and `forSelf`
(`:155-163`); when `includeSignature`, its `createSignature` over the fields
concatenated (`fields.flat()`) for the same protocol, key ID and counterparty,
no `forSelf`, the signature pushed as the last field as the wallet returned it,
no DER read (`:173-185`); the key pushed as the wallet returned it under
`OP_CHECKSIG` (`:166-172`, #545's rule: a compressed answer 33 bytes, an
uncompressed or hybrid one 65); the fields minimally encoded, the
`OP_2DROP`/`OP_DROP` tail and the lock position (`:186-201`). Both calls carry
the originator; a wallet error is returned as it came, and no signature is
asked after a failed key call. The reference's defaults are `for_self` false,
`include_signature` true and `LockPosition::Before`.

Why: the crate had no public wallet-aware lock. The raw `PushDrop::lock`
pushes its `PublicKey` compressed, and #545's reading (the key as the wallet
returned it) was crate-visible alone (`wallet_key_lock`, the five sites of the
key-value stores, the registry, the contacts manager and the identity reveal),
so a downstream composing `get_public_key` and `create_signature` by hand
around the raw lock (the toolbox's permission mint, the reference's
`WalletPermissionsManager.ts:3360-3367`, `:3453`, `:3645`) re-encoded the key.
The raw `lock`, `new`, `with_position`, `decode` and the unlockers are

### Fixed: the atomic writer copies no BUMP for a txid-only entry without a matching index, as the reference does (#766)

From the scoped cold re-read of PR #763's fold (2026-11-04 11:25Z).
`Beef::to_binary_atomic`'s closure (`atomic_closure`,
`src/transaction/beef.rs`) gave a txid-only entry whose BUMP index names no
BUMP holding its txid (an entry read from bytes carries no index; one set by
hand may name another BUMP) the last BUMP of the BEEF holding the txid, this
crate's own fallback. The reference copies a BUMP only for an included entry
`#hasMatchingBump` proves, and copies the entry with the mapped index or
`undefined` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/transaction/Beef.ts:448-470`,
the skip at `:453`; `#hasMatchingBump` `:436-446`: the index names a BUMP whose
level 0 holds the txid). Now the txid-only branch copies the BUMP its index
names when that BUMP holds the txid and no BUMP and no index otherwise; nothing
else of the atomic rule moves (the subject's graph, the proven cut, a raw
entry's BUMP, `from_atomic_beef`). The last-BUMP rule at the merge doors and
`find_bump` (#757, #765) is the reference's and stays.

Measured on `toBinaryAtomic(child)` of the vector's
`txid_only_after_both_with_child` shape with the parent's index cleared: the
reference writes `...0200beef00020262b0...` (no BUMP), this crate wrote
`...0200beef01fe01350c...` (the last BUMP, at 800001) and now writes the
reference's bytes; with the index naming a BUMP that does not hold the parent
(the grandchild's, at 800004), the reference writes `...0200beef00...` and
this crate wrote `...0200beef01fe00350c...` (the parent's BUMP at 800000).

`tests/beef_bump_index_757.rs`'s
`a_txid_only_entry_without_a_matching_index_carries_no_bump_into_the_atomic_beef_766`
on two cases the #757 recorder now writes (`support/beef_bump_index_757.mjs`,
`ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0: `txid_only_without_an_index_with_child`
and `txid_only_naming_a_bump_without_its_txid_with_child`, a step `index:<tx>=`
setting `bumpIndex` before the write, and one BUMP added,
`grandchild_800004`); every earlier entry of `vectors/beef_bump_index_757.json`
unchanged. Both RED on `e7f5d4f7` (the bytes above), green after.

Semver: no public shape changes. The written form of such an entry's atomic
BEEF loses a BUMP: a downstream comparing atomic bytes sees the change, and a
reader that proved the txid-only entry by that BUMP now reads it as an
unproven stub (`verify_structure` refuses it `StubNotProven`, `verify_valid`
answers not valid; pinned in the test). Migration: give the entry the index
of the BUMP holding its txid before writing (`set_bump_index(Some(i))`, or
`merge_bump` of its proof on an entry with no index), or write the whole BEEF
with `to_binary`.

### Fixed: every SLAP tracker backed off refuses in the reference's words, and a cached host list with no host available is not reused (#769)

From the strength read of PR #767 (#762, 2026-11-04 11:48Z). With every SLAP
tracker backing off, `LookupResolver::find_competent_hosts` answered `Ok([])`
(`src/overlay/lookup_resolver.rs:343-345` at `4ed58d05`), `get_competent_hosts`
cached that empty list for `DEFAULT_HOSTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` (5 minutes, `:267-285`)
and reused any entry younger than that (`:186-192`), so `query` refused in `No
competent mainnet hosts found by the SLAP trackers for lookup service:
<service>` for 5 minutes although a tracker's backoff ends after 1 s (growing
to 60 s). The reference's discovery asks only the trackers not backing off and
throws when none is left (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/LookupResolver.ts:2306-2314`,
`prepareHostsForQuery`, caught at `:1963` and thrown by the query at `:1671`):

```text
const soonest = Math.min(...ranked.map(h => h.backoffUntil))
const waitMs = Math.max(soonest - now, 0)
throw new Error(
  `All ${context} hosts are backing off for approximately ${waitMs}ms due to repeated failures.`
```

with `context` `'SLAP trackers'` (`:1958`); and it reuses a cached host list
only while some host in it is not backing off (`lookupCacheHasAvailableHost`,
`:1898-1903`, `refresh` at `:1913-1918`), so an empty entry is never reused.
The reference's incomplete flag (`discoveryComplete`, `:2277-2278`: a failed
tracker, a limit hit or a skipped host) is stored with its entry and read back
into the session (`:1933`), never into the reuse decision: a discovery that
found hosts is cached as before, whatever its trackers did. This crate stores
no such flag (`HostsCacheEntry` holds the hosts and the expiry alone), the
reuse decision unchanged by its absence. Now `find_competent_hosts`
refuses with every tracker backing off, `Error::OverlayError("All SLAP trackers
hosts are backing off for approximately <N>ms due to repeated failures.")`, N
the soonest end of a tracker's backoff less now (the reference's `Math.min`),
the variant the resolver's other host refusals use; the refusal is not cached
(it never was: the cache takes an answer alone), and `get_competent_hosts`
reuses an entry only while some host in it is not backing off. `No competent
<network> hosts found by the SLAP trackers for lookup service: <service>`
stays for the discovery whose trackers were asked and named no host (the
reference's `:1669-1674`, a settled session with no host and no
`noHostsError`); no trackers configured is still no host, as
`prepareHostsForQuery` answers `[]` for an empty list (`:2285`). The two
methods are in `src/overlay/lookup_resolver/backoff.rs` (the parent file under
the ratchet's 800-line bound).

`tests/lookup_tracker_backoff_769.rs`, on #762's scripted facilitator on a
tracker host (three formula answers through the discovery back it off), each
test on its own tracker and host names: the lookup inside the backoff refused
in the reference's words, N at most the tracker's remaining backoff and its
1 s base, the tracker not asked, and the discovery itself refusing; past the
backoff (a sleep to the snapshot's `backoff_until` and 20 ms) the lookup asks
the tracker again, which names a host (a SLAP advertisement by this crate's
writer, `create_signed_overlay_admin_token`), and is answered; a discovery
that named a host cached (the tracker asked once for two lookups); a cached
host list whose one host is backed off (three formula answers from it through
three lookups) not reused, the fourth lookup asking the tracker again. 3 of 4
