## [0.8.9] - 2026-11-13

### Security: the deprecated `KVStoreInterpreter::verify_signature_legacy` answered `true` for every token and every key; it now answers `true` only for a token whose controller field is that key and whose last field is that key's signature over the other fields (GHSA-mj2m-jxgv-r446)

- What was wrong. `verify_signature_legacy(&PushDrop, &PublicKey)` read neither argument and answered `true`: a token no controller signed, a signed token checked against a key other than its controller's, and a PushDrop with no fields all passed. Its documentation said it delegated to the `KVStoreFields`-based `verify_signature`; it did not. Every published version answers this way: `0.2.0`, the crate's first release, through `0.8.8`, and the `0.9.0-beta` line; this release carries the fix.
- The reach. A caller that checks, with this function, a KVStore token it did not write (an overlay lookup's answer, a transaction output a peer hands it) and acts on `true`. No door of this crate calls it.
- The fix (`src/kvstore/legacy_signature.rs`, the function's one caller). `true` only for a PushDrop of five or six fields whose controller field is the given key's compressed form and whose last field is that key's signature over the other fields, under the derivation the token's protocol field names: a plain protocol name with the key ID `kvstore-token`, as this line's writer signs, or the `[level, name]` namespace with the key as the key ID and the locking key derived from the controller, as the `0.9.0-beta` line's writer signs. A field read as `OP_0`'s single zero byte is taken as signed either as that byte or as an empty field, the two values `OP_0` pushes. The tags' bounds are not judged here. The signature of the function is unchanged and it stays deprecated; this change leaves `verify_signature`, `GlobalKVStore` and the interpreter's readers as they were.
- The tests. `tests/kvstore_legacy_signature_verdict.rs` (12): a token whose controller field names a stranger and whose signature is junk, in each derivation, tagged and untagged; a PushDrop of no fields; a signed token checked against another key; one-change copies of a signed token; a token of four or seven fields its controller signed; a namespace token whose protocol field, signed as written, is not canonical JSON; a token its controller signed whose controller field names another key; all `false`. Signed tokens with any tags, an empty or zero-byte value, an empty key or tags field, a plain-name token under any locking key, and 100 generated tokens over the four shapes `true` against their controllers and `false` with any one byte changed. On a scratch copy of the base (`2edb403f`, the `0.8.8` release commit) with the test file alone, 10 of 12 RED, the two cells that answer `true` whatever the door (any tags, any locking key) green; green on the fix; each of the five cells added after the fix's reviews RED on a copy of the fix with the one check it pins weakened. Twenty thousand tokens of every shape this crate's writers make (either derivation, tagged or not, empty and zero-byte fields among them) signed by their controllers answer `true` on the base, on the fix and on the published `0.8.8`, their scripts and answers equal by one SHA-256; checked against another token's controller, 19,999 answer `true` on the base and none on the fix. `fuzz_script_parser` now passes every script `PushDrop::decode` reads through the function and asserts that `true` comes only for five or six fields whose controller field is the key checked; with the base's body planted it fails on a committed seed.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller that relied on `true` for a token whose controller field is another key, or whose last field is not that key's signature over the others, now gets `false`. A token its controller signed, checked against that controller, answers `true` as before. The door is a signature verdict alone: it does not judge the tags' bounds, the push encoding or a plain-name token's locking key. There is no workaround: the fix is in this release.

## [0.8.8] - 2026-11-12

### Security: a transaction's BEEF ends with that transaction: the doors that write one from a transaction's own ancestry no longer sort it, so the read that names no txid takes the transaction back

- What was wrong. `Transaction::to_beef` and `to_beef_v1` collected the transaction's ancestry — each entry's sources above it, the transaction last, BRC-62's own rule for the form ("we must ensure that we end with the tx being evaluated, and its inputs are above, and their inputs are above that") — then handed the assembled `Beef` to `Beef::to_binary`, whose sort writes the dependency order a caller-assembled BEEF takes. A graph whose collected order is not that order — one holding a proven branch beside a branch resting on a missing source — got its subject written before the proven ancestor, and `Transaction::from_beef(&bytes, None)` (its target `txid ?? atomic_txid ?? the last entry`) answered the last entry: a proven root, not the transaction the caller serialized. Every published version reads this way — the doors are as old as the crate's first release (`0.2.0` through `0.8.7`, released without this fix, and the `0.9.0-beta` line; the fix ships in `0.8.8`).
- The reach. A caller that serializes a partial graph holding a proven branch beside a missing source and reads the bytes back without naming the txid: the door answers an ancestor of the transaction it was handed, real and valid, so it is a wrong-identity loss, not a validity loss (1,259 of 2,000 random such graphs misidentify, measured on every published version from `0.2.0` to `0.9.0-beta.7` — the served-without-a-tag `0.2.0` and `0.3.0` and the yanked `0.3.21` included, every one crates.io serves). A read that names the txid always took the transaction; a graph with no proven entry was never misread (the sort leaves its subject last); the atomic word's own read was never misled (it names its subject in the header, and its reader takes it back on every published version), and its BEEF portion, the closure sorted and the subject then moved last, ends with the subject as `0.8.7` writes it, which this fix leaves as it was, while a no-txid `from_beef` of its bytes, which took the header into account only from `0.3.20` on, misread before that the same way. Honest graphs whose collected order is the dependency order — the differential's 20,000 generated single-root trees among them — keep the same bytes: the bytes and the ids every read returns, one SHA-256 digest, are equal on `0.8.7` and on this fix, so whatever a published version writes still reads. A graph whose collected order is not that order — an honest merge of two independent branches among them — takes the Migration's change: 11,263 of 20,000 generated graphs of two or three roots, every root proven, write different bytes at the plain doors, and every read of them is unchanged (the subject, named or not); the atomic door's bytes are equal to `0.8.7`'s on all 60,000 generated graphs (the single-root trees, those, and as many with each root proven at odds of one half).
- The fix, in one place. The collected ancestry is written in the order the walk collects it: `Beef::hold_order` holds a BEEF a transaction door assembles as it stands, and `to_binary` writes it without the sort; the plain transaction doors (`to_beef`, `to_beef_v1`) reach it through one private helper, so every sibling door that shared the behavior is brought under the one piece of code; the atomic door (`to_atomic_beef`) reaches the same helper, and its closure is sorted and the subject then moved last by the atomic writer, as `0.8.7` writes it. The doors that were already safe are pinned by their own cells: a BEEF a caller assembles by hand keeps the documented dependency sort (`Beef::new`/`with_version` then `to_binary`), `merge_beef` then `to_binary` keeps it, and the atomic word's read keeps the subject (the header names it, and the atomic door's closure ends with it). The fix sits exactly at `src/transaction/beef.rs`'s code-health ceiling (3,214 lines, no headroom at the base): the documentation it adds is the short form — the full rule and its reference live at the helper's one caller, `Transaction::ancestry_beef` — and the remaining lines are recovered from three neighboring method docs whose meaning is unchanged.
- The tests. `tests/beef_tx_order.rs` (16): the finding's shape through both transaction doors and the atomic door, the bytes and the reads (the no-txid read, the named read, the parsed last entry, the atomic bytes pinned on the finding's shape, the plain doors' version words asserted, the held order asserted written through `to_writer`); a caller-assembled BEEF, a merged BEEF and a pre-fix version's bytes each keeping their documented order; the invariant as a property over generated graphs, 200 of the finding's population (156 the sort writes differently, 128 of them moving the subject off the last entry; the floors hold the corpus to the measured counts, so the property is never vacuous) and 200 of missing roots only (134 differ, none misread), the counts re-derived and pinned by a census cell in the same file (so a silent generator degradation stays red with the floors gone); and 200 of the differential's honest trees, pinned as the boundary cell; the committed fuzz seed replayed through the no-txid read (the shape checked, so an emptied or vacuous seed is red); a witness of two proven roots under one BUMP (a level-0 multi-leaf path, a shape no cell had built: the BUMP-combine path and the closure's renumbered-index sharing), read back through every door; and the atomic door's order on 605 graphs (the four witnesses, two proven branches fully linked, the 400 property graphs, the 200 honest trees): the Beef-level door's sorted closure of the same graph with the subject moved last, never the collected order where the two differ (280 of them, counted, so the cell cannot go vacuous). `tests/vectors/beef_tx_order.json` (4 witnesses), recorded by `tests/support/beef_tx_order.mjs` by a run at the pin (`ts-stack@edf6e03`, Node v22.18.0): each witness's V1 bytes beside the dependency sort's bytes and the validity verdict. On a scratch copy of the base (`2bfe9db1`, `origin/main`, the `0.8.7` tree) with the test file, the vector and the seed alone, seven of the sixteen cells were red — the no-txid read answered an ancestor, the door's bytes differed from the recorded bytes, both property floors and the census of their counts, the held order through `to_writer`, the replayed seed — and the nine boundary cells green (the atomic cells among them: this line's atomic door already ended its closure with the subject; they are red on a tree whose atomic door drops the move or writes the collected closure); all sixteen green on the fix; the honest-tree cell is green on the base by design (the sort leaves a single root's tree alone), which is what the differential measures. The fuzz target `fuzz_beef_parser` now checks the round trip at both doors (a transaction read from a BEEF, re-serialized through the plain door and the atomic door, reads back as itself, and the atomic closure's last entry is it) and carries a seed for the shape (`fuzz/corpus/fuzz_beef_parser/tx-door-order`, which crashes a build of the base carrying the check and passes on the fix); two 60-second runs clean (121,551 and 143,474 executions). The recursive reference of the 0.3.35 iterative equivalence (`beef.rs`'s `iterative_equivalence_tests`) carries the order hold alike, so the iterative doors and it still write the same bytes.
- Not in this patch. The Beef-level doors keep their documented dependency sort: a BEEF a caller assembles by hand, and one built by `merge_beef`, still write it, and a subject that sits before a proven ancestor in that order is still the last entry's to claim at a no-txid read — the documented behavior of those doors, unchanged since they landed, pinned here by its own cells.
- Migration. No signature moved. The bytes a transaction door writes change for graphs whose collected order is not the dependency order — the entries are the same, each entry's sources above it, the subject last — so a consumer that takes the last entry now takes the subject; a consumer that names the txid sees no change; a consumer of the atomic word sees no change. A BEEF any earlier version wrote still reads, at every door.

## [0.8.7] - 2026-11-12

### Security: a Shamir backup set that carries a share at x = 0 substituted the recovered key for the holder's; both doors now refuse it before interpolating (#854)

- What was wrong. `KeyShares::from_backup_format` and `recover_private_key` checked only that the shares of a set agreed on their threshold and integrity tag, then interpolated whatever x coordinates the set carried. At an x of zero the interpolation answers that share's y — the secret is the polynomial's value at zero, and a share standing there carries it alone — so a set whose zero-x share holds another key recovers that key, its integrity tag agreeing when the tag is that key's own: the recovered key is the one the set names, not the holder's. A set of more shares than the threshold also passed with one share repeated, and the reader took a coordinate at or above the field prime (the prime itself a second spelling of zero), a non-canonical base58 field (a leading `1`) and a field over 64 characters as the same share. Every published version reads this way (`0.2.0`, the crate's first release, through `0.8.6`, released without this fix, and the `0.9.0-beta` line; the fix ships in `0.8.7`).
- The reach. A caller that reads a backup set it did not write itself: a custodian's medium, a share pasted by hand, a set restored from another writer. A set this crate's own writer produces never trips the new refusals — `split_private_key` evaluates at x = 1..=total, distinct non-zero coordinates — and no door outside `primitives::bsv::shamir` reads a share set.
- The fix, before interpolating, at both doors (`from_backup_format` and `recover_private_key`, one scan of the set each). An x of zero is refused (`Zero x coordinate in share <idx>`); a repeated x is refused (`Duplicate share detected, each must be unique.`); each coordinate field is read only as the canonical base58 of a value below the field prime — 1 to 64 characters, reduced on read, and the field's text the canonical text of the reduced value — refused as `Invalid canonical share data in share <idx>` (the length) or `Finite-field point must use a bounded canonical Base58 representation` (the spelling). The writer (`to_backup_format`, `split_private_key`) is unchanged.
- The tests. `tests/shamir_backup_refusals_854.rs` (25): the finding's set refused at both doors, as backup strings and as hand-built points, the forged share first, second and third of three; the zero-x point first, second and last of four at recovery, one built by `PointInFiniteField::from_string` (the composed seam the backup door does not guard); the non-canonical zero x (the field prime); a repeated share at the backup door and a repeated x past the first `threshold` points at recovery, in three shapes — the same share twice, twins not adjacent, one x under another y — at both doors; the overlong, non-canonical (a leading `1`, its refusal's words pinned) and at-or-above-prime coordinate fields on either coordinate, and a 400,000-character field on either refused in under a second (its length read before the field is decoded, where the base's reader decodes it for minutes before answering); a hand-built point at the field prime, placed by struct literal past `PointInFiniteField::new`'s reduction, refused by the integrity tag alone (the tag is the guard that holds there, pinned); the polynomial's own interpolation pinned on a line through x = 1 and x = p − 1; beside them, honest sets at thresholds (2,3), (3,5), (5,10) and (10,10) round-tripped whole, from the first and the last `threshold` shares, in several orders and from a scattered subset, and the boundary set x = 1 and x = p − 1 round-tripped at both doors. On a scratch copy of the base (`4e6f76d2`, `origin/main` as it stands, the `0.8.6` release commit) with the test file alone, the 20 refusal cells RED (every door answered `Ok`, the two cost cells by the base's minutes-long decode of the 400,000-character field) and the 5 green — the 3 honest controls, the boundary set among them, and the 2 pins; green on the fix. `src/primitives/bsv/shamir.rs`'s inline duplicate-shares test now asserts the door's refusal, where it asserted the recovered key. That fix grows the module past 1,026 lines, the file-size ratchet's bound for it at `origin/main`, so the module's 34 unit tests move to `src/primitives/bsv/shamir_tests.rs` — the same split beta's bsv-rs#180 made for the same ratchet — unchanged save the duplicate-shares test named above and `decode_share`'s new index argument at its call sites (`shamir.rs` 484 lines, `shamir_tests.rs` 604).
- Not in this patch. The backup format's port to the reference's own grammar (its integrity tag and threshold text) is #854's rewrite of this module, which this fix keeps small to sit under. The integrity tag stays 4 characters, as the writer writes it.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller that fed a set carrying a zero-x share, a repeated share, a non-canonical or overlong coordinate field, or a coordinate at or above the field prime now gets an `Err` where it got a key: take the shares as the writer that made them wrote them, or re-split the key (`split_private_key`). A set this crate wrote reads as before.

## [0.8.6] - 2026-11-11

### Fixed: Transaction::from_json refuses an input txid that is not 64 hex digits and holds a valid one in lower case (the reader half of #845, cherry-picked from beta `29d8c366`, PR #856)

- What was wrong. `Transaction::from_json`, for a document with no `hex` member, stored each input's `txid` member as given, unchecked (`src/transaction/tx_json.rs`), and the writer wrote a text it could not read as 32 zero bytes. On 0.8.5 (`a8186851`) an input `txid` of `"zz"`, `"abcd"` or `""` answered `Ok`, each written with the outpoint txid `00...00` and one transaction id, `490b76e7...`: three documents were one transaction, spending an outpoint none of them named. An upper-case txid was held as given, so one txid could be held as two strings.
- The fix. `from_json` refuses an input `txid` member that is not exactly 64 hex digits as `TransactionError("Invalid txid of input N: expected 64 hex digits")`, naming the input's index and none of the text, and holds one in upper or mixed case in lower case. A document with a `hex` member is read from the hex as before, a top-level `txid` member beside it unread (stated, as go-sdk@2ca481c's `UnmarshalJSON` leaves it, `transaction/txjson.go:49-66`).
- The tests. `tests/transaction_numbers_844.rs` (3, this line's copy of beta's file, which also carries #844's amount cells, not taken here): `a_json_input_txid_that_is_not_64_hex_digits_is_refused_845` (`"zz"`, `"abcd"`, `""`, 63 and 65 digits, a non-hex digit, a leading space), `a_json_input_txid_in_upper_case_is_held_in_lower_case_845` (the same id and bytes as the lower-case document, written back in lower case), `a_json_txid_member_beside_its_hex_is_unread_stated_845`. 2 of 3 RED on `a8186851` (the stated cell green on both).
- Not in this patch. The writer's half of #845 (`TransactionInput::source_txid` a `String` nothing checks, so a hand-built input with a malformed txid is still written as 32 zero bytes) is beta's #843 typed id, a public break; #844 (the 2^53 amount refusals) is beta's.
- Migration. A caller that handed `from_json` a field-built document with an input `txid` that is not 64 hex digits now gets an `Err`; one that read back an upper-case txid from `source_txid` reads it in lower case. No public type or signature changes.

### Fixed: Signature::from_der reads a DER signature as the reference does; bytes after it, a wrong sequence length, a sequence length byte with its high bit set taken as a plain length and an unneeded leading zero were accepted; the interpreter reads a signature as the node does under a word (cherry-picked from beta `01946931`, PR #846, issues #842 and #847)

- What was wrong. `Signature::from_der` checked only that its input was not shorter than the sequence's length byte said, read every length byte as a number whatever its high bit, and dropped a leading zero byte whether or not the next byte needed it. So a DER signature followed by other bytes, one whose sequence length was not its contents' length and one padded with an unneeded zero read as the signature alone. The reference's `Signature.fromDER` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/primitives/Signature.ts:44-97`) refuses each: `Signature DER invalid`, `Invalid R-length in signature DER`, `Invalid DER entity length`, `Invalid R-value in signature DER`, `Invalid S-value in signature DER`. It reads an input of any length by those checks alone (`30 04 02 00 02 00` is R = S = 0; this crate refused anything under 8 bytes as `DER too short`).
- The reach on this line. Every door that reads a DER signature through this reader: `messages::verify`, `compat::bsm::verify_message_der`, `auth::Certificate::verify`, `auth::validate_certificate_encoding`, `ProtoWallet::verify_signature`, `TransactionSignature::from_checksig_format` (and the templates' checks through it), and the identity client's and contacts' signature reads. On 0.8.5 a signed message, a BSM signature, a certificate signature and a ProtoWallet signature with a byte appended to the DER each verified `true` (the first two pinned by the tests below; the last two by a run on `a8186851` and on this tree, the appended signature `Ok(true)` there and `Err(InvalidSignature("Signature DER invalid"))` here).
- The fix. One reading of the reference's checks, `primitives::ec::signature_der::read` (crate-visible, every byte read with `get`): `Signature::from_der` reads through it and refuses as `Error::InvalidSignature` in the reference's words. `from_checksig_format` takes the last byte as the scope and reads the rest as the reference's `fromChecksigFormat` does: one byte alone is an empty DER, `Signature DER must start with 0x30` (`Checksig format too short` until now); the empty input is the blank signature, unchanged. One cell is this crate's, stated: an integer longer than 32 bytes past its sign byte (a value at or above 2^256) stays `Integer component too large`, where the reference holds a `BigNumber` of any length and its verify answers false; `Signature` holds 32 bytes. `Signature::to_der` writes a zero S as the reference's `toDER` does, `02 00` (it wrote `02 01 00`, which the strict reader refuses as an unneeded zero).
- The interpreter (#847). `Spend` no longer reads a signature through `from_checksig_format`. After the strict BIP 66 encoding check, which runs in every mode as before, one crate-private reading (`src/script/spend/signature_read.rs`, a child file of `spend.rs`) gives the signature to the low-S rule and to the signature check alike. Under a word it is the node's: `ecdsa_signature_parse_der_lax` ported whole (`src/script/spend/der_lax.rs`, bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `pubkey.cpp:32-175`). Without a word it is the reference's `fromDER`. Two cells pass BIP 66 and are read differently by the node and by the strict reader: an R or S that is a lone `00`, and an R or S longer than 32 bytes. The node reads the lone zero as zero and the long value as the all-zero signature (`pubkey.cpp:139-173`); both are low and both fail the check. So under a word each is a failed check: `<op> requires failing signatures to be empty.` where NULLFAIL applies, and otherwise the false; `<sig> <key> OP_CHECKSIG OP_NOT` is valid under the three post-Chronicle words at version 2. On 0.8.5 the lone zero was already the node's verdict and the long value was refused as a format in every mode (#847): 120 cells under the words, 12 of them a script the node reads valid. #14's order exception (`signature_overflows_the_order`) is subsumed by the lax parse under a word and removed; in the default mode it is kept for the values a 32-byte slot holds.
- The default mode's verdicts that moved. `Transaction::verify` runs every input's scripts in the default mode (no word), so these are its verdicts too. A spend whose signature has a lone-zero R or S under `OP_CHECKSIG OP_NOT` was valid on 0.8.5 and is refused now in the reference's words, `The signature format is invalid.`. A spend whose signature has an R longer than 32 bytes, at either version, or an S longer than 32 bytes at version 2, under `OP_CHECKSIG OP_NOT`, was refused on 0.8.5 and is valid now. An S longer than 32 bytes at version 1 is refused on both, in `The signature must have a low S value.` now. Pinned by `the_default_mode_answers_as_the_reference_recorded_842_847` (`tests/script_signature_der_842.rs`).
- The default mode, toward the reference's `Spend` (recorded, `tests/vectors/script_signature_der_842.json`, `tests/support/script_signature_der_842.mjs`, Node v22.18.0): a lone-zero R or S is refused in `The signature format is invalid.` at both versions (it was valid under `OP_NOT`); an R past 32 bytes at both versions and an S past 32 bytes at version 2 verify false (valid under `OP_NOT`; they were refused as the format); an S past 32 bytes at version 1 stays refused, at the low-S check, in this line's words `The signature must have a low S value.` (the reference's are `The signature format is invalid.`, its wrapper's; this line refuses every high S at version 1 in its low-S words; stated below).
- The tests. `tests/signature_der_842.rs` (12) against `tests/vectors/signature_der_842.json` (42 cells, `tests/support/signature_der_842.mjs`): the shapes on three signatures this crate's signer writes, through `from_der`, `from_checksig_format`, `messages::verify` and `verify_message_der`; the reader's short inputs; 2,000 signatures written and read back byte for byte; the zero-S writer; the `0x7f` and `0x80` length bytes. 10 of 12 RED on `a8186851` (`left: "true"`, `right: "ERR:Signature DER invalid"` for the suffixed signed message; `left: "ok 5e2163c3..."` for the suffixed DER). `tests/script_signature_der_842.rs` (5): every cell under the block and standard words of both eras and each block word with DERSIG, STRICTENC and LOW_S cleared, versions 1 and 2, five locks, against the node's verdict, and the default mode's 64 recorded cells; 2 of 5 RED on `a8186851` (the long value, 120 cells; the default mode, 16 cells). `tests/ec_tests.rs`' `test_malformed_der_trailing_data_accepted` is `test_malformed_der_trailing_data_refused_842`, RED on `a8186851`. Unit cells: `src/primitives/ec/signature_der_tests.rs`, `src/script/spend/der_lax_tests.rs`. A fuzz target, `fuzz_signature_der` (98 seeds).
- Migration. A caller that handed `Signature::from_der` a signature with other bytes after it, a sequence length other than its contents' length (shorter, or longer with bytes after it, a length byte with its high bit set taken as a plain length among them; a long-form length was refused already, with other error texts) or an unneeded leading zero now gets an `Err` (slice the signature; re-encode one written with padding), and so does every door above that reads through it: `messages::verify`, `compat::bsm::verify_message_der`, `auth::Certificate::verify` and `ProtoWallet::verify_signature` answer `Err(InvalidSignature(..))` for such a signature where they answered `Ok(true)`, and `TransactionSignature::from_checksig_format` (and the templates' checks) refuse it. An input under 8 bytes that the reference's checks pass now reads (`30 04 02 00 02 00` is `Ok`, R = S = 0, where it was `DER too short`). `Signature::to_der` of a zero S writes `02 00` (it wrote `02 01 00`): a caller that pinned those bytes re-pins them. `Spend` moves verdicts in the default mode (a lone-zero R or S refused in `The signature format is invalid.` where `OP_CHECKSIG OP_NOT` was valid; an R past 32 bytes, and an S past 32 bytes at version 2, a false check where the format was refused) and under a word (a value past 32 bytes a failed check where the format was refused). The error words changed to the reference's (`DER too short`, `Expected sequence tag 0x30`, `DER length mismatch`, `Expected integer tag 0x02 for R`/`S`, `R length overflow`, `S length missing`, `S length overflow` and `Checksig format too short` are gone). No public type or signature changes.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#842)

The reference (`ts-stack@edf6e03`) is followed verdict for verdict and word for word at `Signature.fromDER`, `TransactionSignature.fromChecksigFormat` (`TransactionSignature.ts:460-472`), `SignedMessage.verify` (`SignedMessage.ts:65-105`) and, after `fromDER`, `BSM.verify` (`BSM.ts:71-74`). Stated: R or S past 32 bytes at `from_der` (the row in the root `CLAUDE.md`). The interpreter's judge under a word is bitcoin-sv v1.2.2, its lax parse ported; its default the reference's `Spend`, whose verdicts on the lone zero and the long values it now gives (recorded). Stated, on this line only: two words of the interpreter differ from the recording where the verdict agrees. An S past 32 bytes at version 1 without a word is refused in `The signature must have a low S value.` where the reference's wrapper says `The signature format is invalid.` (beta conforms the version-1 wrapper by #417, not on this line), and under a word the CHECKMULTISIG sites refuse a signature BIP 66 refuses in `<op> requires correct encoding for the public key and signature.` where beta gives the encoding check's own words (#657, not on this line). `ProtoWallet::verify_signature` reads the DER with no argument check ahead of it (the reference's `isCanonicalDERSignature`, `validationHelpers.ts:1795-1801`, is beta's), so a refused shape is `InvalidSignature` in `fromDER`'s words here.

### Fixed: the ratchet tool reads a manifest's name and version by `cargo metadata`, not by a line scanner; `materialize` is pinned by the scratch lock it writes (cherry-picked from beta `f97e94f6`, PR #865)

- The follow-up to 0.8.5's ratchet entry (the cold reads of PR #859 and of PR #865). `package_of` (`tools/ratchet/src/tree.rs`) runs `cargo +1.95.0 metadata --no-deps --offline --format-version 1` on the scratch copy's `Cargo.toml` and takes the package whose `manifest_path` is that manifest; the line scanner of `Cargo.toml`, wrong on some valid manifests, is deleted. No dependency is added and `tools/ratchet/Cargo.lock` does not change. What cargo refuses stops in cargo's words. The tests (28 in the tool on this line; beta's 30 count two `model.rs` tests of another commit) run `materialize` on a Git repository each test builds and read the scratch `Cargo.lock` it writes. Tool and records only; nothing under `src/` moved.

### Fixed: fee(.., ChangeDistribution::Random) over two or more change outputs: a debug panic, and in release every change output but the last written 0 (a change of 2 or more; a change of 1 went to the first change output, save a debug panic over three or more) (#868)

- What was wrong. `Transaction::benford_number` computed `(1.0 + 1.0 / d).log10() / 1_f64.log10()`, a division by zero: the factor infinite, `(range * factor) as u64` saturating to `u64::MAX` for any range above zero, then `min + u64::MAX` with `min` 1. The reference divides by `Math.log10(10)`, one (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:894-897`). Every tag from `v0.3.1` to `v0.8.5` carries it. `fee(.., ChangeDistribution::Random)` reaches it with two or more change outputs (with one, `distribute_change` writes the change to it without the call). The reach is a caller's own choice; no peer's bytes reach it.
- What a run showed, on `origin/beta` (`460e6201`, and again at `f97e94f6`) and on the published `bsv-rs = "=0.8.5"` from crates.io (a scratch project, its own target), the same: in a debug build an overflow panic at the add (`attempt to add with overflow`, `src/transaction/transaction.rs:1676:9` on beta, `bsv-rs-0.8.5/src/transaction/transaction.rs:1549:9` published); in a release build the add wraps, `1 + u64::MAX` is 0, so every change output but the last is written 0 and the last takes the whole change (`n 2, change 12345: output 0 holds 0, not a Benford portion of 12345 ([0, 12345])`): no output of `u64::MAX` reaches the transaction, the sum is the change, and the distribution is no distribution. The issue's "u64::MAX" is the cast's value before the wrap.
- The fix, the random arm of the reference's `#distributeChange` (`Transaction.ts:864-897`) line by line (`docs/lanes/fix-868-benford.md` has the table): the divisor `log10(10)`; the minimum 0, where it was 1 (so a change below the output count leaves outputs at 0, as there: change 1 over 3 is `[0, 0, 1]`; with a minimum of 1, `benford_number(1, 0)` would have underflowed at `max - min` once the change ran out); `floor` as `Math.floor`; each change output but the last a portion of what remains, the last what is left. The random digit is drawn by `rand`'s `gen_range(1..=9)` where the reference takes `Random(1)[0] % 9 + 1`, by necessity. The equal arm is unchanged here (its remainder is the parity note's).
- The class (rule 5): `fee`'s and `get_fee`'s input and output totals were unchecked `+=` on a caller's amounts (a debug panic past `u64`; in release a wrap, so `fee` saw a change of 0 and removed the change outputs, `get_fee` answered a wrapped fee); they are refused now as `TransactionError` in the reference's `addSatoshiAmount` words, `Transaction input total exceeds the maximum valid monetary range.` and `Transaction output total exceeds the maximum valid monetary range.` (`Transaction.ts:80-86`; one helper, `transaction::amount::add_amount`). `total_output_satoshis` returns a `u64` and saturates where `.sum()` panicked in a debug build.
- The tests. `tests/transaction_fee_random_change_868.rs` (6): the random distribution over 2, 3 and 5 change outputs, 2,000 runs per cell at changes of 12,345, 2e15, the count, 2, 1 and 0: no panic, every amount within the change, the amounts summing to the change (inputs less the other outputs less the fee), each but the last the reference's `floor(remaining * log10(1 + 1/d))` for some digit, the last what remains, `get_fee` the fee; no change removing the change outputs; a change below the output count fixed at the reference's answer; the four overflow cells. On `origin/beta` (`f97e94f6`) 6 of 6 RED in debug (five tests panic in the crate, `attempt to add with overflow` at four sites, `transaction.rs:1676:9`, `:1591:13`, `:1598:17`, `:1693:13`, and one fails an assertion, `left: [1, 0]`, `right: [0, 1]`) and 5 of 6 in release (the no-panic sum test passes there: the wrap keeps the sum); the published 0.8.5 the same in both.
- Migration. No signature moved. A caller of `Random` gets a distribution (it got a debug panic, or zeros and the whole change last, or with a change of 1 the whole change first); a caller of `fee` or `get_fee` whose input or output total passes `u64` gets `Err(TransactionError)` where it got a debug panic or a wrapped total: keep the amounts within `u64` (no valid transaction comes near it).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#868)

`distribute_change`'s random arm is the reference's at the pin, with the random digit's source the one difference (the reference's `Random(1)[0] % 9 + 1` weights the digits 1 to 4 at 29/256 and 5 to 9 at 28/256, `gen_range(1..=9)` uniform). Stated, older than #868 and not changed here (the fix kept to the random arm, for the stable line): the equal arm writes `change / n` to each change output and one satoshi more to each of the first `change % n` (5 over 3 is `[2, 2, 1]`), where the reference gives the remainder to the last (`[1, 1, 3]`, `Transaction.ts:886-892`); the reference's `fee` refuses inputs that cannot pay the outputs and the fee (`Transaction inputs are insufficient for the requested outputs and fee.`, `Transaction.ts:812-814,858-860`) where this crate's saturates the change to 0 and removes the change outputs, so `fee` answers `Ok` on a transaction that pays less than the fee asked or whose other outputs exceed its inputs (`get_fee` then 0), and bounds every amount and total at 21e14 satoshis (`requireSatoshiAmount`, `addSatoshiAmount`, `:68-86`) where this crate refuses a total only past `u64`; its `getFee` answers a negative fee where this crate's saturates to 0. go-sdk at `2ca481c` (`transaction/fees.go:21-63`) answers `not-implemented` for its random distribution, writes `change / n` to every change output with the remainder left to the fee, removes every change output when the change is below their count, and refuses insufficient inputs (`ErrInsufficientInputs`).

## [0.8.5] - 2026-11-10

### Fixed: the ratchet's library lock no longer goes stale when the crate's own version moves; a release commit is Cargo.toml and CHANGELOG.md alone on both lines

- What contradicted what. `RELEASING.md` steps 3 and 11 (3 and 17 on `beta`) and the `beta-born` job (`release_commit()` in `ci.yml`) admit a release commit of `Cargo.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md` alone. The ratchet's compiler counters build a scratch copy of the library with `tools/ratchet/library.Cargo.lock` in place and run cargo `--locked`; that lock records the crate's own version (`0.8.3` on `main`, `0.9.0-beta.7` on `beta`), so the version line of a release made it stale and the `ratchet` step stopped (`cargo clippy (pedantic, cognitive complexity >25) failed (exit status: 101); no measurement was recorded ... the library lock is stale`), and `docs/RATCHETS.md` asked for the lock's refresh in the same pull request, which the release-commit rule forbids. Met on PR #858, the 0.8.4 release commit on `main` (2026-11-10 18:49Z); beta's prerelease commits had touched the lock as a third file for the same reason, where `beta-born` does not run.
- The fix, in the tool. Where the scratch copy receives the lock (`tools/ratchet/src/tree.rs`, `lock_for_manifest`), the root package's `version` line is set to the version the scratch copy's `Cargo.toml` declares: the one `[[package]]` entry whose `name` is the manifest's package name and that carries no `source` line. None, or more than one, and the run stops naming what it found (`... has no root package bsv-rs (a [[package]] named bsv-rs without a source line) ...`; `... has 2 root packages bsv-rs (entries without a source line at lines 3, 7); exactly one is required`). Every other byte is the committed lock's, which this change does not edit; its own-version line is whatever it was at the last dependency refresh and is not read. A dependency added, removed or bumped still makes the lock stale and still stops with the message it did.
- The tests. Six in `tools/ratchet/src/tree.rs`: the own version moved (a patch, a prerelease, a longer string with build metadata) differs from the committed lock in that one line alone; no root entry and two root entries stop in the words above; an entry named `bsv-rs` with a `source` line is left alone (either order); a planted dependency moves no other line; the manifest's version read from its `[package]` table alone. Five RED with the change removed (the committed lock written as is), two RED with the `source` condition dropped. Live, from `git archive` copies: `0.9.0-beta.8` in `Cargo.toml` on the base stops stale and on the tip passes and records what the unedited tip records; a planted `semver = "1"` on the tip still stops stale.
- Nothing under `src/` moved.

### Fixed: Transaction::from_binary and from_hex refuse bytes after the transaction, as the reference does; they were kept and hashed into the txid (cherry-picked from beta `7df16cf6`, PR #841, issue #840)

- What was wrong. `Transaction::from_binary(bytes)` and `Transaction::from_hex(hex)` read one transaction from the front of the input, never checked that the input ended there, and kept the WHOLE input as the cached serialization. For block 170's transaction (275 bytes) followed by four bytes: `Ok`, the inputs and outputs read correctly; `to_binary()` 279 bytes and `to_hex()` 558 digits; `hash()` and `id()` the hash of all 279 bytes (`a10aefc1...` on the issue's probe, where the transaction is `f4184fc5...`; the captain's run on this line's `8729f8a5`, 0.8.3, the same). `from_ef`, `from_hex_ef` and `parse_script_offsets` read a prefix too (no cache: the EF transaction's id was its own; `parse_script_offsets` never read the lock time, so it accepted a transaction without one). The reader's lines are the original implementation's: every published version carries them.
- The reach. Any door handing bytes or hex it did not frame itself to these readers and then using `id()`, `to_binary()` or `to_hex()`, `Transaction::from_json`'s `hex` member among them; no `src/` door outside `transaction` calls them, and the BEEF readers frame each transaction before they parse it (`BeefTx::from_reader` reads through `Transaction::from_reader` and keeps the bytes it consumed). One crate-only state moves: a `BeefTx::from_raw_tx` (or `Beef::merge_raw_tx`) handed raw bytes with a byte after the transaction was parsed, its txid the hash of all the bytes; it is now held unparsed (no `tx()`, no input txids), its txid still the hash of the bytes given, as before. The reference's `BeefTx` does not refuse such bytes at construction either: it keeps them, reads its input txids from the prefix (`BeefTx.ts:24-54`) and hashes all of them into its txid (`:110-113`); only its lazy `tx` getter refuses them (`:118-121`, `fromBinaryView`). This line's `from_raw_tx` returns no `Result`, so it cannot refuse without a break (beta refuses at its doors since #817). Every verdict door refuses such an entry since #852's fold (the next section); `to_binary` writes the bytes as given, the byte after the transaction included, as 0.8.3 did.
- The fix. `from_binary` and `from_hex` refuse a byte after the lock time as `Error::TransactionError("Serialized transaction contains trailing data")`, the reference's words (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Transaction.ts:532-535`, `fromBinaryView`; `fromHex` through it, `:548-553`); the cached serialization is the transaction's bytes alone, the hex cache its hex. `from_ef` and `from_hex_ef` refuse in `Serialized EF transaction contains trailing data` (`:419`); `parse_script_offsets` reads the lock time and refuses what follows in the transaction words (`:460-462`). `Transaction::from_reader(&mut Reader)` is public, the reference's `fromReader` (`:466-468`): one transaction from the front of the reader, the rest left unread, the transaction holding no copy of the reader's bytes (its serialization and txid computed from its fields). The crate-private `from_reader_internal` is gone; `BeefTx::from_reader` calls `from_reader`. On this line `from_reader`, the two refusal texts and `refuse_trailing` live in `src/transaction/transaction_reader.rs`, a child file, because the ratchet holds `transaction.rs` at its 3,000 lines of 0.8.3 (beta keeps them in `transaction.rs`); its rustdoc gains an `# Errors` section, so the pedantic count holds at 2,722.
- The tests. `tests/transaction_trailing_data_840.rs` (15) against `tests/vectors/transaction_trailing_data_840.json` (30 cells, ten 53-bit cells and two writer cells; `tests/support/transaction_trailing_data_840.mjs`, the reference under Node v22.18.0, two runs byte-identical), taken from beta unchanged: `a_transaction_followed_by_bytes_is_refused_840` and its siblings for hex, EF, JSON and the script offsets; the clean transaction's id, bytes and hex unchanged; the reader form; three cells refused on both sides in other words, stated. On a scratch copy of this line's `8729f8a5` with the test, the vector and a `pub` on `from_reader` overlaid, 5 of 15 RED: `fromBinary plus_one_byte: Ok with id 9529fd4a...`, `fromHex plus_one_byte` the same, `fromJson plus_four_bytes: Ok with id b5f0b327...`, `fromEF plus_one_byte: Ok with id f4184fc5...`, the offsets `Ok`; the five 53-bit pins and the other five green there, as on beta's base. `fuzz_transaction_parser` asserts that a transaction `from_binary` returns serializes to exactly its buffer, its fields to the same bytes and txid, that the reader form's bytes are the prefix it read, that `from_hex` of the buffer's hex in either case agrees with `from_binary`, that a transaction `from_ef` returns writes the buffer back through `to_ef` and its plain bytes read back to its txid, and that `from_hex_ef` agrees with `from_ef`.
- Not in this patch. The stable line keeps its documented `invalidate_caches` contract (#843): a hand edit of a public field (`version`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `lock_time`) of a transaction `from_binary` or `from_hex` returned still answers the parsed bytes from `id()`, `to_binary()` and `to_hex()` until `invalidate_caches()` is called, where the reference checks its cache against the fields at every read; the cache this patch writes is the transaction's bytes alone, so the read is true until such an edit. `Signature::from_der`'s lenient reader (#842) and the input txid text `from_json` takes (#845) are 0.8.5's (#849).
- Migration. A caller that passed a transaction followed by other bytes to `from_binary`, `from_hex`, `from_ef`, `from_hex_ef`, `from_json` or `parse_script_offsets` now gets an `Err` and must pass the transaction alone; to read a transaction from the front of a longer buffer, use `Transaction::from_reader(&mut bsv_rs::primitives::Reader::new(bytes))` and read `reader.remaining()` after it. A caller that tried `from_binary` first and fell back to `from_ef` for EF bytes now reaches the fallback. `from_reader` is an addition (no signature changes).

### Fixed: a BEEF entry whose raw bytes are not exactly one transaction is never answered valid (#852's fold of #840 on the stable line)

- What was wrong, in two parts. Through 0.8.3, an entry built by `Beef::merge_raw_tx` (or `BeefTx::from_raw_tx`) from raw bytes that are not one transaction was answered valid by `sort_txs`, `verify_structure`, `verify_valid` and `is_valid` in two ways. When no transaction could be read from the bytes at all (a transaction cut short, bytes that are no transaction, no bytes), the entry listed no input, so its parents were never asked about. When the bytes began with a transaction, they were read as that prefix under the hash of all the bytes, so the entry was valid whenever the prefix's parents were present and proven, and always when it carried a BUMP index. #840's port as built at a pre-squash commit of `ed2789fb` held the suffixed bytes unparsed with no input, and so answered them valid with their parents absent too. On `8729f8a5` and a pre-squash commit of `ed2789fb` the table below answers 50 of its 66 non-exact cells valid.
- The invariant. On this line, an entry of a BEEF built from raw bytes is a transaction only if its bytes are exactly one transaction by the strict parse (`Transaction::from_binary`). An entry held unparsed is never answered valid by `sort_txs`, `verify_structure`, `verify_valid` or `is_valid` (with either argument), whatever its shape and whether or not it carries a BUMP index, nor by anything that stands on them. This is the verdict 0.9.0 gives by refusing such bytes at construction (#817); a patch line cannot change `from_raw_tx`'s signature, so here the refusal is at the verdict.
- The kinds. `verify_structure` names the streaming reader's kind for the same bytes: `Kind::TrailingBytes` for a transaction followed by more; `Kind::BadVarint` when the bytes end inside a varint or hold a non-canonical one; `Kind::Truncated` when they end inside a fixed field or a script (pinned at every cut of block 170's transaction against `verify_stream_structure`, `the_held_kind_is_the_stream_kind_at_every_cut_852`). It is answered in the pass that answers `NoInputs` and `NoOutputs`, in the order `NoInputs`, the held kind, `NoOutputs`: a held entry whose version is followed by an input count of 0 stays `NoInputs`, as 0.8.3 named it. `sort_txs` puts a held entry in `not_valid` before its proof is asked, so one with a BUMP index never enters the valid set, and a child that names it falls to `not_valid` through the existing walk. Under an atomic subject the held kind wins over the atomic rule's refusal (`verify_structure` answers it before the atomic rule's verdict). `merge_beef` carries the held bytes forward, and the merged BEEF is refused alike. On 0.8.3 (`8729f8a5`) `tx()`, `tx_mut()` and `find_atomic_transaction` returned the prefix's transaction in the cells with bytes after a transaction (`tx()` and `find_atomic_transaction` in the 20 of them without the entry's own BUMP, which left the bytes unparsed until `tx_mut()`); since #840's port they return `None`. `Transaction::from_beef`, `from_atomic_beef` and `verify_stream` refused on both trees. Each keeps a cell.
- The tests. `tests/beef_held_entry_852.rs` (6) holds a table of 72 cells: twelve shapes by six states, every door asserted. The shapes are the control (exactly one transaction, whose verdicts equal 0.8.3's in every state), a transaction followed by one byte, four bytes and itself, four cuts, 3 and 40 bytes that are no transaction, no bytes, and a transaction of no input followed by a byte. The states are parent absent, parent present and proven, the entry's own BUMP, the atomic subject, the parent of a child, and merged into another BEEF. The doors are `sort_txs` for the entry and its child, `verify_structure`, `verify_valid`, `is_valid(false)`, `is_valid(true)`, `to_binary` then `Beef::from_binary`, `to_binary` then `Transaction::from_beef`, `verify_stream_structure`, `verify_stream` and `find_atomic_transaction`. The fixtures are block 170's transaction and block 9's coinbase, written by this crate's writer. The table runs against `tests/vectors/beef_held_entry_852.json` (`tests/support/beef_held_entry_852.mjs`, the reference at `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.23.3, two runs byte-identical): for every cell that is not one transaction, the reference's end-to-end answer is a refusal too (`mergeRawTx` or `mergeBeef` throws, or `fromBinaryStrict` refuses the BEEF it writes), so this crate's structural verdict is the reference's round-trip verdict. On a scratch copy of a pre-squash commit of `ed2789fb` four of the six tests fail (the table's, the stated cells', the `is_valid` field's and the order's) and 66 of the 72 cells; on `8729f8a5` five of the six tests fail and the same 66 cells; the six controls pass on both. The table's state of the entry's own BUMP index is the witness of a held entry under a BUMP index: on this patch, `verify_structure` made to skip the held kind under a BUMP index turns 10 cells red, every shape of that state that is not one transaction, the transaction of no input aside. Three more pin a held entry's `is_valid` field after `sort_txs` (`Some(false)`), the order and fields `verify_structure` leaves (those of `sort_txs`), and a BUMP whose root does not compute refused ahead of a held entry (`MissingSibling`, as the stream meets the BUMPs before the transactions). A unit test, `the_held_kind_is_exactly_the_strict_parse_refusal_852`, holds the predicate to the strict parse, with and without a BUMP index, and its kind to the stream's, over 676,313 inputs: every single-byte change, cut, one-byte extension, insertion and deletion of the 11 transactions of `tests/transaction/vectors/{tx_valid,bigtx,beef_cross_sdk}.rs` and the recording, and 4,096 strings from a fixed seed. `sort_txs` and `verify_structure` read that one predicate (`BeefTx::strict_read`, crate-private). `fuzz_beef_parser` asserts the same through every door: `verify_structure`, `sort_txs` alone (the entry in `not_valid`, its `is_valid` field false), and `is_valid` and `verify_valid` under a BUMP index over the entry's own hash.
- Cost. One parse per raw entry without a parsed transaction, as before: a `verify_valid` of n proven raw entries makes n parses on `8729f8a5`, on a pre-squash commit of `ed2789fb` and here (the one predicate is that parse, `NoOutputs` read from it, and `verify_structure` hands the sort the held entries it found); a `sort_txs` called alone now parses each proven raw entry that holds no parsed transaction, and so does `to_binary` through it (a review's run on 2026-11-10, release, the median of five, 2,000 raw entries each carrying a BUMP index: `sort_txs` alone 0.90 ms on `8729f8a5`, 0.91 ms on a pre-squash commit of `ed2789fb`, 1.24 ms here; `to_binary` 1.38, 1.43, 1.76 ms). Measured in release, five runs each, the median `verify_valid` of 2,000 raw entries each carrying a BUMP index: 3.02 ms on `8729f8a5`, 3.00 ms on a pre-squash commit of `ed2789fb`, 3.02 ms here; of 2,000 unproven chained entries: 1.16, 1.15, 1.14 ms.
- Migration. A caller merges `tx.to_binary()`; bytes from a stranger are checked with `Transaction::from_binary` before `merge_raw_tx`. A BEEF that held such an entry and was answered valid is now refused by `sort_txs` (the entry and every child that names it in `not_valid`), `verify_structure` (the kind above), `verify_valid` and `is_valid` (`valid: false`); 0.9.0 refuses the same bytes at construction. A caller that matched a kind sees another in two cells that 0.8.3 already refused: a transaction with bytes after it and its parents absent was `InputNamesNoElement` (its prefix's input missing; `sort_txs` listed it in `with_missing_inputs`) and is `TrailingBytes`; an atomic subject from whose bytes no transaction can be read was `UnrelatedTransaction` and is its held kind. No public item, signature or field changes.
- Not in this patch. The writers (`to_binary`, `to_hex`, `to_binary_atomic`) still write held bytes as given: they return no `Result` on this line and cannot refuse, and no verdict door calls such a BEEF valid. #843, #842 and #845, as the entry above says.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#852)

The reference keeps the same bytes and its `verifyValid` reads them as their prefix. `mergeRawTx` builds a `BeefTx` from them unchecked (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Beef.ts:842-846`), against its constructor's own precondition ("If `number[]` must be a valid serialized transaction", `BeefTx.ts:179-180`). The entry's input txids come from a scan of the prefix (`:24-49,52-54`), skipped under a BUMP index (`:200-201`), and its txid is the hash of all the bytes (`:110-113`). `verifyValid` (`Beef.ts:1054-1088`) never asks for the lazy `tx` getter that would refuse them (`BeefTx.ts:118-121`). So it answers valid for a suffixed entry whose prefix's parents are present and proven, and for any bytes under a BUMP index whose BUMP carries their hash; the scan throws at construction for bytes it cannot read without an index. Its own `tx` getter, `fromBinaryStrict` and `Transaction.fromBEEF` refuse the same BEEF, and its `mergeBeef`, which writes and strictly re-reads, throws on it. This crate gives the reference's end-to-end verdict at the structural door; the 23 recorded cells where `verifyValid` alone answers valid are the stated divergence, counted in the test. go-sdk at `2ca481c` never holds unparsed bytes: `MergeRawTx` parses a prefix, keeps that prefix's own txid, and errors on bytes it cannot read, with or without a BUMP index (`transaction/beef.go:820-848`). BRC-62's field table gives the raw field as "RawTx bytes as in standard format BRC-12" with no length field before it and the `Has BUMP` byte after it (`0062.md:67-68`), so the field ends where the transaction's parse ends.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#840)

The reference refuses at each door this crate now refuses, in the same words where they are recorded (`fromBinary`, `fromHex`, `fromEF`, `fromHexEF`, `parseScriptOffsets`), and reads a prefix only through `fromReader`, as `from_reader` does. Three cells refuse on both sides in other words, older than #840: a hex text of odd length is `InvalidHex` here (the `hex` crate), where the reference pads it with a leading zero and fails reading the shifted bytes (`Number can only safely store up to 53 bits` for the transaction, `Invalid EF marker` for EF; `utils.ts` `hexToUint8Array`); a BEEF followed by bytes is refused by `from_beef` in the stream's words (`TrailingBytes`, 0.4.2) where the reference says `Serialized BEEF contains trailing data`; a transaction without its lock time is this crate's `ReaderUnderflow` where the reference's readers say `Reader read exceeds available data` over a `number[]` (`fromEF`, `parseScriptOffsets` and a `fromReader` handed a `Reader`; `parseScriptOffsets` on a `number[]` the recorded cell) and `ReaderUint8Array read exceeds available data` over a `Uint8Array`, which `fromBinary`, `fromHex` and `fromHexEF` always read (`ReaderUint8Array.ts:13-19,46`, `Transaction.ts:523-536,562-564`). go-sdk at `2ca481c`: `NewTransactionFromBytes` refuses a byte after the frame (`used != len(b)`, `nLockTime length must be 4 bytes long`, `transaction/transaction.go:56-67`, `errors.go:10`), and reads EF through the same door (`ReadFrom` detects the marker, `:81-140`); `NewTransactionFromHex` decodes then calls it (`:45-53`), an odd-length text refused by `encoding/hex` as here; `NewTransactionFromStream` and `ReadFrom` are its prefix readers (`:72-81`), as `from_reader` is here.

One cell older than #840 is stated (#844 conforms it on beta): an amount of 2^53 satoshis or more. The reference reads an output's amount, and an EF input's source amount, through `readUInt64LEBn().toNumber()` (`Transaction.ts:388,409,497`) and refuses it in `Number can only safely store up to 53 bits` (`BigNumber.ts:628`) at `fromBinary`, `fromHex`, `fromReader` and `fromEF`; this crate reads a `u64` at every reader and answers `Ok`, the id the hash of the bytes, as go-sdk does (`transaction/output.go:29,53`). No such transaction is valid at the node (`MAX_MONEY`, 21,000,000 BSV, bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 `amount.h:130`; `bad-txns-vout-toolarge` in `CheckTransactionCommon`, `validation.cpp:548-551`; its parser reads the amount as an `int64_t`, `amount.h:18,107-112`, so 2^64 - 1 is -1 there, `bad-txns-vout-negative`, `:543-546`). The reference's writer refuses such a number before any byte (`The number is larger than 2 ^ 53 (unsafe)`, `BigNumber.ts:462`, through `writeUInt64LE`, `Transaction.ts:1083`), recorded for #844 (`writer_53`). Pinned by `an_output_of_two_to_the_53_satoshis_is_read_where_the_reference_refuses_840` and its siblings.

Two prefix readers outside `transaction` are not changed here: `Signature::from_der` reads the DER sequence its length byte names and ignores bytes after it, where the reference's `Signature.fromDER` refuses them (`Signature DER invalid`, `primitives/Signature.ts:64-65`), so a signature parsed from a buffer with a suffix verifies as the signature alone where it is parsed without the wallet's canonical-DER check first (`messages::verify`, whose signature is the bytes after the key ID, `src/messages/signed.rs:191-193`; `compat::bsm::verify_message_der`): #842, the stable line's 0.8.5 (#849); `primitives::bsv::sighash::parse_transaction` reads a transaction's fields from the front and ignores what follows (no cache, no txid; no reference twin), so a sighash over such bytes is the prefix transaction's.

### Changed: `Documentation` runs in `ci.yml` on every pull request and push; a tag's call skips the benchmark comparison (cherry-picked from beta `a67ea411`, PR #524, issue #515)

Two CI facts, taken from `beta` by `git cherry-pick -x`, no code. A Release run
on `beta` failed rustdoc on an unresolved intra-doc link that two reviewed pull
requests had let through: `Documentation` lived in `docs.yml`, which no pull
request and no push starts. The job moves back into `ci.yml` with no
condition, so it runs on pull requests, pushes, dispatches and the Release
workflow's call; its command is unchanged (`cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`
under `RUSTDOCFLAGS: -Dwarnings`), and `docs.yml` keeps `actionlint` alone.
`tests/arch_ci_pr_runs_the_required_set.rs` names `Documentation` in
`REQUIRED_ON_MAIN` (13 contexts) and `REQUIRED_ON_BETA` (12), the intended
protection, not the live one: the captain adds the context to `main`'s
protection only after the job has reported green on `main`, reads it back, and
adds it to the sequencer's required-check list.

`bench.yml`'s `Benchmark Regression Check` refuses a caller on a `refs/tags/`
ref (`if: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}`): a reusable workflow
sees its caller's ref, and on a tag's call the comparison measured the runner's
load. A branch dispatch still compares the commit with the last release tag
before it; `Benchmarks Build` and the `scoreboard` still run on every tag.
`documentation_is_a_pr_and_push_gate_with_warnings_denied` and
`benchmark_comparisons_skip_tags_and_allow_branch_dispatches_and_pr_callers`
pin the two.

### Changed: a push runs exactly the required set; the measurements run on dispatch and before every tag, each in its own workflow with its own badge (the owner's word of 2026-10-27)

The owner's word at 20:1xZ, 2026-10-27, through the keeper: "sick of seeing
all these CI failures... why are none of them passing... they are all so
hardcore and slowing us down". The keeper's read: beta's last push run was red
on the Benchmark Regression Check alone, a job that judges the runner's load,
not the commit. The keeper's ruling, the balance: a push to `beta` or `main`
runs exactly the required set, the same contexts as a pull request to that
line, nothing more; every job that judges something other than the commit runs
on `workflow_dispatch` and once before a tag, each in its own workflow with its
own badge, never on the push run; the README badge points at the required-set
workflow on `main`; a cancelled run under the concurrency rule is never a red.
Nothing is lost: the measurements still run before every tag.

`ci.yml` keeps the required set (`Test Suite (ubuntu-latest, stable)`,
`Clippy`, `Rustfmt`, `vectors`, `deny`, `ratchet`, `fixtures`, `secrets`,
`wasm32 (combined)`, `main-in-beta` on beta, `dependents` on main, `semver` and
`beta-born` on a pull request), the context names unchanged. Two of the
required jobs read a pull request and cannot run on a push: `semver` (the
base's last tag) and `beta-born` (the PR's commits). The five other test cells
(macOS, Windows, the beta toolchain) run on a dispatch of `ci.yml` (the
nightly's `ci-full` on each line, the sync's) and on a tag's call. The
dependents jobs stay in `ci.yml`, since `dependents` is required on `main` and
a called workflow's job reports as `<caller> / <name>`; they leave beta's push
and run on a dispatch on either line and on every tag. The new workflows, each
with `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`:

- `bench.yml`: `Benchmark Regression Check`, `Benchmarks Build` and the
  `scoreboard` (its `needs` now the two bench jobs; it reads artifacts, as
  before). On `main` the bench jobs keep main's bodies: main has no
  `tools/bench-compare` and no `benches/baseline.json`, so no record input and
  no corpus secret; `Benchmarks Build` is `cargo bench --no-run`, and the
  critcmp regression check, which compared a pull request's base and head and
  ran on beta's ref alone, compares the commit with the last release tag
  before it (a `-beta.` tag never, a tag never with itself).
- `msrv.yml`: `msrv`.
- `features.yml`: `features` (each feature alone) and the five wasm32 slices
  other than the required `wasm32 (combined)` (`wasm32 (watchtower)`,
  `(monitor)`, `(chaintracks)`, `(overlay)`, `(relay)`).
- `machete.yml`: `unused dependencies` (non-blocking, as before).
- `docs.yml`: `Documentation` (rustdoc) and `actionlint`, the checks of the text.

`release.yml` calls `ci.yml` and the five on every version tag (main's are
plain `vX.Y.Z`). The publish waits for `ci.yml`, `docs.yml`, `msrv.yml`,
`features.yml` and `machete.yml`, as it waited for those jobs inside `ci.yml`.
`bench.yml` runs beside the publish and does not hold it: a red there is the
runner's as often as the commit's, and it shows on the tag's run and the badge.
Before this change a tag's call skipped the regression check. `nightly.yml` is
unchanged: it is dispatch-only (the entry below) and not callable, so
`RELEASING.md` step 3 names its dispatch before a minor tag.

| Job (context) | Pull request | Push to `beta` | Push to `main` | Dispatch | Before a tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Test Suite (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `Clippy`, `Rustfmt`, `vectors`, `deny`, `ratchet`, `fixtures`, `secrets`, `wasm32 (combined)` | yes | yes | yes | yes (`ci.yml`) | yes |
| the other five `Test Suite` cells | no | no | no | yes (`ci.yml`) | yes |
| `main-in-beta` | into `beta` | yes | no | on `sync/main-into-beta` | no |
| `semver`, `beta-born` | `semver` both; `beta-born` into `main` | no | no | no | `semver` on `main` (against the release before it, #214) |
| `Plan pinned dependents`, `dependent (<id>)`, `dependents` | into `main` | no (was yes) | yes | yes (`ci.yml`) | yes |
| `Benchmark Regression Check` | no | no (was yes) | no | yes (`bench.yml`) | yes, not holding the publish (was skipped) |
| `Benchmarks Build`, `scoreboard` | no | no (was yes) | no (was yes) | yes (`bench.yml`) | yes, not holding the publish |
| `msrv` | no | no (was yes) | no (was yes) | yes (`msrv.yml`) | yes |
| `features`, the other five `wasm32 (...)` | no | no (was yes) | no (was yes) | yes (`features.yml`) | yes |
| `unused dependencies` | no | no (was yes) | no (was yes) | yes (`machete.yml`) | yes |
| `Documentation`, `actionlint` | no | no (was yes) | no (was yes) | yes (`docs.yml`) | yes |

The badges: README carries one per workflow, the required set's first. The
`CI` badge reads `ci.yml` with `?branch=main`, so a beta push in progress or
cancelled never shows there. The five measurement badges read their
workflow's latest run on the default branch. `ci.yml`'s concurrency group
stays per event and ref (`ci-<event>-<ref>`, without the record mark now that
the record input is `bench.yml`'s). A newer push cancels the run it
supersedes, and that cancelled run is never a red: the newer run judges the
same line.

`tests/arch_ci_pr_runs_the_required_set.rs` pins it. A push to each line runs
exactly its required set less `semver` and `beta-born`
(`a_push_to_beta_runs_exactly_betas_required_set`,
`a_push_to_main_runs_exactly_mains_required_set`, both RED on the previous
`ci.yml`, which named every leaving job, the Benchmark Regression Check among
them). A dispatch on each line and a tag's call run every job and the six test
cells. Each measurement workflow is triggered by dispatch and call alone, and
`release.yml` calls it (`the_measurements_run_on_dispatch_and_before_a_tag_never_on_a_push`).
Three edits are refused: the dependents back on beta's push, `semver` on a
push (on `main` the edit removes main's condition, which also admits a tag's
call), an unrequired job on the push run. The evaluator reads `startsWith`.
Nothing under `src/` changes. `CLAUDE.md` (rule 7, the layout),
`RELEASING.md` (steps 2, 3, 5), `README.md`, `docs/NIGHTLY.md`,
`docs/RATCHETS.md` and `benches/CLAUDE.md` say so.

### Changed: the oracles run on demand, the nightly schedule removed (the owner's word of 2026-10-27)

The owner's fleet word of 2026-10-27: the nightly runs were a waste of
resources. The `schedule` trigger is gone from `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`
on both lines (the 03:00 UTC cron of #283 and #284 and its cap are moot);
`workflow_dispatch` stays, so the mutation shards, the fuzz hours, the
scoreboard and `ci.yml`'s full set on each line run when asked: one dispatched
measurement before each minor tag, none for a prerelease. The push matrix on
the protected branches is unchanged (the rule of 2026-10-26). `docs/NIGHTLY.md`
says so. The port of beta's ed1eccb (PR #351).

### Changed: CI's concurrency group carries the event, so a dispatch and a push to one ref never cancel each other

`ci.yml`'s concurrency group was `ci-<ref>`: a `workflow_dispatch` on `beta`
(the bench baseline's record mode, `bench_baseline_record`; the nightly's
dispatch of this workflow) shared the group with every push to `beta`, and
the first record run for #245 (2026-10-27 04:23Z, run 40449439162) was
cancelled by #306's landing twenty minutes in. The group is
`ci-<event>-[record-]<ref>` now: a push to a line cancels the earlier push's
run as before, a pull request's own ref keeps each PR in a group of its own,
a dispatch runs to its end beside a push and a pull request. On `beta` a
record dispatch also runs apart from the nightly's dispatch of the same line
(the group marks it); `main` has no record input and keys the group on the
event alone. The keeper's CI
rule (a pull request runs exactly its line's required
set) is untouched; the `arch_*` guards and `actionlint` pass. The port to
`main` is a `git cherry-pick -x` (RELEASING.md point 11).

### Changed: the nightly's heavy work holds at most six concurrent slots

The mutant shards run six at a time (`max-parallel: 6`, twenty before) and
the fuzz targets six at a time after them (`needs: [source, mutants]`, run
whatever the shards' result), so the night's heavy work never holds more
than six of the account's twenty concurrent slots and a pull request's run
at 03:00 UTC starts within minutes; the shards finish later in the night
and decide the same (the owner's balance rule of 2026-10-26, the keeper's
reading, as the nightly goes live with main's copy of the schedule).

### Changed: the secrets scan covers the commits the event brings (#272)

CI's `secrets` job ran gitleaks over every ref of the checkout (gitleaks's
`git` mode with no range, the checkout fetching every branch), so a
key-looking test literal on any pushed branch failed every pull request's
scan: PR #257 at 2026-10-26 16:46Z, the two findings being the #105
branch's witnesses, with no location printed. On a pull request the scan
now covers the PR's own commits (the base sha to `HEAD`, what decides the
merge; an empty base sha falls back to the line's history), on a push and
on a dispatch the line's full history, and `-v` prints a finding's location
with the value redacted. `tests/arch_secrets_scan_scope.rs` pins the step
(red on the old one). `.gitleaks.toml` judges the two literals by reason:
secp256k1's generator point in compressed form (the public key of the
private key 1, the #105 witnesses' identity key, also in the EC, sighash
and cross-SDK tests and the auth and overlay vectors) and the old revealer
shape's test key of `tests/wallet_http_json_shapes_105.rs` (the Go SDK's
test public key, also across the wallet-wire vectors), beside the BRC-56
vectors and the corpus-gen nonce.

### Changed: a pull request runs exactly its line's required set; the full matrix on a push and nightly

The owner's word of 2026-10-26, through the keeper: CI must pass and must not
put needless load on GitHub. The keeper's count that day: 215 workflow runs on
the account in 24 hours, 99 of them this crate's CI at 32 jobs each, 79
cancelled by concurrency. The merge queue already gives one CI run per PR, so
the jobs per run were what remained.

On a pull request a job of `ci.yml` now runs if and only if its context is
required on the base line's protection (beta's eleven, main's twelve): the
Test Suite matrix produces its `(ubuntu-latest, stable)` cell alone, `wasm32`
its `combined` consumer alone (the six consumers' features moved from
`include` rows to a step's table, so no row can add a cell), `dependents` with
`Plan pinned dependents` and each `dependent (<id>)` (the jobs it needs to
decide) only into `main`; `main-in-beta`, `beta-born` and `semver` as before.
`docs`, `actionlint`, `msrv`, `features`, `unused dependencies`, the other
five test cells, the other four wasm32 slices, `Benchmark Regression Check`,
`Benchmarks Build` and `scoreboard` no longer run on a pull request: a PR into
`beta` runs 11 jobs (32 before), into `main` 13 plus one per consumer the plan
admits. A push to `beta` or `main`, the sync's dispatch and a tag's call run
every job as before; `nightly.yml`'s new `ci-full` job dispatches `ci.yml` on
`beta` and on `main` each night (`nightly.yml` comes to `main` with it, as
`beta` writes it: GitHub fires a schedule from the default branch, `main`, so
its mutation and fuzz jobs start too, on `beta`'s sources), so each line's
own workflow runs its whole matrix at its tip whether or not anything was
pushed (a `workflow_call` from
the nightly would run the caller's ref, `main`'s on a schedule, and share its
concurrency group; a schedule on `ci.yml` fires on `main` alone).
`cancel-in-progress` is unchanged. On `main` the benchmarks job keeps its
body (`critcmp` of a pull request's base and head, which no other event
carries) and runs on `beta`'s ref alone, which `main`'s file never sees;
`beta`'s baseline record input is `beta`'s.

`tests/arch_ci_pr_runs_the_required_set.rs` pins it: the two lines' required
contexts as constants (read by `gh api
repos/Calhooon/bsv-rs/branches/<line>/protection/required_status_checks`), a
string-level reader of each job's `if:`, `needs:` and matrix, and the rule
both ways on each line (every required context proven to run on a PR into
it, no job outside the set and its needs able to run there), plus every job
on a push and on the nightly's dispatch save five named exceptions. A context
added to or dropped from a protection is a change to the test's constants.

### Fixed: a dead function under every slice without `script` (#115)

`after_last_code_separator` (`primitives/bsv/sighash.rs`) has one caller, the
script templates' signing path, but compiled under `primitives`, so a consumer
building `block`, `primitives`, `compat` or `totp` alone with warnings denied
(the Cloudflare workers' CI) could not build the crate. Found by the dependents
check (#83) on its first hosted run, on chaintracks-cloudflare's `block` slice.
The function is gated on `script`; the `clippy` job now checks each published
slice alone with `-D warnings`, which was RED on the pre-fix tree for the four
slices and is the pin.

### Changed: beta carries everything main carries, main nothing beta did not bear, checked by CI (the owner's word, 2026-10-25)

CI only; nothing under `src/` moves. A commit is on a line by sha, by patch
(`git cherry`), or by a cherry-pick link in either direction (a
`(cherry picked from commit <sha>)` line naming a commit of the other line).
`ci.yml` gains `main-in-beta`: on every PR into `beta`, every push to `beta`
and a dispatch on the sync branch it fails naming each commit of `origin/main`
the tree lacks that way; and `beta-born`: on every PR into `main` it fails
naming each commit of the PR `origin/beta` lacks that way, a release commit
(`Cargo.toml`'s version and `CHANGELOG.md`'s headings alone) let through and
said in the log. The new `sync-main-into-beta.yml` opens, on every push to
`main`, one PR from `sync/main-into-beta` into `beta`: each missing commit
`git cherry-pick -x`'d in main's order, landed by rebase merge (both lines
keep linear history; the link lives in the message). A conflicting pick is
aborted, the picks before it kept, the PR labelled `needs-hand` with the
commit and its files; a rerun picks onto a branch that holds beta's tip, so a
hand resolution survives main moving again. `ci.yml` gains `workflow_dispatch`
so the sync starts the suite on its branch. `RELEASING.md` steps 11 to 14
(beta's 17 to 20) write the rule; `tests/arch_ci_lines.rs` pins the three jobs.
On main this is PR #205's three commits by `git cherry-pick -x`: main's
`ci.yml` takes beta's `on:` (`[main, beta]` and `workflow_dispatch`), which
changes nothing a main event runs, since a beta event reads beta's file, and
keeps `main-in-beta`, which runs on nothing here, so the two files and the
test read the same on both lines.

### Added: the key bytes Certificate.toBinary writes for a subject or certifier key, as a public helper named for the operation (#610)

On the keeper's word of 2026-11-01 20:1xZ on the toolbox's ask (shape (2)):
`auth::certificates::certificate_key_bytes(text, field) -> Result<[u8; 33]>`
(`src/auth/certificates/to_binary_key.rs`, under `auth`) is the reference's
`Certificate.toBinary` on a `subject` or `certifier` text (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/auth/certificates/Certificate.ts:240-254`): the text taken as
given, never trimmed, `/^(02|03)[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/` in either case, else
`Invalid certificate <field>: expected compressed public key hex`; the decoded
bytes a key to `PublicKey.fromDER` (`assertCompressedPublicKey`, `:136-143`),
else `Invalid certificate <field>: expected a compressed secp256k1 public key`;
both `Error::CertificateValidationError`. It returns the 33 bytes `toBinary`
writes, so a compressed x at or above p that `fromDER` reduces to a point is
returned unreduced, as the reference writes it; a caller that needs the key
reads the bytes with `PublicKey::from_bytes`, which refuses that x (#183).
`read_to_binary_key` (#585) keeps its name and visibility, crate-private under
`identity`, and is the helper followed by `from_bytes` in the second sentence:
one definition, the identity parsers' reading and words unchanged.

Pinned against `tests/vectors/certificate_key_bytes_610.json`, written by
`tests/support/certificate_key_bytes_610.mjs` (a bun bundle of `mod.ts` at
`ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0; two runs byte-identical): for each of
the subject (an `03` key) and the certifier (an `02` key) 23 texts, #585's eight
and the shapes around them (the other prefix, mixed case, a leading space, a
trailing line break, empty, 64 and 68 digits, `0x`, the prefixes `04`, `05` and
`00` at compressed length, a non-hex and a non-ASCII character, x at p and the
largest x), each with the 33 bytes `toBinary(false)` writes or the words it
throws. `tests/auth_certificate_key_bytes_610.rs`: the helper's bytes equal the
reference's for the 12 accepted texts and its error the reference's for the 34
refused, and the same for the 16 `to_binary` outcomes of #585's vector, none
enumerated apart; an x above p and the largest x written unreduced and refused
by `from_bytes`. Compile-RED on `9640eaa7` (`E0432`, the helper absent); on a
scratch copy, 1 of 3 RED with the text rule cut to the length, 3 of 3 with the
point read by `from_bytes`; #585's three pins green unchanged.

Migration (bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs): drop `internalize_args::compressed_key` and
call `bsv_rs::auth::certificates::certificate_key_bytes(text, "subject")` (or
`"certifier"`) at the key sites, `PublicKey::from_bytes` on its bytes where a
key is held; the texts are unchanged. One input to read at those sites: a
compressed x at or above p whose reduction is a point is written, as `toBinary`
writes it, and `from_bytes` refuses its bytes.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#603)

The reference's `RPuzzle.lock` writes the value as `{ op: value.length, data:
value }` (`RPuzzle.ts:65`). Up to 76 bytes that is a minimal push, and this
crate's bytes are the same. From 77 bytes it is not the minimal push: at 77
the reference writes the value under an `OP_PUSHDATA2` whose length is 77 and at
78 under an `OP_PUSHDATA4` (non-minimal pushes of the value; 78 is read from
`Script.ts:553-560` and is not among the vector's lengths), and from 79 no push
at all, the opcode byte alone with the data dropped (`Script.ts:539-562`; at 256
the single byte `00`). This crate keeps the minimal push at every length,
`OP_PUSHDATA1` from 76 to 255 and `OP_PUSHDATA2` from 256, as the reference's
`Script.writeBin` does (`Script.ts:340-352`). The recorded vector pins both
answers at 0, 20, 32, 33, 75, 76, 77, 100, 255 and 256. An R value or its hash
is 20 to 33 bytes, so no puzzle that either SDK can spend crosses the gap.
The line is in CLAUDE.md's divergence list.
