### Fixed: the contacts manager reads a listed token as the reference's `PushDrop.decode` does, so its count, bounds and envelope refuse in the reference's order and words (#718)

- #717's rule read checked the shared canonical refusal against
  `decodeCanonicalPushDrop` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `PushDropValidation.ts:54-79`) at
  its five callers, but not the identity and contacts sites. None of those calls
  it; each reference counterpart reads with `PushDrop.decode` at its default
  position (`PushDrop.ts:63-121`, the second chunk never read) and runs its own
  checks. The four sites are read in `docs/lanes/fix-718.md`, with a table:
  the contacts manager's `authenticate_contact`
  (`#authenticateContactScript`, `ContactsManager.ts:431-466`), the identity
  revocation's lookup loop (`IdentityClient.ts:768-829`), and the two
  `ls_identity` parsers (the toolbox's `decodeIdentityOutput`,
  `identityUtils.ts:497-559`). Each site's limits equal its counterpart's: two
  fields; a contact ciphertext of 1 to 66,560 bytes and a signature of 8 to 80;
  an identity certificate of 1 to 262,144 bytes and a signature of 8 to 80.
- The contacts site differed. Its read was the canonical lock-before decode
  (`PushDrop::decode_before`), which refuses four kinds of token in its own
  words before the count, the bounds and the envelope: an empty script, a key
  alone, a `05` key, and a token without `OP_CHECKSIG` second. That is the
  issue's envelope-before-bounds class, in the decode's form.
  `authenticate_contact` now reads as the reference does, using the reference
  decode's own words for the read's refusals and `decode_reference_before`
  (#618's reading, crate-visible now) for the fields. A token without
  `OP_CHECKSIG` second with an oversized ciphertext is now refused as
  `contact ciphertext must contain 1-66560 bytes`; before, it was
  `Expected OP_CHECKSIG after pubkey`. The words reach no caller: the listing
  drops the output, and the update and removal replace the error with the
  reference's outer words, as before.
- The identity sites agree with the reference. Every refusal is a skip on both
  sides, and the revocation's run words are the reference's
  (`No authenticated revelation output matches the requested certificate.`).
  The parsers check the record before the envelope, where the toolbox checks
  the envelope first; no caller can see that order.
- The witness is `tests/vectors/identity_contacts_canonical_718.json`, written
  by `tests/support/identity_contacts_canonical_718.mjs` against the whole SDK
  at `edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0; two runs are byte-identical. It holds ten
  shapes, each with the reference's `getContacts` drop words and its
  revocation's run words. The tokens are built by this crate's PushDrop writer
  and pinned to the recorded SHA-256.
- The unit test `src/identity/contacts_auth_718_tests.rs` is RED on 8 of the 10
  shapes with the read put back to `decode_before`, and GREEN after.
  `tests/identity_contacts_canonical_718.rs` pins the agreement at the
  revocation, both parsers and the contacts listing; it is GREEN on both.
- No public API change.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#661)

Three texts this crate writes differ from the reference's, all older than #661
and unchanged by it (the `0`/`-1` and `OP_UNKNOWN<n>` texts stated against the
reference by this note and its row alone): `OP_0` and `OP_1NEGATE` are `0` and
`-1` here and `OP_0` and `OP_1NEGATE` there (go-sdk@2ca481c writes `OP_FALSE`
and `OP_1NEGATE`, `script/opcodes.go:545-546,625`, and its `NewFromASM` cannot
read `0` or `-1`, `script/script.go:46-63`), a public output of every script
holding them, open for the keeper's word; a direct push opcode without data is
`OP_UNKNOWN<n>` here and `undefined` there (`OP[op]`), neither reading back;
and #634's `OP_RETURN` writer, stated there (with empty data, #603 shard B's
bare `OP_RETURN` row). go-sdk holds no such chunk in a script:
`NewScriptFromScriptOps` (`script/script_chunk.go:119-163`) re-encodes a push
opcode's data as its minimal push (`01` with empty data is `00`, `03` with one
byte `01aa`, `OP_PUSHDATA1` with one byte `01aa`) and drops data on every other
opcode but `OP_RETURN`, whose data it appends before it stops, so its bytes
differ from the reference's and this crate's on 11 of the 24 shapes
(transcribed in the recorder, not run). The row is in `CLAUDE.md`'s divergence
list.

### Fixed: the `ls_identity` parsers read the output from the BEEF's subject, as the reference's discovery does (#721)

- #720's rule read found both `ls_identity` parsers
  (`parse_output_to_certificate`, `parse_output_to_verifiable_certificate`)
  taking the transaction of a lookup output's BEEF by `beef.txs.first()`. The
  reference's discovery (the toolbox's `IdentityEvidenceVerifier.parse`,
  `identityUtils.ts:600-612` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`) loads
  `beef.atomicTxid ?? beef.txs.at(-1)?.txid` through `findAtomicTransaction`
  and reads `outputIndex` on it (`TransactionEvidence.ts:110-127`), the rule of
  `Transaction.fromBEEF` and of this crate's `Transaction::from_beef(_, None)`,
  which the revocation already used. Every writer (TS 2, TS 3, this crate)
  lists parents first, so for a revelation whose own transaction is unproven
  (its BEEF carries a parent, proven or not) the parsers read the parent and
  skipped the token; and a
  BEEF listing the subject before its parent with no atomic header was read
  where the reference reads the parent and skips. Both parsers now read
  through `Transaction::from_beef(&output.beef, None)`; a BEEF it refuses is a
  skip. The table of shapes is `docs/lanes/fix-721.md`.
- The witness is `tests/vectors/identity_beef_subject_721.json`, written by
  `tests/support/identity_beef_subject_721.mjs` against #553's bundle (the SDK
  and the toolbox's `identityUtils.ts` at `edf6e03`, `parseEvidence`
  exported) under Node v22.18.0; two runs are byte-identical. Five shapes of
  one proven parent and one subject carrying the reference's revelation token
  (#553's), each with the bytes, the selected txid and `parseResults`' outcome.
  `tests/identity_beef_subject_721.rs` rebuilds each with this crate's BEEF
  writer to the recorded bytes and serves it through `resolve_by_attributes`
  and `discover_certificates`: RED on `0d8546c0` on 3 of 5 shapes (parent
  first, atomic parent first: skipped where the reference reads; subject first
  without a header: read where it skips), GREEN after; the lone subject and the
  atomic subject first agree on both.
- No public API change. The results of `resolve_by_identity_key`,
  `resolve_by_attributes`, `query`, `discover_certificates` and
  `discover_certificates_by_type` move for a multi-transaction BEEF: a
  revelation whose own transaction is unproven is now returned, and one listed
  before its parent in a non-atomic BEEF is now skipped. No error text changes.

`packages/sdk/src/transaction/TransactionEvidenceCoordinator.ts:184`), and

`src/identity/evidence.rs` is `parseEvidence` (`TransactionEvidence.ts:93-201`):

after the frame, as `fromBinaryStrict` does), at most 256 transactions, the

not ported: `tx.verify` on the admitted subject against the wallet's chain
tracker (`TransactionEvidenceCoordinator.ts:317-345`), so an unproven
ancestor's failing script, a BUMP root the tracker refuses or a coinbase proof

(`pendingTransactions`, `consumers`) are not ported either: one discovery
parses its outputs in turn. Where `Beef::from_binary` refuses bytes
`fromBinaryStrict` reads (#86's reserved forms), the output is skipped here.
The reference checks the lookup output's `txid` hint against the subject it
picked (`TransactionEvidence.ts:123-124`); `OutputListItem` carries no `txid`,
so a JSON answer whose `txid` disagrees with its BEEF's subject is skipped
there and read here (#735: the port is a public field, the owner's word).
The reference's `timeout` code comes from the coordinator's tracker verify,
unported, so this check has no timeout path.

### Fixed: `resolve_by_identity_key` reads every output of the lookup answer before it answers, keeps only the asked subject's certificates and returns the first one's identity, as the reference's wallet does (#737)

From the strength read of PR #733 (#730, 2026-11-04 02:2xZ), older than #730
and widened by it: `IdentityClient::resolve_by_identity_key` parsed
`outputs[0]` of the `ls_identity` answer alone, where the reference's wallet
parses every output in order (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/Wallet.ts:950-1016`, `discoverOverlayCertificates`
and `discoverByIdentityKey`, through `parseResults`,
`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/utility/identityUtils.ts:671-707`): a
skipped output (`IdentityEvidenceVerifier.parse` answering `null`, `:596-634`)
is dropped and the next one read, a `limit` rethrown (`:630-634`). Since #730
a first output the evidence check refuses, or one with no identity token,
ended this crate's resolution with `None` where the reference reads the
second. The function now walks every output through the same parser and
returns the first admitted certificate's identity; the contacts override is
unchanged, the signature too.

The reads' fold (the rule and strength reads of PR #738) ports two more rules
of the same path. The subject filter: the reference's discovery keeps only
certificates whose subject is the key asked (`filterCertificatesByIdentityKey`,
`identityUtils.ts:247-255`, `certificate.subject.toLowerCase() === identityKey.toLowerCase()`,
called at `Wallet.ts:1012` inside `discoverByIdentityKey`), where this crate
returned the first admitted certificate whatever its subject (the parser
checks only that a token is signed by the subject it names); a certificate
for another subject is now passed over, the subject's compressed hex compared
with the asked key lower-cased. The whole walk: `parseResults` parses every
output before the discovery answers (`identityUtils.ts:671-707`), so a
`limit` anywhere in the answer refuses the call (`:630-634`, `Wallet.ts:950-955`),
where this crate answered at the first admitted output; it now parses every
output, a limit before or after an admitted one failing the call with
`identity error: Transaction evidence: limit`, an `invalid-evidence` output
anywhere a skip. The other doors are unchanged: `resolve_by_attributes` is
the reference's `discoverByAttributes` path, which filters by attributes
(`filterCertificatesByAttributes`, `identityUtils.ts:283-302`, called at
`Wallet.ts:1078`), not by subject; `query`, `discover_certificates` and
`discover_certificates_by_type` are this crate's own doors, with no
counterpart in the reference's `IdentityClient` (`IdentityClient.ts`, whose
lookups are `resolveByIdentityKey` and `resolveByAttributes` alone); all four
already parse every output before they answer (a `?` on the parser inside
the `for output in &outputs` loop, the result returned after it).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#739)

What the wallet's `discoverByIdentityKey` door does that `discover_certificates`
does not (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Wallet.ts:966-1015`): the overlay query is sent
as `{identityKey, certifiers}` (`:1004`) where this crate sends
`{identityKey, certificatesOnly: true}`; the certificates are filtered and
sorted by the wallet's trust step with `certifierInfo` attached (`:1010-1011`),
unported here (the #737 row); a page of offset and limit (default 10, at most
10000) with `totalCertificates` (`:228-233`, `validationHelpers.ts:1540-1543`)
where this crate returns every admitted certificate; the asked key is trimmed
and lower-cased by `validateHexString` (`:522-533`), so a space-padded key is
found there and answers `[]` here, and a malformed or uncompressed key is
refused there and answers `Ok([])` here after a lookup; a contact-source
shortcut (`:983-992`) and the `IdentityCertificate` result type. The by-type
door's unchecked certificate type is #744.

### Tests: the two `ls_identity` parsers' lock position pinned at their decode site, past the token check (#744)

From #742's cold read (2026-11-04 05:0xZ): since #544 the token check
(`is_authenticated_token`) refuses every lock-after layout on its own:
`is_canonical_signed_pushdrop` requires a 33-byte key push then `OP_CHECKSIG`
as the script's leading two chunks. No lock-after token can pass it, so with
both parsers reverted to `PushDrop::decode` (the lock position either way)
`tests/identity_lock_position_537.rs` stayed green (measured: 2 of 2 under the
mutation). Both parsers now decode through one crate-private function,
`decode_token` (`PushDrop::decode_before`, unchanged behaviour), and the unit
module `src/identity/client_decode_token_744_tests.rs` pins it on the
reference's own revelation token relocked after its fields (the same key, the
same two fields, the same signature): `PushDrop::decode` reads it with the
same fields, the token check refuses it, and `decode_token` refuses it by the
position alone. RED with `decode_token` reading through `PushDrop::decode`
(`the parsers' decode site reads lock-before alone`). The 537 file's relocked
control is unchanged; its helper `subject_of` (#742), which asked `02aa` when
the token carried no `"subject":"` marker, now refuses that case naming the
token, and the #618 key-only case asks `02aa` explicitly (`KEY_ONLY_ASKED`),
so no certificate-carrying case can fall to an ask the subject filter answers
`[]`.

### Fixed: `discover_certificates_by_type` keeps only the asked type's certificates (#744)

From the strength read of PR #742 (#739, 2026-11-04 04:5xZ): the by-type door
sent its `cert_type` in the `ls_identity` query and never checked it on the
certificates it read, so an overlay host answering with another type's
certificate was believed. The door now keeps a certificate only when its type
is the asked one, applied on #742's shared walk (`discover_of_subject`: every
output parsed in order, a `limit` anywhere failing the call, #730, #737) after
its subject filter (`is_asked_subject`, #739), so a certificate is returned
only when both its subject and its type are the asked ones. The comparison is the certificate's canonical base64 text
(`type_base64()`) against the asked text, exactly: a token's `type` is
canonical base64 of 32 bytes or the token is skipped (#553), so its
re-encoding is the token's own text and the text comparison is the bytes'
comparison for every canonical asked text; an asked text no token can carry
(unpadded, spaced) matches nothing. `discover_certificates` and the other
doors are unchanged.

Hardening, not parity: the reference has no by-type door
(`DiscoverByIdentityKeyArgs` carries no type at `ts-stack@edf6e03`), so this
crate's own rule answers the question its own door asks.

Semver: a behaviour change at one public door without a signature change:
`discover_certificates_by_type` drops a certificate whose type is not the
asked one where it returned it. Migration: none.

### Fixed: `IdentityClient::query` keeps only the certificates its question asked for (#746)

From the strength read of PR #745 (#744, 2026-11-04 05:5xZ): `query` sent the
question's `identityKey`, `certificateType` and `certifiers` to `ls_identity`
and kept every certificate the parser admitted, so an overlay host could
answer with another subject's, type's or certifier's certificate, as the two
`discover_*` doors could before #739 and #744. After the walk (every output
parsed in order, a `limit` anywhere failing the call, unchanged) `query` now
keeps a certificate only when it matches every field the question carries:
`identity_key` through `is_asked_subject` (both sides lower-cased, the rule of
the by-key doors, #737, #739); `certificate_type` as the canonical base64
text, `type_base64()` compared exactly with the asked text (#744);
`certifier` (an `Option<String>`, one key, sent as a one-entry `certifiers`
list) as the certificate's certifier key in lower-case hex against the asked
text lower-cased. A field the question does not carry filters nothing: with
`certifier` unset the lookup still asks the default SocialCert certifier, and
a certificate of another certifier is kept; `attributes` is sent and not
checked on the answer.

Hardening, not parity: the reference has no such door (`IdentityClient.ts`'s
lookups at `ts-stack@edf6e03` are `resolveByIdentityKey` and
`resolveByAttributes`), so this crate's own rule answers the question its own
door asks.

Semver: a behaviour change at one public door without a signature change:
`query` drops a certificate its question did not ask for where it returned
it. Migration: none.

### Fixed: the by-type questions send `certificateTypes` with `identityKey`, as the reference overlay reads them (#752)

From the rule read of PR #750 (#746, 2026-11-04 07:0xZ), older than that PR:
`IdentityClient::discover_certificates_by_type` and `IdentityClient::query`
(with `certificate_type` set) sent the type to `ls_identity` as
`certificateType`, a string. The reference overlay's identity lookup service
admits seven keys and refuses any other for the whole question
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/overlays/topics/src/identity/IdentityLookupService.ts:74-82`:
`attributes`, `certifiers`, `identityKey`, `certificateTypes`,
`serialNumber`, `limit`, `offset`; `shared/queryValidation.ts:35-38`,
`Invalid lookup query: unexpected field <key>`), reads `certificateTypes` as
an array of at most 32 base64 texts of 32 decoded bytes (`:97-100`; the
check trims and tests the alphabet, the padding and the length, with no
trailing-bit check, `validationHelpers.ts:488-498`), and
answers by type only beside `identityKey` (`:136-143`, then
`IdentityStorageManager.ts:315-339`, `findByCertificateType`; the overlay's
own `IdentityQuery` type, `types.ts:28-36`). A reference host therefore
refused every by-type question, so #744's and #746's type filters took effect
only against a non-reference host. Both doors now send
`certificateTypes: [cert_type]`; `discover_certificates_by_type`'s question is
`{ identityKey, certificateTypes }`, `query`'s carries the same key beside
its others, every other key as before. The reference wallet asks no by-type
question (`wallet-toolbox` `Wallet.ts:1004`, `discoverByIdentityKey`, sends
`{ identityKey, certifiers }`), so the overlay's allowlist is the reference
for the shape. The refusal is witnessed by reading the allowlist, no live
overlay.

Semver: the question's shape is a wire contract toward overlay hosts, not a
signature: a behaviour change at two public doors without a signature change.
Migration: a non-reference host that read `certificateType` now receives
`certificateTypes`, an array of one; such a host reads the new key or loses
the type (a reference host answered nothing before). `IdentityQuery`'s own
serde JSON keeps its `certificateType` member: it is the struct's
serialization, not the lookup question.

Not changed, a finding for a follow-up: `discover_certificates` sends
`certificatesOnly: true`, a key the same allowlist refuses
(`IdentityLookupService.ts:74-82`), so a reference host refuses that door's
question too; outside #752's two doors.

### Fixed: `Transaction::from_beef` and `Beef::find_bump` take the last BUMP holding a txid, as the reference's index does (#732)

From the strength read of PR #729 (#728, 2026-11-04 01:2xZ): the reference
indexes the level-0 leaves of every BUMP with a `Map.set` loop over the BUMPs
in order, so the LAST BUMP holding a txid is the one `findBump` answers and
`#addInputProof` makes the transaction's `merklePath`
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Beef.ts:570-585`, `:649-680`). This crate's
`add_input_proof` built its index with `or_insert` and `find_bump` scanned
from the front, so both kept the EARLIEST, and the comment on the index claimed
the reference's answer. Both readers keep every BUMP they read and merge none
(`Beef.ts:1257-1261`; `beef/collect.rs`), so two proofs of one txid at level 0
(two blocks after a reorg, two roots at one height, a BUMP the writer did not
merge) reach `from_beef` from the wire, and the attached path, and so the root
a tracker is asked about, was another than the reference's. The index now
keeps the last (`insert`), `find_bump` scans from the back, and the comment
says so. `merge_bump` is unchanged: as the reference's `#findOrInsertBump`
(`:791-810`) it combines only a BUMP of the same height and root.

Semver: a behaviour change without a signature change: for a BEEF carrying
two proofs of one txid, `Transaction::from_beef`, `from_atomic_beef`,
`Beef::find_atomic_transaction` and `Beef::find_bump` answer the last proof
where they answered the earliest. Migration: none for a BEEF with one proof per
txid; a caller that relied on the earliest proof names it (`beef.bumps[i]`).

`tests/beef_bump_lookup_732.rs` against `tests/vectors/beef_bump_lookup_732.json`
(`tests/support/beef_bump_lookup_732.mjs`, the bun bundle of `packages/sdk` at
`ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0; two runs byte-identical): four BEEFs,
each built by this crate's writer (`merge_raw_tx`, `merge_bump`, `to_binary`)
to the bytes the reference's writer recorded: a parent proven at 800000
(root its txid) and at 800001 beside a sibling, in both orders; two roots at
800000; and an unproven child spending both of that parent's outputs. The
attached path, `find_bump`'s answer and both inputs' source paths (the full
link and the stub) are the reference's, the last BUMP; the wire bump index
(the earliest, on both sides) and both BUMPs read back unchanged. 3 of 4 RED on
`9ae3ebcc` (`left: (800000, "86bd3ea1...")`, `right: (800001, "e476c603...")`),
the wire-index agreement green on both.

Residue, stated: `merge_raw_tx` after two BUMPs holding its txid sets the
entry's bump index to the earliest holding it as a txid leaf
(`try_to_validate_bump_index`), where the reference's `#tryToValidateBumpIndex` takes its index's, the
last (`Beef.ts:1329-1340`; probed under Node 22: `bumpIndex 1`), so the two
writers write another index byte for that merge order; no reader's verdict
moves (both BUMPs hold the txid) and a reader's attached path follows the
index, not the byte, but both atomic writers carry the BUMP the byte names
(`atomic_closure`; the reference's `#copySelectedTransactions`,
`Beef.ts:448-470`), so `to_binary_atomic` of that entry carries the earliest
BUMP where `toBinaryAtomic` carries the last, and a reread attaches another
path and asks a tracker about another root (#757; closed there).

### Fixed: the lookup resolver records success for any output list and keeps a freeform answer neutral, as the reference's host reputation does (#760)

From the strength read of PR #759 (#754, 2026-11-04 09:1xZ), outside that
row: `LookupResolver` read a host's answer as valid only when it was an
output list with at least one output or a freeform answer, and recorded
`Invalid lookup response` as a host failure for an empty output list
(`src/overlay/lookup_resolver/query.rs:122-132` at `8601c66b`). Both
references record a success for any output list, the empty one included:
`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/overlay-tools/LookupResolver.ts:2395-2398`
(`isOutputListAnswer`, then `recordSuccess`) and `ts-sdk@9e3ede6`
`src/overlay-tools/LookupResolver.ts:518-528` (`answer.type === 'output-list'
&& Array.isArray((answer).outputs)`, then `recordSuccess`). The host
reputation tracker is one global keyed by host URL with two failures of grace
and a backoff of 1 s doubling to 60 s, so three lookups answered empty (a
subject with no certificates, a key with no record) backed that host off for
every resolver in the process, and the next identity, kvstore or registry
lookup against it failed with `All competent hosts for <service> are backing
off`. The site now records a success for every output list. A freeform answer
recorded a success here, which cleared any backoff; `edf6e03` treats it as
neutral (`:2399-2402`: "A valid freeform response is neutral: it proves this
request reached the service, but it must not erase an availability backoff",

### Fixed: `merge_raw_tx` writes the last BUMP's index for a txid two BUMPs prove, as the reference does; a caller-set merkle path at `add_input_proof` replaced by the BEEF's proof and descended past where there is none (#757)

From the #732 lane (2026-11-04 08:4xZ), two residues at `ts-stack@edf6e03`
(`packages/sdk/src/transaction/Beef.ts`).

The written index. The reference's `#tryToValidateBumpIndex` asks its
level-0 index (`:1329-1340`: `const i = this.#ensureBumpTxidIndex().get(txid)`,
then `newTx.bumpIndex = i`), the index a `Map.set` over the BUMPs in order
(`:576-585`), so an entry merged after two BUMPs that hold its txid takes the
LAST one's index; `BeefTx.toWriter` writes it and the atomic writer carries
that BUMP (`#copySelectedTransactions`, `:448-470`). This crate's
`try_to_validate_bump_index` (behind `merge_raw_tx`, `merge_txid_only` and
`merge_transaction`) scanned from the front and took the EARLIEST, so
`to_binary` wrote another index byte and `to_binary_atomic` carried another
BUMP than the reference's, and an atomic BEEF read back attached another path.
It now scans from the back. An entry merged before a BUMP is unchanged and
agrees: the BUMP present at its merge, as `#mergeBumpEntry` sets only an entry
without an index (`:774-786`). The readers are unchanged: `add_input_proof`
attaches the last BUMP holding a txid whatever the written byte (#732), and
both forms prove the txid.

The caller's path. `#addInputProof` (`:649-668`) sets
`current.merklePath = mp` whenever `findBump(txid)` answers, over a
`merklePath` the transaction already carries, and goes on to the inputs only
when it does not answer, the carried path kept. `add_input_proof` kept a
carried path (`enter` and `bare_stub` attached a BUMP only to a transaction
without one) and treated any carried path as the end of the walk. Both now
follow the reference: this BEEF's BUMP replaces a carried path and ends the
walk; a transaction this BEEF does not prove is descended, its own path kept.
A carried path reaches the walk only through the in-memory API (`BeefTx::tx_mut`,
`merge_transaction` of a transaction with a path, an input's own
`source_transaction`); the readers set none, so `Transaction::from_beef` on
bytes is unchanged. `Transaction::verify` reads a transaction with a path as
proven and does not descend it, so the extra links are not judged.

Semver: a behaviour change without a signature change: for a BEEF holding two
BUMPs that prove one txid, the entry merged after both carries the last
BUMP's index, so the bytes `to_binary` writes change in that entry's index
byte and `to_binary_atomic` carries the last BUMP; readers accept both forms.
`find_atomic_transaction` replaces a path a held transaction carries with the
BEEF's BUMP for its txid, and links the inputs of a transaction that carries a
path the BEEF does not hold. Migration: a fixture pinning the old bytes
re-records; a caller that set a path on a held transaction to override the
BEEF's merges that path as a BUMP instead. The four dependents' fixtures were
scanned (every BEEF found in a test, vector, fixture, bench or example file of
`bsv-overlay-cloudflare`, `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs`, `bsv-wallet-cli` and
`rust-message-box`: 66 parsed) and none holds two BUMPs sharing a level-0 hash.

### Fixed: `merge_transaction` merges the transaction's merkle path as a BUMP and walks its source transactions, as the reference does (#764)

From the #757 lane's reading (2026-11-04 10:2xZ) and the rule read of PR #763.
The reference's `mergeTransaction` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/transaction/Beef.ts:875-901`) runs `#mergeTransactionGraph`,
which pops each transaction off a stack and runs `#mergeTransactionEntry`
(`:849-856`): `current.merklePath` merged through `#mergeBumpEntry`
(`:774-786`) and the returned index taken for the entry, else
`#tryToValidateBumpIndex` (`:1329-1340`); an entry that ends with no index
queues its inputs' `sourceTransaction`s (`#queueSourceTransactions`,
`:858-863`, at `:897`), each txid once per call. go-sdk@2ca481c's
`MergeTransaction` (`transaction/beef.go:875-912`) does the same save a held
entry and a held BUMP: `MergeBump(tx.MerklePath)`, then `MergeTransaction` of
each source when there is no index, but `mergeWouldNotChange` (`:920-950`)
keeps a proven entry it holds instead of replacing it, and its
`tryToValidateBumpIndex` (`:858-868`) never looks up a held BUMP, so for a
transaction with no path that a held BUMP proves Go walks the sources where
the reference and this crate stop (`subject_proven_by_a_held_bump`; read, not
run). This crate's `merge_transaction` stored the transaction alone
(`src/transaction/beef.rs:391-405` at `d14f560d`: `let bump_index = None; //
Could be set if tx has merklePath`): its path was never written as a BUMP and
no ancestor was merged, so `find_atomic_transaction` on such a BEEF descended
past a parent the reference stops at.

It now walks as the reference does (`src/transaction/beef/merge_graph.rs`, a
stack, linear in the graph, no recursion): a transaction carrying a path has
it merged through `merge_bump` and takes the returned index (a path whose
BUMP the BEEF holds, the same height and root, is combined into it, no second
BUMP); one without takes the last BUMP flagging its txid, as before; an entry
that ends with an index stops the walk, one that ends with none has its
inputs' sources merged and walked in turn, from the first input on. A source
the BEEF already holds is replaced in its place, as the reference's
`#replaceOrAppendTx` replaces it (`:531-540`), so an ancestor merged by hand
is one entry still and a graph merged again moves no entry. The transaction given is stored as
given; each ancestor is stored as a copy without its own source links (they
are entries of the BEEF), so the walk clones each transaction once, where the
reference holds the objects. `merge_beef` keeps its one-entry merge of an
in-memory entry (no path or source walk), as the reference's `mergeBeef`
reads a snapshot of the bytes, which carries neither (`:975`).

Since #764's fold every door that replaces a held txid (`merge_raw_tx`,
`merge_transaction` and its walk, the one-entry merge `merge_beef` and
`to_beef` use) goes through one helper, the reference's `#replaceOrAppendTx`
(`beef/index.rs`, `replace_or_append`): the entry is stored at the held one's
position, where it was removed (`Vec::remove`, then the index rebuilt) and the
new one appended. `merge_txid_only` keeps a held entry, as `mergeTxidOnly`
does (`:919-929`). That made a re-merge over a held graph of G entries cost
O(G·N) in a BEEF of N, where the reference's costs O(G), and it wrote another
order: two unrelated transactions A and B held (raw, both proven or both
unproven), A merged again, the reference writes A then B and this crate wrote
B then A, as `sort_txs` keeps insertion order between entries no dependency
orders. Older than #764 (the same on `d14f560d`, through `merge_raw_tx` too);
found by the cold read of PR #770.

Semver: a behaviour change without a signature change. The bytes `to_binary`
writes after `merge_transaction` of a transaction carrying a `merkle_path` or
input `source_transaction`s change: a BUMP and the ancestors appear, and the
entry carries the BUMP's index. A re-merge of a held txid (`merge_raw_tx`,
`merge_transaction`) leaves the entry in its place: the bytes after it change
only where independent entries were written in the moved order (A then B
above, B then A before). Readers are unchanged. `Transaction::to_beef`,
`to_beef_v1` and `to_atomic_beef` write the bytes they wrote: since #764's fold
they store their collected ancestors with the one-entry merge (their BUMPs are
merged already, so a walk would merge each proven ancestor's path again), and
the `iterative_equivalence_tests` byte comparison and `readme_examples` hold.
Migration: a caller that merged a transaction's ancestors by hand as well
merges them once (the replacement dedupes); a fixture pinning the old bytes of
such a merge re-records; a site that re-merges an in-memory entry meant to
stand alone (a root to prune or split from its ancestry, the toolbox's
`create_action/beef_graph.rs:265` and `create_action/beef.rs:84`) keeps the
one-entry merge with `beef.merge_raw_tx(tx.to_binary(), None)`. The dependents' sites (`grep -rn merge_transaction` in
`bsv-overlay-cloudflare`, `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs`, `bsv-wallet-cli`,
`rust-message-box`; 82 matching lines, each read at its window): four
production sites, the rest tests. `overlay-engine`'s `gasp_overlay.rs:461`
merges transactions parsed by `Transaction::from_binary` (no path, no links):
unchanged. `overlay-cloudflare`'s `ef.rs:245` (`strip_subject_bump`'s
fallback, the subject from `transaction_from_beef` with its path cleared but its sources linked) now
writes the subject's ancestry and their BUMPs where its comment says "parents
dropped", the guard (the subject raw, no proof claimed for it) still holding.
The toolbox's `create_action/beef_graph.rs:265` and `create_action/beef.rs:84`
re-merge an in-memory entry's transaction (`tx.tx()` with no raw bytes), which
now walks the sources it carries. Thirteen test sites name a path or a
source link within the forty lines before the call (`overlay-cloudflare`
`submit_census.rs`, `low-app-layer` `compaction.rs`, the toolbox's
`broadcast_memory_tests.rs`, `arcade_tests.rs`,
`arcade_status_vector_tests.rs`, `rust-message-box` `payments.rs`; not run
here): where the transaction merged carries them, its BEEF gains the BUMPs and
ancestors the reference's would hold.

`tests/beef_merge_transaction_764.rs` against
`tests/vectors/beef_merge_transaction_764.json`
(`tests/support/beef_merge_transaction_764.mjs`, the bun bundle of
`packages/sdk` at `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0; two runs
byte-identical): nine graphs over #757's parent, child and grandchild, each
rebuilt here (the transactions' bytes, the paths they carry, the sources their
inputs carry, the case's prior merges) and compared with the reference's
`mergeTransaction` then `toHex` bytes, its BUMP count and its entries'
indices: a lone transaction carrying its path at 800000 (bumps `[alone]`,
index 0) and a lone unproven one; a child carrying its proven parent on both
inputs (one BUMP, the parent indexed, the child raw) and its unproven parent;
a chain of three proven at the middle (the walk stops, the grandparent absent)
and at the root (all three, one BUMP); a child whose parent the BEEF holds raw
and with its BUMP (no duplicate entry, no second BUMP); a child a held BUMP

(no BUMP), `right: "0200beef01fe00350c000101000262b0..."`;
`child_of_a_proven_parent` `left: "0200beef000100010000000262b0..."` (the

The fold's six cases, recorded by the same recorder (its runs byte-identical,

### Notes: cross-SDK parity

Ancestors are held without their links: the reference's `#mergeTransactionEntry`
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Beef.ts:849-856`) stores each source object as given, its
own `sourceTransaction` links kept; this crate stores `clone_for_beef` copies.

### Fixed: a BEEF entry takes the last BUMP holding its txid as any level-0 leaf, flagged on the way, as the reference does; v0.3.5's strict match reversed (#765)

`Beef::try_to_validate_bump_index` (behind `merge_raw_tx`, `merge_txid_only`,
`merge_transaction`, `make_txid_only`) and `update_bump_indices` (behind
`merge_bump`) took a BUMP for an entry only where its level-0 leaf for the
txid was flagged `txid` (the `flags` helper, v0.3.5, `ef98e246`). The
reference's index holds every level-0 hash of every BUMP, the last winning
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/transaction/Beef.ts:576-585`), and
`#tryToValidateBumpIndex` takes it and flags the leaf (`:1329-1340`, the flag at
`:1334-1338`); `#mergeBumpEntry` gives an entry without an index the merged
BUMP through `#tryMarkTxProvenByBump`, which does the same (`:774-786`,
`:813-822`). go-sdk@2ca481c takes any level-0 hash where it attaches a path (`bumpProves`,
`transaction/beef.go:67-83`; `FindBumpByHash`, `:620-630`, the earliest;
`MergeBump`, `:780-785`), but flags no leaf and writes no index for an entry
merged without one (`MergeRawTx`, `:820-849`; `beefBytes`, `:1679-1694`), and
its validator proves an entry without an index only by a leaf flagged `txid`
(`ValidateTransactions`, `:1070-1083`, `:1105-1113`, `:1137-1140`): Go's own
merges leave the p25 BEEF refused, as v0.3.5 left it here, while the bytes
this crate now writes (the entry indexed, the leaf `02`) read valid there
(`:1114-1128`). BRC-74's flag `00` is "data follows, not a client txid"
(`transactions/0074.md:75`), not "unproven". Both sites now take the LAST BUMP

### Fixed: PushDrop pushes the wallet's key bytes as returned, as the reference does (#545)

The PushDrop template pushed its key compressed (`PushDrop::lock`,
`to_compressed()`), so the five sites that lock with a wallet's
`getPublicKey` answer (the local store's `local_token.rs`, the global store's
`global_actions.rs`, the contacts manager's `contacts_actions.rs`, the
identity token's `reveal.rs`, the registry's `token.rs`) re-encoded the
wallet's key. The reference's `lock` pushes the answer as the wallet returned
it: `toArray(publicKey, 'hex')` under the opcode `publicKey.length / 2`
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `packages/sdk/src/script/templates/PushDrop.ts:158-175`;
the unlocker signs with the wallet alone, `:206-247`, no key in it). A
crate-visible `PushDrop::lock_with_key_bytes(&self, key_bytes: &[u8])`
pushes the bytes given, the fields, drops and lock position `lock`'s
(`src/script/templates/pushdrop_key_bytes.rs`); `lock` is it with the key
compressed, unchanged. It is a port helper, not public API: the reference has
one `lock`, taking the key as text, so no second public constructor is added
and the public surface is unchanged. The five sites go through one crate helper,
`wallet_key_lock`: the answer read by `PublicKey::from_hex` (its refusal
unchanged) and pushed as the bytes the reference's `toArray(_, 'hex')` reads
from it (an odd-length text with a leading `0`, #498's `reference_hex`).

Old and new: a wallet answering a compressed key (every `ProtoWallet`, the
toolbox's wallets, the CLI's) writes the same token as before, byte for byte,
so the toolbox's and the CLI's tables are unchanged. A wallet answering an
uncompressed (`04`) key or a hybrid (`06`/`07`) one, which #498's parser
reads, wrote a token whose first field was the compressed key; it now writes
the 65 bytes it returned, as the reference does. A token written before
reads as before (the decoders read either length).

The witness is recorded, never written by hand:
`tests/support/pushdrop_key_bytes_545.mjs` runs the reference's own
`PushDrop.lock` (the bundle of `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0, a
ProtoWallet of the scalar 9 whose answer is rewritten into each form) on a
compressed, an uncompressed, a hybrid and an odd-length answer at both lock
positions, into `tests/vectors/pushdrop_key_bytes_545.json` (8 cases, two runs
byte for byte). The unit tests beside the helper
(`src/script/templates/pushdrop_key_bytes_545_tests.rs`): this crate's
template writes the reference's bytes for the compressed, uncompressed and
hybrid cases, a compressed key's `lock` unchanged, the odd-length residue only
at the reference's truncated opcode. `tests/script_pushdrop_key_bytes_545.rs`:
the local store, the global store, the registry, the contacts manager and the
identity reveal push the 65 bytes a wallet answers (the #318 counting wallet
with #545's key form), through their public paths. On the base `69d315fc` the
five site tests are red (the compressed key pushed; the unit file does not
compile there, its helper absent); with the template's push reverted to
compressed on the tip, the five site tests and one of the three unit tests
(the one covering both non-compressed forms) are red, six of eight.

### Fixed: the identity parsers run the reference discovery's record checks and byte bounds (#553)

The identity client's two `ls_identity` parsers (`parse_output_to_certificate`
under `resolve_by_identity_key` and `resolve_by_attributes`,
`parse_output_to_verifiable_certificate` under `discover_certificates`,
`discover_certificates_by_type` and `query`) read a revelation token's
certificate JSON for the members they need and nothing else (#544 added the
envelope, the lock and the field signature). The reference runs more on the
same answer: the SDK's `IdentityClient.resolveByIdentityKey` and
`resolveByAttributes` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `IdentityClient.ts:559-655`) ask
their wallet's `discoverByIdentityKey` and `discoverByAttributes`, which the
toolbox answers from the `ls_identity` lookup (`wallet-toolbox`
`Wallet.ts:904-1010`, `parseResults`, `identityUtils.ts:671-707`) through
`decodeIdentityOutput` (`:497-559`): two fields, the certificate 1 to 256 KiB,
the signature 8 to 80 bytes, the canonical envelope, then `certificateRecord`
(`:87-132`): the bytes read as `toUTF8Strict` (`TextDecoder`, a leading
byte-order mark dropped), a plain JSON object of exactly the eight members
`type`, `serialNumber`, `subject`, `certifier`, `revocationOutpoint`,
`fields`, `keyring`, `signature`, `fields` and `keyring` objects of 1 to 100
names, every keyring name a field's, every keyring value a string of at most
2048 UTF-16 units. Every failure is caught and the output skipped (`:555-557`).

Until this landing the parsers read, where the reference skips: a
certificate over 256 KiB; a member beyond the eight; a missing `keyring` or
`revocationOutpoint` (the latter when the signed outpoint is the zero
sentinel the default reads); a `keyring` that is no object, empty, naming an
absent field, or carrying a value that is no string or is over 2048 units;
more than 100 fields. They refused, where the reference reads, a certificate
behind a byte-order mark. And `parse_output_to_certificate` returned an
`Err` for a record whose members did not read as a certificate (`identity
error: Missing certificate type`, `Missing serial number`, `Missing subject`,
`Missing certifier`, `Invalid certificate type length`, `Invalid serial
number length`, and the base64, key and outpoint readers' errors), so one
such output in an answer made `resolve_by_identity_key` and
`resolve_by_attributes` fail whole, where the reference's
`new VerifiableCertificate(...).verify()` fails and the output is skipped
(`:540-550`). Now both parsers run the checks in `src/identity/client_record.rs`
before the token is authenticated, and every refusal is a skip: the
resolution goes on with the other outputs. No public shape changes; the six
words above are no longer returned (no downstream named in `CLAUDE.md`'s list
matches them: `bsv-wallet-cli` and `bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs` call neither
resolver).

The witness is recorded, never written by hand:
`tests/support/identity_certificate_record_553.mjs` runs the toolbox's own

`identityUtils.ts` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`, its `@bsv/sdk` imports resolved to

The reference computes a contact's `abbreviatedKey` at one site and stores

`validateContact`'s record, whose `abbreviatedKey` is the caller's as given

### Added: `WorkBudget::charge` is public, so a host that judges inputs itself charges the one per-transaction rule (#567)

Since #519 the per-transaction work rule has had one implementation,
`WorkBudget::charge`, called by `Transaction::verify_with_work_budgets`, its
chain-parameter sibling and both stream verifiers; it was `pub(super)`. A host
that runs each input's `Spend` itself (the toolbox's `InputJudgements`, whose
doors judge inputs under its own spend verifier) could not reach it, so the
toolbox kept its own saturating sum and built this crate's
`NotJudgedCause::TransactionWorkBudgetExceeded { input, limit, total }` by
hand: two implementations of one rule. The keeper's word (the rulings page's
entry of 2026-10-31 18:1xZ, issue #567, shape (a)): the work budget is the
port's own rule, so neither shape is the reference's and the smaller surface
wins; the method public, not a host-verifier hook on the stream verifier.

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `WorkBudget::charge(self, total: &mut u64, input: u32, work: u64) -> Result<(), NotJudgedCause>` | `pub(super)`: the verifiers alone | `pub`: a host charges each input's `Spend::work_spent()` after it runs, in input order, against its running `total`, and gets the verifiers' cause with the same fields |

The signature is the one the verifiers already call, not the issue's
`charge(&mut self, input: usize, work: u64)`: `WorkBudget` is a `Copy` policy
with no running total (the stream keeps its total in the cursor, BSC5), so
the caller holds `total`, and `input` is the cause's `u32`. A `&mut self`
shape would add a field to the type #527 closed. `charge` reads
`per_transaction` alone; a per-input crossing stays the interpreter's
`WorkBudgetExceeded` while the input runs. Done when the toolbox deletes
`InputJudgements::charge` and its sum at its next re-pin, its 2^31 witness
green through this crate's charge. Pinned by
`a_host_charging_its_own_inputs_answers_the_verifiers_cause_567` (the #519
fixture's 68/6/8 inputs charged by hand cross 70 at input 1 with total 74,
equal to the whole verifier's and the stream's cause; RED on `b2531c8a` as a
compile failure, the method private) and
`a_per_input_bound_alone_never_refuses_through_charge_567`.

Semver: one public method added to an existing type, a minor addition; no
other shape or behaviour moves.

### Fixed: an identity record with a lone surrogate escape is read as the reference's discovery reads it (#566)

The reference's discovery reads a revelation token's certificate with
`JSON.parse` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/utility/identityUtils.ts:88`,
`certificateRecord`, under `decodeIdentityOutput`, `:497-559`), which keeps
a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape (`\ud800` without its pair) as a lone code
unit; `certificateRecord` compares the names with those units (`:100-125`),
and `Certificate.verify`'s `toBinary` writes every name and value through
`TextEncoder` (`packages/sdk/src/auth/certificates/Certificate.ts:73-75`,
`:280-296`; `primitives/UTF8.ts:1-5`), which writes a lone surrogate as
U+FFFD's three bytes, in every engine (the WHATWG encoder's rule). Until
#566 both `ls_identity` parsers read the text with `serde_json` into a
`String`, which refuses the escape (`invalid unicode code point`), so a
record the reference reads was skipped: #553's stated residue (#560's), the
keeper's ruling (3) of 2026-10-31 17:1xZ (a JSON body census row scoped to
the identity record fields, a lenient reader or a stated divergence).

The lenient reader (`src/identity/client_record_lenient.rs`), reached only
when the strict reading refuses the record's text: each string read as
`serde_json` reads a byte string, in WTF-8 (its own option, no fork and no
new dependency), the keyring names judged against the field names unit for
unit, then each string held with every lone surrogate as U+FFFD, the bytes
the reference signs, verifies and derives a key ID from. A keyring value
with a lone unit is skipped, as no base64 decrypts there (`:551-552`), and
so, since the cold review, is a revealed field's value with one
(`VerifiableCertificate.ts:182-191`: its `canonicalBase64` throws before the
decryption), which the lane's tip read through a failed decryption. The
`type`, `serialNumber`, keys, outpoint and signature with one are skipped by
the record's text rules, as the reference skips them.

| Record | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| An unrevealed field value with a lone unit (high, low, high before a non-low, a reversed pair, the escape in upper case) | skipped | read, the value held with U+FFFD, the certificate verifying over the reference's bytes |
| A field name with a lone unit, unrevealed or revealed | skipped | read; a revealed one decrypted under the key ID `TextEncoder` writes |
| A keyring name whose lone unit differs from its field's | skipped | skipped |
| A revealed field's value with a lone unit (the cold review's) | skipped | skipped (read at the lane's tip `130047e6`) |
| A keyring value, a member name, `type`, `serialNumber`, `subject`, `certifier`, `revocationOutpoint` or `signature` with a lone unit | skipped | skipped |

`tests/identity_lone_surrogate_566.rs` runs `tests/vectors/identity_lone_surrogate_566.json`
(twenty-one tokens the reference's `PushDrop.lock` signs for the subject 9, each
with `parseResults`' outcome, a read certificate's fields and decrypted
fields as the reference holds them and as `TextEncoder` writes them; written
by `tests/support/identity_lone_surrogate_566.mjs` under Node v22.18.0, two
runs byte-identical) through `resolve_by_attributes` and
`discover_certificates`: 7 of 21 cases RED on `b2531c8a` (the seven the
reference reads, skipped there), the twenty-first (`revealed_field_value`,
the cold review's) RED on the lane's tip `130047e6` (read there, skipped by
the reference), 21 green on the tip, three enumerated (the
note below). The reader's units, including an escape cut at the text's end,
a high surrogate before a non-low unit and a low alone, refused without a
panic: `src/identity/client_record_lenient_tests.rs`.

**Dependency floor:** `serde_json` is required at `1.0.125` (was `1.0`): it
is the first release that reads a lone surrogate escape into a byte string
whatever follows it; 1.0.124 refuses `\ud800\u0041` and
`\ud800\ud800\udc00`, and 1.0.60 refuses every lone high surrogate
(measured on 1.0.40 to 1.0.154 by the cold review). The ratchet's lock
(`tools/ratchet/library.Cargo.lock`) already resolves 1.0.154; a consumer
whose lock holds an older `serde_json` moves to 1.0.125 or later on its
next `cargo update -p bsv-rs`.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#566)

A read string holds U+FFFD where the reference's holds the lone unit: every
byte derived from it is the same (`TextEncoder`), but a caller that writes
the field back as JSON writes the character, where `JSON.stringify` writes
the escape. Three shapes the reference reads are skipped here, enumerated in
the test: two field names differing only in their lone units, and a name
with a lone unit beside one with U+FFFD itself, which one `String` cannot
hold apart (the reference's binary carries the same name bytes twice); and
a name with a lone unit beside one with U+E000 (the recorded case), where
ICU sorts the lone unit first (`localeCompare`, `Certificate.ts:282`, Node
22.18.0) and this crate's collation sorts U+FFFD after U+E000, so the bytes
rebuilt are not the bytes signed; ICU 77.1 weighs a lone unit at its code
point among the implicit weights, so the same holds beside any private-use
or unassigned BMP character above U+DFFF (U+E000 to U+F8FF, U+FDD0, U+FFF0,
measured by the cold review), where ICU and this crate both sort U+FFFD
after them. Beside an assigned supplementary character (U+10000, U+1F600)
ICU sorts both the lone unit and U+FFFD after it and this crate U+FFFD
before it: #249's residue of a name past U+00FF, not this one's. Go at
`2ca481c` delegates resolution to its wallet's discovery
(`identity/client.go:240-276`) and parses no `ls_identity` answer. Out of
scope: the contacts record (its plaintext is the owner's own wallet's
encryption, a row of #544's) and `IdentityClient.parseIdentity`
(`IdentityClient.ts:1044`), which reads decrypted fields, no JSON text.

Census (#375; current reading):

- Row 92: Ours: closed by #566 at the pin: both `ls_identity` parsers read a certificateRecord text with a lone surrogate escape as JSON.parse and TextEncoder do (wallet-toolbox identityUtils.ts:88,100-125 and Certificate.ts:73-75,280-296 at edf6e03), the names compared unit for unit, each string held with U+FFFD; residues the held character where the reference holds the lone unit, two names one String holds and a lone unit's ICU order beside a private-use or unassigned BMP character above U+DFFF (U+E000 recorded). Theirs: none (the witness: tests/identity_lone_surrogate_566.rs; tests/vectors/identity_lone_surrogate_566.json).

### Fixed: the nightly's Mutants jobs resolve the dependency graph once before cargo-mutants (#574)

The nightly's one run (`nightly.yml`, 2026-10-27, run 40474836749) failed all
twenty Mutants jobs at the unmutated baseline, before any mutant was tested:
`cannot create the lock file .../Cargo.lock because --locked was passed to
prevent this`. `nightly_mutants.py` passes `--cargo-arg=--locked`, the library
commits no `Cargo.lock` (`.gitignore`), and cargo-mutants' copy of the checkout
had none to read. The `mutants` job now runs `cargo generate-lockfile` in the
checkout before cargo-mutants, as `ci.yml`'s fixtures job and `bench.yml`
already resolve before their `--locked` commands; `--locked` stays, so the
baseline and every mutant of a shard build one graph. `docs/NIGHTLY.md` says
so. The witness: the script's own command on the merkle shard 0/400 of a
scratch copy with no lock fails its baseline with that text (exit 4), and the
same command after `cargo generate-lockfile` builds the baseline and tests the
shard's mutant (exit 0). The fuzz job passes `--locked` only to
`cargo install`, which reads the installed crate's own lock, and needs no step.

### Added: the reference's public-key validators as public helpers, each named for its site (#579)

bsv-wallet-cli#377 found the lenient `PublicKey::from_hex` (#498, the
reference's `PublicKey.fromString`) at four of the CLI's served doors, where
the reference's validators read a caller's key strictly; the CLI then wrote a
host copy of this crate's crate-private `PublicKey::from_strict_hex`. The
keeper's word (the rulings page's entry of 2026-11-01 01:1xZ, issue #579,
shape (2)): one public helper per reference validator, named for the
reference's site, each returning the parsed key or the reference's refusal;
`from_strict_hex` stays private and `from_hex` is untouched. Not shape (1),
`from_strict_hex` made public: an internal reader as public API names the
port's mechanism, not the reference's rule. The ground is #505's: one
definition of the reference's rule for every host.

| Helper | Reference (`ts-stack@edf6e03`) | Rule | Refusal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wallet::validate_public_key(value: &str, name: &str) -> Result<PublicKey>` (in `wallet::validation`, `src/wallet/validation/crypto.rs`) | `validatePublicKey`, `packages/sdk/src/wallet/validationHelpers.ts:185-191`, through `validateHexString` (`:522-534`) and `isValidCompressedPublicKey` (`Secp256k1Validation.ts:15-22`) | the text trimmed as JavaScript trims it, an even UTF-16 length, hex digits of either case, exactly 66 characters, `02`/`03`, x below p and a point's | `Error::WalletRefusal` of class `InvalidParameter` (code 6): `The <name> parameter must be ` then `even length, not N.`, `hexadecimal string.`, `at least 66 length.`, `no more than 66 length.` or `a valid compressed secp256k1 public key` |

The auth rule is not the wallet rule at another site: it trims nothing and
reads lowercase alone (an upper-case or space-padded key the wallet reads is
refused), and its words are its own. Both return a key equal to `from_hex`
of the same text (the wallet's of the trimmed text, since `from_hex` trims
nothing) and refuse every lenient form #498's reader accepts (an
odd-length key, an uncompressed or hybrid key, an x at or above p). The
wallet helper is the crate-private `public_key_hex` of #420 renamed and made
public, the one definition `Counterparty::from_hex` and the registry's
operator check (#543) already call; the auth helper is #294's private
`assert_auth_identity_key` moved to its own file, returning the key, the
one the requested set's certifiers call. No site is rewired: the
`from_strict_hex` sites (serde's `PublicKey` reading, `KeyringRevealer`, the
Peer's identity pin and own key, the three certificate intakes, the HTTP
answer's identity header at the transport and the payment) equal neither
helper, since `from_strict_hex` reads an uncompressed key and upper-case hex
(the older gap CLAUDE.md states); moving any of them is a follow-up.

### Fixed: the wallet wire's sendWithResults status codes are BRC-100's and the reference's, 1/2/3 (#590)

A createAction or signAction result's `sendWithResults` entry carries its
status as one byte. This crate wrote and read 0 `unproven`, 1 `sending`, 2
`failed`; BRC-100 at `5119a9b` names 1, 2, 3 (`wallet/0100.md:1724-1726`),
the reference writes them (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`WalletWireProcessor.ts:151-156`, called at `:624` and `:775`) and reads them
back (`WalletWireTransceiver.ts:1226-1234`), refusing another byte in its
words, `Unknown sendWith result status code: N`, the byte read signed
(`readInt8`). So a TypeScript wallet's `sending` (`02`) read here as
`Failed`, its `failed` (`03`) was refused (`invalid send with result status:
3`), and on a TypeScript client this crate's `unproven` (`00`) was refused,
its `sending` (`01`) read as `unproven` and its `failed` (`02`) as `sending`.
`WireWriter::write_send_with_result_status` now writes 1/2/3 and
`WireReader::read_send_with_result_status` reads them, any other byte refused
as `Error::WalletError` in the reference's words with the byte signed (`0`,
`4`, `127`, `-128`, `-1` for `0xff`).

### Fixed: the identity parsers' subject and certifier read a key as `Certificate.toBinary` reads it (#585)

The two `ls_identity` token parsers (`parse_output_to_certificate` and
`parse_output_to_verifiable_certificate`, through `src/identity/client_record.rs`)
read a published certificate's `subject` and `certifier` through
`PublicKey::from_strict_hex` (even-length hex, then `from_bytes`), which reads an
uncompressed key. The reference reads them where its discovery verifies the
record: `Certificate.verify` runs `toBinary` first (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`Certificate.ts:425-427`), which takes the text untrimmed and requires
`/^(02|03)[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/` (`:240-254`, else `Invalid certificate <field>:
expected compressed public key hex`), then the 33 bytes read as a point
(`assertCompressedPublicKey`, `:136-143`, else `Invalid certificate <field>:
expected a compressed secp256k1 public key`); a refusal there is `verify`'s
`false`, and the toolbox's discovery skips the token (`identityUtils.ts:497-559`).
An uncompressed subject or certifier was read here, the certificate verified
over its compressed bytes and returned; it is now skipped by both parsers, as
the reference skips it. Closed by #585: the residue #582's entry states for these
two sites.

One definition: `auth::certificates::read_to_binary_key(text, field)`
(`src/auth/certificates/to_binary_key.rs`, crate-private, under `identity`),
`toBinary`'s rule in its two sentences as `Error::CertificateValidationError`.
It is none of the #579 helpers' rules: `wallet::validate_public_key` trims a
space-padded text `toBinary` refuses, `auth::assert_auth_identity_key` refuses
upper-case hex `toBinary` reads, and `wallet::validate_result_public_key`
judges the same texts in the result validator's words. A compressed x at or
above p, which `fromDER` reduces and `toBinary` writes unreduced, stays #183's
refusal at the read: a stated residue. The vector's certificate, signed over
the canonical subject, fails `verify` with it on both sides; a certificate its
certifier signed over those unreduced bytes verifies there (`verify` `true`, a
probe under Node v22.18.0 in #592's cold read, not pinned) and is skipped here.

### Fixed: the nightly's Mutants oracle runs its test binaries under a memory ceiling (#577)

Run 41252901741 lost four Mutants shards' hosted runners (script 1/4, 2/4,
3/4 and substrates 1/4: `The runner has received a shutdown signal`) after
their baselines passed, and the rerun lost script 3/4 again after the same
seven logged mutants: a deterministic loss at one mutant, not the runners'.
Each shard's culprit, measured on a scratch copy of beta with the job's own
oracle (`nightly_mutants.py`'s command, one mutant at a time) under a watchdog,
is a mutant that stops a parser's position advancing, so its loop pushes on
every pass: script 3/4 `src/script/script.rs:79:19` (`+=` to `*=` in
`Script::from_asm`, 16 GB in 16 seconds), script 2/4 `script.rs:120:23` (the
same, 12.6 GB in 17 seconds), script 1/4 `script.rs:210:17` (`+=` to `*=` in
`Script::parse_chunks`, 13.6 GB in 7 seconds), substrates 1/4
`src/wallet/substrates/result_values/raw_tree.rs:168:28` (`+=` to `*=` in
`Snapshot::read`, 14.7 GB in 10 seconds), each far inside the 120-second test
timeout. The `mutants` job now sets cargo's target runner
(`CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_RUNNER`) to
`.github/scripts/test-runner-memory-ceiling.sh`, which execs each test binary
under `ulimit -v` at 12,000,000 KB (`MUTANTS_TEST_VMEM_KB`): the allocation
past the ceiling aborts the binary and the mutant is caught; rustc and the
build scripts do not run through the runner. `docs/NIGHTLY.md` says so. The
local witness, in a Linux container (Rust 1.99.1, the aarch64 runner
variable): under the runner, `script.rs:79:19` is `CaughtMutant` (`memory
allocation of 4294967296 bytes failed`, SIGABRT, a 40-second test phase) and
`raw_tree.rs:168:28` the same (`memory allocation of 15032385536 bytes
failed`); without it, `script.rs:79:19`'s test binary passed 12 GB resident
in 24 seconds before the guard killed it; the five surfaces' baselines pass
under the ceiling (script 491, substrates 96, wire 288, merkle 124, BEEF 392
tests), their largest binary peaking at 805 MB of address space; a build with
the runner set at a 200 MB ceiling compiles, where the same limit in the shell
stops rustc. The CI witness is the dispatch of `nightly.yml` after the landing.

### Fixed: the `get_verifiable_certificates` certifier is checked against the requested set as the reference checks it (#587)

`get_verifiable_certificates` proved and forwarded every certificate its
wallet listed whose subject and certifier read: a valid, lowercase certifier
outside the requested set was proved and returned, and a type the set does not
request was proved with no fields to reveal. The reference checks each listed
certificate before `proveCertificate` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/auth/utils/getVerifiableCertificates.ts:76-81`):
`requestedCertificates.certifiers.includes(certificate.certifier)`, a text
comparison with the set's certifiers, which `assertAuthIdentityKey` holds
canonical (`AuthMessageValidation.ts:124`), and `Array.isArray` of the type's
requested fields; either failing throws `Wallet returned a certificate outside
the requested certifier/type set`, which rejects the `Promise.all` and so the
whole call, and its three `Peer` callers propagate it (`Peer.ts:845,1016,1109`).
This crate now does the same, in that order: the subject's result-validator
check (#582, a skip as before), then the certifier's text and the type against
the requested set, the whole call refused as `Error::AuthError` in the
reference's words, then `prove_certificate`. The refusal is the reference's
verdict, not a skip as the site's other refusals are: the reference throws at
this line, and the Peer, the AuthFetch callback and the initial-request path
here return the error as the reference's callers throw it. A lenient or
upper-case certifier text, none of a canonical set's, is now this refusal where
#498 and #582 skipped it. The certifier's `assert_auth_identity_key` read stays
after the membership, a skip, reached only by a caller's own non-canonical set
(the Peer validates its sets). `get_verifiable_certificates` moved, unchanged in
signature, to `src/auth/utils/verifiable.rs` (the ratchet's bounds on
`validation.rs`).

Pinned against `tests/vectors/verifiable_certificates_membership_587.json`,
written by `tests/support/verifiable_certificates_membership_587.mjs` (a bun
bundle of `getVerifiableCertificates` and `PrivateKey` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`
under Node v22.18.0, a fake wallet counting proveCertificate calls): six cases
(in the set; a certifier outside it; an upper-case certifier; a type outside
it; an outside certificate after and before an in-set one), each verdict and
count of proofs. Tests in `tests/auth_verifiable_certificates_membership_587.rs`:
`a_valid_certifier_outside_the_requested_set_refuses_the_call_587` (every
recorded verdict in the reference's words and its proofs, one count the stated
residue) and `a_lowercase_certifier_outside_the_set_is_not_proved_or_forwarded_587`,
both RED on `cf1c13bb` with the test and the vector overlaid (`assertion left ==
right failed`, `left: Ok(1)`, `right: Err(AuthError("Wallet returned a
certificate outside the requested certifier/type set"))`), GREEN on the tip.
`tests/auth_key_strictness_sites_498.rs`'s
`a_wallet_certificate_key_in_a_lenient_form_is_not_forwarded_498` and
`an_upper_case_wallet_certificate_certifier_is_not_forwarded_582` re-read
against the reference: their certifier cases now assert the refusal.

Texts: one new error text, the reference's. No dependent calls
`get_verifiable_certificates` or matches the text (bsv-overlay-cloudflare,
rust-message-box, bsv-wallet-cli and bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs grepped, `*.rs`
outside `target`: no hit). No public API moves. No census row names the
site (`Row N:` lines of `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/` grepped for
`getVerifiableCertificates`, `get_verifiable_certificates` and the requested
certifier: no hit).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#587)

One residue, stated: the reference's `matchingCertificates.certificates.map`
starts every callback before `Promise.all` rejects, so an in-set certificate
listed after an outside one is still proved there (`proveCalls` 1 in the
recorded `outside_before_inside`) and not here, where the loop stops at the
refusal (0); the verdict is the same. Likewise a wallet's proveCertificate
error on an earlier certificate is returned here before a later certificate's
membership refusal, where the reference's synchronous throw rejects first.
A second residue, older than #587 (#582's): a direct caller's own set whose
certifier text is not canonical (`02` and 64 upper-case hex digits, say) and a
listed certificate carrying the same text pass the membership in both; the
reference proves and returns it (the function asserts no key, its
`Certificate` constructor stores the text, `Certificate.ts:197-213`; probed
under Node v22.18.0: one certificate, one proof), where this crate skips it at
`assert_auth_identity_key` before `prove_certificate`. The `Peer` never reaches
it: its sets are validated (`assert_requested_certificate_set`, #294).
go-sdk at `2ca481c` has no certifier membership check and skips an unrequested
type or one with no requested fields (`auth/utils/get_verifiable_certificates.go:60-71`),
so it proves and returns a certificate of any certifier the wallet lists.

`wallet::validate_result_public_key(value, call, field)` (#582's fold, #584)

### Fixed: the Mutants oracle's memory ceiling at 4,000,000 KB, and a step proving the runner hook is live (#577)

The witness of #595's ceiling, run 41288213777 at `94862392`, lost Mutants
(script, 1/4)'s hosted runner again 21 minutes in, with the runner variable in
the run step's environment and the baseline passed under it, where the shard's
next entries reach the culprit `src/script/script.rs:210:17` (`+=` to `*=` in
`Script::parse_chunks`). Two readings, both closed here. (a) The ceiling was
too high: an unbounded Vec doubles, so under a ceiling of C the process touches
up to about C before its next reserve fails; the 8 GiB reserve fit under
12,000,000 KB and the 16 GB runner, with the system, cargo and cargo-mutants
resident, ran out before any allocation was refused. `MUTANTS_TEST_VMEM_KB` is
now 4,000,000 KB (3.8 GiB), well under half the runner: the five surfaces'
baselines peak at 805 MB of address space in one test binary (#595's
measurement), fivefold room, and the culprits fail their first reserve past
3.8 GiB. (b) Nothing in the job's log proved the hook reached the test binaries
on x86_64: `test-runner-memory-ceiling.sh` now writes the limit in force to
`MUTANTS_CEILING_MARKER` when that names a file, and the new step "Prove the
memory ceiling reaches the test binaries" runs `cargo test --features full,http
--locked --lib -- --list` through the hook (the job's target directory) and
fails the job unless the marker holds `MUTANTS_TEST_VMEM_KB`; the variable is
that step's alone, so no mutant writes it. A platform refusing `ulimit -v`
(macOS) gets a warning and an unbounded run, and the marker then records
`unlimited`, so the proof fails rather than passing silently. `docs/NIGHTLY.md`
says so. The CI witness is a dispatch of `nightly.yml` after the landing.

## [0.9.0-beta.5] - 2026-10-31

The 0.9.0 line's fifth prerelease (RELEASING.md point 14), cut from `beta` at the owner's word through the keeper (14:4xZ on 2026-10-31, the rulings page's entry of that hour, 22.6 of the brief in the one-hour shape of 19.7: bsv-rs 0.9.0-beta.5, then the toolbox's re-pin at the index hour, then the CLI's pin PR with its gate once after) at the tip after #554 landed (`e215aea8`): the beta.5 milestone's content (the per-transaction work budget #519, the public typed word resolver #520, `WorkBudget` `#[non_exhaustive]` #527, R56 for an unsigned action's input #491) and the 0.9.0 landings since beta.4 (the processor request cap #505, the #487 nits #502, the ordered certificate response #400, AuthFetch #423, the preimage witness #375, the Documentation check #515, the one byte bound #512 #526 #532, the local store's lock-before decode #499, the arch allowlist rule #347, the fixtures' Origin header #346, the six sites' lock position #537, the lenient key parser with every validator path strict #498, the contacts protocol and envelope #542 #543, the token-decode record checks #544, a SEC 1 tag `05` refused #550, the registry's definition-token unlock #548, `Contact`'s badge fields and its closing #552): 24 entries. The lenient string parser lands with every validator path strict, never alone (the keeper's 08:1xZ recommendation); `Contact`'s closing is the line's one api-break since beta.4, its migration in #552's notes.

### Fixed: refuse oversized wallet wire requests before decoding (#505)

`WalletWireProcessor::process_message` now refuses a complete request above
256 MiB (268,435,456 bytes) before constructing a reader, decoding arguments
or calling the wallet. It reuses #496's `wire_request_length` and
`MAX_WIRE_REQUEST_BYTES` in `substrates/result_values/boundary.rs`; the length
comparison precedes any allocation. The refusal is
`Err(Error::WalletError("Wallet Wire request exceeds the maximum permitted size"))`
returned by `process_message`, not an error frame. A frame exactly at the cap
still reaches the wallet.

The reference is `ts-stack@edf6e03`: `WalletWire.ts:9` defines
`MAX_WALLET_WIRE_FRAME_BYTES`; `WalletWireProcessor.ts:248-250` (legacy array)
and `:265-269` (compact bytes) reject lengths strictly greater than that cap
with those uncoded words. Both throw from `transmitToWallet` before
`#processMessage` is entered, outside its `try` (`:274`) and so outside the
catch that writes error frames (`:2370-2396`): the caller's promise rejects
and no frame is written. `process_message` is that method here, so the
refusal is its `Err` in the same words, as #496's transceiver returns its own.
This follows the owner's ruling (c): the reference's own resource safeguard
needs no new word.

The toolbox's and CLI's tables change as follows:

| Consumer | Request | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Toolbox error table | Complete frame above 268,435,456 bytes | Decoded; an otherwise valid request reached the wallet | `process_message` returns `Err(WalletError)`: `Wallet Wire request exceeds the maximum permitted size`; no frame, no wallet call |
| CLI operator-visible table | Complete frame above 268,435,456 bytes | Any decode or wallet outcome | The transport hosting the processor receives the error before decoding, as a host of the reference's `transmitToWallet` receives its rejection; the transceiver refuses such a frame itself first (#496) |
| Both | Complete frame exactly at 268,435,456 bytes | Decoded and dispatched | Decoded and dispatched |

`tests/wallet_wire_processor_request_cap_505.rs` builds valid encrypt frames
with this crate's `WireWriter`, using a large plaintext that itself remains
below the byte-field limit. The transceiver cannot supply the over-cap frame
because #496 already refuses it. On base
`8fd26a3ecc61cc485647f2152e5482a211491692`, cap + 1 reached the counting wallet
once (the RED assertion); exactly cap reached it once and returned its answer.
With the guard, cap + 1 makes zero wallet calls and `process_message` returns
the error in the reference's words; exactly cap still returns the wallet's
answer. No recorded vectors change.

The wire decoder fuzz target checks that same size boundary: an oversized
request returns the exact `Err(WalletError)` above; failures at or below the
cap remain framed responses.

Migration: a request above the cap was decoded before; now
`process_message` returns `Err` for it, where every other refusal is an
`Ok` error frame: a host that relays `process_message`'s answer handles
the `Err` as it handles a transport failure. No API change; requests at or
below the cap are unchanged.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#505)

Go at `2ca481c` checks only for an empty message before `ReadRequestFrame`
(`wallet/substrates/wallet_wire_processor.go:24-29`), returning `empty message`.
It has no complete-request upper bound. The keeper's 2026-10-30 08:1xZ ruling
holds this as a stated row: the frame cap is the reference's own resource
safeguard, not a BRC number, and Go's choice stands. This processor cap is
hardening, alongside #496's transceiver cap; it does not reopen that held row.
The reference's exact-cap encrypt decode also hits V8's `Array.from` limit
before dispatch (`WalletWireProcessor.ts:1427`, measured in #496); Rust's
exact-cap control exercises its own existing, accepted decode path.

### Changed: three post-#487 review nits (#502)

- Removed 13 redundant `#[path]` attributes; Rust resolves the same result modules in the same order without them.
- Shared `boundary::MAX_BYTES` with the wire byte check and request-frame cap, formatting the unchanged refusal from that one numeric definition.
- Enabled output-script binding in the 64 MiB dhat pin (`fixture(64, true)`): peak 201,331,778 → 335,550,248 bytes; budget 268,436,568 → 402,654,852 bytes (four → six frame lengths) to cover the encoded request buffers; existing exact pins stay exact.

### Fixed: signed certificate-response JSON order, with a crate-wide body census (#400)

The #400 census was made at beta base `8e57ee462aee6cc5e4888fee7edc02ee2b61d4aa`
against `ts-stack@edf6e03dad39bd7bc4fc6e73e64de3a2b6f805c9`
(`packages/sdk/src/`, `packages/wallet/`, and the AuthSocket client).
Reference filenames below are relative to `packages/sdk/src/`, except
AuthSocketClient in `packages/messaging/authsocket-client/src/`.
Line references to Rust writers identify the base implementation.

**Finding: 31 writer groups, one nonempty finding: `certificates`.**
The reference signs the certificateResponse array at `Peer.ts:1140` and
re-stringifies its restored certificates to verify at `:1203`. Retaining raw
text signed numeric field/keyring names in the wrong order and retained an
incoming certificate's property order instead of the reference class layout.
The fix orders this one body at its signing site: #426's ordered-node parser
restores the class properties, keeps nested objects in their text's order,
and applies JavaScript's numeric-key, string and number rules. The fallback
serializes typed `Vec<VerifiableCertificate>` directly to `RawValue`, preserving
struct declaration order and the nested `IndexMap` entries before using the
same signing function. It never passes through a sorted `Value`.

serde_json's default is unchanged, no key order of any other body moves, and nothing unifies across a consumer's graph.

The transport retains its text; both sides derive the reference's signed
JSON from it. Signatures over noncanonical raw response text are no longer
accepted; callers signing messages use `signing_data()`. No public API shape
or dependency changes. Other direct-map representations retain their
documented integer-name ordering; this is not a general JS serializer.

`tests/auth_response_order_400.rs` has three regressions: received numeric
field/keyring names, the typed fallback without retained text, and reversed
class properties with an ignored extension. All three fail on unchanged
`8e57ee46` for the signed bytes' order with serde_json's default. The expected
bytes come from the pinned Peer's actual `sendCertificateResponse`, using
numeric keys `10,2` and nonnumeric keys `z,a` to distinguish both ordering
rules. `tests/support/auth_response_order_400.mjs` writes the vector under
Node 22.18.0; two runs are byte-identical and the reference receiver verifies
both input permutations. The kept #280 and #394 pins cover signed text and
unchanged ordinary lookup bytes.

A whole-body comparison below means a reader requires particular serialized
bytes or a recorded assertion requires them. A signature on **received**
opaque bytes is listed too: it authenticates that serialization but does
not require the receiver to rebuild JSON in its own key order. Thus the
registry and contact rows are not canonical JSON checks.

Order notation: **V** means Value/Map (sorted keys, unchanged). **I** means IndexMap insertion
order; **H** means HashMap unspecified iteration order. Derived Serialize
uses declaration order. JavaScript puts array-index names first numerically,
then other names in insertion order; the signed-member reserializer applies
that extra rule. The table enumerates all 28 HTTP wallet calls and the other
writer families, including internal serializers and binary-body exclusions.

recorder with serde_json's default and the Node 22 `fixtures_order_400.mjs` writer
confirm byte-for-byte equality; no existing vector needs a key-order rewrite.

sorted. Only the new #400 certificate-response witness is recorded.

The same census is in `src/CLAUDE.md`. Search scope, fixture interpretation,

Migration: no public type or method changes, and every reader here, in the
reference and in Go parses JSON by member and accepts any key order.
serde_json's default is unchanged: no key order of any other body this crate
writes moves, and nothing unifies across a consumer's dependency graph (no
feature, no new crate). Only the certificate response's signed text changes,
to the reference's property order. A peer at 0.9.0-beta.3 or earlier that
sends a certificateResponse with integer-like field or keyring names out of
ascending order signed its raw text, and this crate's Peer now refuses it, as
the reference's does.

go-sdk@2ca481c signs and verifies a certificateResponse over `json.Marshal`
of the certificates (`auth/peer.go:1189` sending, `:898` re-marshalling the
parsed copy): its struct order is the reference class's (`type,

`auth/certificates/certificate.go:34-52`; `keyring, decryptedFields`,
`verifiable.go:19-28`), and every map's keys are sorted by bytes. Its preimage
equals the reference's and this crate's only when the field and keyring names'

there, after it here and in the reference; `z,a` as inserted here, `a,z`

and fails between either and Go. The members' value encodings in Go's
marshalling are not compared here. Theirs: go-sdk, the filing is row 61's (the certificate-response preimage draft, tenth
in the queue; the witness there tests/auth_certificate_preimage_375.rs; this entry's witness:
tests/auth_response_order_400.rs; tests/vectors/auth_response_order_400.json).
